author: azumag
body:
## Summary

Advances #223 without selecting an endpoint runtime/cache design.

The existing diagnostic materializer validates source identity and records payload hashes, but the evidence was still producer-self-reported: there was no separate pass that re-derived the pinned stage/tier blueprint and independently proved the payload bytes still matched the pinned source ranges.

This PR adds `verify_endpoint_payload_materialization.py`, which:
- requires the pinned external-data file plus the expected stage/tier explicitly instead of trusting those claims from the materialization report
- re-derives the deterministic pinned blueprint and provenance from the probe report
- re-hashes the complete source against the pinned identity
- independently re-hashes every referenced source range and every payload, requiring all three digests (source range, payload, producer report) to agree
- validates source coverage, payload geometry/count/total bytes, and exact payload filenames
- requires the payload directory to contain exactly the expected `payload-*.bin` set and rejects symlink payloads
- hashes the exact probe/materialization JSON bytes parsed by the CLI and binds those input-report digests into the verification result
- emits only `decisionStatus=diagnostic-only`; no browser cache/manifest/loader/runtime or vocabulary-axis chunking decision is made

During review of the first implementation, I found a blocking provenance gap: re-hashing only the payload and comparing it with the producer-reported hash would allow a payload and its report hash to be edited together while merely *claiming* the pinned source identity. The current head closes that gap by taking the source file as an independent input and hashing each exact source range before accepting a payload.

A second review pass removed an unnecessary source-symlink rejection: model caches commonly expose immutable blobs through symlinks, and the verifier already proves the dereferenced bytes by pinned size/SHA-256 plus per-range hashes. Generated payload symlinks remain rejected.

Tests cover the passing source-backed path, payload+report collusion, source identity tampering, report geometry/provenance tampering, extra payloads, symlink payloads, explicit stage/tier derivation, and exact input-report byte hashing. Documentation includes the source-backed verification workflow.

## Validation

LLM Proto #373 / run 34071717226 passed on final head `6275dbf6f354658c2690bcf3e1e52c0b2941bea9`, including typecheck, browser harness syntax, pinned SmolLM2 probe, pinned Llama 1B blocker probe, real ONNX split contract tests, and full tests.

author: boburning
body:
Portcove's roadmap now treats broad, current catalog coverage and declining routine maintainer effort as product outcomes. It preserves the seven finite V1 outcomes and Alpha 2's exact-package handoff while scheduling compatible client loading for Alpha 3 and configured-upstream freshness for Beta 1.

The live reconciliation is tracked in #396. New finite owners are #397 (phase 1 of #246, Required Alpha 3) and #398 (configured observation under #177, Required Beta 1 with implementation beginning Alpha 3). #246 retains complete Beta 1 acceptance/publication and depends one way on those components; broad #177 remains Post-V1/Opportunistic. Existing #49 is forecast for Beta 1 because #215 already inherits it as a safety prerequisite; its Blocked status is preserved.

Updated existing scopes: #14, #30, #31, #177, #206, #243, #245, #246, #247 and #254. The documentation clarifies incremental migration without catalog regression, one preparation/launch family, independent delivery through application freezes, repeatable onboarding, and outcome measures with honest unknown baselines. Existing completed evidence and implementation states remain intact.

No runtime code, catalog support/admission, qualification, active-release configuration, automation, repository protection, signing or publication changes are included. References to future capability and publisher behavior are explicitly planned; format 1 remains unchanged. Implementation issues are not closed by this PR.

Validation: full local `just audit` passed at original head `c2d9bf8` (407 core, 41 CLI, 20 desktop and 149 UI tests; 25 rscheck advisories, zero blockers). After refreshing onto concurrently merged #395, the three planning files remain byte-for-byte identical; final `just roadmap-check` (93 tests) and `git diff --check` pass. Live doctor confirms 186 port issues, 67 catalog identities, 22 fields, 10 views and 178 UX origins. Alpha 2 has unchanged 43 required/8 unfinished gates; later graphs add only #397/#398 and have no classification conflicts or cycles. Separate planning/Fallow review is complete. Exact refreshed-head CI must pass before normal merge; no administrator bypass.

The [applied reconciliation record](https://github.com/boburning/portcove/issues/396#issuecomment-5563580148) lists all canonical edits, Project fields, true dependencies, preserved/deferred work, measurements and ordered implementation handoff.

Refs #396, #245, #246, #177, #397, #398.

- **T02 — Redis runs the shared contract suite**: six aggregate contract bodies extracted into `tests/common/repository_contract.rs` and reused by memory, file **and** a new feature-gated `tests/repository_redis_contract.rs` (runs against `RepositorySet::redis` when `ACMEX_TEST_REDIS_URL` is set; otherwise prints an explicit SKIP and exits 77 — a skipped run is not a release pass). Candidate: `57c18a632110e6699eb6a17f6c81a3734e45d8ad`

- First parent / current `dev`: `5d8e97764747da1559738e6073e6e65d6b32a654`
- Second parent / current `main`: `e32a38689acf9137ac6d6dacce67a767cba922c3`
- Original merge base: `23fa6a972723ad39f4beaa4f765be3db76452199`
- Candidate and `dev` share tree `573a38a621f2672d4d56e69ea4518fb6620a5270`; the PR intentionally has no file changes. Its effect is Git ancestry.

Resolved conflicts:

- `.github/dependabot.yml` (add/add): retain the current npm and GitHub Actions updates targeting `dev`.
- `package.json` (content): retain current scripts, dependencies, and scoped Sharp override.
- `package-lock.json` (content): retain the current deterministic lockfile. Direct and transitive main updates are already matched or superseded by `dev`, or removed by its newer dependency graph. Examples: React `19.2.6`, Vite `7.3.6`, React Router `7.18.3`, Rollup `4.60.0`, and Workbox `7.4.1`.

Version impact: **none**; remains `0.12.0`. No product behavior, backend contract, verification gate, or workflow setting changes.

- Production release mode: `VITE_CHIPIN_ENV=prod CHIPIN_TASK_BRANCH=main CHIPIN_TASK_HEAD_SHA=57c18a632110e6699eb6a17f6c81a3734e45d8ad npm run vercel-build` passed (599 tests and production build).
- `npm run version:bump -- none` and `npm run version:check` passed; release version resolves to `0.12.0`.
- `git diff --check`, exact tree equality with `dev`, both-parent ancestry, and the GPG commit signature verified.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree` for both current `dev` and `main` against this candidate succeeded with the unchanged candidate tree.
- Existing baseline: 29 lint warnings, zero errors; npm reports 2 dependency vulnerabilities (1 moderate, 1 high). This resolution does not change the dependency graph.
- Independent Sol 5.6 High review of the pinned resolution: no actionable findings. Reviewed both-parent ancestry, all three resolutions, direct/transitive dependency preservation, unchanged verification gates, and version impact.
- Mandatory Husky pre-push `version:check` and `verify:full` both passed.
- [Frontend CI](https://github.com/ChipIn-one/chipin-frontend/actions/runs/34071434286): **success**, attempt 1, head `57c18a632110e6699eb6a17f6c81a3734e45d8ad`. author: bentripode
body:
The last five, and the end of the alphabetical pass. **All 51 jurisdictions are now on primary text.**

Sources, all read 2026-09-06 from each legislature's own site:

| | |
|---|---|
| VA | [Va. Code § 3.2-5130](https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacode/title3.2/chapter51/section3.2-5130/) — **as amended by 2026 c. 605** |
| WA | [RCW 69.22.010–.110](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=69.22&full=true), full chapter |
| WV | [W. Va. Code §§ 19-40-1 to 19-40-6](https://code.wvlegislature.gov/19-40-1/) and [§ 19-35-6](https://code.wvlegislature.gov/19-35-6/) |
| WI | [Wis. Stat. § 97.29](https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/document/statutes/97.29) |
| WY | [Wyo. Stat. §§ 11-49-102, 11-49-103](https://www.wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title11.pdf) |

---

## Virginia's cap was amended out from under us this year

`state_cottage_food_rules.revenue_cap` held **$9,000**, and the note signed on 2026-09-05 says it "applies to BOTH home-kitchen subdivisions ... each end with 'not exceeding $9,000 in gross sales in a calendar year'". **That was true of the text as it then stood.**

§ 3.2-5130(C)(3), as amended by **2026 c. 605**, now ends at five conditions and none of them is a cap. The $9,000 survives only in **(C)(4)** — "pickles and other acidified vegetables that have an equilibrium pH value of 4.6 or lower".

Left in the state-wide fallback column, that would have paused a Virginian selling nothing but jam and bread at **$9,000.01**, on a limit their subdivision no longer carries. It moves to the programme row as `cap_basis = 'per_category'`, `cap_category = 'acidified'`.

**Virginia is the `per_category` example again — and this is the third figure that row has held.** A seeded $3,000 acidified-only, then a $9,000 annual-total "correction", now a $9,000 acidified-only. The seed had the right shape and the wrong number; the correction had the right number and the wrong shape; the statute has both.

## Four disclaimers were wrong, in two different ways

**Tidied:**

| | stored | statute |
|---|---|---|
| VA | `NOT FOR RESALE - PROCESSED AND PREPARED WITHOUT STATE INSPECTION.` | `NOT FOR RESALE PROCESSED AND PREPARED WITHOUT STATE INSPECTION.` — no dash |
| WY | `This food was made in a home kitchen, is not regulated or inspected and may contain allergens.` | § 11-49-103(k) quotes it lower case with no closing period |

**Inherited from a law that doesn't reach the row:**

* **WV** carried *"This product was produced at a private residence that is exempt from state licensing and inspection. This product may contain allergens."* — that is **Tennessee's** statutory sentence (Tenn. Code § 53-1-118(b)(4)(D)), also Arkansas's. No West Virginia authority prescribes it: § 19-35-6(c) says only that food "shall be labeled in compliance with the department's labeling standards", delegating the whole thing. Removed; the department's standards are what an admin should read next.
* **WI's baking route** carried its own **canning** statute's sentence. § 97.29(2)(b)2.e prescribes it for the canning exemption; the baked-goods route exists by a 2017 Lafayette County Circuit Court injunction and has no statute at all. Removed there, kept verbatim on the canning row.
* **VA's licensed route** carried "WITHOUT STATE INSPECTION" while being, by § 3.2-5130(A), inspected. Same reasoning that emptied Vermont's two licensed rows and Maryland's on-farm one.

## Wisconsin needs a sign, and we had not recorded one

> **97.29(2)(b)2.d** displays a sign at the place of sale stating: "These canned goods are homemade and not subject to state inspection."

A **different sentence** from the label statement at 2.e. `placard_required` was false. Wisconsin is the third state found with that split, after Colorado and Illinois.

Two more from the same subsection: `product_name` is not among the required label items (2.e asks for the preparer, the date, the statement and the ingredients), and the allergen list is **eight**, not the federal nine — sesame is absent.

## West Virginia had five of six axes banned, and the state expressly permits hazardous food

§ 19-40-2(a) creates a *"potentially hazardous cottage food vendor permit"* for exactly that, § 19-40-5(c) says standards "shall be determined, **including acidified foods**", and § 19-40-1 defines "Produce" to include **fermenting** and **preserving**. Refrigerated, acidified and fermented become `conditional` on holding that permit. **Only meat is genuinely banned** — by the definition of "cottage food" itself, which "excludes meat, meat products, poultry, poultry products, seafood, and Grade A dairy products".

Its channel rules also turn out to live somewhere else entirely: § 19-40-6 sends the ordinary case out of the cottage food article into **§ 19-35-6**, whose (b) permits sale "whether in person or **remotely**, or by an agent of the producer or a third-party vendor" and delivery by "a third-party carrier". Online, mail and retail were right on the summary and are now on the words.

## Wyoming bans meat with seven exceptions, and tells the buyer first

Every axis read `allowed`. § 11-49-103(c)(v): transactions shall "Not involve the sale of meat products", then lists the exceptions — poultry under a 1,000-bird own-raising limit, live animals, portions before slaughter, domestic rabbit meat, farm-raised fish that is not catfish, an animal share, and (n) meat products. `conditional`.

And Wyoming joins the predisclosure list **by the same route as Utah** — through the structure of the exemption, not a labelling rule. § 11-49-102(a)(v) defines the "informed end consumer" as one "who has been informed that the product is not licensed, regulated or inspected", and (e) makes telling them the producer's duty. Substance prescribed, wording open → a `seller_statement`, shown on the listing.

Its $250,000 stays and is a real boundary: § 11-49-102(a)(vi) puts it in the definition of "Producer", so a person over it is not a producer and the Act does not reach them. It is a **two-part test** — 250,000 individual products *and* $250,000 gross revenue — and only the money half is modelled.

## Washington: confirmed, and one element added

RCW 69.22.020(4) read in the chapter rather than a compilation: *"Cottage food products may only be sold directly to the consumer and may not be sold by internet, mail order, or for retail sale outside the state."* Washington stays one of the states where a food listing here is unlawful outright.

Its label gains `allergens` — 69.22.020(3)(e) requires allergen labelling flatly, not conditionally, and it was missing — plus the contrasting-colour instruction that sits in the same clause as the 11-point minimum. `recipe_approval` drops to `no`: the chapter has none, only the director's power to list permitted foods in rule, which `cat_shelf_stable = list_only` already records.

## Why WA's and WI's figures stay in the cap column and VT's and VA's did not

The line is **which row the figure sits on**, not whether crossing it needs a licence. Washington's $35,000 and Wisconsin's $5,000 bound the programme rows they belong to — a seller who outgrows the exemption moves to a different programme. Vermont's $30,000 and Virginia's $9,000 were in the *state-wide fallback*, reaching sellers the figure had nothing to do with. Washington also says it outright: RCW 69.22.050(2), the operation "must either obtain a food processing plant license ... or cease operations".

## Left open, deliberately

* **WV's label elements are not sourced.** § 19-35-6(c) delegates to the department's labelling standards, which could not be located. The elements are kept so a label prints, and the note says plainly that they are the summary's and that the missing piece is the department's standards.
* **WI's baking route rests on an injunction I have not read.** The row follows the description in the admin-verified state rule note; the injunction's own terms and DATCP's guidance are the gap to close.
* **VA's licensed route** beyond permit-and-ins

author: alfredo1996
body:
Closes #1399.

## The bug

Dark styling for Leaflet's own furniture — zoom control, attribution strip, popups, tooltips — was written into `component/src/index.css` for #1154. **Only Storybook loads that file.** The app's `globals.css` starts with `@import "../../../component/design-tokens.css";` and pulls in nothing else from this package.

So those seven rule blocks reviewed correctly in Storybook and did nothing in the product: a dark map still showed white zoom buttons and a white attribution bar.

`dark-basemap.test.ts` already guards the tile-pane filter against precisely this mistake, and spells the trap out in its own docblock:

> a dark-mode rule placed in index.css therefore looks correct in Storybook review and silently does nothing in the product — which is exactly how the #1154 Leaflet dark styling shipped broken

That test caught the filter. The rest of the chrome it was warning about was still in the wrong sheet.

## The change

The blocks move into `design-tokens.css`, directly after the tile-pane filter, comments intact — including the specificity note explaining why the attribution selector needs `.leaflet-container` in it, and the `hsl(var(--ring))` note from #1553.

`index.css` keeps only its `@import`, the Tailwind directives and the base layer. Storybook still gets everything through that import, so both surfaces now load the same rules.

Also: the comment in `map-chart.tsx` pointed at `index.css` for the tile filter, which has lived in `design-tokens.css` since #1529.

## Verified

Storybook `charts-mapchart--default` in dark mode, computed styles after the move:

```
zoom button   background rgb(24, 27, 32)      color rgb(243, 244, 246)
attribution   background rgba(18, 20, 23, 0.8)
```

## Required tests

| Layer | File | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Vitest unit | `component/src/__tests__/dark-leaflet-chrome.test.ts` (new) | each of the eight selectors is present in `design-tokens.css`; `index.css` contains no `.leaflet` rule at all; the attribution link still reads `hsl(var(--ring))` rather than a copied literal |

`npm run verify` EXIT=0, `npm run build` EXIT=0, `heavy-widgets` Playwright 10/10 green — a stylesheet the whole app imports is worth exercising end to end.

author: cclabsnz
body:
## Why

`connected-app-inactivity` reads `LoginHistory` and calls an app inactive when it has no OAuth login in 90 days. That is the wrong signal for the failure mode that actually took customer data over the last year. A refresh token means the app never logs in again: it presents the token, gets an access token back, and no `LoginHistory` row of `LoginType 'OAuth%'` is written for the exchange. **An app can be reported as dormant and low risk while holding a working key to the org.** The existing check's own detail text concedes this ("Inactive apps still hold valid OAuth credentials") without measuring it.

That gap is the shape of Salesloft Drift (Aug 2025), Gainsight (Nov 2025) and Klue (Jun 2026): a vendor was breached, tokens they already held were replayed against customer orgs over the REST API, and the remediation each time was to revoke access and refresh tokens rather than disable a login. No org can execute that without first knowing which apps hold live tokens and for how many users, and nothing in the plugin could answer it.

## What

New check `oauth-token-inventory`, wired through all six touchpoints (impl, registry, `mapping.ts` base + `network` domain, `CheckMeta`, unit test, README/CHECKS row and count 90 → 91).

Three findings:
- **MEDIUM** — app holds live tokens but is absent from the connected app inventory
- **MEDIUM/LOW** — tokens unused for 90+ days, or with no recorded last-used date
- **INFO** — full per-app inventory, always emitted, so the report carries the revocation worklist

## Design notes

`OauthToken` exposes `AppName`, `UserId`, `LastUsedDate`, `UseCount` and `CreatedDate`. Three platform facts drive the implementation:

- `LastUsedDate` and `CreatedDate` are filterable and sortable but **not groupable**, so aggregation must be client-side. A `GROUP BY` on either is rejected, and a rejected query here would surface as "no tokens found".
- `AccessToken`, `RequestToken` and `DeleteToken` are **queryable strings**. Findings are written to HTML/JSON on disk, so `NEVER_SELECT` is enforced where the query is built rather than by keeping the preferred list tidy. A test feeds describe all three to prove the filter holds.
- Fields are intersected with `describe()` at runtime. This is not about edition variance, which was an assumption that did not survive checking. It earns its place as the accessibility probe: an org that cannot read `OauthToken` throws there and goes inconclusive, where a fixed SELECT would fail and be read as "no standing tokens" — the one output that must never be wrong.

## Failure modes closed

An empty `ConnectedApplication` read makes every token trivially "unmatched". That would emit a wall of HIGH findings and break `--fail-on HIGH` for anyone whose audit user lacks read access on that object, which is a common permission gap. The cross-reference is now skipped and reported as an inconclusive INFO instead, because an org that returned no inventory has not been shown to have a problem, it has failed to provide evidence.

Salesforce-owned clients such as `Salesforce CLI` never appear in `ConnectedApplication` by design, so matching them against it always fails. They are excluded from the unmatched finding and still listed in the inventory. The set is a documented floor: an unrecognised first-party client is reported, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.

Unmatched is MEDIUM rather than HIGH. Absence from `ConnectedApplication` has several benign explanations, so it is a lead, not a verdict.

## Checks

- 14 unit tests covering all inconclusive paths, the empty-inventory guard, first-party exclusion, and the `NEVER_SELECT` invariant
- Full suite **1171 passing** across 121 suites, including the read-only invariant, referential integrity and `CheckMeta` guards
- `npm run build` clean, DCO sign-off on all commits

author: atsokolas
body:
The stand was a list of issues sorted by date. That is a pile, not a newsstand — a newsstand is organised by *paper*.

## Papers, not a pile

Editions arrive newest-first across every profile, so two papers interleaved by date and neither read as a thing that keeps turning up. `byPaper` groups them back into runs: a first issue, the ones since, and the one being written now.

Each paper is a front page. **One column per section**, so the shape of the paper is the shape of the week, and an empty section is an empty column with its head still set. It now knows its tense: an issue inside its window says *"Nothing yet"*, one past it says *"Nothing that week"*. Same silence, different claim.

A headline carries the front page and the **finding folds open underneath it** — reading the stand and reading a finding are the same act. The archive is a **run of issue numbers you turn back through**, and the nameplate stays put while you do, because it is the same paper.

## A section keeps its own byline

Two agents can keep one paper now, which stopped the masthead being the whole truth — it names whoever wrote *last*. So:

- an item records **who filed it**, taken from the token rather than from what the caller claims to be
- each column carries its own byline: *"Filed by Jarvis and Hermes"*
- a whole-issue rewrite **keeps the byline an earlier filing earned**, the way it already kept the reader's saves

## The stand is alive

While an issue is still filling it refreshes itself — only that issue, only while the tab is visible, once a minute. When something lands: *"Jarvis filed one just now."* And what arrived since you last looked is marked in the margin, per issue, per browser. An issue you have never opened marks nothing, because everything in it is new and marking all of it says nothing at all.

## What a paper does

Ears carrying the two facts that are not the reading. A Scotch rule under the nameplate. Small caps where mono was — a dateline is read, not operated, and mono in Noeis means "press this". An asterism between papers. A drop cap on the finding. The day named in the folio. A print stylesheet, so the Sunday papers print with every story unfolded.

## One real bug found on the way

`runLine` replaces `agentRunLine`, which counted consecutive windows across *every* paper at once — three papers filed in the same week would have read as a three-week run. It now measures each paper against its own cadence, so a monthly is not accused of missing fifty weeks.

Also caught while looking at it in a browser: `repeat(var(--columns), …)` is invalid CSS — a `repeat()` count cannot come from a custom property — so the columns are driven by a `data-columns` attribute instead, which media queries can also override where an inline style could not.

## Verified

Rendered and measured live: three equal 292px tracks, dividers on all but the first column, the fold opening to full height with the finding at full opacity, and the drop cap computing. Screenshot taken.

- UI: **2985/2986**. The one failure, `LibraryColumnKept`, is a pre-existing time bomb — its fixture hardcodes today's date and `formatSurfaceDate` renders anything under a week old as "12h ago". It passed while that date was in the future and passes again from the 13th. Flagged separately.
- Server: **569/570**, the one failure `notionFetchTool`, pre-existing and unrelated.
- Cacheless `react-scripts build`: clean.

author: rohan5046
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of the post-sidebar feature pass (Phase 1 — delete/search/views — already merged; agent editor redesign and templates/top-nav follow in separate branches).

Catalog previously showed almost nothing: the record-type list was just a name and a count, and a type's own records rendered as a vertical stack of raw `"field: value"` text lines, width-capped at `max-w-3xl`, every value printed through a bare `String()` regardless of its declared type — a currency field showed a plain number, a date showed its raw ISO string, a reference showed an opaque id. None of that helps a business understand its own data, despite typed fields already existing in the schema.

- **Catalog list** — each record type now shows its fields as badges (name + type), so you can tell what's in a type without opening it.
- **Record type detail** — replaced the text stack with a real table, full width, one column per field, type-aware rendering: currency formatted with the organisation's currency symbol, dates as a locale date not an ISO string, booleans as a chip, references resolved to the target record's own label and linked to its edit page. Plus a client-side search filter over the table.
- **Reference resolution is batched per type, not per record or per cell** — for each reference field, the target type's records are fetched once into an id→label map, so rendering N records with a reference field costs one extra query total, not N.

## Test coverage note

This project has no component-rendering test setup (no jsdom/testing-library — every existing test is either pure-logic or a real-DB integration test), so the cell-formatting logic (`lib/entities/format-record-value.ts`) is deliberately a plain, DOM-free module rather than living inline in the table component. That's what makes it unit-testable at all — 12 new tests cover every field type including boolean/date/reference, none of which happen to exist in live data in this org to click through and verify visually.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` / `pnpm typecheck` / `pnpm build` / `pnpm test` — all clean, 470/470 tests passing (12 new)
- [x] Live-verified via Playwright against the running dev server: field-type badges render correctly on the Catalog list; the Product record type's currency field renders as `£849.99` (correct GBP symbol from the org's currency setting); search correctly narrows to a match and shows the right empty state on no match; re-verified after refactoring the formatting logic out into its own module, identical rendering.
- [ ] Boolean/date/reference field rendering is unit-tested but not live-browser-verified — no record type with those field types currently has data in this org to click through.

body:
## Problem

`docs/lastplayed.md` and `docs/playlog.md` contain committed, unresolved merge conflict markers. They were introduced by the #203 merge (`a44f025`) and carried forward through every merge since, so both files render broken on GitHub and both swallow their Uninstall sections.

## Fix

Keep both sides — nothing was wrong with either half:

- The PID-verification paragraph stays in the install/usage prose where `HEAD` had it.
- LastPlayed's `## Arcade games` section follows it.
- Both `## Uninstall` sections move to the end of their documents, matching the layout every other app's doc already uses.

## Guard

Adds a `mage checkConflicts` target and a CI job so this fails the build rather than shipping. It walks `git ls-files`, skips binary files, and only reports a `>>>>>>>` line that follows a `<<<<<<<` and a `=======` — so Markdown tables and setext headings do not trip it.

Verified it catches a planted marker and passes on a clean tree.

## Problem

The s07 conflict chain (#450 slot canonicalization + #444/#455 conflict-slot promotion) is live-proven end-to-end — when the two contradicting lease claims land in the `status`/`duration_limit` slots, a `(office lease, status)` COMPETING pair forms. But hermetic battery run `stmtq22rtp` exposed the **extraction landing lottery**: the same two corpus turns can land BOTH arms as `(office lease, state_change)` — an append_only transition-event predicate where no conflict pair can form by design. Which predicate the arms land in varies draw to draw; the machinery only fired on the canonicalizable landings.

## Fix

Extend the declared alias table with `state_change → status`, with TWO guards on top of the existing mention-path/alias conditions:

- **Calendar-anchor gate** (existing `CALENDAR_ANCHOR_RE`): full month + 4-digit year, or ISO date. Verified against the battery corpus: none of the s02/s03/s10/s11 transition spans carries one (`replaced my laptop today`, `joined/quit/rejoined the chess club today`, `Signed up for the standing desk trial this morning`, `Returned the standing desk by evening`, `Sold the Canon R6`) — the corpus's ISO dates live only in verb-less log-header sentences the harvest lanes' clause capture cannot cross into. All pinned verbatim in the unit spec.
- **Non-person subject gate** (new, per-entry): the transition lanes bind `state_change` to PERSON holders exclusively (`bindStateHolder`: `customer` | `staff`, else the speaker), so a person's own lifecycle history never reroutes, whatever dates it mentions. An unknown subject type (a caller that does not thread it, e.g. the document commit path) misses conservatively — no reroute, never a false hit. `duration_limit` keeps its live-proven anchor-only gate; the person guard does not spread to it.

The subject entity's extraction type is threaded minimally: mention persist (per-fact and batched paths) passes `extraction.entities[f.entityIndex].type` into the resolver input, read only by `canonicalSlotFor`. No new flag: gated by the existing `CONFLICT_SLOT_CANONICALIZATION` (default off ⇒ byte-identical, pinned in tests).

## Unit tests

- The stmtq22rtp `state_change` lottery landing reroutes: both arms bind `status`, are re-embedded with the canonical slot text, and compose with `CONFLICT_MENTION_FACT_SLOT` into the bitemporal margin doctrine.
- Every s02/s03/s10/s11 corpus transition span pinned verbatim as no-reroute under person AND asset subject types; person-subject with a calendar anchor never reroutes; unknown subject type never reroutes; direct path untouched; flag-off byte-identical (including `entityType` inertness).

## Live verification (worktree app on :3057, scratch SurrealDB, full dogfood flag set)

Full `pnpm eval:state-transitions` battery, fresh user each run:

| run | config | scenarios | checks | s07-serve | s03/s10/s11 | s02 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stmtqi40g4 | stand as-is | 8/12 | 21/25 | fail (one side) | pass | serve+belief pass, history fail (= baseline) |
| stmtqijarx | stand as-is | 7/12 | 20/25 | fail (one side) | pass | serve+belief pass, history fail (= baseline) |
| stmtqiundv | + `SYNTHESIZE_ANSWER_ROUTER_ENABLED=1` | 9/12 | 22/25 | **pass — names both sides** | pass | serve+belief pass, history fail (= baseline) |

s02-history fails in all three runs AND in the last four baseline runs on main (stmtq22rtp, stmtq1rxni, stmtpzc8gk, stmtpxw49e) — pre-existing, untouched by this change (no anchored `state_change`/`duration_limit` facts are involved in that scenario). The remaining variance (s05/s06/s08 serve abstentions) is baseline-class serving flakiness, orthogonal to the write side.

**Landing determinism, measured at the slot level.** In every run and in 8/8 cache-cold probe ingests of the two s07 conversations (traced with `x-brain-debug`), both lease arms land in the `status` slot; when both bind the office-lease entity the COMPETING pair forms every time:

```
office lease (asset) | status = "until December 2026"     | competing
office lease (asset) | status = "ends in September 2026"  | competing
```

Run 3's serve answer: *"The office lease ends in September 2026 [fact]. However, there is a conflicting statement that the lease is until December 2026 [fact]. Which one is correct?"*

## Findings (documented in the battery README + s07 note)

1. **Serve side requires the router.** Even with the pair perfectly formed, `detectEvidenceConflicts` returns `[]` when the contradiction lane is absent, and the lane set is empty without `SYNTHESIZE_ANSWER_ROUTER_ENABLED=1` — the T3 both-sides note never renders and serving names one side (runs 1/2, and every recent baseline run: the stand has never run with the router). With the router on, s07 passes end-to-end (run 3). Config fix, not code — now pinned in the battery README.
2. **Runs on one app boot are not independent.** Extraction memoises in an in-process LRU keyed on turn text: run 2 inherited run 1's extraction draws verbatim (0ms `ingest.nlu.extract` in the trace). Documented in the README; restart the app between runs that must sample the lottery.
3. **Residual entity-binding lottery (out of scope).** One cold draw (frozen across runs 1–2 by the cache) extracted the December claim as `(Sasha[staff], duration_limit)` with a junk `December 2026` entity — the lease entity was never emitted for that turn, so no slot logic can form the pair (canonicalization deliberately never crosses entities). The pre-existing `duration_limit → status` alias then rerouted it into Sasha's `status` slot, where the promoted single_active pool paired it with an unrelated `(Sasha, status, "work laptop")` fact. 8/8 fresh probes bound the office lease correctly, so the draw is rare; if it becomes a problem, extending the non-person guard to `duration_limit` is the natural next step — deliberately NOT done here to keep the live-proven duration_limit behaviour pinned.

## Gates

- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm test:unit`: 360 suites, 4011 tests, all pass
- `pnpm format:check` clean

author: stevehu
body:
Re-entering a completed task step reopened a create form for a record that already existed, populated with only the identifying context keys. Saving that would blank every other column.

Task steps can now declare where to go once they are complete, and update forms can load the record they are about to edit.

Step routing:
- TaskStep gains completedRoute plus completedRequires. A completed step opens its update form only when the identifying keys resolve; completion alone is not enough, since a task can be complete because a record exists without having identified which one. Otherwise it falls back to the create route.
- buildTaskStepRoute takes an optional status. Omitting it reproduces the previous route exactly, so existing callers are unaffected; only TaskDetail opts in.
- Creation defaults such as apiType and transportConfig are not carried onto the update form, where they would overwrite the record's real values.

Form prefill:
- A form definition can declare an identity-only read. Form issues it when the caller supplied identity but no record, so task steps, deep links and bookmarks populate the way list pages already do via location.state.data.
- getFresh* actions cannot serve this: their request schemas mark aggregateVersion required and their handlers unbox it into an int. The two destinations here use getApiVersion and getAgentDefinition, whose projections carry every field the update form needs plus aggregateVersion, so the concurrency version is preserved.
- The row must match every identity field it carries, exactly one row may match, and it must carry a numeric aggregateVersion. A form declaring a prefill is never rendered as editable without its record; failure and unidentifiable states block submission and offer retry or back.

Scope is deliberately limited to the two register-ai-agent steps whose read paths were verified. Routing and prefill ship together for each destination, enforced by tests, so a step cannot be pointed at a form that has no verified way to load its record.

Also fixes the API step itself, which auto-navigated back to the checklist whenever an apiId was in context. Since the checklist links back with the resolved context, the step became impossible to re-open and the create-new-API branch unreachable. It now preselects the API and stays, auto-returning only on an explicit autoSelect hand-off, and ignores an apiId captured under a different host.

author: filipeforattini
body: Reported from a WSL machine on v0.17.0: the update said it worked, and reopening still showed the old version. Two separate faults, both ending the same way. **`mise upgrade` respects the pin.** red-dev writes an exact version into `~/.config/mise/config.toml`, and a plain `mise upgrade` only moves inside the range the config already allows. mise says so and exits 0: ``` mise Newer versions are available but do not match the configured version ranges: github:reddb-io/redcode 0.20.0 → 0.21.0 (~/.config/mise/config.toml) Run `mise outdated --bump` to view all, or `mise upgrade --bump` to update the configuration and upgrade. ``` So the upgrade did nothing, successfully. It now runs `mise upgrade --bump`, which is mise's own idiom for moving the pin as well. That is what the person asked for when they accepted an update to a specific version. **The check asked the wrong question.** It verified that the target was *installed*. mise keeps every version it ever fetched and the shim runs whichever is *active*, so on this machine `mise ls --json` reports five installed versions with exactly one `active: true`. A target could be on disk while the old one kept running, which is the state that used to be reported as a successful update. It now requires the target to be active, and distinguishes three outcomes: not offered at all is the release-age gate, offered but not installed is a failed install, and installed but not selected now says so and gives the command that fixes it. Reproduced on my own machine, which was pinned to 0.20.0 with 0.21.0 released: `mise upgrade --dry-run` confirms the no-op, `mise upgrade --bump --dry-run` confirms the install and the bump. Tests: the existing mise upgrade case now asserts `--bump` and an active target, plus a new case for installed-but-not-active. 16 pass across `test/installation` and the global HTTP handlers; typecheck clean. Worth knowing for anyone on an older build: this fix ships in the next release, so the machine that hit it still needs one manual `mise use -g github:reddb-io/redcode@latest` to get onto a version that has it. https://claude.ai/code/session_013JrKXL4pdgTu2EtCjgiYyq --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

author: rodrigoteamx
body:
The first real consumer of `ActionContract` (milpa/live v0.20.0), and deliberately the least flattering one.

**`desktop-settings::save` does not save.** The write is `POST /desktop/settings`; this handler only records what the door answered. Until an action could declare its intent, the **name was the only signal** a reader had — and here the name says the opposite of the truth. An agent reading the contract would have concluded this button persists something.

So it now declares: `mutating: false`, `EffectProfile::readOnly()`, and a summary that names who does write.

**The other 41 actions stay bare on purpose**, and a test asserts they still read as *undeclared* rather than as *harmless*. If that ever flips, silence has started meaning "safe" and the additive promise of `decisions/0214` is gone — that guard is the point of the slice, not decoration.

Also raises `milpa/live` to v0.20.0 and `milpa/command` to v0.23.0.

294 tests, 2997 assertions.

duncaneddy
body:
## Description

Collects the Cartesian state kinematics used by every frame transformation into one crate-internal module, `frames::kinematics`, with a constant-rotation state map, the rotating-axes pair that applies the transport term `omega x r`, and a helper that derives a body-frame angular velocity from a rotation matrix and its time derivative. The GCRF/ITRF, TOD/ITRF, EME2000, lunar, Mars, custom, PCK, synodic, and router state paths call these functions instead of carrying their own copies of the same arithmetic. Public signatures, results, and tests are unchanged; the only numerical effect is floating-point reassociation far below any test tolerance.

## Changelog

### Changed
- Frame modules share one implementation of state rotation and rotating-axes transport in `frames::kinematics`; no user-facing behavior changes.

## Note to Reviewers
The ITRF and TOD/ITRF paths now form `R = W R3 C` and `omega_b = W [0, 0, omega]` and call the shared rotating-axes map, which is the same expression as the previous hand-expanded form because `W` is a rotation. Synodic frames derive `omega_b` from `S` and its derivative through `[omega_b]x = -S_dot S^T`.

author: ewen-poch
body:
## Problem

Stopping a review could still send a correction or leave a tracked assessment running. Historical reruns could target a newer conversation context and lose the original approved plan evidence. A session read error left historical verdicts looking current, failed cards lacked a retry, and empty assessments looked like successful checks.

## Proposed change

- Propagate the chain AbortSignal to tracked assessments and check cancellation after durable loads and at the correction send boundary. Preserve completed dispositions if cancellation arrives after a successful assessment commit.
- Carry the captured branch ID through historical card reruns, command admission and assessment scope resolution. Pin automatic correction to the audited scope's branch and originating turn. Cancel automatic correction when that context changes, retain the review and explain the interruption, with access to its original transcript. Do not switch branches automatically.
- Return a transient verification-unavailable marker for completed reviews on evidence read failure, preserve it across pushes, and clear it after successful verification. Running and error reviews do not acquire a historical verdict marker. The card retries evidence loading without calling the review model.
- Recover the latest archived authority for the audited prompt before testing approval, so rejected replacements cannot resurrect older approved plans. Record the stored plan checksum or an explicit plan-coverage limitation in new scope snapshots.
- Reuse the historical error card's existing rerun callback and exact scope, with pending and retryable failure feedback. Present an explicit empty submission neutrally. Translate new copy into all eight locales.

- Await descendant exit after POSIX SIGKILL even when the parent exits first. Reuse the existing one-second forced-exit grace and retain unconfirmed teardown when a process survives; this prevents premature installer cancellation failures.

- Add a command-to-persistence regression for archive conflict recovery: after loading current authority, the next version-checked user action remains valid when autosave observes the refreshed projection. Retain the archive-authority handling now provided by main and capture the existing mobile archive success notice in E2E.

## Scope and non-goals

The existing Review identity, correction owner, conversation graph and disposition lifecycle remain authoritative. The rerun request gains an optional scope branch ID; legacy callers may omit it. No database columns, tables, enum values or migrations are added. Context cancellation uses the existing aborted/unaddressed disposition and note; the read model now exposes that note. Verification state is transient. New scope snapshot JSON may contain a plan checksum and coverage limitation; existing immutable snapshots are not rewritten.

Deleted-session history remains readable. Missing legacy submitted-check projections are not treated as known-empty submissions. Plan history remains bounded: absent history is disclosed, not backfilled or guessed. This does not introduce a permanent per-turn plan ledger or automatic cross-branch correction.

## Acceptance criteria and validation

Before production changes, seven regression cases covering all reported behaviors failed in two identical focused runs on the original implementation; 114 existing tests passed. Failures were the reported behaviors, not setup errors or timeouts. Two additional failing regressions proved that the historical branch ID was dropped at the actual card request and command boundaries before that path was fixed. The delayed POSIX descendant-exit regression failed twice on the old terminator for both Linux and macOS scheduling models; running/error review marker regressions also failed before the lifecycle guard. Tests use existing command, process, runtime-send, evidence and React boundaries; no production test seam or live model was added.

Reviewer and process-termination evidence after those final behavior changes:

| Behavior / boundary | Check | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cancellation, scope guard, shared orchestration, IPC/preload/web/CLI consumers | `npm run test:module -- reviewer_orchestrator` | 652 passed |
| Historical plans and snapshots, unavailable evidence, durable submission/disposition projection, reviewer and artifact cards, store presentation, manifest validation, eight locales | Focused Vitest run of `turn-evidence`, `scope-snapshot`, `repository`, `flag-stale-reviews`, `reviewer-resilience`, `artifact-version-review`, `ReviewerCard.render`, `ArtifactProvenancePanel.render`, `WorkspaceMessageScroller.interaction`, `reviewer-submission-presentation`, `validate-module-impact`, `module-test-impact`, and `i18n/resources` tests | 1084 passed |
| Process-tree termination and real installer cancellation | Focused `process-tree`, `provisioner-runtime`, and `package-manager` tests | 139 passed |
| ACP connection, framework, shell and settings termination consumers | Focused `connection-resource-owner`, `agent-connection-adapter`, `agent-framework/codex`, `shell-process`, `codex-detect`, `codex-auth`, `claude-install`, and `managed-codex` tests | 278 passed |
| Framework Reviewer and kernel teardown contracts | `npx vitest run src/main/notebook/kernel-executor.test.ts src/main/acp/runtime.test.ts -t 'reviewer\|Reviewer\|correction\|teardown\|reaped\|terminate\|shutdown'` | 73 passed; 623 unrelated tests filtered out |
| Main, sandbox and renderer types | `npm run typecheck:node`; `npm run typecheck:web` | Passed |
| Source style | `npm run lint`; `git diff --check` | Passed |
| UI interactions | ego-browser, actual ReviewerCard and project styles with isolated example data | Verified evidence retry, failed rerun recovery and original-record navigation; screenshots retained locally |

Local tests were scoped as requested by the maintainer. The module manifest change only adds a regression test, with the matching architecture assertion updated. The impact classifier selects full CI for the manifest input; that fallback remains intact. Exact-head PR CI is authoritative for complete portable and platform validation. The original installer cancellation case passed locally on macOS; actual Ubuntu execution remains a CI check. No live provider or packaged cross-platform UI was exercised locally; screenshot navigation uses an isolated fixture callback, while the production callback continues to use the existing transcript path.

Additional validation after integrating the final main conflict resolution:

- An existing-store/API-boundary archive regression failed twice on the prior code: autosave echoed revision 4 back as revision 5, so the fresh archive action rejected with another revision conflict. The final main implementation retains external authority without suppressing dirty local edits; the new regression passes against it. No production test seam was added.
- Session persistence bridge and subscription, archive ordering, store architecture, workspace controller, undo store/snackbar, shared Store, workspace events, message scroller, artifact card and tooltip consumers: 634 tests passed.
- Process-tree, provisioner runtime and real installer cancellation: 139 tests passed.
- Reviewer Module: 652 tests passed.
- `npm run build:e2e` passed. The existing mobile-sidebar archive journey passed three consecutive Electron runs on the final merged build on macOS, including two injected conflicts and the successful final archive. It now captures the successful undo notice. Native Windows execution remains an exact-head CI check.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `git diff --check` passed. No additional schema, state, copy or interaction is added by this follow-up. The archive production fix is inherited from main; this PR retains the retry regression and screenshot capture.

author: ronaldlokers
body:
Closes two cards from the 6 September review, which the review itself says are one act:

- **"/me and the auth gate still ship the retired room's design"** (high, design)
- **"pile.css ships 2,006 lines of the dead room on every /me load"** (medium, four lenses)

`pile.css` was the room's stylesheet — 2,006 lines against the board's 748 — and `/me` and the gate went on loading it after the room stopped existing. Both shipped a design `DESIGN.md` had already declared dead: a 3px sticker outline, 14px corners, a 999px smoked-pill timer, a pill to sign in with. Only 39 of its ~148 selectors matched surviving markup.

Both pages are drawn from `board.css` now and **the file is deleted**. One stylesheet for one product: **913 + 145 lines, against 2,861**.

Two shapes deliberately not carried across: the running timer is a strip rather than a pill, and *let me in* is a stamp — the same rectangle, cast and caps as every press on the board.

### The test that stopped me getting it wrong

I made `.youface` a 3px square, on the card's line about "circular chips". `TestBrowserYourFaceIsRoundEverywhere` failed: *"a picture of you is square on the settings page"*. The board's own `.chip.face` is a circle and always has been — a picture of a person is the one place this product draws one. The card's complaint was about chips floating with no ground, not about roundness. Reverted; both screens agree.

### Three bugs the move turned up, all true before it

1. **`.strip.opened .wordfix` is 14.5px** — under the 16px floor, so focusing the only way to correct a strip's wording zooms the page on a phone. The zoom-floor test was measuring `.slot textarea` and `.wordbox textarea`, **neither of which has existed since the room went** — its own comment warned that "a list here that names a field no screen has is a floor holding nothing up", and that is exactly what it had become. Now measures the three live fields, across both stylesheets.
2. **`board.html` declared `theme-color` `#472e70` while drawing a `#3b2560` bar** — an installed app met its own status band in a seam. Both pages now declare the bar they draw.
3. **`--paper-deep` was used by `board.css` and defined only in `pile.css`** — a fallback value hid it, and deleting the file would not have.

Also caught by the cascade: my first phone override for the reword field sat *before* the base rule, so it lost on source order. `TestEveryFieldStillClearsTheZoomFloorOnAPhone` failed at 14.5px until it moved to the end.

### Verification

`gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` and the full browser suite clean — including both contrast sweeps, the 44×44 touch-target sweep, the 320px no-sideways-scroll sweep and `TestEveryCustomPropertyIsDefinedSomewhere`.

The recorded appearance moved and was regenerated: four values, all the change itself — text and outline going from cream to the outline's ink on the now-card-stock settings blocks, and a border dropping from 3px to 2px.

Tests updated where they named `pile.css` or a selector the room took with it: `heading`, `zoom`, `pwa`, `assets`, `novelty`, `boardempty` (the mood grid's unfilled days are legitimately dashed).

body:
## Summary

- Replaces on-demand rendering of each entry's Pick'em picks share image with a background pre-generation pipeline: the image GET route (`/api/og/pickem/{contestId}/picks?tokenId=...`) now only reads a Redis status record and 307-redirects to a persisted Vercel Blob URL — it never touches the blockchain or ESPN.
- A successful single-entry lookup (Bankr's `entries?tokenId=` branch, or a visit to `/pickem/{id}/entries/{tokenId}`) claims the render job (`SET ... NX` in Redis, so concurrent viewers don't double-render) and fires the render via `after()` without blocking the response.
- Failed renders retry with exponential backoff (1m/5m/15m/1h/4h, 5 attempts max) via a new `/api/cron/pickem-images` sweep (every 2 minutes), which also deletes the blob + status record once an entry has been terminal (`ready`/`failed`) for `PICKEM_IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30).
- Both consumers gate on readiness: the Bankr skill polls `share.status` a few times before attaching the image (falling back to `share.fallbackText` if it stays `pending`/goes `failed`); the entry page shows a "rendering" message until ready, then a direct download link, and its `generateMetadata` points `og:image` at the blob once ready (falling back to the contest-level card otherwise).
- Added a "View & share my picks image" button on the contest page's share modal, linking to the wallet's newest owned entry.
- New env vars: `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` (Vercel Blob write access — auto-injected once a Blob store is linked in the Vercel dashboard) and optional `PICKEM_IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS`. `CRON_SECRET` is reused from the existing oracle cron.
- Full architecture/setup writeup: `docs/pickem-entry-images.md`.

`entries()`/`entryShare()` in `src/lib/bankr/service.ts` are untouched — `share.status` is merged in additively at the two call sites only. No contest-visibility instructions were added to `skills/pickem/SKILL.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test` — 104 pass, 17 of which are new (status/queue/retention math + lifecycle, cron sweep, zero-live-read image route, Bankr `share.status` passthrough). The only failures (10, pre-existing) are in `src/lib/bankr/service.test.ts` and are unrelated to this change — confirmed via `git diff origin/main -- src/lib/bankr/service.test.ts` (zero diff) and by running that file alone with no other test files loaded (same failures reproduce): a `mock.method`/`mock.restoreAll` API mismatch with the installed Bun 1.3.14 binary.
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warning patterns only, same style already present elsewhere in the repo).
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — no new errors (only the pre-existing repo-wide `bun:test` ambient-type gap that affects every test file, and one pre-existing unrelated type mismatch in `service.test.ts`).
- [x] `npm run build` — compiles and type-checks successfully. The full build cannot finish "Collecting page data" in this sandbox because `THIRDWEB_SECRET_KEY`/`NEXT_PUBLIC_THIRDWEB_CLIENT_ID` aren't set here (no credentials were provisioned per task constraints) — this is on the pre-existing, untouched `/api/tokens` route, not anything in this PR.
- [ ] Manual smoke test in a deployed environment (Blob store linked, real Redis/thirdweb env) — not done, no deploy/credentials in scope for this PR.

## Blockers / follow-ups for whoever merges & deploys

- A Vercel Blob store must be linked to the project (Storage → Blob) before deploy — `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` is otherwise unset and every render will fail (harmlessly retried by the cron, but no images will ever go `ready`).
- After deploy, reinstall the hosted Bankr skill (`install the skill from https://bankrball.com/skills/pickem/SKILL.md`) so Bankr picks up the new `share.status` polling step — installed skills don't auto-refresh from repo edits.

author: peternaame-boop
body:
Closes #159

Marks on every track list: `v` toggles the highlighted track, `V` starts a range that follows the cursor, `Escape` clears. Ctrl-click, Shift-click and a click on the new leftmost column do the same with the mouse where the terminal passes the modifiers on. `A` adds every marked track through the playlist picker in the displayed order, hidden (filtered-out) marks included; with no marks it still adds the playing track.

A mark belongs to a row occurrence, not a video ID, so two copies of a track are marked and submitted separately. Marks survive sorting and filtering and a background re-render of the same list: the table carries them across by occurrence key (queue entry ids, which the QueueManager now mints per entry; video IDs in Recently Played), along with the sort, filter, cursor, range anchor and baseline. A dropped occurrence or a replaced list advances the selection generation, so a picker opened earlier clears only the marks it submitted. The table shows its own status line while anything is marked, independent of the selection-info bar.

Also in this change: filtering a sorted list now keeps the sort; appending under a sort places the new rows where the sort puts them; the picker reloads an open playlist instead of appending when the submission held duplicate ids; a newly created playlist gets the same duplicate confirmation as an existing one, retrying against the same playlist.

Docs: `docs/keybindings.md` and the changelog.

author: clarklab
body:
## Summary

**Player name.** A kawaii name card asks "What's your name, champ?" on first launch (max 12 chars, stored in `localStorage`). The title screen greets the player and the **Hi NAME! ✏️** pill lets them change it.

**Global world records, synced instantly and never lost.**
- `netlify/functions/scores.mjs` serves `GET/POST /api/scores` on **Netlify Database** via `@netlify/database`. `GET` returns the top 10 per game; `POST` accepts a batch of round results and returns the fresh leaderboard so the client is in sync the moment a score lands.
- `netlify/database/migrations/0001_create_scores/migration.sql` creates the `scores` table (Netlify applies migrations and provisions the DB automatically on deploy; the function also has a `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` fallback so a fresh DB never errors). Deploy previews get an isolated DB branch.
- Client side, every finished round goes into a `localStorage` outbox immediately and flushes asynchronously in the background: retry with exponential backoff, `sendBeacon` on page hide, re-flush on reload / `online` / tab focus. Client-generated ids + `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING` make every send idempotent, so retries and beacon re-sends never double count. Gameplay never waits on the network.
- Beating the world's best on a game triggers **🌍 NEW WORLD RECORD!** (fanfare + confetti) on the round-end card; beating your own best shows **⭐ new personal best**. The finale counts new world records for the session.
- New **🌍 WORLD RECORDS** screen: record holder for every game with hand badge and a "lefties hold X · righties hold Y" tally; tap a game for its top 10 (your own name highlighted). Reachable from the title and the finale.
- A small status line shows `synced` / `saving…` / `offline · will retry`.
- `netlify.toml`: functions directory + `no-store` on `/api/*`. `package.json` + lockfile for the one dependency. README documents the flow and the backend.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test`: 5 unit tests for the function (validation, idempotent batch insert with in-batch dedupe, leaderboard shape, 400/503 paths) against a fake `db.sql`.
- [x] Headless Chromium end-to-end against a mocked `/api/scores`: name prompt → title greeting → records list and per-game top 10 → full session where the second half runs offline: 6 scores stayed in the outbox, survived a reload, and flushed in one batch when back online with exactly 13 rows (seed + 12 rounds), no duplicates, no JS errors.
- [ ] First production deploy: confirm Netlify provisions the database and applies the migration (check **Data & Storage → Database** in the Netlify UI), then play a round and open World Records.

body:
Reorganiza `/admin/marketing` em abas e transforma o lead em entidade própria, com importação de base externa, biblioteca de templates e um motor de automação por gatilho.

## O que muda

**Base de leads** — `leads_marketing` passa a ser a entidade de lead, independente de ter pedido no chat. Recebe quem veio do chat, quem criou conta, cadastro manual e importação de CSV, tudo deduplicado por WhatsApp e e-mail. Filtros, edição, opt-out, export e um botão de sincronizar o que já existe no site.

**Templates** — biblioteca de conteúdo separada de quem recebe, em três canais: e-mail (Resend), WhatsApp (template aprovado na Meta ou texto via Z-API) e mala direta (peça física: formato, arte, peso e custo). A base de leads ganhou CEP e endereço completo pra sustentar a mala direta; integração com os Correios fica pra depois.

**Automação** — fluxos com gatilho (lead novo, pedido parado, pós-compra, lead frio), público e passos com espera em dias. Fila por lead em `automacao_execucoes`, cron de hora em hora.

**Campanhas** — disparo manual ou agendado por segmento, em lotes retomáveis, sem envio duplicado.

## Travas anti-spam

Opt-out respeitado em tudo, com link de descadastro one-click no rodapé dos e-mails. Ninguém entra duas vezes no mesmo fluxo, há teto de toques por lead, janela de horário em America/Recife e cap por rodada. O gatilho é reavaliado na hora de cada envio: quem comprou sai do fluxo de retomada em vez de receber cobrança de um pedido já pago.

## Atenção ao revisar

As duas migrações já foram aplicadas em produção (`20260907120000` e `20260907140000`).

A antiga nutrição automática virou o fluxo seed "Retomada de pedido parado" e `/api/cron/nutricao` foi aposentado — manter os dois motores ligados mandaria a mesma mensagem duas vezes. O fluxo nasce **pausado**, e o toggle antigo já estava desligado em produção, então nenhum envio novo acontece até alguém ativar na tela.

O canal WhatsApp de campanha ainda depende de um template de marketing novo aprovado na Meta; o `retomar_pedido_v3` existente só serve pra retomada do próprio pedido.

author: rm-you
body:
Stacked on #122 (`codex/p99-operational-hardening`).

The development launcher currently replaces custom Unix-socket database URLs and chooses whether to start logFaker before expanding dotenv references. It now resolves configuration once for migrations and child processes, preserves custom URLs/socket directories, and translates only the shipped Compose template to host TCP while retaining the configured database and credentials.

Container startup now runs the real fake-log writer once after migrations and before the smoke check. Missing or failing writer code stops startup; smoke validation checks nonempty Blue, Green, and Red log files. Its disposable Compose override uses independent container names, temporary configuration, and no build instruction, so it can coexist with a running deployment.

Both PR and main image jobs use one reusable build/smoke workflow. PR checks load a local image with read-only repository permissions. After unit and integration checks pass on main, the workflow pushes an untagged candidate digest, pulls that exact digest for smoke testing, and assigns the commit-SHA and latest tags only after smoke succeeds. Publishing never rebuilds the image.

## Problem
Week 1 Fast Publisher now accepts submissions authored by any approved production worker, but `worker_fail_week1_fast_submission` still carries the old `generation_worker_id = 'chatgpt-week1-fast'` restriction. author: ja-neh
body:
A projectile could be a bullet, missile or anything that's shot in this context

The ProjectilePool creates and stores a bunch of meshes for these "projectiles" to avoid multiple instantiation during gameplay which could affect performance.

When a projectile is fired, it takes a mesh from the pool then go wherever it was directed. During updates, the projectile pool checks where the active projectiles are and checks for collisions(hits) then handles them(_onHit method for this). If the projectile hasn't hit anything, it expires. Expired porjectiles and those that have hit something are returned to the pool.

author: fabrykjoh12
body:
FAB-26 findings 1 and 2 — the two the security audit named as things to close before a store submission. Sibling to #247 (findings 3 and 7). **Nothing here has been executed anywhere.**

**Reworked after review round 1 (REQUEST_CHANGES).** The headline change is that **finding 1 no longer has a migration**, because checking the review's concern against the catalog showed the one I wrote could not have worked.

## Finding 1 — `pg_net` is reachable by `anon`, and no migration can close it

The finding stands and is unchanged: `pg_net`'s twelve `net.*` functions carry Postgres's default ACL, which grants EXECUTE to `PUBLIC`, so `anon` and `authenticated` both have it (`has_schema_privilege('anon','net','USAGE')` true, `has_function_privilege('anon', net.http_post, 'EXECUTE')` true, `proacl` NULL on every one). Anyone reaching one makes the **database** issue arbitrary outbound HTTP. The only thing stopping it today is that PostgREST does not expose the `net` schema — a config value, not a grant.

**What changed is the disposition.** The reviewer flagged that the revoke might apply cleanly and change nothing. The catalog says it *would*, every time:

- `net`'s schema, all twelve functions and the `pg_net` extension are owned by **`supabase_admin`**.
- `net`'s `nspacl` is `{supabase_admin=UC/supabase_admin, =U/supabase_admin, postgres=U/supabase_admin, anon=U/supabase_admin, …}` — every grant made *by* `supabase_admin`, none carrying a grant option.
- The `postgres` role a migration applies as is not a superuser, and `pg_has_role('postgres','supabase_admin','MEMBER')` is **false**.

A `REVOKE` by a role that is neither the grantor nor a member of it does not error in Postgres — it warns and returns success. The migration would have applied cleanly, been ticked off, and left the privilege intact. That is precisely the *"no-op that looked like a fix"* its own header warned about, reached by a route the header never considered: it guarded the PUBLIC-versus-named-roles variant, not the grantor one, which is the one that applies to a platform-managed extension.

**So the migration is deleted, not patched.** There is no version that works from here — making it self-verifying would mean shipping a migration that always fails, which breaks `supabase db reset` for everyone. `docs/BACKLOG.md` now carries the evidence and the remedy that does work: **disable the `pg_net` extension from the Supabase dashboard** (Database → Extensions; it runs as `supabase_admin` and removes the objects outright), and **confirm PostgREST's exposed-schema list excludes `net`**, which is the entire current mitigation. A spec fails if anyone re-adds a pg_net migration believing it works.

Measured while establishing that, and worth recording: there is **no `supabase_functions` schema** in this project, so Database Webhooks are not enabled and nothing but the (absent) webhooks would have reached `net.*` through the PUBLIC grant. The review's second concern — that revoking from PUBLIC would strip `service_role` and the platform roles along with the client ones — was real in principle and empty here.

## Finding 2 — unpublished chapters readable through the child tables (`20260907001000`)

`stories` is correctly scoped to `is_published`; three siblings never joined back to it. `story_utterances` and `story_questions` are `USING (true)` for `authenticated` — **115 utterances and 45 questions** of unpublished stories, `correct_index` included — and `tts_audio` is readable by **anon** at `status = 'ready'`, so an unauthenticated caller holding the publishable key reads unreleased chapter text through `source_text`. **33 of 295** stories are unpublished. An embargo boundary rather than a privacy one, and live.

No client flow can reach an unpublished story's children today anyway — every read is `.eq('story_id', story.id)` on a story that already came from an `is_published = true` query — so this closes the direct path that went *around* that step.

## What review round 1 changed

| Finding | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Major** | The pg_net revoke could apply and change nothing, with no post-condition to catch it. | Confirmed from the catalog that it *always* would. Migration withdrawn; finding reclassified to dashboard-only with the evidence and remedy. |
| **Major** | "Zero risk to apply" / "there is nothing left to break" rested on `public` having no `net.http` caller, and ignored that revoking from `PUBLIC` also strips `service_role` and the platform roles. | Moot for the deleted migration; the underlying check was done anyway and recorded (no `supabase_functions` schema, so no webhooks). |
| **Minor** | `alter default privileges` without `for role` is inert for objects an extension upgrade creates — the comment and its spec claimed otherwise. | Gone with the migration. |
| **Minor** | `source_type <> 'story_utterance'` is a blacklist: a future third `source_type` would arrive anonymously readable. | `source_type = 'vocabulary'`. Identical today, fails closed tomorrow. |
| **Minor** | "The admin audio tooling is unaffected" was true of `tts_audio` only. `story_utterances` and `story_questions` had **no** admin policy, so scoping them would have left the planned admin audio-review surface unable to read the utterances behind an unpublished story's clips. | Both get the same admin escape the repo already uses for `tts_audio`. |
| **Minor** | `tts_pronunciation_overrides` has the same shape of leak and went unmentioned. | Named in the migration header and in `docs/BACKLOG.md`, deferred with the reason (scoping it needs a join the table does not have). |
| **Minor** | Specs used raw file text for positive assertions, so a header paraphrase could make them pass on deleted SQL. | Everything runs over comment-stripped code now. |
| **Minor** | "scopes all four leaking policies" passed on a file containing only the DROPs — which would deny all four reads outright. | Every drop is paired with its create, both directions. |
| **Minor** | The ordering spec compared indices in a lexicographically sorted list of timestamp-prefixed names, so it held by construction; covered 2 of 4 files; and `indexOf` → `-1` passed vacuously. | Compares timestamps, and fails if a named migration is missing. |
| **Minor** | `ROADMAP.md` not updated, which CLAUDE.md requires. | Added under **Now** — in-progress, not shipped: nothing reaches a learner until the migration is applied. It covers #247 too, so the two branches do not both edit the same region. |
| **Minor** | The staging note named the reader flows, which are the safe ones. | It now names the **signed-out** path, which is the one that could break — with the reason it does not today (`anon` holds table-level SELECT on `story_utterances` and `stories`, `relacl` checked live, so the policy subquery is false rather than an error). |

## Evidence the specs bite

Five mutations, each caught:

| Mutation | Specs that fail |
|---|---|
| the blacklist escape restored | 1 |
| the vocabulary escape removed entirely | 1 |
| the child-table admin escapes removed | 1 |
| a policy dropped without its create | 2 |
| one `is_published` test dropped | 1 |

The specs remain **structural** and say so in their own header: there is no Postgres in this repo's test environment, so nothing here proves a policy behaves. A staging apply is still required.

## Before applying

Signed out, confirm vocabulary audio still resolves through `tts_audio` rather than the legacy bucket fallback. Migrations are idempotent and committed before they are applied, per CLAUDE.md §8.

## Verification

`npm run verify:pr` — green, 196 files / 4770 tests, 0 lint errors.

## Scope

One migration under `supabase/migrations/`, `anonSurfaceMigrations.test.mjs`, `docs/BACKLOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md`. No application code, no data write, **no migration applied**.

**Do not merge or apply without Fabian's explicit approval.**

1. The scanner exports the scan as a function (`scanShaderSources`) and runs its
   CLI only when it is the entry point, the way the CHANGELOG gate does. The
   suite calls it directly instead of spawning a `tsx` process per case.
2. The scan takes the tree to scan as a parameter, and the suite introduces its
   defects into a copy under `os.tmpdir()` rather than into the real shaders.

## Why

**Cost.** Eleven cases, eleven `tsx` processes, each re-compiling the scanner
and its dependencies: 5.1s idle and past 15s under load, where it timed out. A
suite that fails on machine contention rather than on the code it covers. Now
2.3s.

**Correctness.** The suite mutated `src/rendering/webgl2/shaders/sprite.vert` in
place - emptying it, stripping its `#version` line - and restored it afterwards.
Vitest runs its files in parallel workers, so a shader emptied for one assertion
is read in that state by whichever worker loads it next. Full runs on this
branch failed 30 renderer-conformance tests with `Attribute "a_localBounds" is
not available` - a file that names neither this test nor its cause. The same run
with the pre-change versions of both files was green.

The race predates neither file's contract nor this branch's intent: the test was
built to mutate real shaders on purpose, because orphan detection and the
stripped-output check are properties of a file *at its place in the tree*. The
copy keeps that property - real shaders, real paths, an importer written beside
them - without reaching into the sources the rest of the suite renders with.

## Verification

- `test/ci/shader-sources.test.ts`: 12 passed (11 cases plus a new one asserting
  the untouched copy is clean, so no defect case can pass for the wrong reason).
- Full `exojs` project: 494 files, 8652 tests, 0 failures.
- `pnpm lint:shaders` unchanged: `74 shader file(s) checked, no problems.`
