author: santhreal
body:
# Rooms: peer driving conversations in one terminal

Target: `chore/settings-cleanup` (#945), then `plugin-main-integration` once #945 lands. Refs #927.

## What changes

**Registry.** A room is a process-global set of driving agents (`kind: "main"`). `AgentRef`
and `RegisterInput` carry `room`; `AgentRegistry` gains `isPeer`, `peers`, `roomMembers` and
`ensureRoom`, and `canAddress` admits a peer alongside the existing spawner and spawn scopes.
Peer reach is driver-to-driver only: a spawn is scoped to its own conversation tree and never
addresses a peer, and a peer is neither a spawner nor a subordinate. `sdk.ts` registers the
driving ref with `FactoryOptions.agentRoom`; `main.ts` and `background-sessions.ts` accept
`{ room }` on the interactive session factory.

**irc.** `irc list` marks a room peer and states how to address it. `to: "all"` reaches the
caller's own spawns only; a peer is addressed by id, so one broadcast never charges every
conversation in the room a turn.

**Model context.** Peers reach the model through the per-turn `<session-state>` block
(`session/session-state.md`, `#buildSessionStateMessage`), never the system prompt, so a peer
joining or leaving does not invalidate the prompt cache. The block is `display: false`.

**Terminal.** `/room` lists the room, `/room new` opens a peer conversation beside the
displayed one, `/room <n>` switches by ordinal. `→→` on an empty composer opens an anchored
room strip (`components/dashboard/room-strip.ts`); `←`/`→` move, Enter switches, Esc closes.
`ArrowDoubleTap` (`controllers/arrow-double-tap.ts`) detects the gesture and the opposite
arrow resets it, so `← → ←` is never a double tap. `RoomController` re-roots the cwd on a
switch, hands the previous session to `BackgroundSessions.keep` and reclaims the next one
with `BackgroundSessions.release`, so a still-streaming peer leaves the background count the
moment it is on screen. The status line gains a `room` segment (`N peer(s)`), hidden at zero
and present in every preset, unranked in the quiet-row shed order.

**Slide.** A switch is a viewport slide. `TUI.captureViewport()` snapshots the committed
window and `TUI.slideViewport(from, direction)` paints one column window per step on the
borrowed alternate screen the resize drag already uses (`#emitResizeViewport`), then settles
in the same authoritative full paint a drag ends with; a render requested mid-slide is folded
into that paint rather than committed to the normal screen. The slide is refused, painting
nothing, before the first paint, under an overlay, during a resize drag, after a resize since
the capture and in a multiplexer session, and the controller's plain forced repaint then
stands. `RoomController` captures before the attach changes anything and slides toward the
peer in room order: a later member enters from the right, an earlier one from the left.

**Where the engine code lives.** The slide pushed `core/tui.ts` past its 3800-line ratchet, so
two subsystems come out of it: `core/render-scheduler.ts` (the render clock, its timers and the
frame-pacing arithmetic, now a `RenderCadence`) and `core/viewport-slide.ts` (the slide itself,
driving the engine through a host of closures over the `TUI`'s private state). Both are
re-exported from the `@veyyon/tui` barrel, so no import path changes, and
`render-scheduler.ts` joins the core split's shared vocabulary in
`tui-core-modules-do-not-cross-import.test.ts`. `TUI.captureViewport()` and
`TUI.slideViewport()` keep their signatures and their semantics: the ceilings in
`module-size-gates.test.ts` record both new modules and the measured 3782 lines that remain.

On the wire and on disk nothing moves: no session entry, RPC frame, bus channel or directory
changes.

## Proof

`proof/scenes/room-peers.sh`, recorded with `proof/docker/record-x11.sh` (after, at this
head) and `PROOF_BASE_REF=cc3948b913 proof/docker/record-x11-before.sh` (before, held at the
tip of #945). llama.cpp serving qwen2.5-1.5b on the recorder's network, `--tools irc`. The
same keystrokes drive both arms; each guard is written for the arm it runs in.

| State | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/room new` while session 1 is streaming | ![before-room-new](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59017be0-8603-4816-a08d-344594e691c4) | ![after-room-new](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21fdd395-dcab-4715-bcbb-f311c12f8834) |
| `/room` listing | ![before-listing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/005ebef7-85a7-4814-9873-50e62e5311b1) | ![after-listing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5e126c3-e6a5-41a7-a481-02621ee7bc89) |
| `→→` on the empty composer | ![before-strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9c6b763-a526-4e58-af87-c079e12e7a0d) | ![after-strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93a66f96-698b-445c-854c-c6497f1cfe3d) |
| Enter: back to session 1, still running | ![before-switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21d614e6-6ed8-4bc3-83bb-9546965b356b) | ![after-switch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/097af1f4-b494-4c2e-a048-f611a99a4cc3) |
| `irc list` from session 2 | ![before-irc](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12d1d0ce-b5b5-47dc-9166-70c74dad53df) | ![after-irc](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/049a0454-61a1-4f67-baf9-a18e33024cee) |

Before: `/room` is an unknown command, `→→` moves nothing, the status line has no peer chip
and `irc list` has no peers. After: session 2 opens with `1 peer` on the status line, the
listing stars session 2 with session 1 `[running]` beside it, the strip opens with the cursor
on session 1, the switch lands on session 1's transcript with its answer advanced and `1 bg`
for session 2, and `irc list` names session 1 as a room peer with the `to: "all"` note.

The switch is an animation, so it carries a clip pair: the same eight seconds of each arm's
recording (30 fps), from the strip opening through `→→ Enter` to session 1 and `/room 2` back
to session 2.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before-switch-clip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c53beedb-6b87-486e-8ac8-81345c7778f9) | ![after-switch-clip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfa553e7-4142-418c-a15e-d5893f258a28) |

Before: Enter and `/room 2` change nothing but the composer. After: on Enter the screen slides
right, session 1 entering from the left (it is earlier in the room); on `/room 2` it slides
left, session 2 entering from the right; each settles in the full repaint with the peer's
transcript advanced.

The trailing `</session-state>` in the after `irc list` frame is the 1.5B model echoing the
tag inside its own list; the block itself is `display: false`.

Rooms add no setting: the feature is reached by `/room new` and does nothing to a session
that never runs it, so there is no off/on settings differential to record; the before/after
pair above is the differential, with the before arm the tree without the feature.

## Bench

Two committed benches, each an off arm and an on arm on the same inputs.

`packages/coding-agent/bench/room-peers.bench.ts` (`bun bench/room-peers.bench.ts`): the two
paths that run on every turn in `#buildSessionStateMessage`, over a registry carrying 400
spawns. Off arm: one driver, no room. On arm: four drivers in one room. The off-arm block is
the pre-rooms block to the byte (the template's peer line is conditional), which the bench
pins. The registry scan is measured against its previous shape, kept verbatim through the
public API, and the bench fails unless both return the same ids in the same order.

| Arm | `peers()` before (`list().filter(isPeer)`) | `peers()` after (one pass) | `<session-state>` render | block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off: 1 driver, no room | 3.61µs | 0.45µs (−87.6%) | 41.4µs | 212 bytes |
| on: 4 drivers, one room | 3.88µs | 0.75µs (−80.6%) | 38.8µs | 568 bytes |

The block is delivered once per change (deduped against the last delivered), so the on arm's
356 extra bytes are paid when a peer joins or leaves, not p

author: smeredith15
body:
Every asset now carries a mark bottom-right of its picture, and which mark it is follows from what the asset is rather than from a choice anybody makes: a club's crest on a team-sport player, a country's flag on a golfer or a driver, a league's mark on a club, a confederation's shield on a national side.

Decided in one place. `corner_badge` answers it and `asset_profiles` carries the answer, so a roster row, a standings tile and the profile window all badge the same asset the same way without three derivations of one rule drifting apart.

The mark sits *over* the picture rather than beside it -- side by side, these would double the width of every asset column on the site -- with a ring in the page's own colour, so a dark crest on a dark photograph is a separate thing rather than a smudge in the corner of one. It is drawn on the monogram too: a player with no photograph still plays for somebody, and of that pair the crest is the more useful half. Under twenty-four pixels it is dropped entirely, since a crest at nine pixels costs a request and says nothing, and the row it would sit in names the club in words anyway.

The confederation table is written down because nothing carries it: a country's continent is not a fact about a football match. It covers the nations a slot here plausibly holds and no more, and an unknown one gets no shield -- a wrong shield is worse than none, and adding a line is a smaller job than noticing a quiet mistake.

Two things only real images could have shown, both found by looking at the rendered page:

Rory McIlroy read "14.0 · Northern Ireland". Golf files a *finishing* position under the same key a soccer feed uses for "F", and the identity line preferred it over the role. A position is a word; a number there is a place on a leaderboard, so it is skipped and the line reads "Golfer".

And Arsenal's cannon came out clipped at both ends. Cropping a photograph to a circle costs a corner of the background and is better for it; cropping a crest to one costs the top of the shield and the bottom of the scroll, which is most of what makes it that club's. A crest is fitted now, a face still filled.

author: sophium
body:
Closes #2335

## A fix that shipped and was never run

The chart pinned the sidecar image as a literal:

```
{{- $dindImage := default "ghcr.io/sophium/erun-dind:28.1.1-2" (index $imageOverrides "erun-dind") -}}
```

That is a second source of truth beside `erun-devops/docker/erun-dind/VERSION`. Bumping the VERSION publishes the new image; the chart keeps deploying the old one.

Observed, not hypothetical — a `daemon.json` change bounding BuildKit's GC was released as `erun-dind:28.1.1-3` and verified published, while every environment kept running the old sidecar:

```
erun-dind:28.1.1-2 PUBLISHED      code1  erun-dind  ghcr.io/sophium/erun-dind:28.1.1-2
erun-dind:28.1.1-3 PUBLISHED      code4  erun-dind  ghcr.io/sophium/erun-dind:28.1.1-2

daemon.json in every running dind: defaultKeepStorage   (the key that fix replaced)
```

It was caught by checking the deployed `daemon.json`, not by anything in the release.

## Second bug on the same line

The literal hardcoded the registry too, so `containerRegistry` was silently ignored for this one image while every other in the chart honours it — including `$devopsImage` two lines above.

## Verified

```
default                                erun-dind:28.1.1-3
--set dindImageTag=28.1.1-9            erun-dind:28.1.1-9
--set containerRegistry=example.io/x   example.io/x/erun-dind:28.1.1-3
```

All `erun-devops/k8s/*_test.sh` chart tests pass.

## Scope

This reduces two sources of truth to one greppable place; it does not eliminate them. The sidecar's tag tracks the upstream docker version rather than the erun release, so it cannot derive from `.Chart.AppVersion` the way `$devopsImage` does. Threading the dind VERSION in at package time (the release already rewrites chart metadata) would remove the last manual step.

author: dani811
body:
1.15.0 encoded the delete-user id as 2 bytes; the lock's user id is **32-bit**.

**Proof (live):** a `password` access-log row `user_id_raw=03000280` decodes little-endian to `0x80020003` = 2147614723, which matches that credential's cloud id (`/dev/lock/query`) exactly. So the on-wire/internal id is the full 32-bit cloud id in LE, and the delete frame carries all four bytes (`fixBitString(record.userId, 2)` over the raw 4-byte hex is a no-op).

- `build_delete_user(user_id)` now takes the full 32-bit id → `03 + id.to_bytes(4,'little')`.
- Tests updated; suite 314 pass; ruff clean.

Note: end-to-end live delete confirmation needs a keypad-awake local table read (the 0x1f read only replies with the front panel awake); the frame format itself is proven by the id match above.

author: adriana-cmd
body:
Pedido da Adriana em 06/09: continuar recomendando, mas sem a pessoa clicando — "acho que o treco que recomenda conteúdo está ruim".

## O que saiu

- **O questionário inteiro.** Eram cinco telas de chips — objetivos, temas, ritmo, palestrantes imperdíveis, conhecimento ou prática — e um roteiro montado por filtro no fim. Foram junto `PERGUNTAS_JORNADA`, `perguntaDaJornada`, `escolhasDaJornada`, `seletorPalestrantesDaJornada`, `fecharJornada`, `SESSOES_POR_DIA`, `botaoAvancar`, o CSS do seletor de palestrantes e o `PERFIL.jornada`, que ninguém lia fora dele. Nada ficou como código morto.
- **O pedido de clique quando o texto não casa tema.** Abria-se uma tela de chips pedindo que a pessoa apontasse o tema mais próximo do que tinha acabado de escrever. A resposta da IA já foi dada; um questionário depois dela devolve o problema para quem já explicou.
- **O "~1 min" do card do Concierge.** Ele media as cinco telas. Do outro lado agora é conversa, e conversa não tem duração para prometer.

## O que entrou

- **Uma pergunta aberta**, com as palavras da Adriana, em `PERGUNTA_DE_ABERTURA` — uma constante só, porque é conteúdo, não motor. Vem depois do welcome dela e é a mesma pelos dois caminhos: quem abre o Concierge sem assunto, e quem toca no card "Monte sua jornada no Summit".
- **A resposta em texto vai para a IA antes de qualquer card.** É a mesma ordem que o fluxo do desafio já tinha: entender antes de recomendar. O que saiu foi o caminho por botão, não a regra.
- **O sinal `temas` continua saindo para o Core**, agora dos temas que o texto da pessoa casou. Era o botão que mandava; sem isso, tirar o questionário levaria junto o que o sistema aprende sobre quem está falando.

## O que deixou de ser mandado

Os sinais `objetivos`, `ritmo`, `experiencias` e `palestrantes_imperdiveis` só existiam nos chips. `JOURNEY_FIELDS` no `mindagent-chat` aceita todos e não exige nenhum, então nada quebra do lado do backend — o que a pessoa conta em texto passa a chegar pela conversa, que é onde a leitura é melhor.

## Prova

- 204 testes passando. Os quatro que cobriam o questionário foram reescritos: garantem que ele não volte (nenhum dos símbolos removidos reaparece, nem o CSS) e que o que ele entregava de útil continue saindo (o sinal de temas, a IA antes dos cards, o aviso do que o ingresso libera).
- Conferido no navegador em 390px, com backend simulado para exercitar o caminho local:
  - abertura pelo card → welcome + pergunta, **zero botões na conversa**, foco no campo;
  - "quero aprender sobre liderança e saúde mental na minha equipe" → a mensagem vai para a IA, a IA responde, os cards de sessão aparecem depois, e o sinal `temas` sai com os temas casados;
  - "que horas abre o credenciamento" na abertura → só a resposta, sem cards e sem chips.

## O que não mudou e vale dizer

O casamento de tema com o texto continua sendo o mesmo de antes — comparação de palavras com os rótulos dos temas e os títulos das sessões. Ele é grosseiro: "liderança e saúde mental" casou quatro temas, dois deles por título de sessão. A substância da recomendação agora é a resposta da IA, que lê a base; os cards são o complemento visual. Se o casamento tiver que melhorar, é outra mudança e passa por você.

      "content": "2026年9月7日，KubeCon + CloudNativeCon + OpenInfra Summit + PyTorch Conference China在上海国际会议中心正式开幕，CNCF、OpenInfra与PyTorch三大开源社区首次在中国同台，把'生产级AI基础设施'推到了聚光灯下。与此同时，Kubernetes v1.37（Garhwal）本周完成最后一批特性落地：Pod Certificates与Cluster Trust Bundles正式GA、metrics.k8s.io API坚守九年终达Stable，为AI与高性能计算工作负载铺平了身份与调度之路。服务网格侧，Envoy连发多个补丁版本，修复包括HTTP/3内核级漏洞在内的两项高危安全告警，提醒业界在网关与安全层做足功课。

## 主要新闻 (Main News)

### KubeCon China 2026上海开幕：三大开源社区首次合体，聚焦规模化AI落地

KubeCon + CloudNativeCon + OpenInfra Summit + PyTorch Conference China 2026于9月7日至9日在上海举行，CNCF、OpenInfra基金会与Linux基金会AI & Data（含PyTorch社区）首次以联合大会形式集结。第一天议程由中国开源组织（COS）协办，涵盖云原生技术委员会、分论坛、项目与示例演示、CNCF/AI日等活动，紧随其后的是9月8日至9日的主会议。作为34场预定活动（含AGNTCon+MCPCon抢先亮相环节）之一，本届大会以超1000名开发者、400多家企业、150多场演讲的规模，聚焦生产级AI基础设施、大规模云原生平台工程及开源治理三大主题。华为作为战略赞助商深度参与，与Cannonballs、EDRATA、Raymick等新赞助商共同支撑起这一社区通道。

**Source:** [KubeCon + CloudNativeCon + OpenInfra Summit + PyTorch Conference China 2026](https://www.lfopensource.cn/kubecon-cloudnativecon-openinfra-summit-pytorch-conference-china/)

### Kubernetes v1.37：Pod Certificates与Cluster Trust Bundles双GA，工作负载身份迈入X.509时代

Kubernetes v1.37（代号Garhwal，发布于8月26日）本周完成特性收尾：Pod Certificates与Cluster Trust Bundles两个特性正式转GA，允许集群内置的Certificates API直接为Pod与服务重载X.509证书，为解决长期安全反模式——把具备广泛权限的服务账户令牌直接挂到工作负载上——提供了官方出路。叠加已稳定八年的ClusterAddress字段，社区用内置API实现了'边发放边撤换'的证书生命周期管理，让沙箱插件、远程调试与短期工作负载的身份获取从此不再依赖共享长期密钥。

**Source:** [Kubernetes v1.37: Pod Certificates and Cluster Trust Bundles](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/08/28/kubernetes-v1-37-pod-certificates-and-cluster-trust-bundles/)

### metrics.k8s.io API九年终达Stable，HPA scale-to-zero进入Beta，etcd RangeStream降低大列表读内存

v1.37同期宣布多项调度与可观测性改进：metrics.k8s.io API历经约九年努力终于进入Stable，为HPA等指标消费方提供了稳定的横向扩缩依据；HPA scale-to-zero升级为Beta，且默认启用，可在配置的工作时间窗或流量阈值下自动将无负载Deployment缩放至零副本；配合gang scheduling（弹性组调度）Beta特性，AI/HPC作业得以按整组完成Pod创建，避免部分资源被抢占导致训练任务悬挂。etcd方引入RangeStream特性，以流式分页替代一次性加载，显著削减大规模列表（如all-namespaces Pod枚举）下的内存占用。

**Source:** [Kubernetes v1.37 Release Announcement](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/08/26/kubernetes-v1-37-release/)

### Envoy连发四个补丁版本，修复HTTP/3与URL规范化高危漏洞

Envoy本周密集发布安全更新，1.39.1、1.38.4、1.37.6与1.36.10四个补丁版本同步推送，修复CVE-2026-73511（URL重写/规范化过程中的请求处理缺陷）与CVE-2026-73512（HTTP/3内核中因回调竞争导致的use-after-free漏洞）两项高危问题。官方安全发布流程要求使用受支持版本的用户立即升级；由于两项漏洞均可能被远端位姿攻击者利用，社区在各主流发行版跟踪页面同步放出了修复指引，强调凡暴露于互联网的边缘代理都应第一时间跟进。

**Source:** [Envoy v1.39.1 Security Release](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/releases/tag/v1.39.1)

## 分析 (Analysis)

三大社区首次在中国合办大会，是对'云原生调用方」正在向AI演进'这一判断最直白的注脚。PyTorch本是模型训练与推理的天然落点，如今与Kubernetes生态正面同场，意味着从'AI on Kubernetes'的兼容叙事升级为'Kubernetes原生支持AI工作负载'的平台叙事——gang scheduling、HPA scale-to-zero、以及各类GPU设备插件，都是这一平台化的具体体现。对国内一线团队而言，这不仅是技术栈对接，更是本地化GPU调度、多芯适配与开源治理的交汇窗口。

v1.37把'工作负载身份'推到正式可用，是持久性的安全兑付。此前CSR由kubelet以服务账号身份代理，签名权局限，难以承载大规模证书签发；GA后的Pod Certificates让发布平台能以Scope=Node身份在集群内直接签发Pod证书，配合Cluster Trust Bundles，kubelet实现单一信任域即可验证签发方。这为未来集群间联邦、多信任域互认保留了解耦空间——对安全审计者而言，运行负载的密码学身份获取通道从此不再依赖bearer令牌的模糊职责边界。

Envoy的补丁节奏则揭示了网关层的现实处境：代理作为AI流量的第一道关口,既要承载越来越复杂的路由、重写与可观测性逻辑，又要直面HTTP/3这类新生协议的实现风险。两个高危点（请求规范化与UAF）都发生在协议解析与请求处理的交界处，恰好是代理最容易出错、也最容易被构造特殊报文攻击的区域。安全团队应把'边缘代理按安全策略打补丁'列入与K8s控制面升级同级的例行评审，而非寄望于核心组件的单点固若金汤。

最后，本周一系列稳定性相关的GA/Beta特性（metrics.k8s.io、scale-to-zero、RangeStream）都指向同一目标：让集群在大规模AI负载下既站得住、又用得省。从身份到调度再到数据面安全，v1.37把'AI时代的生产级Kubernetes'从口号变成了可审计、可升级、可依赖的工程事实。

## 结论 (Conclusion)

KubeCon China站在上海开启的，不只是三大社区的物理合体，更是云原生平台承接AI工作负载从实验走向生产的里程碑时刻。Kubernetes v1.37在工作负载身份、调度弹性与可观测性三方面同时提速，Envoy的高危补丁则提醒运维方安全升级永不停摆。建议重点关注：Pod Certificates/Cluster Trust Bundles的落地路径、HPA scale-to-zero的生产化节奏，以及边缘代理的安全更新排期。"

## 主要新闻 (Main News)

### 一周密集发货引爆'模型疲劳'，企业采购陷入比选困局

CNBC周日报道，Anthropic周二发布Claude Fable 5.1与Mythos 5.1，Meta周三放出Muse Spark 1.3，谷歌同日升级Gemini 3.8 Flash，OpenAI周四推出强调网络安全与计算机操控的GPT-6 Astra，阿布扎比MBZUAI同天开源K2 Horizon系列——科技公司较量的同时，企业IT负责人却因持续评估成本与能力陷入'模型疲劳'。Runpod CEO Zhen Lu直言'环境里泡沫太多，必须不停制造声量'，Gartner预计2026年AI支出达2.59万亿美元、同比增47%，其中超1万亿美元投向服务与工具。分析人士指出，模型开发商正'抢夺钱包份额'，智能体快速部署带来的威胁面扩张被专家警告为'若不小心就是彻底混乱'。

**Source:** ['Model fatigue' sets in as AI labs race to roll out new versions at frenetic pace - CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/06/meta-google-openai-anthropic-ai-model-fatigue.html)

### TCS投资74亿美元，打造海得拉巴1GW级AI算力园区

印度IT巨头塔塔咨询服务公司（TCS）宣布对HyperVault AI工厂投资约74亿美元，在海得拉巴建设规模达1GW的'超级AI工厂'。该项目计划分阶段推进，目标是依托整栋数据中心与电力保障承载超大模型训练的持续算力需求。分析人士认为，此举与TCS过去两年在Kubernetes与云原生平台上的布局相互呼应——从'服务式交付'向'基础设施自有化'转型，也折射出全球企业对亚太AI算力冗余的迫切需求。

**Source:** [TCS HyperVault commits $7.4B for 1GW AI data-center campus in Hyderabad - AI Weekly](https://aiweekly.co/alerts/tcs-hypervault-commits-74b-for-1gw-ai-data-center-campus-in-hyderabad)

### OpenAI首席科学家刊文《异质心智》：对齐问题未解，主动降速将成常态

OpenAI首席科学家Jakub Pachocki在9月6日发表长文《An Alien Mind》，罕见地系统阐述其对AI安全的内部立场：尽管推理模型已能处理复杂规划，但大型语言模型'异质认知'的内部机制外界仍难断言，对齐可靠性无法被轻率打包承诺。文中明确提及PyS（推理时监督）进程中主动放弃额外轮次推理的'良性降速'案例，指出监督信号随任务难度曲线而下的现象，主张把'可控减速'列为下一代系统设计的显性原则——这被解读为对短期内以竞速换能力的行业惯性的一次公开反调。

**Source:** [An Alien Mind - OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/an-alien-mind/)

### NVIDIA以129亿美元收购Hugging Face，模型分发格局生变

NVIDIA于周三正式宣布以约129亿美元收购开源AI平台Hugging Face，交易预计在达成分发与硬件整合后收尾。Hugging Face托管着数十万开源模型仓库，月活开发者规模庞大，交易意味着NVIDIA由'卖铲子'向'建集市'扩张——其OpenAI/CUDA栈生态可将推理负载直接导向自家GPU云。分析认为，此举同时冲击既有模型市场平台与大模型厂商的渠道策略，也让开源生态的托管信任与中立性重新成为行业议题。

**Source:** [Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for almost $13 billion - CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/nvidia-agrees-to-buy-hugging-face-for-almost-13-billion-ai-expansion.html)

## 分析 (Analysis)

'模型疲劳'是供给端竞争加速直接传导给需求端的典型症状。Anthropic与O

author: chozandrias76
body:
## The defect

`git` exports `GIT_DIR` to hooks run from a **linked worktree** but not from the main checkout.
Measured with `scripts/measure-git-hook-env.sh` on git 2.55.0:

```
main     pre-push   GIT_EDITOR GIT_EXEC_PATH GIT_PREFIX
linked   pre-push   GIT_DIR GIT_EDITOR GIT_EXEC_PATH GIT_PREFIX
```

`GIT_DIR` beats cwd, so any gate that builds a throwaway repository and configures it with
`git -C <fixture> config …` writes to **this** repository instead of the fixture.

## It already happened, twice

A push from `.worktrees/teardown-outcome` on 2026-09-06 came back with
`scripts/check-gate-config-guard.sh` reporting that the suite had rewritten the configuration it
was checking:

```
core.hooksPath  scripts/hooks -> /home/banon/projects/er-mods-rs/scripts/hooks
```

— an absolute path computed for a fixture, landing on the shared checkout that every other
worktree and every other agent reads. The guard caught it and refused the push, which is the
system working; but the value was already written, and the same shape had hit that key once
earlier in the same session (it presented as an unrelated `check-git-hooks-installed.sh` failure
and was misdiagnosed).

Reproduced directly, both directions:

| | shared config | fixture |
|---|---|---|
| without the scrub | **`/BOGUS/unscrubbed`** ← the write landed here | *(nothing)* |
| with the scrub | `scripts/hooks` (untouched) | **`/BOGUS/scrubbed`** |

## Fixed at the hook, not in each gate

`unset $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars)`, after the `cd` that establishes which tree the hook is
about and before the first gate it invokes.

"Every script that might build a git fixture remembers to unset these" is not a property anything
enforces, and the gates number ~250 and grow weekly. `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` is git's own
list of the variables that pin a command to a specific repository; with them gone, every `git`
below resolves from cwd. `repo_root` is captured first, so the scrub cannot change which tree the
hook is about.

## Proved behaviourally, not by grep

`scripts/test-pre-push-scrubs-git-env.sh`. What is easy to lose here is not the line but its
**position** — moved above the `cd`, or below the first gate, it still greps fine and stops
working. So the test builds a real main-plus-linked-worktree pair under `mktemp`, exports
`GIT_DIR` exactly as git does, and measures where a fixture write actually lands. It leads with a
**negative control**, because a test that cannot leak proves nothing about a fix that prevents
leaking:

```
ok  negative control: without the scrub, a fixture write DOES hit the shared config
ok  with the scrub, the shared config is untouched
ok  with the scrub, the write reaches the fixture it was aimed at
ok  scrub is at line 33 -- after the cd (7), before the first gate (47)
```

It touches no repository but the pair it creates, and is ledgered `portable` in
`docs/ci-gate-portability.tsv`.

## Self-validating

This branch's own push ran from a linked worktree — the exact configuration that corrupted the
config an hour earlier — and came back `223 passed / 0 FAILED` with `core.hooksPath` still
`scripts/hooks`.

author: mmikanov
body:
## Summary

Adds campaign-based batch sending (C3 of the messaging plan): send an authored tip to a whole opted-in scope as individual per-recipient emails, de-duplicated by tip so re-runs reach only new sign-ups. Built, deployed to production, and tested.

## What's included

**Campaigns (messaging worker)**
- Two D1 tables: `campaigns` (UUID id, unique name, tip_slug, scope, mode, status) and `tip_sends` (tip-keyed send record, `UNIQUE(tip_slug,email)`, `pending`/`sent`/`failed`, `sent_at`).
- Full campaign CRUD (create with unique-name check, list, get, update draft-only, delete — delete preserves send history).
- Chunked, resumable `execute` with a **required explicit `mode`** (`dry-run`/`production`; no default, so you can't send by forgetting a flag).
- Individual per-recipient sends (never BCC), consent re-checked at send time, `pending`→`sent`/`failed` recording with a Resend `Idempotency-Key` (at-most-once).
- `new_only` (default; only those who haven't received the tip) and `resend_all` (deliberate full re-send) modes. Dedupe keyed by tip, so deleting a campaign never causes re-sends; ids are UUIDs, never reused.
- `run-campaign.ts` driver loops chunks with pacing; **dry-run lists who would receive it**, not just the count.

**send-tip `--record` flag**
- Optional flag so a one-off `/send-tip` counts toward the tip's dedupe history (a later campaign skips that recipient). Off by default so test/preview sends don't affect dedupe.

**Docs & spec**
- `messaging-batch-send` spec (requirements/design/tasks); README + `messaging-operations` updated with campaign CRUD, the driver, dry-run, and `--record`.

## Tested

- Verified locally (curl + local D1) and in production: CRUD, unique-name 409, auth 401, dry-run counts + recipient list, mode-required 400, consent/scope filtering, tip-keyed dedupe, delete-preserves-history, driver dry-run, and `--record` causing campaign exclusion.
- A real production send succeeded end to end.

## Notes

- Deployed: remote D1 migrated (`campaigns`, `tip_sends`) and the worker deployed.
- No secrets committed (`.dev.vars`, `.wrangler`, `node_modules` gitignored; Resend/admin keys are Wrangler secrets).
- Requirement 9 (campaigns dashboard UI) is deliberately deferred pending evaluation of Resend's own dashboard.

author: daojim
body:
Two lines of `DefaultItemExcludes`, and a long note in CLAUDE.md about why this took three attempts
to see.

## What was happening

The e2e suite's API `webServer` had been blowing through its ten-minute timeout for weeks. It was
blamed on the machine, then on a live virus scanner. It was neither — it was a workaround this
repo already documented, feeding on itself.

The SDK excludes `$(BaseOutputPath)**` from the default globs, which is enough while that is its
default `bin/`. **Two things here override it**: the e2e run sets `bin/e2e/`, `dotnet test` is told
`bin/testrun/`, both to dodge the Windows build lock. With it pointed at `bin/e2e/`, the sibling
`bin/testrun/` is no longer excluded — so it is globbed as ordinary Content and **copied into the
output**. The next run copies the now-larger tree back the other way. It doubles every run.

## Measurements

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/` across both projects | **289,490 files, 1.68 GB** | 200 files |
| Nesting | `bin/e2e/…/bin/testrun/…` **25 levels** | none |
| No-op incremental build | **3m21s** | **7.6s** |
| `dotnet test` end to end | minutes | 28s |
| `npm run test:e2e` | **timed out at 10m**, needed a hand workaround | **2m37s, 100 specs, unattended** |

37.9s of that no-op build was inside `DefineStaticWebAssets` and 23.2s copying — in an API with no
`wwwroot` at all. Both were just walking the pile.

## Why it hid

Worth keeping, which is why CLAUDE.md gets a section rather than a line. Playwright reports a slow
`webServer` exactly as it reports a missing database. `git status` is clean throughout, because
`bin/` is ignored. The build genuinely is compute-bound, so "the machine is busy" fits. And it is
**intermittent by construction** — it only crosses the ten-minute line once the pile is big enough,
so it worked, then flaked, then failed reliably.

`-clp:PerformanceSummary` is what broke it open. CPU sampling had already cleared the virus
scanner: the build burned ~1s of CPU per second of wall clock, where AV interference looks like the
opposite — low CPU, high wall time.

## Consequences

The `--no-build` restructure named twice in the docs as "the real fix" is **unnecessary and
removed**. It would have halved a number that had no business being large.

Checked by reintroducing the fault, as this repo asks of a rule that exists to prevent something:
delete the two lines, run `BaseOutputPath='bin/testrun/' dotnet build`, and
`bin/testrun/Debug/net10.0/bin/` appears after one build.

379 backend · 100 e2e, both green after the change.

author: corneliusmith
body:
## Summary

**858 headwords sit in `data/vocab_exclusions.tsv` and every one was still being served.** The file is applied by the loader, and no seeder deletes a vocabulary row — nor may it: `user_cards.card_id` references it and the review draw INNER JOINs, so a delete empties a learner's session (CHECKS §12).

The owner met the consequence twice on one card: English `em` survived its exclusion, and the Spanish UI showed its gloss faithfully translated to **"eme"** — the wrong definition (a printer's quad) rendered as the letter M.

**Migration 20261016** adds `vocabulary.retired_at` (owner-applied). `reconcile` sets it from the exclusions file and **clears it for any word that leaves the file**, so deleting a line restores the card and the file stays the source of truth in both directions. The rollback writes the inverse of each change.

- Review draw and Learn intake skip retired words.
- `auto_translate` stops glossing them into further locales — the half the translate guards cannot catch, because that pipeline did its job on an input that should never have entered it.
- The learner's card, history and schedule are untouched: retiring stops a word being **drawn**, it does not take away progress.

**Absence of the column is probed, never caught.** Every pooled connection runs inside one transaction, so a query naming a missing column doesn't merely fail — it aborts the transaction and every later query in the same request (decision 0001, `table_present`'s reason). The review draw is the hot path.

## Test plan

- [x] 9 new tests: both directions of the sweep, an already-retired word, a database without the column, the rollback's inverses, and a well-formedness check on the exclusions file — a malformed row silently excludes nothing, the failure that hides worst
- [x] 2,712 passing (the 9 failures are `ConnectionRefused` from a fake DSN used to satisfy the integration skip marker; **`main` fails identically**), `ruff` clean
- [ ] CI green

## Owner action

1. `supabase db push` — applies migration 20261016.
2. `reconcile -l all --apply` — retires the 858, `em` among them.

Until step 1 the retire step reports "skipped" and nothing changes.

author: yiwssx
body:
## Phase C3 round-9 field finding

Protected C3 run `34079016467` on master SHA `7bb407a9759462b1796a38565f28f119d6a0a992` passed production preflight, clean namespace verification, disposable editor provisioning, login, Save fallback, and deterministic cleanup. The authenticated browser flow failed immediately after Save while waiting for the filtered content row.

Playwright reported the row count as 0 for the default 15-second locator assertion, but the failure snapshot captured immediately afterward showed the exact disposable row rendered with title `Phase C3 QA 34079016467-1`, draft status, and action controls. This confirms the server-side filtered response and Save were successful; the remaining issue is bounded UI render settlement after the successful filtered response.

### Fix
- keep waiting for the exact filtered `/api/admin/content?q=...` response
- keep requiring that response to be successful
- keep requiring the table `aria-busy=false`
- add an explicit 30-second bounded wait for the exact row to render after that successful response
- require the row to be visible before returning it to Publish/Delete steps
- add a repository contract guard for the explicit rendered-row settlement timeout

No production CMS behavior, authentication policy, role capability, mutation retry, normal Admin credential, or production data contract is changed.

### Safety evidence from round 9
- production D1 identity preflight passed
- preflight namespace: `{ user: 0, credential: 0, session: 0, content: 0 }`
- disposable editor provision verified
- deterministic cleanup passed
- final cleanup verification: `{ user: 0, credential: 0, session: 0, content: 0 }`

### Completion gate
PR CI green -> merge -> master CI + exact-SHA Vercel + Phase A production browser smoke green -> protected C3 round 10 -> require full authenticated CMS flow, deterministic cleanup, and zero-row verification before closing C3/Phase C.

author: roasbeef
body:
In this PR, we close out the first cut of background jobs (#183) with the acceptance fixture the design note promised and the documentation of what landed. Stacked on #264; it retargets when that merges.

`daemon_shipped_jobs_test` runs the motivating case on the shipped daemon with a scripted provider: a turn backgrounds `tail -f build.log`, the fixture appends lines from outside the jail, the next turn's poll carries exactly those lines with `pending: true`, a kill reads killed by owner with `cancelled: true`, and the payload's birth-qualified fence departs. A second scenario goes through code mode with a real hermetic build and a real satellite: one program starts a job and reports its id, a later program finds the record. A third takes the VM down with SIGKILL and proves the sweep commits `Lost`, the model's next listing reads it, and nothing respawns. All three ran for real on macOS with live enforcement; on the unjailed Linux gate the fixture declares its skip through the shared enforcement probe, now lifted into `test/support/enforcement` so the census matches one reason rather than two drifting copies. The scripted provider gained a computed exchange for the one thing a fixture cannot script ahead: a job id minted during the run.

The fixture found two things. A one-line bug in the code-mode bridge's job row, which named a terminal state without the fields that state carries, so `job.list()` failed for any strand holding a finished job; fixed here. And a real collision with decision 4: a code-mode execution ends by aborting its operation to reap its satellite, and a job started by that program cleared under the same operation, so the teardown killed it the moment the program returned, against what the note and `cap/job` promise. The fixture asserts the durable half of that scenario and leaves the state unasserted with the reason written at the spot; the fix is a step-scoped abort for the satellite's own clearances and is on its way as the next PR.

The docs: a "Background jobs" section in `docs/architecture/effects.md`, the design note (carried onto this branch from the drafting branch) with its status and what changed on contact with the code, `docs/next.md` with the follow-ups, and the client and codemode package docs with their mirrors.

Part of #183.

author: iderex
body:
Closes #339 once the class reaches zero. This is the repair half of it; the register entry comes out afterwards, for the reason in the last section.

## What the alert says, read rather than recalled

```
$ gh api "repos/Flowfin/jellyfin-plugin-whisper-subtitles/code-scanning/alerts?state=open&per_page=100" \
    --paginate --jq '.[] | select(.rule.id=="cs/complex-condition") | "#\(.number) \(.most_recent_instance.location.path):\(.most_recent_instance.location.start_line)"'
#161 Jellyfin.Plugin.WhisperSubtitles.Tests/NamedChecksTests.cs:324
```

One alert, one site, and `docs/code-scanning-dispositions.md` already records the class as `repair owed` with this repair named in it: extracting the paired test into a named helper.

## What changed

`Unquote` tested a length and two quote pairings in one expression. The pairing moves into `IsWrappedIn(value, quote)`, which carries the length test with it, and what is left at the call site is one `||` over two named calls.

The behaviour is the same. A value is unquoted only when the same quote character stands at both ends of a value with two ends, which is what the nested expression said and what the helper says in fewer parentheses.

## How I know nothing moved

The suite is green on the line the gate runs, at this head:

```
$ dotnet build -c Release -f net10.0
Der Buildvorgang wurde erfolgreich ausgefuehrt.
    0 Warnung(en)
    0 Fehler
$ dotnet test -c Release -f net10.0 --no-build
Bestanden!   : Fehler:     0, erfolgreich:  4357, uebersprungen:     0, gesamt:  4357
```

`NamedChecksTests` is the class that reads job names through `Unquote`, and its nine tests are inside that count:

```
$ dotnet test -c Release -f net10.0 --no-build --filter "FullyQualifiedName~NamedChecksTests"
Bestanden!   : Fehler:     0, erfolgreich:     9, uebersprungen:     0, gesamt:     9
```

## What was not run

The `net9.0` line. This machine has no .NET 9 runtime installed, and installing one is not a thing I will do here:

```
$ dotnet test -c Release -f net9.0 --no-build
Framework: 'Microsoft.NETCore.App', version '9.0.0' (x64)
The following frameworks were found:
  10.0.9 at [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]
  10.0.11 at [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]
Testlauf abgebrochen.
```

It builds on that line (`dotnet build -c Release -f net9.0` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings), and the `Suite with no display and no elevation (net9.0)` job is what actually runs it.

This is a refactor of a private helper rather than a new guard, so no proof that a guard bites is owed and none is claimed. Nothing here asserts that the alert is closed: an alert closes on a scan of the mainline, which happens after a merge, and the issue stays open until that scan reports the class at zero.

## The means

C#, in the file the alert points at, changing one private helper of the test project. No language, runtime or dependency arrives with it, and the suite that already judges this file judges the change.

## What this deliberately does not do

The `cs/complex-condition` entry in `docs/code-scanning-dispositions.md` stays. That register refuses an entry for a rule the scan no longer reports **and** refuses a reported rule no entry covers, and a scan of the mainline runs only after a merge - so removing the entry here would turn every dispositions run on this branch red for a rule the platform still reports. The entry comes out in a second change once the mainline scan has closed alert #161, which is the order #335 walked for `cs/inefficient-containskey`.

No second reader is on this board tonight. What stands in for one is the run above and the diff, which is one helper and one call site.

author: ifiokjr
body:
## Why

When a Solana Kit dApp opens in Chrome on an Android phone, the Mobile Wallet Adapter was unavailable: `isMwaSupported()` used `Platform.isAndroid` (dart:io, which doesn't exist on web) and the association intent launched through the native Pigeon plugin. Mobile browser users were limited to browser-registered Wallet Standard wallets even though an MWA wallet app is installed on the same device.

**Feasibility was verified on the attached Android device** (Android 16, Solana Mobile wallet `com.solanamobile.wallet` installed): the example app builds for web and runs in Chrome via adb-reversed localhost (a secure context), and the association URI produced by the web implementation — `solana-wallet:/v1/associate/local?association=…&port=…&v=v1` — resolves through the Android intent system to the installed wallet's MWA handler (`com.solanamobile.wallet/.MWABottomSheetActivity`), the same entry point the reference JS SDK launches from web pages.

## How

- `solana_kit_mobile_wallet_adapter`: the protocol stack was already platform-neutral Dart (pointycastle + web_socket_channel). The two native pieces are now conditional imports:
  - `platform_check` — web variant returns `true` for pages in a secure context (HTTPS or localhost), which the localhost WebSocket transport requires.
  - `intent_launcher` — web variant launches the association URI through a hidden iframe with page-blur confirmation (3s), matching upstream's reference JS implementation; https app-link URLs navigate directly.
- `LocalAssociationScenario` accepts an optional `launchIntent` override; `transact` replaces the removed `clientApi` parameter with `launchIntent`.
- `solana_kit_wallet_adapter`: the default **web** registry now registers the Mobile Wallet Adapter wallet alongside browser-registered Wallet Standard wallets when the page runs in a mobile browser on Android (user-agent gated), so the picker shows both.
- The MWA example app gains the web platform for on-device verification.

**User presence note:** after the association intent, the wallet app shows a pairing bottom sheet that requires the user's approval — that step is inherent to MWA's security model and cannot be automated.

_Created on behalf of Ifiok Jr. ([\@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr)) by pi using GLM 5.3 Flash (glm-5.3-flash) at xhigh thinking._

author: lenamonj
body:
`useSWR` reads `config.fallback[key]` and `config.cacheData[key]` on plain objects, so a key that names an `Object.prototype` member (`constructor`, `toString`, `valueOf`, `hasOwnProperty`, ...) resolves to the inherited function and the hook returns it as `data`. With `fallback: {}` in `SWRConfig`, `useSWR('constructor', fetcher)` renders `data` as a function instead of `undefined` and never shows the fetched value as the initial state.

Both reads now go through a small own-property helper. An own entry under such a name is still delivered; nothing changes for other keys.

Three tests in `use-swr-config.test.tsx`: fallback and cacheData with a prototype-named key, and the own-property control. The first two fail on main.

`pnpm build`, `pnpm run-all-checks`, `pnpm attw`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:build` pass.

author: chemicalwolf1836
body:
## Problem

The English cocktail name and its Japanese reading sat side by side separated only by whitespace, reading as one run-on label. Adding a divider helped, but exposed a balance problem underneath.

Japanese glyphs are **full-width**, so the reading's width is set by *character count*, not font size. Measured on the menu card:

| Cocktail | English | Reading | Reading / name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cyber Espresso | 118px | **121px** | **1.03×** |
| Neon Highball | 106px | 99px | 0.93× |
| Midnight Ume | 106px | 77px | 0.73× |

The supporting text ran 73–108% of the name's width at only 59–69% its size — the gloss competed with the name it supports, and in the worst case was physically wider.

## Solution

Shrinking the type only buys 3–6 percentage points, because width is priced per character. So the reading moves to **its own line** instead:

```
Cyber Espresso
▬
サイバー・エスプレッソ
```

The name owns line one, a short accent rule sits beneath it as the divider, and the reading reads as a caption. The reading now takes **0% of the name's line** rather than ~47%.

Applied to all three places the pair appears, with rule width scaled to each card:
- Featured card (28px rule) — this one previously had **no divider at all**
- Menu item cards (20px rule)
- Finder best-match card (24px rule)

Slight negative tracking (`-0.02em`) on the reading. The rule inherits `var(--accent)` at 60%, so it retints across the jade / ruby / cyber / amber palettes. `SectionHead` keeps its own inline EN/JP divider — it's a heading lockup, not a cocktail name.

## Verification
- `eslint` — clean
- `next build --webpack` — compiles, TypeScript passes, all pages generate
- Rendered headless at 412px and 1280px: 5 stacked rows detected at both widths, no page errors
- Visually confirmed on the menu card and featured card
- Checked **JP language mode**, where the roles swap (`ネオン・ハイボール` on top, `Neon Highball` beneath)

author: walbarellos
body:
💡 **What:** Improved the focus styling and ARIA labels on the interactive process and jurisprudence cards in the UI. Replaced the `focus-within` tailwind utility with direct `focus` states, and updated the `aria-label`s to be more descriptive and action-oriented. Also logged this learning in `.Jules/palette.md`.

🎯 **Why:** Using `focus-within:` on a card means that if a user clicks on any element *inside* the card, the focus outline triggers for the entire card, which can be visually confusing and unexpected. Changing this to direct `focus:` states ensures the ring only appears when navigating to the card via keyboard. Additionally, providing action-oriented ARIA labels ("Ver detalhes do processo 123" instead of "Processo 123") gives context to screen reader users about what activating the card actually does.

📸 **Before/After:**
*   Before: Keyboard focus ring could misfire on internal clicks. ARIA label was "Processo 123".
*   After: Focus ring only shows on keyboard navigation. ARIA label is "Ver detalhes do processo 123" / "Ver detalhes da jurisprudência do processo 123".

♿ **Accessibility:**
*   Improved keyboard navigation clarity by preventing unexpected focus outlines.
*   Enhanced screen reader experience by making ARIA labels describe the action ("Ver detalhes...").

author: fordpiggy1
body:
### What this is, honestly

A hotkey's engine calls run on the main thread. `hotkeys.rs::install_handler` hands the event to `events::on_main`, which is `DispatchQueue::main().exec_async` — always enqueued, never run in place — and `dispatch` then calls into the engine synchronously. So the UI is blocked for as long as the engine takes.

**This is a hitch, not a bug, and the original diagnosis of it was wrong by about 20x.** The claim that started it was "the release waits up to 5 seconds." That 5 seconds is `recv_timeout`'s *timeout value*, not work. Measured properly, in release, with synthetic audio and no microphone:

| take | `AudioRecorder::stop()` |
|---|---:|
| 5 s @ 48k | 9.8 ms |
| 60 s @ 48k | **55 ms** |
| 300 s @ 48k | 235 ms |

55 ms is not worth a PR.

### The part that is worth it is `recopy`

`recopy` is on the same main-thread path, and it is not 55 ms:

- `insert.rs::simulate_paste` opens with an unconditional `sleep(200 ms)`, then shells out to `osascript`.
- Measured `osascript` startup on this machine, median of 31: **53.3 ms** bare, **59.4 ms** for the System Events round trip this call actually makes.
- `settings.rs:473` asserts the default `insert_method` is `Paste`.

So pressing the re-copy hotkey freezes the menu bar, the overlay and Settings for about **259 ms**, on the default configuration, every time. That is visible, and it is the whole case for this change.

### What changed

The engine calls move to one serial worker thread. `hotkey_pressed`, `hotkey_released` and `recopy` all go through it, so ordering is preserved — a press cannot overtake the release before it.

One thing deliberately stays on the main thread: `commit_pending_edits`. It is the only AppKit part of a hotkey, it is synchronous, and it runs before the press is handed on, so a capture still sees the value the user typed into Settings but never committed.

Routing is extracted to a free `route` function over a `HotkeyTarget` trait, because building a real `Engine` opens the database and the keychain and driving one needs a microphone — the trait is what makes the ordering testable at all.

### Verification

Gate: fmt clean, clippy clean with `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` **169 passed + 2 ignored** (baseline 166 + 2; the three added are below).

- `releasing_the_key_does_not_hold_up_the_thread_that_delivered_it`
- `hotkeys_reach_the_engine_in_the_order_they_arrived`
- `an_unbound_chord_and_a_recopy_release_reach_nothing`

Forged by making the release run on the delivering thread again: the first two go red, and green again on restore.

Only `crates/openflow-native/src/hotkeys.rs`, which nothing else open touches — merges clean into a tree of all 21 other open PRs, with clippy clean on the result.

### Take it or leave it

This is polish. If you would rather not carry a worker thread for a quarter-second hitch on one hotkey, the cheaper half of the benefit is available by moving the `sleep(200 ms)` in `simulate_paste` off the calling thread instead, and I would not argue against closing this in favour of that.

author: rowan-claude
body:
A PACKET union's tag enum carries `None`, the variants, `Count` and `Max`
plus a debug-name function in all nine targets (#597, F-15). A TABLE-CLOSURE
union's tag shape is a different emitter — `internal/codegen/cpptable`'s
`emitTableUnion`, written beside the tables rather than among the packet
declarations — and it carried `None`, the variants and `Max` alone. One
construct, two surfaces, and `Count` free as an arm name on one side only,
because the member did not exist there to collide with.

This closes that. `Count` and the `EnumName` overload land beside `Max`, and
the reservation moves from "where the member exists" to every union, because
the member is now on every union.

Merge, not rebase: `origin/main` at `bb5f3bd4` fast-forwarded in before the
first commit.

## The measurement, before anything moved

Thirteen tag enums across seven committed C++ table headers carried `Max`
with no `Count` beside it:

| golden | tag enums |
|---|---|
| `tables/arms/{Carry,Gate,Nest,Ring}Table.h` | 6 |
| `tables/messages/MessagesTable.h` | 3 |
| `tables/lists/SaveTable.h`, `tables/maps/DepthTable.h`, `tables/stream/StreamTable.h`, `tables/wide/CaptionTable.h` | 1 each |

Against them, every packet tag enum in `testdata/golden/cpp/` already
carried `Count = N, // the declared variant count (SPEC §4.2)`.

`internal/codegen/cpptable/unions.go:50` is the ONE emitter of that comment
outside the nine packet backends, which is what makes this a one-target
change where F-15 was a nine-target one: the table layer is the C++
reference's (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §11, §15). **The Go table backend emits no
tag enum at all** — `gotable` references `<Union>TypeNone` from the codecs
but declares nothing — so there is no oracle view of the enum to move.

## Red first

`1211337a` commits the gates alone, so the red is a fact in the history
rather than a claim in a report:

```
--- FAIL: TestATableClosureUnionArmNamedCountIsRefusedByName (0.00s)
    tagenumsurface_test.go:192: a table-closure union's arm named count passed check, and its tag enum defines Count twice
--- FAIL: TestTableClosureUnionTagEnumExportsCountAndItsDebugName (0.00s)
    tagenumsurface_test.go:257: cpp: the table-closure tag enum's surface is short, "    Count = 2, // the declared variant count (SPEC §4.2)" not emitted
    tagenumsurface_test.go:257: cpp: the table-closure tag enum's surface is short, "inline const char * EnumName( WeaponFireType value )" not emitted
--- FAIL: TestTableClosureTagEnumDebugNameCoversNoneVariantsAndOutOfSet (0.00s)
    tagenumsurface_test.go:272: cpp: the table-closure tag enum has no name function, "inline const char * EnumName( WeaponFireType value )" not emitted

--- FAIL: TestDiagnostics/union_variant_named_count_on_a_table-closure_union_(exported_spelling) (0.00s)
    diagnostics_test.go:592: compiled clean — the language broke silently (want "carries its declared variant count as the member Count")
```

The probe unit declares an enum of THREE variants beside a union of two,
the trap #597 found running the packet control: with both at two, the
declared enum's own `Count` line satisfies a claim meant for the tag enum.
The debug-name gate is anchored to the function's BODY, because `None`,
`Laser` and `Missile` all appear elsewhere in the same header.

`TestATableClosureUnionArmNamedCountIsAccepted` is deleted. It pinned the
split as law and the split is gone.

## The change

**The emitter.** `emitTableUnion` writes `Count` beside `Max` and the
`EnumName` overload beneath the enum, to the character the packet emitter
writes them, so a table arm and a type arm read as one family. Nothing on
the read or write path calls the function and no generated code does.

**The reservation.** `Count` moves out of `resolveUnion`'s post-loop block
and into the switch beside `None`, `Max` and `Type`, which is where it
belongs once the kind no longer has to be known: the arm errors and stops
rather than resolving on. `ir.Union.TableClosureOnly` keeps its three other
callers.

## Every id stays put

`Count` is a generated member, not a wire fact:

- `git diff origin/main -- testdata/wire` is **empty**.
- `git diff origin/main -- generated/` is **empty** — the packet corpus
  declares no table-closure union.
- `testdata/golden/id.txt` and `testdata/golden/build-version/` are
  untouched.

The CORPUS MOVE the reservation forces moves no id either, because it is a
`was` rename. `tables/messages`'s `EditBody` arm becomes
`tally int32 | min = 0, max = 100, was = "count"`, and every one of its ids
in `MessagesTable.h` stays `0xb1e5e28e4479a274` — the file form's dispatch,
the message form's, the reflection descriptor and the arms table.
`examples-wide/Caption.schema`'s `Body.count` moves the same way. The
baseline records it and says so:

```
arm tally id=0xb1e5e28e4479a274 kind=4 min=0 max=100 was=count
...
### 2026-09-07 (UTC) — the EditBody arm count is renamed to tally under was: every union's tag enum now carries the member Count, so the name is reserved (#601)
- no compatibility-affecting edits; the wire absorbs the rest
```

Fixtures that carry no stored data move by plain rename with no alias:
`test/tables/R1.schema` and `R2.schema` (to `amount`, since `tally` is
taken there by a keyed array), `test/tables/RT2.schema`,
`ir/buildversion_test.go`, `internal/baseline/baseline_test.go`,
`compiler/wasrows_test.go` and the harness's `rowdemo` unit. No pinned
instance selects any of them.

## The finding this turned up, and why it lands first

`688acf77` is not the pass. It is what the pass depends on.

The `was` rename only keeps the id if **every** id derivation reads the
alias, which docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §5 states outright: *"Every id derivation
reads the alias: the node record, the cooked node directory, the
connection's announced vocabulary (§3.3), the baseline and the build
version."*

Three arm-dispatch sites did not. The announcement's entry is
`ir.TableArmEntry`, whose own comment says it hashes the WIRE name, and the
encoder spends that id. The message form's readers matched on the DECLARED
name's hash instead:

- `internal/codegen/cpptable/messageload.go`, `<Table>LoadMessageBody`
- `internal/codegen/cpptable/messagecodec.go`, the union-arm extent walk
- `internal/tablewire/messagedecode.go`, the Go engine's arm dispatch

So a `was`-renamed arm was written under the old name's hash and read under
the new one: **lost by its own build**, counted `unknown`, in the C++
reference and in the engine alike. The file form was always right —
`decode.go` and every other cpptable site call `WireName()` — and no corpus
carried a message-form `was` arm, so nothing pinned could catch it.

```
--- FAIL: TestAWasRenamedArmSurvivesTheMessageForm (0.00s)
    wasarmmessage_test.go:116: the was-renamed arm was lost: the union reads back None, report {Unknown:1 KindMismatch:0 Widened:0 Clamped:0 Duplicate:0 Malformed:false Refused:false}
```

The C++ gate slices `NoteLoadMessageBody`'s own body rather than the output,
because the old name's hash is already in the header twice over, in the file
form's dispatch and in the reflection descriptor. Its control, the one line
put back:

```
--- FAIL: TestTheMessageFormsArmDispatchReadsTheWasAlias (0.00s)
    wasarmmessageid_test.go:57: cpp: the message form does not dispatch the renamed arm on its old name's hash, "case 0xb1e5e28e4479a274ull: // tally" absent from NoteLoadMessageBody
    wasarmmessageid_test.go:60: cpp: the message form dispatches the renamed arm on its DECLARED name's hash, "case 0xaa3f4d29d02d54ddull: // tally" — the announcement writes the alias's
```

No committed golden moves at that commit: no corpus declared a `was` arm
reaching a message form yet, and `R2.schema`'s two pin no golden.

## The goldens, every moved file and why

| file | why |
|---|---|
| `tables/arms/{Carry,Gate,Nest,Ring}Table.h`, `tables/lists/SaveTable.h`, `tables/maps/DepthTable.h`, `tables/stream/StreamTable.h` | the added `Count` line and the added `EnumName` overload,

body:
The console half of `23-35` — see [ago-calendar#47](https://github.com/golyakoff/ago-calendar/pull/47) for the backend and the `Money` reasoning, and ago-root for `adr/0142`.

## The price is two fields, deliberately

An amount, and whether it is exact or a floor. The alternative was for **us** to decide once, for every service, what «2000 ₽» means on a service whose price genuinely varies by master or by duration — and that decision belongs to the tenant who set the price.

## Two defects the ux-gate found, neither of them asserted

| | |
|---|---|
| **`"NaN ₽"`** | A stale mock fixture missing the new fields rendered an untranslated NaN. Fixed in `ux-gate/fixtures/data.ts`. |
| **842×22.5** | The new «от» checkbox row measured **1.5px under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px floor**, because `.ago-row`'s height was whatever its text line-height happened to be. |

The second is fixed **on the shared class, not on the one row**. `CalendarSetupPage`'s own Publish checkbox carries the identical latent defect through the same class and simply isn't gated (`/calendar/setup` is this gate's one stated exclusion), so fixing it here fixes both rather than leaving a second, differently-shaped patch for whenever that screen is gated. No other `.ago-row` can get shorter from a floor — they all clear 24px from their own contents already.

## Verified independently

`tsc -b --noEmit` clean, `eslint src ux-gate` clean, **905 tests in 91 files**, ux-gate **59 passed / 5 skipped** (the desktop-only specs), 0 failed.

author: vedanshimesvaniya
body:
### Summary

This PR improves Mochi's conversational understanding and action handling, making it easier to interact with multiple tasks/reminders, reference previously discussed items, and have more natural conversations.

### What's changed

* **Multi-target selection**

  * Support phrases like "all of them", "both", "the first two", "the last three", and "three of them".
  * Resolve selections against previously listed candidates without guessing when the requested quantity is invalid.
  * Execute complete/cancel actions across multiple items while accurately reporting partial failures.

* **Better contextual references**

  * Added numbered clarification lists when Mochi cannot determine which item the user means.
  * Follow-up references such as "the second one" or "both" now work from the remembered clarification context.
  * Support type-qualified references such as "that timer", "that reminder", or "the task I just added".
  * Cross-type clarification lists can now correctly remember and resolve tasks, reminders, and timers independently.

* **Timer purpose preservation**

  * Timer requests now retain the purpose provided by the user instead of always using the generic "Timer" label.
  * Fixed duration parsing so plural units do not leak characters into the timer label.

* **More natural relational conversation**

  * Added handling for messages such as "did you miss me" and "I'm back".
  * Responses are based on Mochi's existing familiarity context without triggering database actions or inventing memories.

* **Structured action results**

  * Multi-item operations now record explicit success/failure results before generating a response.
  * Prevents the assistant from claiming an action succeeded when some operations actually failed.

* **Chat UI improvements**

  * Fixed chat bubble width calculations to match the actual CSS padding and prevent text clipping.
  * Added a dedicated background for the chat message log to improve readability.

* **Tests and documentation**

  * Added coverage for multi-target selection, clarification flows, cross-type references, relational conversation, timer labels, and chat UI behavior.
  * Updated `README.md` and `PROJECT_ARCHITECTURE.md` with the new conversational behavior.

### Overall impact

These changes make Mochi's interactions more contextual, deterministic, and natural while improving the reliability of multi-item actions and the readability of the chat interface.

The buttons went to 4px and left everything around them at 5/6/7/8 and the 10px `--r` — panels, bars, tab row, confirm strip, callout, minted-invite box — so the console read as two design systems arguing. One radius for every rectangle.

| | |
|---|---|
| **4px** | panels, bars, tab row, nav items, chips, code blocks, confirm strip, callout, minted box, buttons, copy |
| **999px** | the three pills — **kept** |

Round badges are circles, not rectangles with soft corners; flattening them would make them squares.

## Why `theme_test.go` moves in the same commit

`--r` goes 10px → 4px, and it lives in the `:root` block that test pins **byte-identical** against clawee.org's `style.css`. A token changed on one side only is exactly what it exists to fail on. Verified the two blocks still match after both edits:

```
:root blocks byte-identical across the two sheets: True
--r in each: --r: 4px; | --r: 4px;
```

Multi-value radii keep their zeros — the tab row's `6px 6px 0 0` → `4px 4px 0 0`, the callout's `0 8px 8px 0` → `0 4px 4px 0` — so a corner deliberately square against an adjoining edge stays square.

author: gunflo1011-debug
body:
Technical UI-support slice for the image-first premium Marketplace direction.

What changes:
- adds a memoized `PublicListingImage` primitive for buyer-visible Marketplace imagery
- resets failure state whenever the signed public URL changes
- falls back to a premium neutral image state on network/decode/expired-URL failure instead of leaving a broken image surface
- reuses the shared premium image placeholder tokens introduced in #144
- keeps `resizeMode="cover"`, bounded layout ownership, and accessible image/fallback labels

Why now:
Current Marketplace browse/detail surfaces render signed public images directly. If a signed URL expires, the request fails, or Android cannot decode the image, the image-first premium surface can remain visibly broken. Inventory already has resilient private-image handling; Marketplace needs the same technical primitive before the next UX-led screen pass.

Safety:
- public presentation component only; no private image source or fallback
- no backend/schema/RLS/RPC/storage policy/navigation/state/lifecycle/price changes
- no seller-private metadata exposure
- Estimate / Asking Price / Offer / Final Price semantics unchanged

Handoff:
Product & UX keeps visual hierarchy ownership. The next Marketplace screen touch should replace direct public `<Image>` rendering in browse cards/detail gallery with this primitive while preserving the current image dimensions and layout.

author: mboyd1
body:
`scripts/check_surface.py:shared_query` found a module-level shared parameter constant by one exact spelling:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"^const ([A-Z_]+): Query = \{", source, re.MULTILINE):
```

`export`, a leading indent, a missing space after the colon and a wrapped `=` all change nothing about what the declaration means, and each one made the constant invisible. A route citing it then read as taking **no parameters at all**.

Unlike the four fixes in OPL-4513, this one fails **loud**: the parameters go missing from the upstream side, so they surface as `(in PARAMETERS, no longer documented upstream)` and the check exits 1. Nobody gets a false all-clear — they get a report telling them to delete mirror entries that are correct, on a run where nothing upstream actually changed.

## The fix

The pattern now matches what the TypeScript reader matches (`scripts/check-surface.mjs`), and the relaxation and comment blanking land **together**. Allowing an indent is what puts the scan inside block comments, where a superseded copy of a declaration is indented under its `*` — that is how `apidoc.ts` explains itself. The quoted copy comes last and wins the map, so every route citing the identifier reports one missing parameter and one extra, both naming a name nobody serves.

`parameters()` blanks the whole file once and hands that to every scan, rather than blanking only the `DOCS` table after balancing. `strip_comments` is length-preserving, so no other offset in that function changes.

## Tests

Two ported from `test/surface-parser.test.ts`, beside the OPL-4513 cases, each verified to discriminate against the half of the fix it covers:

- *a shared constant is resolved however it is declared* — the four re-spellings; red with the old pattern.
- *a shared constant does not resolve to a copy quoted in a comment* — a live declaration and a superseded one in a block comment; red if the pattern is relaxed without moving to comment-blanked source.

The stale `# Flush left:` comment on the OPL-4513 fixture, which said this divergence was left alone, comes out.

## No change to today's answer

`web/lib/apidoc.ts` spells both constants flush left with the one space, so the check reports 56 routes, 90 parameters and 7 constants both before and after.

Closes OPL-4514.

# The expert gate/up fused-row cap at four

Effort: max

## Base

Promoted frontier `97939dc`. The frontier's own mechanisms are spread across the editable sources listed below (the host-side decode tables, one lock in the dequantized-plane cache, the engine shutdown, five prompt-plane kernels, the prompt attention's value GEMM loader, the dense gate/up dispatch, the dense activation-sum table, the prompt expert gather's store epilogue, the resident sliding attention's token walk, the decode glue's RMS reductions, the tied head's packed plane and operand table the generic RMS norm body, the sliding walk's boundary trips, its softmax reference and affine dequantize, the dense prompt MLP's activation epilogue and three tensor-unit tiling guards): the full-attention decode chain in `RaggedTwoPassDecodeAttentionV1.swift` (a norm-and-RoPE ring-store kernel, an attention twin with a run-sum epilogue, the registration keys), the o_proj tier in `AttentionOQMVV1.swift` (a pair-table acceptor and its kernel twin), and the registration seam in `Gemma4Text.swift`:

This submission's change is one default value in one file,

The promoted frontier's own mechanisms are reproduced byte for byte and this
change is not one of them.

## Expert gate/up fused-row cap at four

The expert gate/up kernel processes a run of consecutive assignments that share
an expert in one threadgroup, and ships implementations for runs of one, two,
three and four rows. `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_GU_RUN_CAP` selects the largest run it
will fuse; this submission moves the default from two to four, which the file
documents as the value the kernel was written for.

**Exactness.** The cap selects only how many rows one threadgroup fuses, not what
any row computes. Each row's output is the same `qmv` accumulation over the same
k values in the same order whether it is executed by the single, pair, triple or
quad implementation; the run election, the leader rule and the stores are
unchanged. The eight-stream free-run token plane is unchanged, verified by hash
against the frontier build.

Kill switch: `DARKBLOOM_GEMMA4_GU_RUN_CAP=2` restores the shipped cap.

## Summary
Follow-up to #1107, addressing direct feedback from the live merged page.

- **Dead collapse toggle**: the sole-account accordion computed `isOpen = openAccounts.has(id) || filteredGroups.length === 1`, forcing it open unconditionally whenever there's exactly one bank — clicking the PNB row to collapse it visibly did nothing. Now auto-opens the sole account once (tracked by id via a ref, not re-derived every render), so the toggle actually toggles afterward.
- **Clipped date inputs**: the To-date filter shared a flex row with the Clear button, leaving too little width for "dd/mm/yyyy" plus the native calendar-icon affordance. Each date input now gets its own grid column (6-col grid instead of 5).
- **Small KPI glyphs + no animation**: KPI card icon badges/value type now match `MetricCard`'s `variant="elevated"` tokens from #1108 (rounded-xl badge, `font-display` value) — a step bigger again per feedback that they still read too small — plus the same entrance/hover animation (`KpiEntrance` staggered fade-rise, hover lift) #1108 already established for Ledger's KPI row, so both pages animate identically.

- **"Both sections start collapsed"**: reproduced the exact reported scenario (one bank, one failed import, one in-progress job) against this code and could not confirm it — `aria-expanded="true"` and a `ChevronDown` path render by default in both the DOM and a direct interaction test. Most likely stale cache from immediately after #1107's merge; flagging rather than guessing at a fix for something I can't reproduce.
- **Handwritten annotation near the hero**: still deliberately out of scope, per the explicit decision on #1107 to skip decorative hand-drawn assets for this page.

## Summary

`tests/interop_src` was an uninitialized git submodule, so the suite's glob matched nothing and the interop test reported success having run zero cases. author: shimabell0619
body:
## Summary

Address the Astra reviews that exposed gaps between the Foundation's declared contracts and what CI actually guaranteed.

- removes version/action fixed-value assumptions from regression tests and validates coherent current/next-patch/next-minor Foundation states
- parses every GitHub Actions workflow as YAML and structurally validates permissions, external `uses:` refs, required quality steps, conditions, `continue-on-error`, and the reusable CI contract
- parses Google DESIGN.md front matter as YAML instead of custom line matching
- replaces unconditional `changeset status` CI gating with lockfile-tooling verification plus release-state validation
- exercises a complete synthetic Changesets release cycle in CI, including Changeset consumption and the no-pending-Changeset release state
- requires check/typecheck/test/build by default, with explicit reasoned opt-outs only for check/typecheck/test
- strengthens the consumer fixture to prove `CI=true` and execution order of check → typecheck → test → build
- locks `@changesets/cli` and `yaml` as exact devDependencies covered by `package-lock.json`
- clarifies AI approval/completion boundaries, partial PR handling, same-SHA deployment gating, E2E lifecycle, and independent-review exceptions

## Issues

Closes #6
Closes #7
Closes #8

## Acceptance criteria evidence

- #6: `package.json` is the version source; README / AGENTS / lockfile mirrors use exact matches; regression tests derive versions dynamically and run against current, next patch, and next minor; all workflow files are YAML-parsed and all external action refs must be immutable 40-character SHAs.
- #7: reusable CI requires check/typecheck/test/build by default, requires explicit non-empty opt-out reasons for the first three, keeps build mandatory, sets `CI=true`, supports `working_directory`, and is exercised by a real consumer fixture plus direct negative preflight tests.
- #8: AGENTS defines approval boundaries and completion gates; PRs use `Refs` versus `Closes` based on AC completion; the PR template supports completed, unnecessary, and required-but-unavailable independent review states.

## Validation

Final HEAD: `062e855f989504ac4e34a1af4da51e8b4900e91e`

Foundation CI run #10 passed on the PR merge ref for this HEAD.

The validate job confirmed:

- `npm ci` with Node 24.20.0 / npm 11.19.0; 0 reported vulnerabilities
- structural Foundation validator passes
- validator regression suite passes across `0.1.0`, `0.1.1`, and `0.2.0`
- direct reusable-CI preflight tests pass for required scripts, reasoned opt-outs, mandatory build, and E2E contract
- synthetic release cycle passes `0.1.0 → 0.1.1`, consumes its Changeset, then passes `npm ci`, Foundation validation, and release-state validation with no pending Changeset
- current release metadata passes
- lockfile-installed Changesets CLI reports `3.0.2`

The `consumer-smoke` job also passes the actual reusable workflow and proves `CI=true` plus execution of check → typecheck → test → build.

The final `main...HEAD` diff contains 23 expected files. Temporary write-capable workflows used only to let npm refresh the lockfile are not present in the final diff.

## AI self-review

Reviewed the final `main...HEAD` change as if it were another engineer's PR and iterated on findings rather than treating the first green run as complete.

1. **Original H1 regression:** initial tests depended on literal `0.1.0` / current action SHA values.
   - Correction: tests derive the source version, generate next patch/minor dynamically, mutate YAML structurally, and assert every mutation actually changes its fixture. A different valid reviewed full SHA explicitly passes.
2. **Original H2 regression:** validator used regex/includes for executable workflow contracts.
   - Correction: `yaml@2.9.0` is an exact direct dependency; all workflow files are parsed and traversed structurally. Top/job permissions, external actions, required commands, gate conditions, `continue-on-error`, local reusable workflows, and DESIGN front matter are checked structurally.
3. **Original H3 regression:** unconditional `changeset status` rejected legitimate release PRs after Changeset consumption.
   - Correction: it is now a local diagnostic only. CI verifies the installed CLI, validates release metadata separately, and executes an actual synthetic release/version cycle to prove the post-consumption state succeeds.
4. **Regression-test implementation finding:** the first dynamic-mutation helper used `matchAll()` with non-global regexes and failed CI.
   - Correction: the helper now constructs a global counting regex independently from the replacement regex; run #9 passed after this correction.
5. **Self-review hardening:** the first corrected version still relied mainly on consumer happy-path coverage for opt-outs and documented release behavior.
   - Correction: added direct execution tests for the actual inline script-contract code and an executable release-cycle test. Final run #10 passes both.

Final self-review found no unresolved Blocker/High issue against Astra's R-H1/R-H2/R-H3 findings. Because this PR changes a reusable Foundation workflow, an independent Astra review of this final HEAD is still recommended before merge.

## Security / runtime-network impact

- reusable quality CI remains `contents: read` and checkout credentials are not persisted
- every external Action/workflow reference in every committed workflow must be a full commit SHA
- top-level/job-level workflow write permissions are rejected by the Foundation validator
- package-manager cache remains npm download cache only; no `node_modules` cache
- deploy/publish credentials remain outside reusable quality CI
- temporary write-capable lockfile-refresh workflows were removed before the final HEAD

## Changeset

Added a **minor** Changeset because the stricter reusable CI contract is an intentional pre-1.0 breaking Foundation-contract change.

author: seungrye
body:
Closes #409 · 앱 쪽 seungrye/work_log#63

work_log 앱이 죽으면 자취가 폰에만 남아, **사람이 '진단 내보내기' 로 옮겨 줘야** 볼 수 있었다.
중간 한 단계라도 빠지면 아무것도 못 본다 — 실제로 세 판을 자취 없이 고쳤다.

## 왜 Firebase 가 아닌가

견줘 봤다. 결론은 **"자동으로 읽을 수 없다"** 였다 — Crashlytics 콘솔은 브라우저 로그인이고,
크래시를 읽는 공개 REST API 도 없다. 붙여도 사람이 옮기는 단계가 그대로 남는다.

그래서 **이미 있는 통로를 쓴다.** APK 배포에 쓰는 앱↔사이트 길(`x-app-key`)이 이미 있고,
사이트 DB 는 직접 들여다볼 수 있다.

## 무엇을

`POST /api/work-log/diag` — APK 와 달리 **글자**라 작아서 MinIO 가 아니라 DB 에 그대로 담는다(1MB 상한).

**여러 벌 보관한다.** 릴리스는 최신 하나면 되지만 **크래시는 되풀이되는 것 자체가 단서**다 —
같은 자리에서 세 번 죽었다는 사실이 한 번보다 훨씬 많은 것을 말해 준다. 최근 20벌.

## 업로드 3계층 — #407 에서 겪은 것

새 업로드 라우트는 nginx · Next middleware matcher · 라우트 검증 셋을 같이 봐야 한다.

이번 것은 **1MB 상한이라 middleware 의 10MB 벽에 안 닿는다.** 그래서 matcher 에서
**빼지 않았다** — 뺄 이유 없이 빼면 얻는 것 없이 보안 헤더만 사라진다.

## 확인

시험 **14건**: 무엇을 받아들일까(8, 한글은 바이트로 재는지 포함) + 키가 없으면 아무 일도
안 일어나는지·**방금 올린 것을 걷지 않는지**(6). 뒤엣것이 틀리면 제일 알고 싶은 자취를
그 자리에서 잃는다. tsc·lint 통과.

body:
**What changes.** The blog post page stops rendering the site's own comment component and loads the Commently embed from `comments.aristotle.me` instead. Two lines on the page, plus a small inline script so the embed gets the theme the site is actually showing (the site has a manual dark toggle; the embed's default follows the OS).

- Each thread is keyed to the post id via `data-page`, so comments follow a post if its URL changes.
- `public/_headers`: the Content-Security-Policy now allows the embed script and frame from `https://comments.aristotle.me`. Nothing else in the header changed.
- The old comment API routes, the admin page, and the D1 tables are untouched, so existing comments stay readable until they are migrated or retired.
