author: ip2k
body:
### Summary

Adds `firmware-images/v15/` for the stock V15 package (`FM-1_015`, the CDN release dated 2026-07-30) in the same layout as `v14/`: the `.fwsc`, a `fetch.sh` that verifies the download (the CDN URL is unversioned), the unchanged `extract.sh`, the JLFS unpack produced by the pinned `3rd-party/jl-misctools` submodule, and `analysis/strings_raw.txt` generated with `scripts/extract_binary_strings.py`. `SHA256SUMS` covers the package and the key outputs. The index tables in `firmware-images/README.md` and the top-level README get a V15 row. Relates to #1.

### What V15 changes (details in `firmware-images/v15/README.md`)

- Only `app.bin` differs: 581564 bytes, 3392 bytes smaller than V14. `uboot.boot`, `isd_config.ini`, `cfg`, `cfg_tool.bin` and the nested `ota.bin` (package offset `0xA5F14`, was `0xA6F14`) are byte-identical; `scripts/extract_ota_loader.py` accepts it and yields the same 23324-byte `usb_hid_ota.bin`.
- The application area shrinks by `0x1000`: `cfg_tool.bin` moves to `0x920DC` and the VM region to `0x93000` (`0x56000` bytes); `BTIF`/`USR` are unchanged. The decrypted flash images agree for the first `0x4000` bytes.
- The SDK build stamps are identical to V13/V14, so only M-VAVE's application code changed. New strings: glide (`Fingered`/`Full Time`), three sequencer pages, two `Globe` pages, reordered operator pages, a patch `Rename` UI. The msfa algorithm table is at `app.bin` offset `0x8BE8C`.
- The vendor's current macOS updater DMG (app binary dated 2026-07-08) still embeds V14 byte for byte, so V15 appears to be CDN-only.
- Not included: the linear disassembly and function map, which need the vendor toolchain pipeline (`scripts/analyze_v14.sh`).

### Verification

- `cd firmware-images/v15 && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`.
- Re-running `raw_fw/extract.sh` with the pinned submodule reproduces `FM-1.fwsc_unpack/` byte for byte, and `scripts/extract_binary_strings.py` reproduces `analysis/strings_raw.txt`. Both checks, plus the existing unit tests, run in a small dispatch-only workflow on my fork: https://github.com/ip2k/FM-1-RE/actions/runs/34082195697 (14 unit tests OK; JLFS unpack, `strings_raw.txt` and the nested OTA loader all reproduced from the committed files).
- On top of #2, `python tools/verify_reflash_record.py --firmware firmware-images/v15/raw_fw/FM-1.fwsc` reports `verified local stock package` (this is the package the recorded reflash used).
- The README includes the identity reply of a stock `FM-1_015` unit (a `00 59 11` block containing `FM-1_015`), which decodes with #2's parser; it may serve as a hardware fixture.

Nothing outside `firmware-images/` changes except the two index lines.

### Context

The work behind this PR is public at https://github.com/ip2k/mvave-fm1-open-firmware: bench notes from a stock `FM-1_015` unit, the V14/V15 comparison, and an open RP2040 `USB_KEY` dongle design with a ROM-side simulator, aimed at a dump-and-restore recovery path before any non-stock flashing.

author: dlangenk
body:
The chat interface bundles the Markdown renderer (`marked`) and the HTML sanitizer (`dompurify`). Because the navbar mixin is rendered on every page, every page load pulled in 82 kB of JavaScript plus the chat stylesheet, although most page loads never open the chat.

`chatbot.js` still mounts with `biigle.$mount`, but it mounts a small loader component now. The loader waits for the `ask-biigle:open` event and then renders the interface as an async component, so each page only loads the loader and the interface and its stylesheet are fetched when a user opens the chat for the first time.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| loaded on every page | 82.46 kB JS + 3.26 kB CSS | 2.14 kB JS |
| loaded on first open | – | 82.41 kB JS + 3.26 kB CSS |

Two details worth reviewing:

- The loader dispatches `ask-biigle:open` again once the interface has mounted. The interface registers its own listener for that event in `mounted()`, which happens after the event that started the loading is gone. Every later open is handled by that listener, so the interface itself is unchanged.
- The build uses a relative base. The assets are published to `public/vendor/ask-biigle`, but the Laravel plugin derives the base from the build directory (`/public/`), so the stylesheet of the async chunk would be requested from a path that does not exist. With a relative base, Vite resolves both URLs relative to the entry script, which also keeps working if BIIGLE is served from a subdirectory. The base is only set for `vite build`, so the dev server is unaffected (verified: the `hot` file and the dev server URLs are unchanged).

Verified with the built assets served from `/vendor/ask-biigle/assets/` on a page that mimics the navbar mixin and uses a copy of the `mount` helper of `biigle/core`: the page load requests only the loader, the first click loads the async chunk and the stylesheet (both 200) and opens the modal, closing and reopening works without another request, and there are no console errors. `npx vite build` and `npm run lint` are clean.

- The video sits inside the hole drawn into that art. author: camshaft
body:
perf(dc/cca): add CCA-bypass experiment knob (S2N_DC_CCA_BYPASS) to locate the 64k throughput cap

Experimental dcQUIC's send path uses BBR with pacing. Intra-datacenter (high BW,
~60us RTT, low loss) BBR's bandwidth probing + pacing can under-shoot the true
available bandwidth — especially with one stream sprayed across 64 5-tuples,
which fragments BBR's per-connection delivery-rate sampling — pacing the sender
below line rate. The observed ~55-59 Gbps 64k ceiling (vs ~74 line rate) may be
(partly) BBR capping throughput rather than the link.

Add an A/B experiment knob to LOCATE the cap: env S2N_DC_CCA_BYPASS=1 makes the
congestion Controller bypass BBR throttling —
- earliest_departure_time() -> None (pacing disabled: packets depart immediately),
- is_congestion_limited() -> false (never cwnd-limited),
- congestion_window() -> a fixed 1 GiB (effectively unlimited).
Read once at Controller construction; default OFF = normal BBR (zero behavior
change). Transport safety does not depend on the CCA throttle — flow-control
credits + the send budget still bound in-flight data — so bypass removes only
the BBR *throughput* throttle. This is a locate-the-cap EXPERIMENT, not a
shipping default; if it lifts 64k throughput toward line rate the fix is a
DC-tuned CCA, not a naive disable.

Framed on THROUGHPUT (not cpu-ms/GB).

Data (correctness):
- Full s2n-quic-dc lib suite green (905 passed, 0 failed).
- New unit test (congestion::tests::cca_bypass_disables_pacing_and_cwnd_limit):
  a bypassed Controller reports not-congestion-limited, the fixed 1 GiB cwnd, and
  no earliest-departure-time (pacing off); the default (env-unset) Controller is
  normal BBR (not the bypass cwnd). Default-OFF path is unchanged (no
  snapshot/metric change).

Data (the throughput answer) - RIG-GATED, pending: does bypass lift 64k (and
1MB) sustained throughput toward line rate vs OFF, at c1/c16/c64, and vs
TCP/salty/protobuf/extracted? To be A/B'd by dcquic-perf-rpc
(S2N_DC_CCA_BYPASS=1 vs unset). If bypass materially closes the 64k gap, that
confirms BBR is the cap and motivates a DC-tuned CCA follow-up. DRAFT /
do-not-merge until that throughput data lands.

author: huikai79
body:
## Scope

Complete the next multilingual engineering gate by decoupling public article slugs from internal Hugo bundle directories. This allows one Translation Group to reuse the same public slug across languages without forcing multiple Notion records into one physical bundle.

### Design
- Existing single-language articles keep their current internal bundle path equal to `slug`.
- When a Translation Group reuses the same slug across languages, the canonical `Source` keeps the bare bundle path and translated members receive deterministic language-suffixed internal paths such as `slug--zh-cn` or `slug--en`.
- Public URLs remain governed by front matter `slug`, so routing stays `/posts/<slug>/`, `/zh-cn/posts/<slug>/`, etc.
- `translationKey` remains the Hugo language-family linkage.

### Why separate internal bundles
Notion translations are separate source pages and may have independent localized images, covers, attachments, comments identity, hashes and rebuild lifecycles. Separate internal bundles preserve those boundaries and avoid cross-language resource collisions while keeping public URLs stable.

### Changes
- Added deterministic `article-bundle-contract.mjs` with collision and family validation.
- `sync.mjs` manifest v2 now persists `bundlePath`; generator hash includes the bundle contract.
- Reuse, staging, rebuild, bundle hashing and reports use `bundlePath` instead of assuming `slug` is the directory.
- Article routing and homepage source lookup honor `bundlePath` while rendered URLs remain slug-based.
- Cover resolution, multilingual source verification and video verification now follow routed language-specific source files.
- GitHub Actions source checks and comments-policy hashing use `bundlePath // slug` for backward compatibility.
- Added regression tests for shared-slug family path assignment and a cover fixture where slug and bundlePath differ.

### Compatibility
Current production articles continue to resolve to the same bundle directories and public routes. The existing manifest remains readable through fallback-to-slug behavior; the first production sync after merge upgrades it deterministically to manifest version 2 and writes explicit bundlePath values.

### Boundary
No Notion page content, article body, public slug, Translation Group, Home setting, provider secret or translation target is changed by this PR. No paid translation is activated. Production merge/deployment remains subject to the existing validated main sync and exact-SHA deployment pipeline.

body:
The Portfolio page could list what you own but never *show* it. Pokémon cards are a visual hobby
and the collection already carries image URLs, so this adds a grid of card art beside the existing
table.

Extracted from `feat/phase-1-holdings-view` — see the last section for why the rest of that branch
should not be merged.

## What ships

A `TABLE` / `GRID` toggle on the holdings panel, remembered in `localStorage`. Both views render
the same filtered, sorted rows, so the switch is presentation only and a search set up in one
carries into the other.

`HoldingsTable.tsx` is renamed `HoldingsPanel.tsx` — it owns the filter chrome and now delegates to
either view, so the old name had become a lie. Git tracks it as a rename (75% similarity).

The grid has no column headers to click, so it gets its own sort control. Picking a field there
sets a sensible direction rather than toggling it, since toggling is what a header *re*-click means
and would be surprising from a dropdown.

Tiles show number, name, variant, price and **location**, with `xN` and condition badges over the
art.

## Three judgement calls worth reviewing

**Location goes on the face of the tile, not behind a hover.** "Where is this card?" is the question
a grid is otherwise worst at answering. It needed wider tiles — 7 columns at `xl` rather than 9 — to
fit `Box 2 - B332` without truncating, because a truncated slot label answers nothing. There is a
browser assertion that no location cell overflows its box.

**The condition badge is suppressed for NM.** 3,323 of 3,450 rows are NM, so badging it labels 96%
of tiles and buries the 127 that actually want attention. This is the same reasoning the original
branch used to suppress a `x1` quantity badge, applied to the other badge.

**Grid caps at 120 tiles, table stays at 500.** A tile is an image request; 500 of them is a slow
page even lazily loaded. The "showing the first N" line reports whichever cap applies.

`localStorage` is wrapped in try/catch on both read and write — it throws in a private window or
with site data blocked, and a holdings list that fails to render because of a remembered *view
preference* would be a bad trade.

## Why the source branch is not being merged

`feat/phase-1-holdings-view` built a parallel holdings feature in August: server-side
sort/filter/pagination, `services/holdings.py`, `HoldingsBrowser.tsx`, and roadmap tasks it numbered
1.15–1.17. I merged main into it to check. The result **does not compile** — two `useHoldings`
hooks — and 4 of its API tests fail, because both sides define `GET /collection/holdings` with
incompatible response models.

It predates `collection_item` becoming one row per physical card, so its endpoint returns ungrouped
rows with no way to ask for anything else. Of what is on it:

| | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Card grid + `CardTileBase` | **Taken** — this PR |
| Server-side pagination | Superseded — main returns the collection whole by design |
| `/holdings/sets` filter options | Redundant — main derives these client-side |
| Sort by cost basis / gain | Moot — `acquired_price` is null on all 3,450 rows |
| `services/holdings.py` + 16 tests | Superseded by `portfolio.list_holdings` |

`docs/06-roadmap.md` records this so the next person to find the branch does not repeat the
analysis. `CardTileBase` is that branch's refactor, taken as-is — the set-browse tile and the
holdings tile want the same presentation and different badges.

## Verification

- **18 browser checks** in a real headless Chrome against the ingested collection: toggle, tiles
  rendering art, `xN` and condition badges read off the badge elements themselves, location fitting
  untruncated, the grid's sort control, filters carrying across the switch, and the view surviving a
  reload. No page errors.
- Re-checked at **1024 / 1280 / 1440 / 1800** for overflow.
- `npm run build` (tsc + vite) clean. **257 backend tests** still passing — no backend change here.

**Not covered:** `npm run lint` cannot run. `eslint` is declared in `package.json` scripts but is not
installed, so no frontend linting has run on this or any previous frontend PR.

body:
## Overview
세컨드 브레인(SecondBrain) 영역의 일기(Diary)와 참고자료(References) 기능을 고도화했습니다.
일기에는 하루 다중 감정 슬롯(하루/아침/오후/저녁/밤)과 수면 타임라인 제스처 인터랙션 및 패턴 인사이트 대시보드를 추가했고, 참고자료에는 링크와 쪽지(Note) 갈래 분리, 색상 팔레트, 바탕화면 데스크톱 플로팅 쪽지 위젯 기능을 구현했습니다. 이에 맞추어 SwiftData 스키마 마이그레이션(V5~V8) 및 단위/통합 테스트를 구축했습니다.

## Change Log
### 1. 일기 (Diary) 고도화
- **도메인 정책**: 다중 감정 슬롯(`DiaryMoodSlot`), 감정 기록(`DiaryMoodRecord`), 감정 연속성 정책(`DiaryMoodStreakPolicy`), 감정 전이 정책(`DiaryMoodTransitionPolicy`), 수면 윈도우 정규화 정책(`DiarySleepWindowPolicy`) 추가
- **수면 타임라인**: 24시간 가로축 기반 취침·기상 제스처 타임라인(`DiarySleepTimeline`), 수면 축 커스텀 설정(`DiarySleepAxis`, `MemoPage`)
- **인사이트 패널**: 우측 리사이즈 사이드 패널에 감정 추이 차트(`DiaryMoodTimelineChart`), 감정 전이 맵(`DiaryMoodTransitionMap`), 스트릭 카드(`DiaryMoodStreakList`) 및 통계 카드 제공
- **스키마 V5 & 마이그레이션**: `sleepStart`·`sleepEnd` 필드 추가 및 `LegacyDiary` 경유 경량 마이그레이션 적용
- **HealthKit 정리**: 불필요한 HealthKit 권한 및 미사용 `HealthSleepGateway` 어댑터 제거

### 2. 참고자료 (References) 및 데스크톱 쪽지 위젯
- **갈래 및 색상 도메인**: 링크와 쪽지 갈래(`ReferenceKind`), 쪽지 색상(`ReferenceNoteColor`), `ReferenceChange` 추가
- **데스크톱 플로팅 쪽지 위젯**: `NSPanel` 기반 독립 위젯 창(`StickyNoteWidgetPanel`, `StickyNoteWidgetView`), 창 크기/위치/접힘/앞뒤 순서(`widgetBehind`) 영속화 및 앱 시작 시 자동 복원
- **브라우저 UI 개선**: 카드 격자 및 상세 분할 뷰, 링크 도메인 표시, 색상 팔레트 선택기(`ReferencePalette`), 외부 변경 동기화(`ReferenceChangeBroadcast`)
- **스키마 V6~V8 & 마이그레이션**: 단계별 스키마(`HorongHorongSchemaV6`~`V8`) 및 `LegacyReference` 사본을 통한 무손실 경량 마이그레이션, 기존 데이터 백필 로직 구현

### 3. 검증 및 테스트
- 전체 1,039개 단위 및 통합 테스트 작성 및 100% 통과 (0 failures)
- 도메인 정책 테스트(`DiaryMoodPatternPolicyTests`, `DiarySleepWindowPolicyTests`)
- 스키마 버전 및 마이그레이션 라운드트립 테스트(`SchemaVersioningTests`, `SwiftDataDiaryRepositoryTests`, `SwiftDataReferenceRepositoryTests`)
- ViewModel 테스트(`DiaryViewModelTests`, `ReferencesViewModelTests`)

## To Reviewer
- SwiftData 스키마가 V4에서 V8까지 단계별 경량 마이그레이션으로 처리됩니다. `SchemaVersioningTests`에서 V4~V8 각 버전의 저장소 마이그레이션과 필드 보존을 검증하고 있습니다.
- 쪽지 위젯은 `NSPanel`의 레벨과 컬렉션 동작을 조율하여 바탕화면에 자연스럽게 머물도록 구현했습니다. `ReferenceChangeBroadcast`를 통해 위젯과 메인 허브 브라우저 간의 동기화가 즉시 반영됩니다.
- MVVM + Clean Architecture 원칙에 따라 View에서 `@Query`를 배제하고 Domain 값 타입(`ReferenceItem`, `DiaryDay`)과 Repository 패턴을 유지했습니다.

author: bwsalmon
body:
Two bugs, one root: grain treats a repo name as a key but never had
anything authoritative to key it on, so a deployment could hold two
spellings of one repository and never let go of either.

1. AddTargetRepo now asks GitHub how a repository spells its own name
   before writing it into the allowlist.

   The allowlist is where a deployment's canon is set: Client.parseRepo
   spells every repo a task, schedule, template or repo_config names the
   way the allowlist spells it, so an entry typed as `Bwsalmon/grain-home`
   became the spelling every task filed afterwards inherited. Nothing
   forced it to be right -- GitHub resolves owner/name case-insensitively,
   so the wrong case clones, pushes and opens pull requests exactly like
   the right one -- and it was never checked against the repository
   itself.

   github.(*RESTClient).RepoFullName reads full_name off the endpoint
   DefaultBranch already uses; that follows GitHub's rename redirect too,
   so a repo that has moved is stored under the name it answers to now.
   It is deliberately not on the github.Client interface -- nothing in
   the reconcile loop asks -- so pkg/ui declares the one-method interface
   it needs (ui.RepoNames) and cmd/grain publishes the client through it
   the way livePullRequests already does.

   Adding a repo already on the list under a different spelling now
   repairs that entry rather than silently no-opping, which was the
   obvious fix to try and did nothing. Only on GitHub's word: with no
   client, no network, or a repo the credential cannot see, the entry is
   left exactly as it stands and the add still succeeds under the typed
   spelling. Respelling on the operator's word would just mean the last
   typist wins.

2. The repos list no longer shows a repo that only past tasks mention.

   A row was held up by three sources, one of which was "some task
   targets it" -- so removing a repo from targetRepos could not remove
   it. Its old tasks kept the row alive, and because such a row is
   `configured: false` the pane draws no Remove for it, leaving it
   permanently listed and unremovable. It stayed in the target-repo
   dropdowns too, offering a repo whose only outcome now is a parked
   task.

   Tasks raise a row only where targetRepos is empty, which is the
   unrestricted deployment that has no other evidence and the reason
   tasks were a source at all. A repo carrying configuration of its own
   keeps its row regardless -- that configuration is editable nowhere
   else. Rows are keyed case-insensitively, so the two spellings collapse
   into one row named the way the allowlist names it, and a task filed
   under either counts towards it.

   repoSummaries (`grain repo list`) applies the same rule: the two
   derive one list and a shell that disagrees with the page is worse than
   either answer alone.

   knownRepos stays wide -- it is what the read-only and extra-write
   pickers offer, and CreateTask gates neither on the allowlist.
   targetableRepos is the narrow list, for the three fields that pick a
   task's own target.

author: dasilvadub
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the multi-method devigging PR: four fixes from code review of `cfb_analytics/models/devig.py` and `cfb_analytics/features/market.py`.

1. **`additive` no longer scored by default.** Verified numerically: for every two-outcome market, `additive` and `shin` are identical to within float noise (<=1.8e-13 over 20k random books) — they only diverge at 3+ outcomes. Since every market this pipeline builds (moneyline, spread, total) is two-sided, having both in `METHODS` meant the backtest was scoring one estimator against itself under two names. `additive` stays reachable via `devig.CANONICAL_METHODS` or `devig(quoted, "additive")` for a future 3-way market.

2. **`odds_ratio` documented as not-yet-persisted.** `market_consensus` has no `prob_odds_ratio` column, so adding it to `STORED_METHODS` would compute it in memory and silently drop it before it reaches the database — the backtest would never see it. Left out of `STORED_METHODS` with an explicit docstring note on what a promotion would require (schema migration in `db.py` + the INSERT in `features/build_market.py`).

3. **New `FLAG_SHIN_FALLBACK`.** `devig.shin()` silently returns `multiplicative` for any individual book whose own hold is negative (no informed-money interpretation exists for an arbed book). The existing `FLAG_ARBITRAGE` only reacts to the *median* hold across books, so one rogue negative-hold book sitting among several healthy ones previously blended a disguised multiplicative estimate into the "shin" consensus with no signal anywhere. This flag fires on that per-book case.

4. Fixed the `devig()` unknown-method error message, which referenced the (now narrower) default `METHODS` instead of the full valid input set `CANONICAL_METHODS`.

## Test plan

- `tests/test_devig.py::TestDevigAll::test_allow_failures_omits_failing_methods` updated to request `CANONICAL_METHODS` explicitly (additive no longer fails via the default set).
- Added `test_default_methods_excludes_additive`.
- Added `tests/test_market.py::...::test_one_rogue_negative_hold_book_flags_shin_fallback_even_if_median_is_fine` — 4-book market where one book arbs and the other three don't; asserts `FLAG_ARBITRAGE` absent (median stays healthy) but `FLAG_SHIN_FALLBACK` present.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_devig.py tests/test_market.py` — 125 passed.
- `python -m ruff check cfb_analytics/models/devig.py cfb_analytics/features/market.py tests/test_devig.py tests/test_market.py` — clean.
- `python -m mypy cfb_analytics/models/devig.py cfb_analytics/features/market.py` — clean.

body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
`test_lldp_entry_table_after_all_batched_flap` flaps every port in a single batch, which drives heavy `orchagent`/`swss` churn as BGP tears down and re-establishes on all ports and routes are reprogrammed. The `memory_utilization` fixture's teardown `docker stats` snapshot could be taken before `swss` reclaimed this transient memory, tripping a `docker:swss` memory-usage alarm (e.g. ~4.8% -> ~10.2%) that is **not** a real memory leak.

This adds a `wait_until` on `check_bgp_session_state` after LLDP recovery so the BGP sessions reconverge and `swss` settles before the teardown memory snapshot is taken — mirroring the existing pattern already used in `test_lldp_entry_table_after_syncd_orchagent`.

Fixes the intermittent `docker:swss` memory false alarm on `lldp/test_lldp_syncd.py::test_lldp_entry_table_after_all_batched_flap`.

| testbed-bjw3-can-t1-7060-1 | Arista-7060CX-32S-C32 | [`6a9e3bd8`](https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a9e3bd8d47d7ec0360c73e4) (re-verify on fresh backport) | PASS — 25 tests (23 pass, 0 fail, 2 skip) | 2.54% (201.3 MiB / 7.74 GiB), ~0% increase |

`test_lldp_entry_table_after_all_batched_flap` passed on every run with `swss` memory sitting flat and well below the alarm thresholds and no growth across setup->teardown. Prior to the fix the same case intermittently crossed the `docker:swss` high threshold at teardown (~10.2%).

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

The batched-flap case intermittently raised a `docker:swss` memory-utilization alarm during teardown. Investigation showed this is a transient spike from `swss`/`orchagent` reprogramming while BGP re-establishes across all ports at once — not a real leak. The `memory_utilization` fixture snapshots `docker stats` at teardown, and could sample `swss` before it reclaimed the churn memory.

#### How did you do it?

Added a `wait_until(300, 10, 30, duthost.check_bgp_session_state, bgp_neighbors)` after `_verify_interface_lldp_recovery(...)` so BGP sessions reconverge and `swss` settles before the teardown memory snapshot. This mirrors the existing wait already present in `test_lldp_entry_table_after_syncd_orchagent`.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Ran `lldp/test_lldp_syncd.py` on two hwskus (7060, 7260) across three testbeds with `memory_utilization` enabled — see the Test result section. All runs passed with `docker:swss` flat and well under the 10% high / 5% increase thresholds; the batched-flap case that previously false-alarmed is now stable.

#### Any platform specific information?

None — the change is platform-agnostic and only affects the batched-flap LLDP test flow.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A — existing test case.

author: cliffhall
body:
Closes #2242 Connection Info labeled a CIMD registration **Dynamic (DCR)** even though no `POST /oauth/register` ever happened. The Client ID shown was correct (the metadata-document URL); only the provenance was wrong. ## Screenshots Same server, same flow, same Client ID — a live CIMD login against a test authorization server advertising `client_id_metadata_document_supported`, with a real HTTPS client-metadata document. Neither run made a single request to a registration endpoint. The **after** shot was recaptured against the final commit. | Before (`v2/main`) | After | | --- | --- | | | | | `Client registration` → **Dynamic (DCR)** | `Client registration` → **Client ID Metadata (CIMD)** |
The connection both runs produced
## Cause `BaseOAuthClientProvider.saveClientInformation` accepts two shapes: our own pre-registration callers pass `{ registrationKind }`, and the SDK passes `{ issuer }`. It treated *every* save without an explicit kind as DCR. The SDK reaches that method from three places in `auth()`, and only one of them is a dynamic registration: | SDK call site | What it is | Old kind | Correct kind | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | back-stamp an existing registration with its `issuer` (SEP-2352) | issuer binding | `dcr` | whatever it already was | | `client_id = clientMetadataUrl` when the AS advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported` | the SDK's own CIMD write | `dcr` | `cimd` | | `registerClient(...)` | a real DCR | `dcr` | `dcr` | So `ensureCimdClientRegistration` stored `cimd` correctly before authorization, and the issuer-binding write silently overwrote it moments later — which is why clearing OAuth state and reconnecting never helped. ## Fix SDK v2's `saveClientInformation` contract passes only `{ issuer }`, so the mechanism cannot be handed to us. But it does not have to be inferred either. **`auth()` calls `saveDiscoveryState` before it reads or writes client information**, and it takes its URL-based-client-ID branch — rather than `registerClient` — exactly when that metadata advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported` and a `clientMetadataUrl` is configured. So the branch the SDK took is read back from the state the SDK itself just wrote, using the same predicate it branched on. `resolveSdkRegistrationKind` first requires that CIMD is in play at all: configured for this connection, and the incoming `client_id` equal to that metadata-document URL. Anything else is `dcr` immediately. From there it is **two cases**, told apart by whether a registration already exists for this issuer: | Case | Answered by | | --- | --- | | A registration exists for this issuer under this `client_id` — the SDK is only adding the `issuer` to it | that registration's **recorded kind** (kind and credential are written and cleared together, so a stored registration always has one) | | Nothing exists for this issuer — this save creates the registration | the **persisted discovery state**, guarded on its metadata naming this same issuer so a state left over from a previously resolved AS cannot answer for a different one | The URL comparison only decides whether CIMD is *in play*; the two cases decide what actually happened. That matters because RFC 7591 §3.2 leaves a dynamically issued `client_id` opaque, so an AS may mint the metadata URL itself. Consequences, each of which was a defect on the way here: - An **existing DCR** whose `client_id` happens to be the metadata URL stays `dcr` — it takes the back-stamp case and its recorded kind says so. - **`invalid_client` recovery** stays `cimd`. `auth()` answers that error with `invalidateCredentials("client")` and an immediate retry; the clear removes the registration *and* its kind, so the retry takes the new-registration case and is answered from discovery state, which the clear does not touch. - A **second authorization server** behind one resource gets its own answer, since discovery state describes the issuer the SDK actually resolved. One that does not advertise CIMD is `dcr` even when it mints the metadata URL as its `client_id`. - A **transient failure in our own CIMD preflight** costs nothing, because what this reads is the SDK's own discovery. Supporting changes in `ensureCimdClientRegistration`: it binds its pre-registration to the issuer it just discovered (SEP-2352 keys registrations per AS, and its "already registered?" check is keyed the same way — read ctx-less it resolved through the *active* issuer and early-returned for every later one); it reuses `provider.discoveryState()` before fetching; and a discovery failure now skips pre-registration rather than propagating, since this helper is an optimization over what `auth()` does for itself. No UI or storage-schema change — Connection Info already renders whatever kind is stored. ## Tests The auth suites are at **627 passing**, and the CIMD OAuth E2E at **34**. New coverage spans both mocked cases and end-to-end ones driven against a real `OAuthStorageBase` and the real `ensureCimdClientRegistration`, since several of these behaviours are about how storage promotes and clears slots across issuers — which a mock would assert away. Every guard was mutation-checked independently: | Reverted | Result | | --- | --- | | the whole dispatch back to `: "dcr"` | **6 failed** | | back-stamp ignores the stored kind | **2 failed** — including the end-to-end existing-DCR case | | new registration ignores CIMD support | **2 failed** | | drop the issuer guard on the discovery state | **1 failed** | | `ensureCimdClientRegistration` back to its ctx-less early-return | **2 failed** | | drop the `issuer` from the pre-registration save | **2 failed** | | drop the cached-discovery reuse | **1 failed** | | make a discovery failure fatal again | **1 failed** | Reverting the dispatch also fails the CIMD OAuth E2E test on **both** transports — that failure is the reported bug itself, a completed CIMD connection reporting `registrationKind: "dcr"`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01Lmj6X2epWpPE7ScdSKQmtA

body:
`compare()` checked whether the *current* outcome was `NOT_DRILLABLE` before consulting the previous one, so a control that passed last run and has nothing to prove this run was filed as benign.

Deleting the classifier from the validator — to check that #31 actually depended on it — produced exactly that:

```
10/10 drills passed (2 with nothing to prove), 10/10 claims held
workstation-local: no control got worse. 10/10 proven.     exit 0
```

…while a drill had silently stopped testing anything.

`DISAPPEARED` already existed for a control that *leaves* the suite, and its docstring states the principle: *"untested is the state this whole package exists to stop being mistaken for safe."* A control that stays listed and stops proving is the **quieter** version of the same harm — and it was the one case the alarm could not reach.

Now:

```
workstation-local: 1 REGRESSED. 10/10 proven.
REGRESSED (1)
  [!!] shell.guarded    passed -> not_drillable
        was drilled in the previous run and has nothing to prove in this one;
        it is now untested, which is not the same as passing
                                                            exit 1
```

**The bound matters as much as the alarm.** A control that was *never* drillable stays benign, so `fs.read_file` — IDEMPOTENT by design — does not cry wolf, and a first sighting with no previous run is not a regression either. Both are tested.

A fresh run against the committed `assurance/workstation-baseline.json` is unchanged: **11/11 proven, exit 0**, so the nightly is unaffected.

**Mutations 3/3 caught**: reverting to the benign bucket; alarming even when it was never drillable; emitting the wrong change type.

Recorded as finding 14 in `docs/ADAPTERS.md`.

**Checks**: 579 passed / 14 skipped, ruff clean, mypy clean.

body:
## 증상

모바일에서 포켓몬 선택창을 열고 검색 입력을 탭하면 페이지가 확대되고, 선택을 마쳐 창이 닫혀도 **확대된 상태로 남아 있음**.

## 원인

iOS Safari는 포커스된 폼 요소의 `font-size`가 16px 미만이면 자동으로 페이지를 확대하며, 블러 시 원래 배율로 되돌리지 않는다. `.picker-search`(포켓몬/기술/도구 선택창 검색)가 `0.88rem`(≈14px)라 매번 발생.

## 수정

`≤760px`에서 `input`·`select`·`textarea`의 `font-size`를 `16px`로 강제(`index.css`). 확대 트리거 자체를 제거하므로 "되돌리기"가 필요 없음. 뷰포트 `maximum-scale` 제한(핀치 줌 비활성) 대신 이 방식 채택.
- 개별 컴포넌트가 더 작은 `font-size`를 지정 중(`.picker-search` 등)이라 `!important` 사용.

## 검증

- `tsc -b` / `oxlint` / `build` 통과
- dev 서버에서 `.picker-search` 계산값: 규칙 없을 때 `14.08px` → `@media(max-width:760px)` 규칙 적용 시 `16px` 확인

author: pareelamre
body:
Comment-only. No behaviour change.

## The claim that isn't true

`_AGENT_TRADING_BOARD_STALE_AFTER_S` is justified by:

> The board publishes far less often than the MTM ledgers (every ~15 min, best-effort under GitHub's scheduler)

That's the cron's *intent*, not its delivery. Measured over 2026-09-06/07, scheduled runs of `agent-trading-board-publish` — cron `"27,57 * * * *"`, so four per two hours — actually fired at:

```
19:21Z   21:29Z   23:22Z   01:10Z
```

Roughly **one slot in four**. What keeps the board alive between them is a separate even-hour `workflow_dispatch`, and that path runs a full agent tick (20–40 min) before publishing.

The workflow's own header already suspects this — it notes three consecutive slots missed on 2026-09-05 — but the threshold comment next to the number doesn't reflect it.

## Consequence

Effective publish gap is ~1 hour and frequently over the 3600s threshold. I watched the board cross it four separate times tonight; `freshness.stale` is true for part of most hours, which makes the flag close to uninformative.

## What I did and didn't change

Corrected the comment. **Left the number alone** — whether the flag should track delivered rather than intended cadence is a product decision about what you want it to mean, not something a measurement settles. Raising it to ~7200 would make it meaningful again; keeping 3600 and fixing delivery would too, and those are different bets.

The point of the change is that the next person tuning this shouldn't reason from "~15 min", which is off by about 4×.

## Tests

`python -m unittest discover -s tests`: **OK, 1460 tests, 5 skipped**. `ruff check src tests` clean.

author: yiliang114
body:
## What this PR does

Extends the negotiated active-work hold set with one aggregate `session` category for child-owned work that blocks Session settlement but was not previously reported: goal and cron processing, history mutation, and queued or running Monitor continuations. The same derived hold is used by heartbeat snapshots and conditional close, and existing change notifications now publish its transitions promptly.

## Why it's needed

Automatic cleanup currently authorizes conditional close from a narrower predicate than the drain waits on. A Session doing one of these unreported jobs advertises no holds, enters close, then waits on that job until the drain deadline and repeats the same failed probe indefinitely. Reporting one aggregate hold makes automatic reclamation lose to work the Session already owns without cancelling or otherwise disturbing that work.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Start goal, cron, history-mutation, and Monitor-continuation work independently and confirm the Session reports one `session:active-turn` hold while each operation is outstanding.
- Confirm `onlyIfUnheld` refuses immediately with that hold instead of entering the drain timeout loop.
- Let the work settle and confirm the next derived snapshot releases the hold and ordinary cleanup can proceed.
- Confirm foreground prompts remain represented only by the daemon-owned prompt count.
- Exercise a mixed-version handshake and confirm a new daemon grades a child that omits `session` as partial and disables ordinary automatic cleanup for that Session.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — protocol and lifecycle logic only; no UI change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not run |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not run |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not run |

### Environment (optional)

No local test, build, typecheck, or CI command was run. Verification was limited to two clean static diff reviews and `git diff --check`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this intentionally widens the public `activeWork` meaning. During a mixed-version window, a new daemon with an older child reports partial coverage and fails closed; an old daemon cannot consume the new hold until it is upgraded or restarted.
- Not validated / out of scope: running Monitor processes, follow-up suggestions, logical Agent watchdogs, runtime-generation draining, non-cooperative Agent escalation, and cross-generation background-shell delivery.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: no persistence migration or wire-version bump; category negotiation handles compatible peers.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #11118

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

在协商式 active-work hold 集合中新增一个聚合的 `session` 类别，用来覆盖会阻止 Session settle、但此前没有上报的子进程自有工作：goal 与 cron 处理、history mutation，以及排队中或执行中的 Monitor continuation。heartbeat snapshot 与 conditional close 共用同一个派生 hold，既有 change notification 也会及时发布这些状态变化。

## 为什么需要

自动清理当前用来授权 conditional close 的判据比 drain 实际等待的判据更窄。Session 执行这些未上报工作时会宣称没有 hold，进入 close 后又等待该工作直到 drain 超时，然后无限重复同一轮失败探测。新增一个聚合 hold 后，自动回收会让位于 Session 已经拥有的工作，而且不会取消或扰动这些工作。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

- 分别启动 goal、cron、history mutation 与 Monitor continuation，确认每项工作未结束时 Session 都会上报一个 `session:active-turn` hold。
- 确认 `onlyIfUnheld` 会立即携带该 hold 拒绝，而不是进入 drain 超时循环。
- 让工作结束，确认下一份派生 snapshot 会释放 hold，普通自动清理可以继续。
- 确认前台 prompt 仍只由 daemon 自己的 prompt 计数表示。
- 覆盖混合版本握手，确认新 daemon 会把未上报 `session` 的旧 child 评为 partial，并为该 Session 禁用普通自动清理。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A —— 仅协议与生命周期逻辑变更，无 UI 改动。

### 已测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未运行 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未运行 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ 未运行 |

### 环境（可选）

未运行本地测试、构建、typecheck 或 CI 命令。验证仅包含两轮干净的静态 diff 审核与 `git diff --check`。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：本改动有意扩大公开 `activeWork` 的语义。混合版本期间，新 daemon 与旧 child 组合会报告 partial coverage 并 fail closed；旧 daemon 在升级或重启前无法消费新 hold。
- 未验证 / 范围外：运行中的 Monitor 进程、follow-up suggestion、Agent 逻辑 watchdog、runtime generation draining、不响应 cooperative abort 的 Agent 升级处理，以及跨 generation 的后台 shell 投递。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：没有持久化迁移，也不提升 wire version；兼容 peer 通过 category negotiation 处理。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #11118

author: lesnik512
body:
## Why

`AGENTS.md` carried a per-repo copy of a doc-placement convention: a four-homes table, an admission check to run "before writing a line anywhere", an ADR row prescribing `NNNN-slug.md` and revisit triggers, and a ratchet rule.

Doc placement is a domain-modeling convention. Restating it in every repo means ~25 copies that can drift from it, in a file loaded on every turn — the failure the removed text itself named: "it is always loaded, so a line that restates a docstring… costs every turn and rots in two places at once."

The local ADR rule was also weaker than the convention it duplicated: it had no reversibility gate, so any non-obvious rejected alternative qualified.

Piloted and merged in `lite-bootstrap` (#188); this applies the same cut here.

## Design

Removed:

- the `Where a fact goes` section in full — four-homes table, the "before writing a line anywhere" admission check, "prose about mechanism has no home", the ratchet rule
- `Workflow`'s "the spec for a change is its PR body" rule, the "two things outlive the PR" ADR sentence, "there is no change file and no lane to choose", and "there is no separate truth-home directory"
- `Architecture`'s "behaviour detail has no prose home… run the admission check" tail, where present

Kept:

- the `INVARIANT:` docstring shape, with its ADR and lychee clauses trimmed
- one `Workflow` fact: unscheduled work becomes a GitHub issue
- every other section, unchanged
- inline `docs/adr/` citations inside architecture prose. Those cite a specific decision at the point it is relevant; they are not the convention being dropped.

No replacement pointer is added, by design.

## Non-goals

- No ADR is changed, removed or renumbered. `docs/adr/` is untouched.
- No code or test changes.

## Verification

The remaining `docs/adr/` mentions in this file, if any, are inline citations to specific decisions, not a rule about when to write one.

It is now the same lucide `Anchor` the site header uses — a ring, a shank, and flukes curving down and out — with the bottom arc written as **two cubic Béziers instead of an SVG arc command**, which Satori draws unreliably. The circle loses its `fill` so it reads as a ring, matching the header.

Four files each carried their own copy of the markup: the home, jobs and news cards plus the root Twitter card. All four now match.

## Outcome

Grok Build is now a first-class bootstrap client, matching Codex/Claude for catalog, instructions, hooks, plugins, and doctor evidence.

An operator who already has the shared MCP catalog still got a Grok TUI that only inherited Claude-compat copies. After this change, `./bootstrap` writes native Grok surfaces and `./bootstrap doctor` fails closed when they are missing.

## What changed

- install Homebrew cask `grok-build` (xAI CLI). The Homebrew formula named `grok` is an unrelated regex tool and is not installed.
- merge the shared MCP catalog into `~/.grok/config.toml` with the existing Codex TOML merger (same `[mcp_servers.<name>]` schema; no `grok mcp add`, so install does not start OAuth).
- write `~/.grok/rules/AGENTS.md`, `~/.grok/hooks/codegraph.json`, Ponytail with `--trust`, and a relative `hooks/hooks.json` symlink because Grok auto-loads that filename only.

- record the decision in `docs/adr/ADR-0002-grok-native-client.md` (Proposed) and refresh `docs/product-technical-gap-baseline.md`.

`codegraph install --target` still has no Grok id. This PR does not invent one; the catalog TOML stanza registers `codegraph serve --mcp`.

`grok_surface_coverage` 6/6 and local `scripts/test` GREEN, including Python helper executable-line coverage 100%.

Independent of open PRs #3 (skill deny list) and #4 (public docs surface). Those remain open. Do not close them; they are blocked on the central Dependency Review HTTP 403 (`ContextualWisdomLab/.github#810`), which this repository cannot substitute.

Merge only through normal protected governance after terminal applicable checks, current reviews/threads, current base ancestry/mergeability, and then-live protection. Do not treat sibling OSV/Trivy/Scorecard as a Dependency Review substitute.

author: jmf-pobox
body:
## Summary

Pilot of the cross-tool agent-config standard ([punt-kit context-mgmt.md](https://github.com/punt-labs/punt-kit/pull/340)) in z-spec. Makes z-spec's agent instructions **portable across Claude Code, codex, opencode, and pi** by generating both `CLAUDE.md` (Claude) and `AGENTS.md` (the flat file codex/opencode/pi read) from one `.rulesync/` source, and applies progressive disclosure so the always-loaded file stays lean.

## What changed

- **`AGENTS.md` freed** — bd's onboarding boilerplate moved to a lean `BEADS.md` pointer (`bd prime` provides detail on demand).
- **`.rulesync/rules/` is the single source** — one `root:true` lean overview (portable, ~6.5 KiB) plus a `targets:[claudecode]` rule for Claude-only content (MCP/ethos/delegation) that stays OUT of the portable AGENTS.md.
- **`AGENTS.md` + `CLAUDE.md` generated** by `rulesync generate`, drift-checked in CI.
- **Progressive disclosure** — big docs (WORKFLOW, TESTING, punt-kit standards) are *referenced* not inlined; the always-loaded file is **6,481 bytes**, 20% of codex's 32 KiB cap (vs. ~98 KiB if flattened naively).
- **Nothing dropped** — content the lean rewrite would have lost (module map, plugin structure, `ZSPEC_PLUGIN_ROOT`) is rehomed into `docs/development.md` and referenced; org-standard material (PR boundaries, CHANGELOG/README discipline) is referenced to its single home in punt-kit standards. DRY, don't-delete, standalone all honored.
- **CI gate** — `make check-rulesync` runs `rulesync generate --check` (fails on drift) + an `AGENTS.md` 32 KiB size assertion; wired into `make lint` and the lint workflow.

## Why

Today's config is Claude-only (built on `@`-imports no other tool follows). This makes z-spec's guidance work in every major coding agent, keeps one source of truth, and enforces leanness so codex never silently truncates.

## Verification

- `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` = 6,481 bytes, under the 32 KiB cap and the repo's own gate.
- `make lint` green (markdownlint, ruff, shellcheck, `check-rulesync` drift check).
- Drift gate verified both directions (passes clean; fails on hand-injected drift).
- Full formal-methods test suite not run — config/docs-only change.

Pilot for the org-wide effort; enable/disable standard revision (the tool-user path) follows separately.

author: augustas11
body:
## Summary

Fix SPEC-041 SQLite replay cleanup at fractional-second retention boundaries. Direct RFC3339Nano string ordering could delete a live entry early, allowing the same envelope to be recorded again, or keep an expired entry too long.

- Use one shared cleanup predicate for `RecordRelayBlindReplay` and `RelayBlindReplaySeen` within their existing immediate transactions.
- Keep the indexed whole-second candidate bound, then compare the stored UTC timestamp without its terminal Z against a fixed-nine-digit UTC cutoff.
- Support existing persisted whole-second and variable-fraction timestamps without migration or changing the writer format.
- Preserve duplicate-before-capacity ordering, exact-expiry reclamation, and rollback behavior. No routing, quota, receipt, or settlement changes.

This is the separate cleanup follow-up identified in #1413. It starts from fresh main and does not include that PR's wallet-throttle changes.

## Validation

- Regression first: baseline failed eight precision cases across both public methods and one live-row capacity case; all pass with the fix.
- `go test -race ./internal/storage/sqlite -run '^TestRelayReplayRetention' -count=1`: passed (3.391s).
- Tests include 1,521 timestamp comparisons across all fractional precisions, timezone normalization, indexed query-plan assertion, database reopen, and cleanup rollback after injected insert failure.
- `go test -race ./... -count=1`: passed across all seven test-bearing gateway packages (router 79.998s, SQLite 12.680s); storage interface package has no tests.
- `go vet ./...`, SPEC governance validation, JSON parsing, generated-index check, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Astra Ultra code/security/architecture review of the full two-file diff: each 0 Critical / High / Medium / Low findings; architecture CLEAR.
- PR governance declaration validated before publication.

## Boundaries

The predicate relies on the existing sole writer's UTC RFC3339Nano format. Manually corrupted or offset-bearing SQL values are outside that storage contract. Reopening is tested in-process; a separate-process crash test and live signed gateway journey were not run.

No conformance status, authority, production readiness, provider-side crypto, or signed journey evidence is promoted or changed.

## 취약점 (ICS/OT 고전 결함)
**제어포인트 읽기 인가 누락 (missing authorization)**: SCADA HMI 는 제어포인트(Modbus/DNP3 레지스터에 대응)를 id 로 노출한다. **인증만 하고 인가를 안 해서** 인증된 아무 운영자나 `GET /api/points/{id}` 로 restricted 안전/기밀 포인트까지 읽는다. 체커가 그 restricted 포인트(`SAFETY_INTERLOCK`)에 라운드 플래그를 심고, 공격자는 포인트 id 를 훑어 탈취한다. 실 ICS 사고의 전형(authentication ≠ authorization).

body:
## Summary

Help a human SRE investigate broader incident symptoms, use bounded helpers without losing the original question, and receive outputs proportional to the task. This PR contains the approved follow-up branch work after merged #235, including the helper exchange and Codex review corrections; it remains **unaccepted for adoption or merge**, regardless of review-ready status. The exact-revision human acceptance decision is still open.

## What changed, and why

- Generalized incident advice for login failures, intermittent errors, slowness, stale/wrong data and missed jobs, with user-outcome recovery and retained uncertainty.
- Aligned bounded helper completion, caller/owner separation, claim-level evidence and caller continuation across agent and skill consumers. Review verdicts stay scoped to the reviewed change.
- Made alert and trace answers task-sized, introduced abbreviated postmortems, and reused one follow-up record across incident closeout, postmortem, operational learning and scribe.
- Replaced one-sided incident examples with a complete dispatch/returned-evidence/parent-reconciliation exchange. The parent preserves useful observations, rejects unsupported current-state/causal claims, and accepts genuinely supported scoped pressure. Documented explicit advisor invocation as a fallback without disabling automatic selection.
- Retained the earlier platform/runbook example repairs, focused asset/scope checks, historical evaluation evidence, roadmap decisions and generated Copilot projections.
- Addressed four Codex comments in `941dc286`: unsupported restart headroom now routes directly to the named engineering lead; impact-end and human-confirmation timestamps are separate; unknown postmortem metadata uses YAML null; bounded helper results distinguish mitigation not assessed from assessed with none supported. The P1 adoption thread remains open, not treated as a code defect or implicitly accepted.
- The earlier generalized-incident work adds the symptom reference to task-context accounting and changes the human-incident budget from 64,000 to 73,000 bytes and the skill corpus ceiling from 571,000 to 576,000 bytes. The later task-sized and helper-exchange slices do not raise those ceilings again. No new execution framework or tool grants.

## Reviewer briefing

- **What a serious defect looks like in this change:** a helper observation becomes an unsupported claim of current state, cause or recovery; dispatch loses its caller or human owner; a small lookup becomes a full incident workflow; a production recommendation becomes implied authority; a generated adapter differs from its source.
- **Look hardest at:** incident and SRE helper source/consumer contracts, recovery and timing examples, postmortem/closeout follow-up preservation, reviewer target scope, platform/runbook examples, and the branch-wide budget changes.
- **Least sure about:** automatic advisor/reference selection and native dispatch/continuation on the final bytes. Earlier Sonnet trials contain failures; source examples and passing local checks do not close them.
- **Please still make an independent pass beyond the above and say what it found, including if that is nothing.**

## Verification

- [x] [verified] `python scripts/gate_a.py` — 4/4 structural steps green, rerun before publication.
- [verified] Final review-fix source: `python -m pytest scripts evals -q` — **466 passed, 5 skipped, 923 subtests passed**. The new parsed-template regression first failed against the old metadata (four subtest failures), then passed; it checks fields/defaults, not model reasoning.
- [verified] `python scripts/generate_platform_adapters.py --write` — 126 adapters generated and matching; projections included.
- [verified] `python scripts/check_context_cost.py` — 7/7 within their current budgets; human incident path 68,769/73,000 bytes.
- [verified] `python scripts/check_weight.py` — skill corpus 575,921/576,000 bytes, agents 114,243/115,000 bytes, eval Python 9,252/9,900 lines. Review corrections raise no ceilings.
- [verified] `python evals/build_probe.py --validate` — 65 specs and 324 expectations. No scenario/grader changes in this PR; this is a structural consistency check, not a paid campaign.
- [verified] `git diff --check` passed. Final review-fix plugin digest: `ed5f99592fac39992f57c3b69a6c0142669dbdb9aac859ecf6a3e1f7809bfcc0`.
- [sourced] Independent source review of the final exchange found and reopened a missing human-facing observation summary; the correction is included. No material source finding remains in that scoped review, which is not an independent review of the whole branch.
- [sourced] Independent static review also found no material issue in the four Codex-comment fixes. That does not resolve the adoption gate or establish model compliance.

### Behavioral gates remain open

- [sourced] The earlier second-pass Sonnet campaign completed 24 initiated sessions, estimated CLI cost $2.5634535, and **failed behavioral acceptance**. Actual child return and parent continuation worked in the sampled workflow; advisor/reference selection, caller/owner dispatch, causal exclusions and resumed timing did not all pass. Those results bind the report's older digest, not this PR head.
- [unverified] Final task-sized-output and helper-exchange model comparisons have not run; their separate budget decisions remain outstanding. Three helper-exchange cases were frozen before edits and source-reviewed, not executed as model tests.
- [unverified] No fresh final-byte native selection, reference loading, dispatch, return or continuation proof. Terra has zero model calls and remains paused on its previously documented host-context/tool-inventory limitation.
- Prompt-behavior red/green and tools-off evidence are therefore not complete. Focused structural tests do not substitute for them. Keep the adoption hold until the owner decides the next bounded verification and accepts the exact candidate; review-ready status is not that decision.

Evidence:

- [Generalized incident guidance](https://github.com/latent-sre/save-toolkit/blob/8b80eacc3296f7619a4a896c9e0dd91134f80f02/docs/reviews/2026-09-06-general-incident-help.md)
- [First decision-quality repairs](https://github.com/latent-sre/save-toolkit/blob/8b80eacc3296f7619a4a896c9e0dd91134f80f02/docs/reviews/2026-09-06-sre-decision-quality-repairs.md)
- [Second-pass Sonnet results and adoption hold](https://github.com/latent-sre/save-toolkit/blob/8b80eacc3296f7619a4a896c9e0dd91134f80f02/docs/reviews/2026-09-07-incident-quality-second-pass.md)
- [Task-sized output changes](https://github.com/latent-sre/save-toolkit/blob/8b80eacc3296f7619a4a896c9e0dd91134f80f02/docs/reviews/2026-09-07-task-sized-skill-outputs.md)

## Risk

Incorrect incident inference can send the human down the wrong path even when a response is well formed. Shorter outputs can lose evidence or distinct follow-up states; a written load rule does not force native skill selection. This PR makes no claim of increased runtime enforcement or proven model reliability.

No production operation or irreversible external effect was performed. Publishing the branch is not installation, deployment or acceptance. If rejected, prepare a scoped revert of the named commits and regenerate projections; preserve the earlier evidence rather than rewriting published history.

## Deliberately not done

- No merge, deployment, live-system operation, tool-grant expansion, automatic learning or candidate promotion.
- No additional Sonnet/Terra campaign without its separate approval; no paid judge

author: aliz-nancy
body:
## Summary
- HNSW 索引ノードの f16 常駐表現（`ResidentPrecision`。既定 F32・opt-in の `build_with_precision`）と、F16C／NEON fp16 デコード付き dot カーネル（`isa.rs` の `F16cToken`／`NeonFp16Token`・`F16Kernel`、`f16.rs` の共有変換）を実装
- `EXPLAIN` の `hnsw_params:` へ `resident=` を追記し、`check_simd_codegen.sh` へ `vcvtph2ps`／`fcvtl` 期待命令検査を追加
- 最終スコアは常に `kernel::dot` で f32 再計算する契約・既定エンジンは無変更

Closes #514


## 対象外（out-of-scope）
- AVX-512 f16 変種（_mm512_cvtph_ps）は未実装（ADRのトークン表に無く対象外）
- RecallEngine fixture への hnsw_f16 追加・recall.yml matrix 拡張・Recall 3ゲート同一閾値検証は Issue #515 の担当
- 25k/100k/500k×dim128/768 規模での常駐メモリ・レイテンシ前後比較実測は Issue #516 の担当
- 既定常駐精度をF16へ反転するかはIssue #515/#516実測後のオーナー判断待ち
- wire-serverへのHNSW/精度opt-in CLI追加は対象外
- NEONカーネルのApple Silicon等実機での生成コード・性能確認はクロスコンパイル確認までが本Issueの範囲

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the HNSW search hot path and adds target-feature SIMD dispatch, but behavior is opt-in with F32 defaults, range-based residency fallback, and unchanged final f32 score recomputation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **opt-in f16 resident HNSW node vectors** while keeping the default engine and default `ResidentPrecision::F32` unchanged. Callers opt in via `ValidatedHnswParams::with_resident_precision(ResidentPrecision::F16)`; graph build still runs in f32 and **freezes** to either `NodeVectors::F32` or `NodeVectors::F16`, with automatic **F32 fallback** when any component is outside f16 range.
> 
> **Shared f16 layer:** `f32`↔`f16` conversion moves into `f16.rs` (`encode_rows`, `fits_f16`) so HNSW and `batch_search` `pack_f16x2` share the same bit layout and rounding.
> 
> **SIMD:** `isa.rs` gains `F16cToken` / `NeonFp16Token`, `F16Kernel`, and `dot_f16` (F16C `vcvtph2ps` on x86_64, NEON `fcvtl` widening on aarch64, scalar fallback). HNSW layer scoring during search uses this path; **final hit scores remain `kernel::dot` on f32 arena vectors** per existing `hnsw_cache` contract.
> 
> **Observability & CI:** `EXPLAIN` `hnsw_params:` includes `resident=`; `check_simd_codegen.sh` expects memory-operand `vcvtph2ps` / `fcvtl` when f16 kernels are exercised. F16 resident indexes use `node_matches` for overlay diff detection instead of `vector()` (which returns `None` for F16).
>

## 문제
#95에서 추가한 grafana-alloy 사이드카가 기동 직후 종료됨. CloudWatch 로그: `Error: unknown command "sh" for "alloy"`

## 원인
grafana/alloy 이미지는 ENTRYPOINT가 `/bin/alloy`로 고정돼 있어, ECS `command` 필드(=Docker CMD)만 바꾸면 그 값이 alloy의 인자로 붙는다. `command = ["sh", "-c", "..."]`를 주면 실제 실행은 `alloy sh -c "..."`가 되어 즉시 종료됨.

## 수정
`entryPoint = ["sh", "-c"]`를 명시적으로 지정.

author: rishika3d
body:
## Summary
Three redirects in the feedback-management views (`orga/views/submission.py`) passed the user-supplied `next` query parameter straight into `redirect()` with no validation:
- `FeedbackBulkAction.post` (empty-selection branch and end of method)
- `FeedbackUpdateStatus.get`

An authenticated organizer following a crafted link like `.../submissions/feedback/bulk/?next=https://evil.example.com` was redirected to the external URL — an open redirect (CWE-601), usable for phishing.

The sibling method `FeedbackUpdateStatus.post` in the same file already guards this with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(...)`. This PR applies the same allow-list check to the other three paths, so an external `next` is ignored (falling back to the event feedback page) while an internal `next` still works.

## Severity
Low-to-medium: the endpoints require an authenticated organizer with `base.orga_update_submission`.

## Proof / test
Adds `tests/talk/orga/views/test_orga_views_feedback_redirect.py` with two cases:
- Against the original code the block test FAILS — the response is `302 Location: https://evil.example.com/phish`.
- Against this fix both tests PASS — the external `next` is rejected, and a safe internal `next` is still honored.

Video attached below.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98f51a0a-43b4-4a08-90b7-196823ce07bb



Fixes #5485

## Summary by Sourcery

Protect feedback-management redirects from open-redirect vulnerabilities while retaining safe internal navigation.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent unauthenticated external redirects from feedback-management views by validating user-supplied `next` URLs against the current host and connection security.
- Preserve valid internal feedback redirects while falling back to the event feedback page for unsafe destinations.

Tests:
- Add coverage for blocking external redirects and honoring safe internal redirects across feedback bulk-action and status-update flows.

author: lesnik512
body:
## Why

`AGENTS.md` carried a per-repo copy of a doc-placement convention: a four-homes table, an admission check to run "before writing a line anywhere", an ADR row prescribing `NNNN-slug.md` and revisit triggers, and a ratchet rule.

Doc placement is a domain-modeling convention. Restating it in every repo means ~25 copies that can drift from it, in a file loaded on every turn — the failure the removed text itself named: "it is always loaded, so a line that restates a docstring… costs every turn and rots in two places at once."

The local ADR rule was also weaker than the convention it duplicated: it had no reversibility gate, so any non-obvious rejected alternative qualified.

Piloted and merged in `lite-bootstrap` (#188); this applies the same cut here.

## Design

Removed:

- the `Where a fact goes` section in full — four-homes table, the "before writing a line anywhere" admission check, "prose about mechanism has no home", the ratchet rule
- `Workflow`'s "the spec for a change is its PR body" rule, the "two things outlive the PR" ADR sentence, "there is no change file and no lane to choose", and "there is no separate truth-home directory"
- `Architecture`'s "behaviour detail has no prose home… run the admission check" tail, where present

Kept:

- the `INVARIANT:` docstring shape, with its ADR and lychee clauses trimmed
- one `Workflow` fact: unscheduled work becomes a GitHub issue
- every other section, unchanged
- inline `docs/adr/` citations inside architecture prose. Those cite a specific decision at the point it is relevant; they are not the convention being dropped.

No replacement pointer is added, by design.

## Non-goals

- No ADR is changed, removed or renumbered. `docs/adr/` is untouched.
- No code or test changes.

## Verification

The remaining `docs/adr/` mentions in this file, if any, are inline citations to specific decisions, not a rule about when to write one.

author: a-thomas-22
body:
The deployed app cannot load anything. Every request fails with:

```
Could not load history: Failed to construct 'URL': Invalid URL
```

**Cause.** `Dockerfile.web` bakes `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api/v1`, which is right: the api and the app are served from one hostname behind the tunnel. But `buildUrl` did `new URL(API_BASE_URL + path)`, and `new URL()` cannot parse a path without a base, so it threw on every call. Local development never saw it because the default base is absolute.

The socket had the same flaw for the same reason: `"/api/v1".replace(/^http/i, "ws")` leaves the path untouched, and `new WebSocket("/api/v1/ws")` is invalid. So live updates were broken too.

**Fix.** Paths are assembled by string, which `fetch` resolves against the document. The socket resolves a relative base against `window.location.origin`, picking `wss` for an https page. An absolute base behaves exactly as before.

**Tests.** A relative base now has coverage in `core.test.ts` (base, `isRelativeBase`, both path forms with and without a query) and in `ws.test.ts` (https to wss, http to ws, a trailing slash on the origin, and an explicit `NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL` still winning). Both fail without the fix.

Gates: lint, typecheck, 461 tests, coverage 99.79% lines, and a build with `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=/api/v1`, the value the image uses.

author: badshuang
body:
## 现场表现

用户**撤回**一个分析项后发现，那一行的计算列渲染成了这样：

```
imp_weight_lookup    ["1.0\n1.0"]
imp_cf_lookup        ["---\n---"]
imp_report           ["—\n—"]
```

一个元素里塞着换行的**假数组**，MultiValue 控件原样显示出来。而同一行的 `list` 型列（`imp_name` / `imp_area`）显示的是正常的 `1, 1`。

**存的数据没坏** —— 三个 `imp_repeat` 分析项的值一直是 `["1", "1"]`（两个元素、无换行）。这一路只影响渲染。

## 根因

```python
# bika/lims/browser/analyses/view.py, _folder_item_calculation
if not is_editable:
    interim_field["value"] = interim_formatted        # ← 不再是 JSON
```

分析项**不可编辑**时（提交 / 撤回后），core 把值换成显示文本。而 `calculatedlist` 的显示文本是 `patched_get_formatted_interim` 用 **`"\n".join()`** 连起来的，不是 JSON。于是 `patched_folderitem` 的兜底：

```python
text = _safe_text(value)                 # "1.0\n1.0"
try:
    parsed = json.loads(text)            # 失败
except (ValueError, TypeError):
    value = json.dumps([text])           # ← 包成 ["1.0\n1.0"]
```

**同一个函数里 20 行之上的 `list` 分支一直是对的**，注释就写着 *Already formatted display text — keep as-is*。**两个分支对同一种情况处理相反** —— 这种不一致本身就是信号。

## 关于 [#48](https://github.com/NingboMaiTux/senaite.docker/pull/48) 的定位（要说清楚）

包装这个 bug **在 #48 之前就存在**：当时那行是 `json.dumps([str(value)])`，对纯 ASCII 如 `"1.0\n1.0"` 产生**一模一样**的垃圾，只在非 ASCII 时崩。

| 值 | #48 之前 | #48 之后 | 本 PR 之后 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `["1.0\n1.0"]`（ASCII） | 同样的垃圾 | 同样的垃圾 | **`1.0`** |
| `["—\n—"]`（em dash） | **整页 500** | 垃圾 | **`—`** |

所以 **#48 把「崩」换成了「显示垃圾」** —— 它是对的也是必要的（崩更糟），但**只修了一半**，另一半是用户撤回一次照出来的。

## 改动

`except` 分支从 `value = json.dumps([text])` 改成 **`pass`**，与 `list` 分支一致。

`json.loads` 成功但结果不是 list 的情况**仍然包装** —— 那部分是对的：一个裸数字确实需要变成单元素数组给 MultiValue。

## 验证

**页面实测**（AS-Grouped 与 Classic 都 200）：

| 格子 | 修复前 | 修复后 |
|---|---|---|
| `imp_weight_lookup` | `["1.0\n1.0"]` | **`1.0`** |
| `imp_cf_lookup` | `["---\n---"]` | **`---`** |
| `imp_pct` | `["---\n---"]` | **`---`** |
| `imp_report` | `["—\n—"]` | **`—`** |

**用户已在页面上确认通过。**

**`tests/test_folderitem_unicode.py` 从 14 条扩到 28 条**，分成 half1（不崩）/ half2（不包装），并且对源码断言 **`json.dumps([text])` 只能出现一次** —— 谁把包装写回去就会红。纯值断言抓不到这个回归：所有 ASCII 用例照样全绿。

**既有测试全过，合计 247 条断言**：

```
test_engine                  S0-S7 engine helpers: 204/204 passed
test_folderitem_unicode      folderitem: non-editable interim: 28/28 passed
test_collector_unicode       collector unicode safety: 15/15 passed
```

`lint_addon.py --addon maitux.calcenhance` → **0 ERROR / 0 WARN / 0 INFO**。

## 开发规则

- **R13** 的事故表补第四行（这一族在本环境已出四次）
- **新增 R13b**「不可编辑时 core 会把值换成显示文本 —— 别把它当数据」

R13b 值得单独立规，因为这一条**同时**是崩溃（#48）和数据错乱（本 PR）的源头。两条推论：别对它做 `str()`；解析失败也别把它包成数组。要真拿数据，得像 `maitux.worksheet` 的 `_raw_interim_values()` 那样绕过这次替换去读对象 —— 它的 docstring 记着为什么必须这么做。

## 生效方式

`customers` 层 → **`docker restart` 即可**。不用重建镜像、不用重装 profile。

## 一个仍然开着的问题（不在本 PR 范围）

修完之后，撤回/提交后的 calculatedlist 列显示的是**换行连接的整段文本**（和 `list` 列显示 `1, 1` 一样），而**不是多行**。这是 core 那次「替换成显示文本」的固有结果，不是本 PR 引入的。

`maitux.worksheet` 的 AS-Grouped 布局已经有 `_raw_interim_values()` 绕过它、恢复多行渲染；原生 Classic listing 没有。**如果希望 Classic 也保持多行，那是另一件事**，需要在 `patched_folderitem` 里改成从对象读存储值而不是用 `item[kw]["value"]` —— 影响面比本 PR 大，建议单独立项。

body:
Launch-day and countdown automations fail because Home Assistant renders datetime variables as strings. Keep date objects inside individual templates and pass timestamps between variables, repairing day, countdown and pet alerts.

Correct countdown evening fallback so launches days away do not alert tonight, enforce quiet hours during catch-up, and initialize reschedule history silently so later changes can notify. All four alerts ignore invalid, completed, in-flight and past launches; action guards also apply to manual Run actions.

Validation: 25 offline blueprint regression tests and 66 Node card tests passed locally. Regression tests reproduce both reported errors and cover midnight/DST, fallback timing, helpers, deduplication and reschedule initialization. Blueprint tests now run in Validate and Release. All 13 uploaded files match the tested local files by Git blob SHA. Live Home Assistant verification remains pending.

v0.3.2 includes release notes and update instructions. Users must re-import existing blueprints and reload automations; a HACS card update alone does not update imported blueprints. Existing inputs remain compatible, with an optional earliest-morning countdown setting. The launch-day check must occur before launch; the default 8 AM check cannot warn before a 7:26 AM launch.

author: stan-2021131
body:
## Descripción

Se implementó la suite de pruebas de integración correspondiente a **TEST-08 — Transversal**, enfocada en validar los principales controles de seguridad, autorización y consistencia de datos del backend utilizando el entorno real de integración.

## Cambios realizados

### IT-34 — Autorización por dueño de recurso (IDOR)
- Se validó que usuarios ajenos no puedan editar, eliminar o cambiar el estado de publicaciones y anuncios.
- Se verificó la protección de acuerdos privados frente a usuarios que no participan en ellos.
- Se comprobó que los propietarios y participantes legítimos mantengan el acceso correspondiente.
- Cobertura de regresión para **BG-02 y BG-03**.

### IT-35 — Rate limiting
- Se verificaron los límites de intentos de autenticación mediante Redis.
- Se validó el rate limiting global de la API REST.
- Se comprobaron los límites por usuario en eventos de Socket.IO y la ausencia de persistencia al excederlos.
- Cobertura de regresión para **BG-12**.

### IT-36 — Validación de archivos
- Se verificó la validación por **magic bytes** en imágenes y PDFs, evitando depender únicamente del MIME declarado.
- Se probaron los límites máximos de tamaño y cantidad de archivos.
- Se comprobó que uploads rechazados no generen registros inconsistentes.
- Cobertura de regresión para **BG-05 y BG-15**.

### IT-37 — Consistencia R2 ↔ PostgreSQL
- Se verificó que un fallo durante la subida a R2 no altere el estado persistido.
- Se comprobó la compensación cuando R2 completa la subida pero falla la persistencia posterior.
- Se validó el flujo exitoso de actualización y eliminación del recurso anterior.
- Cobertura de regresión para **BG-14**.

### IT-50 — Autorización de conversaciones y mensajes
- Se verificó que únicamente los participantes puedan consultar el historial de una conversación.
- Se bloqueó el acceso y envío de mensajes por parte de usuarios autenticados ajenos a la conversación.
- Se validó la autorización tanto mediante REST como Socket.IO, comprobando que los intentos rechazados no generen persistencia.

## Verificación

- **221** pruebas de integración exitosas.
- **153** pruebas unitarias exitosas.
- **164** pruebas de contrato exitosas.
- Sin regresiones detectadas ni cambios requeridos en código productivo.

author: rob-reynolds
body:
When a QuestionnaireResponse contains a Coding answer and its extraction profile constrains an Observation value to CodeableConcept, extraction currently drops the answer. This can leave a subsequent PlanDefinition apply paused despite a supplied answer.

Convert Coding to CodeableConcept before assignment when the assignment parent matches the resource profile and the selected element is unsliced and has exactly one type. Preserve the complete Coding and repeated-property cardinality. Nested Extension and sibling-type-slice regressions prevent borrowing an unrelated profile constraint. Existing unsupported conversions and their diagnostic behavior remain unchanged.

### Validation

- Reproduced the original failure on unmodified main and v4.7.0 baselines.
- 21 conversion tests across DSTU3, R4 and R5, including 27 real extraction-entry cases, all passing. Cases cover differential/snapshot profiles, both choice-path spellings, metadata, repeated values, Boolean false and unsupported slices/multi-type elements.
- Combined with the separate generated-ID correction, main CR + utility suites: 3,626 passed, 24 skipped, zero failures/errors. Final test-only assertion rerun: 21 passed.
- A pinned-4.7 runtime comparison exercised 12 apply calls across original, Coding-only and combined configurations. Corrected configurations pause on missing data, reach the expected affirmative/negative activity after answers, and pause again after clearing an answer. Complete returned values and issue sets were compared.
- Formatting and main-source Checkstyle passed.

This PR contains only the Coding change. Generated IDs are in a separate stacked PR. The tested v4.7.0 backport is available on codex/qr-extraction-backport; upstream currently has no 4.7 maintenance branch to target. No installed runtime or release was replaced.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

PR #86 tried to route npmjs traffic through `registry.npmmirror.com` by overriding the built-in `npmjs` alias in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, but deployment builds still hit `registry.npmjs.org` and timed out with `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` / `error (23)`. The `prefix: npmjs` alias only applies to lockfile reverse-routing and explicit `npmjs:` specifiers; it does **not** change the default registry that pnpm uses for ordinary package resolution.

This PR actually moves the default registry to the mirror:

- `.npmrc`: adds `registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com/`
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: removes the ineffective `registries` / `prefix: npmjs` block and keeps the `fetchTimeout` / `fetchRetries` / `networkConcurrency` settings added in PR #86

Because the lockfile omits tarball URLs and lets pnpm reconstruct them from the active registry, all metadata and tarball requests now go to `registry.npmmirror.com` instead of `registry.npmjs.org`.

Local `docker build` with a clean layer cache completed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the workspace build without touching `registry.npmjs.org`.

author: elanthus
body:
Configuration construction and snapshot validation previously accepted values that file loading rejected unless each caller remembered a private validation helper. Modes, severities, risk levels, constrained path patterns, and the conditional approval-environment requirement are now enforced by the Pydantic section models themselves.

The loading boundary retains TOML parsing, whole-section replacement, and friendly `ConfigError` translation. Errors now attribute each invalid section to its own source file, including when both user and repository files contain errors. Defaults, aliases, and snapshot/digest serialization remain unchanged. Snapshot consumers no longer call a private validator; their protected-policy, attestation, and session error boundaries are covered by regression tests.

Read-only severity consumers accept `Sequence[str]` to accommodate the narrowed literal types, and the review executor no longer needs a type cast. Tests exercise the same invalid inputs through construction, dictionary/JSON snapshots, and both TOML sources, plus section replacement, aliases, valid patterns, and the existing fixed digest contract. See this PR's CI checks for hosted validation, coverage, and packaging results.

Preflight review: all 27 delivered diff units examined; no code or documentation findings required remediation. The attestation records reported coverage and stage evidence as an audit trail, not proof of review quality or a substitute for CI and human review. Repository policy requires manual review and merge for `config.py` and `risk.py` changes.

Review feedback addressed: `3e0ad36` handles empty validation locations/error lists and separates file groups with newlines. `51db864` resolves the CodeRabbit path finding by checking both separators and rejecting Windows drives, UNC paths, and parent traversal across every constrained pattern field. Accepted patterns retain their stored bytes.

Closes #102.

author: richartvt
body:
Adds the smallest CI pipeline that is actually useful for this repository.

Two independent jobs running in parallel, so a red badge says *which* half broke:

- **backend** — `uv sync --locked`, `ruff check`, `pytest -q`
- **frontend** — `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`

### No PostgreSQL service, on purpose

Only 10 of the 534 tests touch the database, all in `tests/test_cruce_python_sql.py`,
and they query materialized views over the ingested dataset — which CI cannot have:
ingestion takes hours and `stats.nba.com` drops datacenter IPs. An empty Postgres
container would leave those tests skipping anyway.

Verified by pointing `DATABASE_URL` at a dead port: **534 collected, 524 passed,
10 skipped, 0 failed, 2.07s**. The skips are clean and instant.

No services, secrets, env vars, migrations, seed data, coverage or version matrix.

### Local run before pushing

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `uv sync --locked` | ok |
| `uv run ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `uv run pytest -q` | 534 passed in 2.17s |
| `npm ci` | 0 vulnerabilities |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm run build` | built in 454ms |

Opening this PR also verifies that the `pull_request` trigger fires.

## Resumo

Adendo ao plano de integração de produção do Mixlirous, com validação linha a linha contra o código atual e priorização Pareto (80/20) das ações de maior retorno.

- `production.yaml` já usa `${DATABASE_URL}` via secrets manager — não precisa de migração.

O bloco "Ainda pendentes" do README está desatualizado e já induziu análises externas a diagnósticos incorretos sobre o estado do projeto. Recomenda-se corrigi-lo como primeira ação.

### Conteúdo
- Tabela de correções validadas contra o código.
- 12 ações priorizadas por impacto/esforço.
- Cortes recomendados para não sobrecarregar o MVP.
- Cronograma de ~4 semanas para uma alpha honesta.

body:
Step 5 of the installer program (`.scratch/installer-os/installer-os-spec.md`, S5; ADR-0011). The read-only half of job facts: every crew role, installers included, sees the job's answers on the unit they are standing at.

## What changed
- A "Job facts" card on the unit sheet, directly under the spec card. Shows only answered fields, in this order: exterior finish, set depth (with the inch), flashing, fasteners as one line, sill pan, the note for this unit's elevation, site rules, GC contact (phone is a tap-to-call link).
- When the unit's own spec carries an inset/outset that disagrees with the job's set depth, the spec's value is shown with the sentence "This unit's spec says …; it wins." Both languages.
- Elevation is derived from the mark's elevation-reference captions (the same logic the elevation crop uses). When no caption names a side, every non-empty elevation note is shown, each labelled.
- Empty state: "No job facts yet. Ask your foreman." with a link into Ask. Degrades to the empty state when the table is missing.
- Reads through the same `buildFacts` and `elevationViews` query keys the job page and map already warm, so the card never adds a network read and works offline.
- Five new catalog keys (en + es), appended at the end; every other label reuses the S4 keys. CSS appended at the end of the stylesheet.

## Gate (app/, Node 22, on the merge with master cec64f2)
- vitest: 383 files, 5,308 tests, green
- lint: 25 warnings (pin)
- tsc: clean; build: clean; entry chunk 240.7 kB gzip (budget 260)
- e2e (targeted, port 5211): opening-sheet 14/14, clock-in-once 1/1 — fixtures have no job-facts table, so this proves the empty state and that nothing else on the sheet moved

No migration. No data-flow change.
