## What this is

The **cost half** of the five meters. `T-FCORE-012` named them and `T-FCORE-010` priced them; this adds the cost each rate must clear, and the lists of what is never charged for at all.

## The design

**`BM-17`'s floor had nothing to measure against.** No worst-case unit COGS figure existed anywhere in the suite — `BM-26` records that the inherited estimates were unverified, and the document carrying them is retired. So the ≥40% floor named a number nothing held.

**The owner ruled `BM-17` read backwards.** A published rate already implies the highest cost its unit may carry — the rate divided by 1.4 — and that ceiling IS the worst case until the vendor rate cards land. Recorded as a status note on `Q1`; the rate cards remain that row's revisit trigger.

**`WorstCaseCogs` sits ON the rate**, never in a table beside it, so a rate cannot be authored without the figure that judges it. It has no `verified` field: `BM-26` says no COGS figure here is verified, and a flag that cannot be written cannot be rendered as a claim.

**`commerce/costs.ts` is the other side of `METERS`** — the absorbed costs `BM-24` swallows, the capabilities `BM-19` and `BM-23` promise free, and `BM-25`'s proxied upstreams with no tenant-facing configuration shape anywhere. Containment is a platform duty, and a setting that cannot be written cannot leak onto a screen.

## The consequence, recorded rather than hidden

Four of the six IN rows clear the floor by **nothing at all**:

| Meter | Rate | Floor | Headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voice minute | ₹6.00 | ₹5.99 | 1 paisa |
| AI detection | ₹10.00 | ₹10.00 | **none** |
| WhatsApp conversation | ₹1.50 | ₹1.50 | **none** |
| SMS | ₹0.35 | ₹0.35 | **none** |
| Email | ₹0.10 | ₹0.10 | **none** |
| Tracked seat-month | ₹99.00 | ₹98.99 | 1 paisa |

A real cost a paisa above its ceiling makes that row invalid. `metersBelowCogsFloor` is what says so. That is the ruling's own shape, not a defect.

## Verification record

`pnpm verify` exits **0** — build · lint · boundaries · typecheck · gates · 409 unit tests · invariants.

**Two gates seen RED on injected violations:**

| Injected violation | Result |
|---|---|
| Voice COGS raised by one paisa (428 → 429) | `expected [ 'voice_minutes' ] to deeply equal []` |
| `'storage'` added to the absorbed-cost list | `TS1360: Type ... does not satisfy the expected type` |

Recorded as `M96` and `M97` in `mechanisms.md`.

## Done-when

The **cost** half of every done-when line is met and proven. The **runtime** half is not authored here and is not a gap: every row cites `M12` for its mechanics, and those citations land on named tasks — `T-M12-010` (`M12-33`, `M12-37`) owns the per-meter ledger rules and the per-tenant quotas, `T-M12-009` owns storage enforcement on new uploads. Written into `F-core.md` so nothing reads as a gap later.

| Line | This PR | Owner of the rest |
|---|---|---|
| Overage ≥40% above worst-case COGS (`BM-17`) | proven, red-tested | — |
| A manual roof outline bills nothing (`BM-19`) | declared in `NEVER_METERED` | `T-M12-010` |
| Storage enforcement touches new uploads only (`BM-20`) | ceiling has no rate, by type | `T-M12-009` |
| Quotas engage with no tenant surface (`BM-25`) | list declared, no config type exists | `T-M12-010` |
| Check-in/out bills nothing on any tier (`BM-23`, `BM-24`) | declared; a meter here is a compile error | `T-M12-010` |
| Tracked-seat-months are the only people-count (`BM-22`) | the meter and its allowances exist | `T-M12-010` |

## Two side effects

- `metersBelowCogsFloor` is the **first runtime reader of `METERS`**, so `commerce/meters.ts` earns a 100% coverage bar and `M71` is corrected.
- `T-FCORE-016` now builds after this task too — a book stored between the two would have paid a second migration for the COGS column.

author: veritasderman-rgb
body:
Součást hromadné přípravy všech osmi webů na Google Analytics. Tenhle web už GA měl (`G-6GPVS7CRY6`), ale načítal ji rovnou a bez souhlasu — pro české weby to není v souladu s GDPR/ePrivacy. Zbytek webů teď dostává stejný vzor, tak ho dorovnávám i tady.

## Co se mění

- `lib/consent.ts` — klíč souhlasu (`produktivni.cookieConsent.v1`), čtení a zápis volby, promítnutí do gtag.
- `components/CookieConsent.tsx` — lišta se souhlasem s odkazem na ochranu osobních údajů.
- `app/[locale]/layout.tsx` — Consent Mode v2 před gtag.js, lišta pod obsahem, GA nově jen v produkci.
- `lib/i18n.ts` — texty lišty v cs i en.

## Tři věcné změny chování

1. **Souhlas.** Před gtag.js se nastaví Consent Mode v2 s výchozím stavem `denied`. Dokud návštěvník neklikne, GA neukládá žádné cookies (cookieless ping režim). Volba se pamatuje v localStorage a rovnou se promítne do gtag.
2. **GA se nenačítá ve vývoji.** `npm run dev` na localhostu dosud posílal zásahy do produkční property a špinil data. Nově je gtag.js podmíněný `NODE_ENV === "production"`, stejně jako na ostatních webech.
3. **Lišta jen s nastaveným GA ID.** Bez `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` se nevykreslí ani skript, ani lišta.

Vlastní událost `tip_feedback` v `components/Pomohlo.tsx` se nemění — volá `window.gtag?.()`, což bez souhlasu tiše propadne, a po souhlasu funguje dál.

## Poznámka k implementaci

Lišta čte localStorage přes `useSyncExternalStore`, ne přes `useState` + `useEffect`. Serverový snapshot vrací hotovou volbu, takže se lišta při hydrataci nemihne a zároveň to projde pravidlem `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, které tenhle repozitář má zapnuté.

## Ověření

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — bez chyb
- `npm run lint` — bez chyb (zůstává jedno nesouvisející varování v `gadgety/page.tsx`)
- `npm run build` — v SSR HTML je `consent default` před gtag.js a lišta v něm není (žádné bliknutí)

author: zzcoding530
body:
## 🎯 Changes

### 1. 新增 `ai-infra-demos` 目录及核心功能
- 整体合入全新的 `ai-infra-demos` 目录，包含 70 个文件，约 4400 行代码。
- 该目录旨在提供一套面向“大模型 AI Infra 岗位面试考点”的可运行演示代码库。
- 实现 27 个考点的 CPU 可运行数值验证与 AB 对比实验，并配图留档。
- 包含 3 个需 GPU (A800) 的大模型脚本、共享工具库、验收记录与使用文档。

### 2. 详细考点实现与演示
- **Transformer 核心机制 (Part 1)**:
  - `d01_multihead_attention.py`: 从零实现 MHA，验证缩放、多头投影与梯度行为。
  - `d02_layernorm_vs_batchnorm.py`: 对比 LN 与 BN，证明 LN 对离群值鲁棒性。
  - `d03_position_encoding.py`: 对比 sin/cos、RoPE、ALiBi 位置编码，验证 RoPE 平移不变性。
  - `d04_gqa_mqa_attention.py`: 对比 GQA/MQA，量化 KV cache 显存下降。
  - `d05_infini_attention.py`: 数值验证 Infini-Attention 压缩记忆能力。
  - `d06_ssm_recursion.py`: 验证 SSM 递推与卷积等价性。
- **预训练与扩展 (Part 2)**:
  - `d07_three_stage_tiny_gpt.py`: 演示 tiny GPT 预训练/SFT/RL 三阶段。
  - `d08_scaling_law_calculator.py`: 实现 Scaling Law 幂律拟合与 FLOPs/数据规模计算器。
  - `d09_moe_top2.py`: 从零实现 MoE top-2 路由，展示稀疏激活与负载均衡。
  - `d10_catastrophic_forgetting.py`: 演示灾难性遗忘及缓解手段。
- **微调与对齐 (Part 3)**:
  - `d11_lora_from_scratch.py`: 从零实现 LoRA，验证冻结参数梯度与可训练占比。
  - `d12_rlhf_bandit_ppo.py`: 实现 bandit 版 RLHF，对比有无 KL 惩罚的跑偏现象。
  - `d13_dpo_family.py`: 从零实现 DPO/SimPO/ORPO，比较偏好差距与 win-rate。
  - `d14_grpo_rlvr.py`: 实现 GRPO + RLVR 训练，观察 pass@1 提升。
  - `d15_reward_hacking.py`: 演示 Reward Hacking 及 shaping 修复方案。
- **推理优化 (Part 4)**:
  - `d16_kv_cache.py`: 演示 KV Cache 增量解码提速、显存公式与 PagedAttention。
  - `d17_quantization.py`: 扫描量化误差，对比位宽、逐通道 vs 逐张量。
  - `d18_speculative_decoding.py`: 实现 n-gram draft + 拒绝采样投机解码，测量加速比。
  - `d19_sampling_strategies.py`: 对比 greedy/temperature/top-k/top-p/beam 解码策略。
- **分布式训练 (Part 5)**:
  - `d20_dp_tp_pp.py`: 分析 DP/TP/PP 通信量与 PP 调度 bubble。
  - `d21_zero_memory_accounting.py`: 演示 ZeRO/FSDP 各阶段显存记账。
  - `d22_train_memory_calculator.py`: 实现训练显存估算计算器。
  - `d23_ring_allreduce_simulation.py`: CPU 模拟 Ring AllReduce，验证正确性与通信量。
  - `d24_flash_attention_tiled.py`: 数值验证 Flash Attention 分块 softmax 与 HBM 写入量。
- **数据工程 (Part 6)**:
  - `d25_synthetic_data_mix.py`: 演示合成数据配比实验导致模型崩溃。
  - `d26_data_pipeline.py`: 实现数据清洗/去重/配比漏斗 pipeline。
  - `d27_eval_pollution.py`: 演示评测集污染现象。

### 3. 共享工具库与文档
- `common/`: 包含 `corpus.py` (语料生成)、`tinygpt.py` (可配置 tiny GPT 模型)、`toylm.py` (推理缓存小模型)、`train.py` (训练循环封装)、`viz.py` (图表保存工具)。
- `README.md`: 演示库总览，包含设计原则、运行环境、考点→文件索引与目录结构说明。
- `RUNBOOK.md`: 验收记录与复现指南，记录 CPU demo 实测命令/结果及 GPU 待测回填清单。

### 4. GPU 实验与输出
- `gpu/`: 包含 `g01_qlora_7b_qkv_vs_ffn.py` (7B QLoRA 实验)、`g02_grpo_7b_rlvr.py` (7B GRPO+RLVR 数学推理训练)、`g03_infer_13b_4bit_and_awq_7b.py` (13B nf4 量化推理与 7B AWQ 对比)。
- `outputs/`: 包含 27+ 张各 demo 运行产出的对比结果图与 tiny GPT 缓存文件。

## 💡 Technical Highlights

- **从零实现**: 大部分考点通过 `numpy` 或 `tiny torch` 从零实现，确保对底层原理的深刻理解和数值验证。
- **可复现性**: 采用固定随机种子、确定性语料生成等方式，确保所有实验结果可复现。
- **可视化验证**: 结合 `common/viz.py` 工具，将实验结果以图表形式输出，直观展示概念与效果。
- **模块化设计**: 将通用功能封装在 `common` 目录下，提高代码复用性与可维护性。
- **面试导向**: 紧密围绕 AI Infra 岗位面试考点，将理论知识转化为可讲述、可演示的代码与图表素材。
- **GPU 实验**: 提供实际 GPU (A800) 上的大模型实验脚本，覆盖 QLoRA、GRPO、量化推理等前沿技术。
- **详尽文档**: 提供 `README.md` 和 `RUNBOOK.md`，详细说明项目结构、运行环境、复现步骤和预期结果，降低上手门槛。

author: amrtawfik160
body:
Analysis of two stranded runs, and the skill changes each gap demands. Both runs executed the skill correctly and wrote complete ledgers — so every gap below is the skill's fault, not the run's.

| Run | Progress | Ended as |
|---|---|---|
| `thr_crgqjihta3` | 8 of 19 tickets, **52 human turns** | `state: running`, no pause, nothing queued |
| `thr_qanmy8ufx3` | 1 of 16 tickets | paused on a check that also fails on `main`, pause had no `class` |

## 1. The run waited for a human between every unit of work

Both ended `turn/completed` cleanly with context to spare — 496K/1M and 181K/258K. Nothing was broken. The skill simply never said "keep going", and only scheduled a self-resume for *transient pauses*.

```diff
 end of turn
-  report progress
-  wait for a human to say "continue"        # 52 times
+  if state is finished/landed/decision-paused
+    delete the queued continuation
+  else
+    it is already queued (--mode queue), and fires when this turn ends
```

Because a queued continuation is a loop, it gets its own caps: run-level worker and continuation budgets, plus a `no_progress` pause after two continuations that record no ledger transition.

**Long runs also outgrow one thread.** The orchestrator now reads its own context from `thread/contextWindowUsage/updated` and relays past 70% to a fresh successor, handing over the ledger and nothing else. Never a fork — a fork inherits the context that ran out.

## 2. A red target branch stranded the entire stack

This is why nothing could merge:

```text
main                    FAIL "Typecheck, lint, tests"
                        FAIL "Runtime adapter contract"
   └── PR 1151          FAIL ×2   (same two)
   └── PR 1168…1174     FAIL ×2   (same two, every one)
```

Seven PRs, seven branches, identical inherited failures. `land-stack` requires "no failing check", so the stack could never land. Both orchestrators independently invented a workaround — `ci_baseline_red`, `checks: fail_preexisting` — which is the strongest possible signal the concept belongs in the skill.

The run now measures `ci_baseline` before the first ticket:

| Outcome | `pr.checks` | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Every failure is in `ci_baseline` | `baseline_fail` | Mark ready, report inherited failures |
| Any failure outside it | `fail` | Pause — this one is the ticket's |

`land-stack` applies the same rule at the merge gate.

## 3. Checks were recorded once and never revisited

Seven PRs sat at `checks: pending` while GitHub had final results. The turn moved on and nothing brought it back. `gh pr checks --watch` isn't the answer either — it spends the turn that should implement the next ticket. Checks are now **swept at the start of every turn**, and watching is rejected in `pr-stack.md`.

## 4. An unwritten review gate passed silently

All seven tickets reached `in_review` with `loop.gate.verdict: null`. The skill said "require `LOOP_GATE.verdict: PASS`" but nothing forced the value into the ledger, so the gate was satisfied implicitly by `best_burden: 0`.

The PR step now reads the recorded verdict. An absent one blocks the PR: neither a finished loop nor a zero burden says *which axes ran*.

## 5. One green run cannot tell a passing test from a flaky one

Ticket #1108 shipped a timing bug that passed validation once, then needed a force-push and a rebase of #1109 to repair. The run said so itself:

> A single green run doesn't distinguish 100% from 80%, and that's exactly the gap this slipped through.

A diff touching time, clocks, concurrency, ordering, or randomness now reruns its suite.

## 6. Smaller

- A pause without `class` reaches nobody and clears itself never. The record's exact keys are now in the protocol, and an unclassified pause is a `decision` pause.
- Run B recorded `notify.command: "bb notify send"` for a **disabled** plugin, so every notification silently dropped. A command is now recorded only after it is probed.

## Is serial still right?

Yes, and the runs are the evidence. The orchestrator verifies every worker claim in the worktree and reruns validation itself, so **its own context is the bottleneck, not wall-clock** — 496K tokens for eight tickets. Running them concurrently spends the same context sooner and makes the ledger harder to keep consistent. Throughput comes from turn continuation and the relay, not from more workers at once. Read-only workers remain the documented exception.

Isolation and review depth held up well under load: 48 workers, one job each, one worktree per ticket, and the loop did real work (#1105 needed fix → closure → fix 2 → closure 2). The gaps were all in *continuity* and *gate recording*, not in isolation.

## Tests

13 scripts pass. `tests/run-continuity.sh` is new and pins each gap to the run that found it, so a future edit cannot quietly reopen one.

Worker prompts moved to `references/worker-prompts.md` to stay inside the 130-line skill budget — the pressure valve that budget exists for.

author: apsantiso
body:
We have a throughput of 3k/minute on the EP that uses this query, but the indexes we have currently are not optimized for it.

This PR creates a new index that covers both the uniqueness guarantee index and the folder_uuid + user_id lookup used for navigation between files in a folder. It's built with the collation we use for correct ordering (taking into account numeric values), so all queries using that collation get faster too.

### Prod
Folder with ~8.5k files, order performed in memory, this is an example of how bad the query perfoms on prod:

author: daniborisov
body:
## Summary

Implements the DAN-47 daily "new episode airing" poll job: per-item schedule diffing with per-user fan-out via DAN-45's `deliverPush`.

## Changes

- New `AiringState` entity (`tmdbId` + `mediaType` unique; last season/episode/air-date) + sqlite/postgres `1782000000006` migrations (sqlite `up` verified against real SQLite) + registered in `testEntities`.
- New `server/lib/notifications/airingPush.ts` (`runAiringCheck`, re-entry guard + cancel):
  - Groups `tv`/`anime` rows with `notifyOn` `episode_airing`/`both` per item — one metadata lookup per show no matter how many users track it.
  - TV: TMDB `last_episode_to_air`; notify only when strictly newer **and** aired (future-dated episodes stay pending until air date passes; missing air-date counts as aired).
  - Anime: crosswalk TMDB→AniList + `getAiringSchedule`; a bumped next-episode means the stored one aired.
  - First sight of any item seeds the baseline **silently** — never a mass notify. Per-item failures log and continue. State advances only on notify (or silent schedule corrections for anime).
  - Fan-out mirrors DAN-46 (own subs only, dead-row deletion, VAPID only on the real path, injectable `send`/fetchers). Payload `{notificationType: 'EPISODE_AIRING', subject, message, actionUrl: '/tv/{id}'}` renders via the existing generic SW handler.
  - `ensureVapid()` extracted from `availabilityPush.ts` and shared (no behavior change; DAN-46 tests re-pass).
- Scheduler: new `airing-push-sync` JobId, default daily `0 0 6 * * *`, registered in `startJobs` with running/cancel.

## Tests

- `airingPush.test.ts` (6 tests, all acceptance cases): two users on one item each get independent pushes; no-change → silent; first run seeds silently; `none` + rowless users excluded; anime bump via real crosswalk announces the aired episode; future episode held.
- 6/6 new; DAN-46 6/6 re-pass; server `tsc` clean; ESLint clean.

author: urlmonitor
body:
## Summary

Implements `BO-2900d-1` and `BO-2900d-2`. Built by a fast lane running **concurrently with a second one**, as half of the two-lane experiment recorded against `KI-BO-20260901-1450` (#727).

**`BO-2900d-1` — the reachability refusal.** For an otherwise-eligible criterion, resolve the modules its covers-tagged tests import and refuse when a resolved unit defines no entry point of its own **and** nothing outside the test tree imports it. A unit only its own test can reach is not shipped code. A recorded, exact-match, **reasoned** exemption releases the refusal and is attached to the verdict.

**`BO-2900d-2` — the exemptions become visible.** Every exemption in force is listed, with its reason, on **every** run regardless of outcome. `main()` was restructured so the previous early `return 0` on a clean run no longer skips the report — that early return was precisely the defect the criterion describes.

New shared seam `_reachability_inventory.py` (`load_exemptions`, `exemptions_in_force`, `is_exempt` — exact match, no globs; corrupt registry raises, missing one is zero exemptions), plus the registry file and a write-if-absent scaffold entry so a fresh consumer install gets a valid empty one.

## The halt, and why it was the test rather than either spec

The lane stopped at its green gate on one failing test:

```python
assert "module_a" not in combined.replace("recorded exemption for module_a only", "")
```

…whose own failure message read *"the exempted unit (module_a) must not itself be reported as a **finding**"*. The intent was right; the implementation checked the **entire** output. `BO-2900d-2` — landing in the same change — *requires* printing every exemption's item, and that item is `src/module_a/helpers/no_entry_unit.py`. The `.replace()` stripped the reason but not the item.

**So the two criteria looked irreconcilable and were not.** `BO-2900d-1`'s own text already distinguishes the exempted unit being *"not reported"* as a finding from the exemption *"appearing in the guard's output as an accepted exemption"*. Both clauses hold at once; only the assertion conflated them. **No AC amendment was warranted and none was made.**

The assertion now matches the guard's real finding shape — `[check-done-proof] <ac_id>: <reason>` — which structurally cannot match inventory lines, since those read `[check-done-proof] exemption in force: …` (space, not colon, after the leading word). No second `.replace()` was added; chained substring carving is how the defect arose.

**Mutation-tested in both directions**, because a narrowed assertion never shown able to fail is worth nothing. A fake finding line naming `module_a` was injected into the guard and the test went red; the implementation was then restored and confirmed byte-identical against its template (`diff` exit 0, zero occurrences of the mutation text remain).

## Test plan

- **8 tests green** under `AC_ENFORCE_STRICT=1` across the three affected files — verified independently, not taken from the agent's report.
- Wider suite the implementation touched: **712 passed, 3 skipped**, no regressions.
- Both criteria marked done through **`mark_ac_done.py`'s own coverage gate**, not by assertion.
- `BO-2900d-3`, `-4`, `-5` arrived as connected-set members, were not built, remain `todo`.
- `docs/agents/cards/python-coder.card.md` is build output, not staged. `scripts/commit_guardian/check_done_proof.py` is a gitignored deployed copy, verified byte-identical to its template.
- `check-build-drift`/`check-output-drift` skipped: three `commit_guardian` templates that landed on main today are absent from the shared install tree, none of them in this change.

author: srimon12
body:
## Summary

Closes the remaining pre-release audit findings for 0.3.2 across `qql-core`, `qql-plan`, `qql-runtime`, and all four host SDKs.

## What was done

### qql-core — placeholder formatting & bind gates
- `format_stmt` / `Stmt.toString()` render positional parameters as a bare `?` everywhere (page `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, formula `TARGET`, `TEXT`, `HYBRID TEXT`, `CROSS RERANK TEXT`). The stored `?N` index used to leak into output like `LIMIT ?1`, which did not re-parse (`QQL-PARSE-TRAILING`) and broke `parse(format(x)) == x`.
- `SCROLL` renders its LIMIT placeholder instead of `LIMIT None`; `FACET` keeps its LIMIT placeholder instead of silently dropping the clause.
- The AST bind path now rejects non-finite vector elements (`QQL-VALIDATION-VECTOR`, same message as the textual parse path) — an f64 source beyond `f32::MAX` (JSON `1e39`) previously bound a silent `inf` vector to the wire.
- Bound `LIMIT 0` is rejected across `QUERY` / `SCROLL` / `FACET` (`QQL-BIND-INVALID-INTEGER`), matching the literal `LIMIT 0` parse error. Bound `OFFSET 0` remains valid.
- New round-trip pins: every parameter-placeholder position must re-parse after formatting.

### qql-plan
- The `USING bm25` → `Qdrant/bm25` default lives in a single `default_model_for_using` helper instead of three hard-coded literals across the lowering paths.

### qql-runtime
- Under `on_error = "continue"`, an unbound-placeholder statement now collects a per-statement `BIND` failure row (like PREPARE/PLAN defects) instead of aborting the script and discarding every already-collected result.
- gRPC failures carry the correlation id: the interceptor records each outgoing RPC's `x-request-id` and `grpc_error` attaches it to the message and `.fields["request_id"]`, mirroring the REST echo. Best-effort under concurrent RPCs on one client; exact for the executor's sequential awaits.

### Node SDKs (`nqql`, `nqql-edge` via `nqql-common`)
- `execute([])` fails closed with `QQL-VALIDATION-EMPTY-SCRIPT` — previously a silently-empty `ok: true` report while Python raised.
- `params: null` means "no params" everywhere — previously raised `QQL-BIND-INVALID-PARAMS` on `nqql`.
- Shared `run_then_close` guard: one-shot `execute()` / `executeStmt()` close the temporary executor on the error path (no connection leak; for nqql-edge, on-disk shards and the loaded model), and a close failure after a successful dispatch is surfaced instead of masking the report.
- `nqql-edge`'s free `bind` accepts `truncate_vectors` (snake_case alias parity with `nqql`).
- `groups()` declared in both `index.d.ts`.

### Python SDKs (`pyqql`, `pyqql-edge`)
- `execute_async_hits` raises typed `QqlError` subclasses (`.code` / `.kind` / `.span` / `.fields`) — previously a plain `RuntimeError`, so `except QqlTransportError` silently missed.
- `pyqql-edge`'s `__init__.pyi` regenerated against the real 0.3.2 surface (missing `bind`, `compile_route(params)`, `explain`, `execute_hits`, `params` args; wrong `Client.execute` return types).
- `pyqql`'s `.pyi` gains `ScoredPoint.vector` / `.shard_key`.
- `report.hits()` / `.points()` return `[]` for FACET results — facet entries (`{value, count}`) previously surfaced as pseudo-`ScoredPoint`s with `id=None, score=0`. Shared copy kept byte-identical.

### qql-wasm
- `compile(query, params?)` on the module and `Client.compile(query, params?)` — parity with the Python and Node `compile(params=…)` surface.
- Empty-array `executeStmt` fails closed like the executor.

### Repo
- `language/v1/spec/versioning.md` 1.7 conformance counts corrected to **276 statements / 62 invalid cases** (the actual corpus; the row claimed 278/59).
- VS Code extension manifest bumped to **0.3.2** (it ships the 1.7 parser); `editors.mdoc` parser reference corrected. `scripts/check_release.py check` is now warning-free.
- README install snippets are copy-paste runnable; `pyqql` / `nqql` README export tables list `execute_hits` and the typed report accessors; SDK references document `report.groups()`.
- New scheduled `security` workflow: weekly `cargo audit`, CodeQL (Rust), `npm audit` for both Node SDKs, `pnpm audit` for the website.

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` ✔ · `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✔ · `cargo fmt --check` ✔
- `cargo test`: qql-core 233 ✔ · qql-plan 126 ✔ · qql-embed 49 ✔ · qql 96 ✔
- Conformance: 40 valid / 276 statements / 62 invalid / 40 snapshots / 40 formats ✔
- `qql` compiles with `--no-default-features --features grpc` and `--features rest` ✔
- Python suite 164 ✔ · Node suite 116 ✔ · shared-copy diffs (`dx-common.js`, `test_dx.js`, `_dx_report.py`) clean ✔
- Live probes: empty-array error, `params: null` executes, `QQL-BIND-ALREADY-BOUND`, `LIMIT ?` toString, SCROLL fmt ✔

author: herrfrei
body:
**Problem:**
Currently, `tc-config` reads the RTC on boot, but `rc.shutdown` never writes the system time back to the RTC on shutdown. As a result, any time drift or NTP-based correction made during the session is lost, and the hardware clock gradually becomes stale across reboots.

**Fix:**
Added a step in `etc/init.d/rc.shutdown` that writes the current system time back to the RTC via `hwclock -w`, mirroring the boot-time logic in `tc-config`:

- Respects the `nortc` boot code — RTC write is skipped entirely if RTC handling was disabled at boot.
- Respects the `noutc` boot code — uses `hwclock -l -w` (local time) if set, otherwise `hwclock -u -w` (UTC), consistent with how the clock was read at boot.

author: antoniosaaranen
body:
## Summary

- Authenticates `promote_latest()`'s `npm dist-tag add … latest` call, which npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC) never covers — OIDC authorizes `npm publish` only. Production run 34114664962 published five `alpha` prereleases correctly and then failed every `latest` move with `E401`, for all five packages, deterministically (not a flake — it will repeat on every future prerelease publish until authenticated).
- The move is applied via its own credential (`secrets.NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN`), scoped to the single `npm dist-tag add` invocation through a throwaway `--userconfig` file created and deleted around that one call. It is never written to the job's ambient `~/.npmrc`, so it cannot substitute for OIDC on the `npm publish` calls — those keep authenticating exactly as before. Without the token, `promote_latest()` now fails closed with a named `GUARD:` line instead of a bare `E401`.
- The publish loop's "already on npm" branch now also calls `promote_latest()` instead of skipping outright, so **a re-run heals a stale `latest` idempotently**: `npm publish` rejects a duplicate version, so nothing already registered can be re-published, and a healthy re-run's only new work per package is one `npm view` and, where needed, one `npm dist-tag add`.
- The four-guard channel wall (#2421 / #2536 / #2580) is unchanged in shape: a `0.0.0-dev.*` snapshot is refused by `promote_latest()`'s existing version-shape check **before** the new token check is ever reached, so the new guard only adds a requirement on the path the old guards already allow — it cannot loosen anything.

## Why the issue stays open

**Refs #2647**, not `Closes` — this PR cannot close the issue by itself. `secrets.NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN` does not exist yet; provisioning it is an operator step (checklist below). Until it is set, `promote_latest()` fails closed with a named `GUARD:` — a clear, diagnosable refusal, not the opaque `E401` the incident produced, but still a refusal. `scripts/ci/operator-verify-close-guard.mjs` enforces the bare `Refs #2647` on the title, this body, and every commit message.

## Operator checklist (not performed by this PR)

- [ ] Provision a **granular npm automation token** scoped to `dist-tag` operations only (must NOT be able to publish) for the `@haven_ai` packages, and store it as the repository secret `NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN`.
- [ ] After the secret is set, re-run (or `workflow_dispatch` with `channel=prod` on `main`) the **Publish packages** workflow to heal the `latest` tag left stale by run 34114664962 for `sdk`, `signer`, `mcp`, `connect`, `cli` — no version needs to change; the recovery path added here does this without re-publishing.
- [ ] Verify on the registry afterward (`npm view @haven_ai/<pkg> dist-tags`) that `latest` matches the currently-published `alpha` version for all five packages.

Nothing in this diff states or implies the secret has been set — every reference is by name only (`secrets.NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN`).

## Changed Surfaces

- [x] Backend / API — n/a, this is CI/release tooling, not backend code
- [ ] Frontend UI
- [ ] SDK
- [ ] MCP / hosted MCP / signer
- [x] Money movement, agent authority, or payment execution — money-path **control surface only** (`.github/workflows/publish.yml` is a `controlGlob`); no runtime payment/delegation code touched. See the CASP shard.
- [ ] Generated artifacts, examples, credential handoffs, or demo scripts

## Workflow Used

- Captain: Antonio's session (AntonioSaaranen), incident triage `gh issue view 2647` + skill routing
- Agents used: none — direct implementation per the issue's explicit scope
- Agents skipped, with reason: `haven-reviewer` intentionally **not** run by this session per the captain's explicit instruction — the captain runs the independent review pass separately.
- Worker ownership boundaries: `.github/workflows/publish.yml` and its tests/docs only. Did **not** touch `packages/backend/src/config.ts`, `packages/backend/src/infra/__tests__/`, `packages/backend/src/db/migrations/`, `docs/contributing/testing-strategy.md`, `docs/operations/promoting-dev-to-main.md`, `docs/operations/package-dev-channel.md`, or `docs/operations/mcp-runtime-compatibility.md` (three sibling PRs / explicit exclusions).

## Local Checks

- [x] `git diff --check` — clean
- [x] `node --test scripts/release-bump.test.mjs` — 69 passed / 0 failed (61 pre-existing + 8 new for #2647)
- [x] `node --test scripts/ci/*.test.mjs` — 498 passed / 0 failed (the `Repo CI config checks` suite)
- [x] `node --test scripts/ci/money-path.test.mjs` — 11 passed / 0 failed
- [x] `node --test scripts/ci/operator-verify-close-guard.test.mjs` — 39 passed / 0 failed
- [x] `node --test scripts/docs/*.test.mjs` — 175 passed / 0 failed
- [x] `npm run docs:check` — clean (one pre-existing advisory chain-size warning on an untouched doc)
- [ ] `npm run docs:coupling` (strict) — **BLOCKED, deliberately not fixed here**: see below

### `docs:coupling` — known, deliberate gap

Three contract docs `cover` `.github/workflows/publish.yml`. One — `docs/contributing/branch-and-release-flow.md` — is re-verified in this PR (no claim it makes about the workflow moved: the tag-derivation and latest-move *behavior* is unchanged, only which credential authorizes the move and whether a re-run retries it). The other two are **out of this PR's file ownership** per explicit instruction and are left untouched:

- `docs/operations/mcp-runtime-compatibility.md` — explicitly excluded (sibling in-flight work).
- `docs/operations/package-dev-channel.md` — explicitly named as a contract doc I must **not** edit if the gate blocks on it; instructed to stop and report instead.

So `npm run docs:coupling --strict` still exits non-zero, naming those two. This is expected and reported here rather than worked around — captain/owner: please reconcile with whoever owns those docs (re-verify or fold in) before merge, or explicitly waive the gate for this PR.

## Mutation Proof (guards this PR relies on)

Three independent mutations against the real `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, each restored via `cp` and verified byte-identical with `cmp` before the next mutation:

1. Removed the `NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN` presence check inside `promote_latest()` → 2 tests red (`#2647: an absent token fails closed…`, `#2647: an already-published package with NO token…`).
2. Removed the `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=` scoping from the `npm dist-tag add` call → 1 test red (`#2647: the token is scoped to the ONE dist-tag call, never to npm publish`).
3. Reverted the "already on npm" branch to its pre-#2647 skip-only behavior → 3 tests red (`RECOVERY IS IDEMPOTENT`, the recovery-failure reporting test, and the no-token-plus-already-published composition).

All three restored and the full 69-test suite re-verified green before opening this PR.

## Intentionally Left Out

- Provisioning `secrets.NPM_LATEST_TAG_TOKEN` (operator step above).
- Actually re-running the workflow to heal the stale `latest` for the five packages stranded by run 34114664962 (needs the secret first).
- Re-verifying or editing `docs/operations/mcp-runtime-compatibility.md` / `docs/operations/package-dev-channel.md` (out of ownership scope — see `docs:coupling` section above).
- Widening scope to a "policy reversal that stops moving `latest` for prereleases" — the issue's diagnosis comment named this as an alternative; not pursued, since the owner decision behind #2536 ("we should not have users run old versions") is still standing and nothing in #2647 revisits it.

## Generated Artifacts And Handoffs

- [x] No generated artifacts or handoffs changed

## CASP / MiCA Guardrail Check

- [x] Applicable and reviewed against `docs/regulatory/casp-risk-guardrails.md`
- Notes: shard at `docs/regulatory/casp-changelog/2026-09-07-2647.md`. Money-path classification: **control surface only** (`.github/workflows/publish.yml` is a `controlGlob`), re-derived with `scripts/ci/money-path-classify.mjs origin/dev` — 0 runtime-glob + 1 control-glob =

author: aldenks
body:
## Summary

Change the GFS pgrb2b representative resume probe from geopotential height on the +0.5 PVU surface to pressure-level geopotential height at 125 hPa.

This is config-only. It does not change which refs `file_refs` builds, chunk contents, or source byte ranges. It changes only the cell used by `filter_already_present` and the probe-coverage assertion.

## Root cause and measured selection

The public upstream object at init 2024-10-20 18:00 UTC, lead 249 hours is a consistently truncated publication, not a systematic lead or era omission:

- Data object: 71,229,440 bytes, versus 238,663,733 at f246 and 238,092,315 at f252.
- Index: 112 lines, versus 349 at normal nonzero leads. It ends at HGT 375 hPa.
- A range read from the final indexed offset finds one complete HGT 375 hPa message of 701,575 bytes, followed by only 386,509 of the next TMP 375 hPa message, whose declared length is 737,601 bytes. No complete unindexed tail messages exist.

A sweep covered 5,643 real pgrb2b indexes: all 209 scheduled leads, f000 through f120 hourly and f123 through f384 three-hourly, across 27 sampled cycles in every year from 2021 through 2026, including the incident cycle. The former +0.5 PVU HGT probe was present in 5,642/5,643 and absent only in the truncated f249 index. The replacement HGT 125 hPa cell was present in 5,643/5,643.

HGT 125 hPa is line 42/349, 12.0% through a normal index. The old probe is normally line 317/349, 90.8% through it. The earlier probe therefore survives truncations that remove most of the file rather than only truncations after roughly 91%.

## Result for the truncated forecast position

With this probe, the file is accepted and contributes exactly the refs represented by its short index. `file_refs` builds 77 pgrb2b-owned refs instead of the normal 308; 231 chunks remain absent. The difference from the 237 absent source messages is six trailing messages duplicated from pgrb2 and intentionally owned by that product.

All 80 variables supplied by pgrb2b are affected, out of 274 catalog variables:

- All 63 root variables are absent: 36 PV-surface fields across six signed PV levels, 25 fields across the five 60-30 through 180-150 hPa layers, and both UV-B flux fields.
- The three height-above-mean-sea-level variables have no pgrb2b refs at 305, 457, 610, 914, or 4572 m.
- All 14 pressure-level variables are partial. Geopotential height is absent at the ten pgrb2b levels 425 through 875 hPa; the other 13 variables are absent at the eleven pgrb2b levels 375 through 875 hPa.

The final indexed HGT 375 hPa ref spans the partial TMP fragment because the last index range ends at the object size. Gribberish decodes that oversized ref identically to the exact 701,575-byte HGT message, so HGT 375 hPa remains readable. The missing cells are an honest representation of data that the upstream archive did not publish completely.

The absence is **unflagged**: no validator, log line, or alert reports the 231 absent chunks. A reader learns about them only from the dataset validation report's external **Review notes — noaa-gfs-forecast-virtual**, under **Unavailable data**. That note, maintained outside this code diff, discloses:

> The 80 variables carried by the secondary source product are absent at init time 2024-10-20 18:00, lead time 249 hours. NOAA published that source file at 30% of its normal size, so 231 of its 308 chunks are missing: every single-level and layer field it supplies, its height-above-mean-sea-level levels, and its pressure levels from 375 hPa (425 hPa for geopotential height) through 875 hPa. The truncation is in the published data itself rather than in its byte index, so backfill is not possible from the upstream archive. No other instance appeared in a sweep of 5,643 source indexes spanning 2021 to 2026.

The position is not sealed, but it is **no longer self-healing**. [#952](https://github.com/dynamical-org/reformatters/pull/952) made `process_virtual_refs` bypass `filter_already_present` under `overwrite_chunks`, so a republished complete object remains recoverable through a deliberate overwrite-chunks run aimed at this position. An ordinary resume will see the representative chunk and never revisit it automatically.

## Incident-path effect and detection gap

On the incident path this change is purely assertion suppression. The failed backfill ran with `overwrite_chunks`, so `filter_already_present` was never in play and the resume-probe half of the change did nothing there. Moving the probe only lets `_assert_probe_chunk_covered` accept the partial ref set, instead of killing one worker before it commits any of its 8,360 files for 20 init times and permanently blocking finalization of the 391-pod run.

Probe depth was never a truncation detector: a truncation at 95% would also have passed the old probe at 90.8%. This change widens an existing silence rather than creating one.

The actual detection gap is at neither probe level. Nothing checks source-object size or index line count against expectation during ingest, and the manifest scan is file-granularity, so a partially ingested file is indistinguishable from a complete one. Detecting and flagging partial source ingestion is a follow-up; this PR deliberately does not change assertion behavior or add that ingest/validation mechanism.

## Related probe exposure, not changed here

- GFS analysis shares the instant pgrb2b probe, so this shared fix also moves that probe to line 42. Its windowed-only pgrb2b coord was generated from the real template and contains exactly two data variables: DUVB at line 272/349 (77.9%) and CDUVB at line 273/349 (78.2%). Both were present in 162/162 real indexes across every analysis lead f001-f006, 27 cycles, and every archive year from 2021 through 2026. DUVB is already the earliest covered probe, so no config-only move exists and this path remains exposed by design rather than oversight. The follow-up remedy is to relax the data-cell coupling with an explicit per-source-file ingestion marker written atomically with the refs and used for resume.
- HRRR sampled in 2018 and 2024: the surface instant probe is line 1, 0.6-0.7%; the analysis surface-windowed CRAIN probe is 54.7-58.8%; the forecast pressure probe is 76.3-77.4%; the analysis pressure probe is 75.3-76.4%; and the native-level probe is 1.2-1.3%.
- GEFS sampled in 2021 and 2024: the instant GUST probe is 4.5-7.7%; the analysis windowed TMAX probe is 32.4-34.2%. GEFS also asserts that every coord variable matched a ref, so a truncation dropping any catalog variable fails independently of representative probe depth.

No HRRR or GEFS behavior is changed.

## Validation

- `uv run ruff format`
- `uv run ruff check --fix`
- `uv run ty check --output-format concise`
- `uv run pytest -m "not slow" -n 4`: 2,624 passed
- Every GFS module containing slow tests, one `.py` path per invocation: 185 passed across nine modules
- Focused forecast and analysis representative-probe tests: 2 passed



## Interaction with the assert-classification work

Moving the probe to 12% of the index means a truncated file no longer trips anything. The
incident file passes this probe, passes the last-offset header check, and is accepted with
77 of its 308 refs: no rejection, no ERROR, no skipped-file count, and because those partial
refs land in the manifest the position is not re-offered on a later run. Recovery needs a
deliberate `overwrite-chunks` run aimed at it.

So until an ingest-time check on object size and index line count exists, this class of
source damage is accepted silently and no detector fires. That check is being raised as its
own PR, ahead of #1029, because #1029 cannot supply it: probe absence is not the signal, and
after this change it is not a truncation signal at all.

The bound on that silence is measured rather than assumed: one such file in 2,925,247
ingested in a single full backfill, and none in a sweep of 5,643 source indexes spanning
2021 to 2026.

author: broody
body:
`build-projects.mjs` describes assessments as cached on `head_sha`, but its initializer falls back unconditionally to `prev.assessment`. Once a verdict has `facts_v2`, it therefore suppresses reassessment even after the repository head changes. Current contracts, transaction verification, tooling, and README-derived descriptions can be published alongside an older verdict.

For example, [the generated Stake Wars entry at this PR's base](https://github.com/starkience/strk20-hackathon/blob/9627e4f/projects.json) has one mainnet contract, three verified pool transactions, and Cairo evidence, while its assessment says there are no deployed contracts or complex Cairo implementations.

Reuse the cached verdict at initialization only when the repository head matches and the verdict has `facts_v2`; otherwise start with `null`. This lets the existing assessment block use the current evidence when judging is enabled. Add behavioral regression coverage for changed heads, same-head cache hits, older rubric verdicts, and missing assessments, using the source-extraction pattern already used by the pagination tests.

Operational scope: `STAR_ENABLED` is currently `false`, so merging this does not itself enable model judging. The existing sticky-star presentation policy is outside this fix. This prevents the unconditional reuse on subsequent head changes; it does not retroactively identify stale verdicts already stored under a newer `head_sha`. Maintainers would need an explicit refresh for those existing entries. Merging the indexer change triggers the existing `Index projects` workflow.

Validation:
- The changed-head and older-rubric regression tests fail against the original initializer.
- `node --test`: all 9 tests pass after the fix.
- `node --check scripts/build-projects.mjs` and `git diff --check` pass.

author: benzn-tech
body:
Three defects, all surfaced by the move to `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` on OpenRouter, all silent before it. Each was found on TEST or prod, not read off the code.

### 1. A report named the wrong model

`_report_metadata.model` and the debug record read `CLAUDE_MODEL`, which is set on every function regardless of provider. A TEST report whose own log line says `qwen call: model=meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` was stamped `claude-sonnet-4-6`. That label is what a reader uses to decide which model produced a bad report, so it sends them at the wrong model.

`llm_utils.active_model()` already answers this question — and returns `None` rather than guessing for a provider it does not know. It was added when this same bug was found on the Ask path; the sweep stopped there, leaving six sites in report-generator and two in meeting-minutes.

### 2. The schema example leaked into the customer's report

`MEETING_MINUTES_SCHEMA` showed the shape as `"Bullet 1: Meeting purpose and context"`. muse-spark copied the prefix:

> "Bullet 1: Morning subcontractor coordination meeting on 2026-09-02 to review safety, programme, design, QA …"

— rendered verbatim as an `<li>` in the customer's report. Placeholders are now angle brackets, which cannot be mistaken for text worth keeping.

### 3. `executive_summary` has been an array for six months; four consumers still read a string

`config/prompt_templates.json` made it an array at v3.0 (2026-03-18). The in-code fallback schema still emits a string, so **both shapes are live** — a deploy without the S3 config produces the string, which is exactly the state TEST was in until today.

The Word export did `doc.add_paragraph(list)`. That does not raise: python-docx concatenates with no separator, so five bullets shipped as `"Documented Level 2 progress with site photosDocumented Level 3 progress…"`. The weekly and monthly prompt builders interpolated the Python `repr` of a list into the prompt.

`summary_text()` normalises both shapes for prose. The Word export now renders bullets as `List Bullet` paragraphs — the rendering meeting-minutes already used.

### Tests

Eleven, and each was watched fail first. The two `save_debug_record` tests and the Word-export test **drive** the code and read what it wrote; the Word-export one was re-checked by mutating the branch back and confirming it goes red. One test scans source text rather than behaviour — it pins that the `CLAUDE_MODEL` sweep reached the six sites that sit inside functions needing S3, a corpus and a model, and it says so in its own docstring. That is wiring, not behaviour, and it is there because the last time this bug was fixed it was fixed in one file and left standing in two.

### Not in this change

`config/prompt_templates.json` and `config/prompt_templates_meeting.json` were missing from the TEST bucket entirely, so TEST had never exercised the prompts prod runs. Copied to `s3://fieldsight-data-test-509194952652/config/` and verified: TEST report `executive_summary` went from string to array, matching prod. `custom_vocabulary_construction_nz.txt` is still prod-only — copying it changes TEST transcription, so it is left for a moment when no one is measuring TEST.

author: quazardous
body:
Installing the published release the way the README tells a stranger to,
on a machine nobody had tried it on. Two things came out of it.

## `install.ps1` has never verified a download

It fetches `SHA256SUMS`, looks for the line naming the file it just
pulled, finds nothing, and prints:

```
no sum published for this file — NOT verified.
```

The sum **was** published. GitHub serves a release asset as
`application/octet-stream`, so PowerShell hands `Content` back as a
`Byte[]` rather than a string — and splitting that into lines splits the
**bytes**:

```
($sums.Content -split "`n" | Select-Object -First 3) -join ' | '
49 | 101 | 50
```

Those are the decimal codes of `1e2`, the first three characters of the
file. No line ever matched a filename, so `$want` was always empty, so
every Windows install this script has ever done went unverified — and
said so in words that read like the release's omission rather than the
installer's bug.

Decoding the bytes first finds the line, and the sum it holds matches the
zip. Verified against the live v0.5.12 assets.

## Smart App Control, which the README had backwards

The README said downloading a published release avoids it and building
does not. Measured on Windows 11 with it on:

- `install.ps1` fetched the v0.5.12 zip;
- its SHA-256 matched what that release published, byte for byte;
- the binary inside still would not start — `os error 4551`, the same
  refusal a freshly built one gets, from PowerShell and from bash alike.

It blocks unsigned executables **whatever their origin**. There is no
per-file exception to grant: the policy is Microsoft's own, and the only
control offered is on / evaluation / off. Nothing in this repo makes that
binary run on such a machine except signing it — which is a decision with
a price tag and not this PR's business.

What this PR does do is stop the script ending in a stack trace when it
happens. Asking the binary its version was the last line, and PowerShell
throws about `StandardOutputEncoding` — a message naming nothing, printed
directly under a line saying the install worked. It did work. It now says
what is actually in the way.

## Version

`### Fixed` alone, so PATCH: `0.5.13`, with `Cargo.toml` and the lockfile
following the changelog as `the_version_matches_the_changelog` requires.
The date follows the convention `c8d8145` set — corrected to the day it
ships, if that is not today.

## Summary

A `dev-env` profile started every service with its own ports except the `outbox-worker`, which was handed no `PUBLIRA_PLATFORM_APP_URL`. `platformConsoleURL` in `server/internal/outbox/platform_auth.go` then fell back to `defaultPlatformAppURL`, `http://platform.localhost:3080`, so the platform console links in a profile's auth mail pointed at the shared development stack rather than at the profile that produced them. The token in such a mail is valid, so the link is not rejected — it is consumed against whichever console answers on `3080`. The profile already stores the correct value and already passes it to `platform-api-server`; this passes it to the worker as well, the way `e2e/scripts/outbox-worker.sh` already does.

`task dev-env:test` passes. It covers profile derivation in `scripts/dev-env/lib.sh`, which already loads and exports `PUBLIRA_PLATFORM_APP_URL` as a required value, so the variable is guaranteed non-empty at the call site.

The pass-through itself was verified by running the `outbox-worker` start line from `scripts/dev-env.sh` against a written profile, with a stub binary in place of `server/bin/outbox-worker` that dumps its environment: the value the worker receives (`http://platform.localhost:13702` for a slot-7 profile) matches that profile's `PUBLIRA_PLATFORM_APP_URL` instead of the `3080` default.

End to end, on a started profile: request a platform console password reset on that profile's web-platform and confirm the delivered mail links to the profile's own port.

author: justfiguringitout-ship-it
body:
## Why

`<lastmod>` had lost its signal again. The live sitemap has **659 of 723 URLs (91.1%) sharing just two dates** — 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-01. Meanwhile all five of the newest review pages sit in GSC as **"Discovered - currently not indexed."**

That state is a change from last week, and it is the useful signal: a week ago they were *"URL is unknown to Google."* PR #9's internal links fixed **discovery**. Google now knows the URLs exist and is choosing not to crawl them. A sitemap where 91% of URLs claim they changed three days ago is exactly how you spend a crawl budget on 659 pages that did not change.

## Cause

`scripts/generate-page-dates.mjs` dated the four data-driven route families from `newest(<template page.tsx>, <structure lib>, padel-courts.ts)`. The Aug 28–29 video-hero wave and the Sep 1 pricing commit each touched every template `page.tsx`, so all ~645 club/state/city/metro URLs rolled forward together. Adding a hero video is not a content change.

`src/app/sitemap.ts`'s own header describes this precise failure mode as the reason the script exists.

## Changes

**1. Structural vs presentational.** Template dates now come only from the libs that decide which routes exist and what data they carry (`court-adapter.ts`, `site-structure.ts`, `metros.ts`). The template's own `page.tsx` is no longer read. A new `TEMPLATE_CONTENT_CHANGES` map lets a template edit that genuinely did change rendered content be recorded deliberately, with a date — so the honest case stays expressible.

**2. Per-club dates.** The script walks `padel-courts.ts` through git history and diffs it record by record, so a club's `lastmod` is the commit in which *that club's* record last changed. State, city and metro pages are club listings, so `sitemap.ts` dates each from the newest of the clubs it actually lists (`CityInfo.courts`, plus a per-state index).

## Effect (measured on the built sitemap, not predicted)

| | URLs dated inside the last 7 days |
|---|---|
| before | **659 of 723 (91.1%)** |
| after | **11 of 723 (1.5%)** |

328 club pages now carry their own date; 16 distinct dates site-wide. The five unindexed review pages keep their true 08-29 / 09-01 dates and are now among the only 11 recent URLs rather than lost among 659 — which is the whole point.

## Verification

- **Falsification test:** a simulated presentational commit touching all four template `page.tsx` files produced a **byte-identical** `page-dates.json`. The regression cannot recur from a styling change.
- `npm run build` passes, run in an isolated `git worktree` so the main working tree was never touched (another agent works in this repo).
- `tsc` reports **zero** errors in `sitemap.ts`. The pre-existing errors elsewhere are untouched.

## Expected effect and how it gets checked

This is a crawl-prioritisation fix, not a ranking fix. The read is next week: if the five "Discovered - currently not indexed" pages get crawled without manual submission, both discovery levers are working and the site regains organic indexing for every future page.

## Noted, not fixed

The built sitemap has 723 `<loc>` entries but **719 unique URLs**. Three club names are duplicated in `padel-courts.ts` (`Matt's Pickle and Padel`, `Padel California`, `Padel Country Club`), and slugs derive from the name, so they collide. Pre-existing data issue, out of scope here.

Revert path: `git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>`.

body:
The workspace shell put its mobile chrome in a top header: a menu button
and the workspace switcher an arm's reach away, opening a full-height
left drawer. The rest of the app moved to bottom sheets in #915; the
workspace was the surface left behind.

The bar now sits at the foot of the shell and its menu button opens the
navigation tree as a bottom sheet, so the trigger and the surface it
reveals are both under the thumb. Sheet already treats the bottom edge as
a first-class side, so the drawer arrives with the grabber, the rounded
top corners, and the safe-area padding for free.

The bar is a flex sibling of the scrolling content rather than a fixed
overlay, so the shell reserves its height and no document scrolls behind
it, and it comes last in the column so the content keeps the reading
order. The sheet takes a definite height instead of only the side's cap,
which gives the document list a resolvable flex basis: it scrolls inside
the sheet rather than stretching it.

Renamed from workspace-mobile-sidebar since it is no longer a sidebar.

body:
### ⚡ Nexus -- IPC & Core Performance Triad Ⅱ (3 cycles, 3 bottlenecks, 3 measured deltas)

Autonomous backend/IPC cycle set: profile -> isolate ONE bottleneck -> optimize ->
benchmark. Every number below is an **in-process A/B on this host** (`scripts/nexus_bench.py`,
median of 3 runs); the old path is re-measured in the same process rather than quoted from
the journal, because cross-host numbers on this box differ by ~1.5x.

All three cycles are guarded by 28 new tests. `make check` green: compile + ruff + mypy +
241 tests + e2e (20 properties).
(benchmark deltas)

All numbers from `scripts/nexus_bench.py` (rewritten for this triad), measured
**in-process, both paths, same host, median of 3 runs**. Cross-host comparison
against triad-1 numbers is explicitly avoided (this box is ~1.5× slower).
Gate: compile + ruff + mypy + **241 tests** + e2e all green.

| Focus | Headline metric | Before | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | event → 3 text consumers | **23.20 µs** | **11.59 µs** | **2.00×, −11.61 µs** |
| A | marginal cost per extra consumer | **6.62 µs** | **0.79 µs** | **8.4×** |
| A | shared-memory ring write | 7.20 µs | **2.43 µs** | **2.96×** (graveyard fixed) |
| A | UDS burst delivery, producer+consumer | 6.62 µs | **2.35 µs** | **2.8×**, zero disk/pipe |
| A | retained-event memory | 48.9 MB/200k | **39.7 MB/200k** | **−18.8 %** |
| B | per-tick trigger eval (8 triggers) | 8.34 µs | **1.45 µs** | **5.76×, −6.89 µs/tick** |
| B | `elapsed_s()` per tick + per event | 1.42 µs | **0.60 µs** | **2.38×** |
| C | archived-ledger single-record lookup | **7 552 µs** | **80.9 µs** | **93.3×** |
| C | `archive_stats()` | 8 356 µs | **899 µs** | **9.3×** |
| C | `verify_archive()` | 21 357 µs | **1 546 µs** | **13.8×** |
| C | ledger growth | unbounded, manual | **self-compacting**, 0 records lost | bounded by policy |

**Not a regression, stated plainly:** the one-text-sink case is a wash
(9.95 → 10.01 µs) and the `emit` floor moved +0.03 µs (0.9 %) for the
per-sink capability probe — encoding has to happen exactly once either way. The
optimization is structural (cost no longer scales with consumer count), plus the
new plane removes the disk from the hot path when a live consumer exists.

**Files**
- `orchestrator/events.py` — shared-line fanout (`write_prepared`), lazy rendering,
  `_render_line` + bounded `_LITERAL_CACHE`, `render_record()`.
- `orchestrator/uds.py` — **NEW** `UDSBroadcastSink` + `UDSBroadcastServer`
  (non-blocking datagram broadcast, drop counting, stale-inode recovery,
  abstract-namespace fallback, 0600).
- `orchestrator/ring.py` — `write_prepared` fast path, non-raising drop accounting
  on the hot path (`dropped`), strict `write()` kept.
- `orchestrator/scheduler.py` — `_CONDITION_CACHE` + `_compile_condition`,
  frozenset `_COMPARISONS`, memoized `elapsed_s()`.
- `core/protocol.py` — `timestamp_epoch_s()` (+ `_EPOCH_CACHE`), fast `Timer.elapsed()`.
- `orchestrator/transport.py` — `write_jsonl_indexed`, `snapshot_index`,
  `lookup_archived`, `stale_entry_count`, `maybe_compact`, digest fast path in
  `verify_archive(force=…)`, verify-before-prune, manifest-based `archive_stats`,
  self-maintenance gate in `archive()`.
- `orchestrator/cli.py` — `watch --uds/--uds-batch`, `bus tail`,
  `archive lookup|verify`, richer `archive stats`.
- `scripts/nexus_bench.py` — rewritten: in-process A/B for all three focuses.
- `tests/test_nexus_triad2.py` — **NEW** 28 guards (line parity, lazy render,
  ring fanout/drop, UDS delivery/perms/no-consumer, condition parity + bounded
  caches, clock anchor, index rebuild, tamper both paths, no-data-loss, auto-compact,
  stale-socket takeover vs. live-listener refusal).
- `README.md` — the new opt-in ops surface.

### Contracts deliberately untouched
- `FileTransport` (inbox/processing/done + `fsync`) remains **the** delivery mechanism; the
  UDS and ring sinks are an opt-in *observation* plane. No fallback was removed.
- Nothing re-parses or re-compiles a JSON schema per tick. `schemacheck.validate` was
  re-profiled this cycle and stays **cold** (95 µs, CLI-only) -- so per the standing rule the
  closure-compilation item waits until a schema actually lands on the tick path.
- The ledger can no longer grow unbounded: compaction is self-triggering (every 64 archives,
  entries older than 7 days, >= 64 stale) and **verifies before it prunes** -- a violation means
  no movement at all. Index/digest artifacts are derived: missing -> rebuilt, mismatched ->
  parity fallback to the slow path.
- `Event` line output is **byte-identical** to `json.dumps(record, separators=(",", ":"))`;
  `render_record()` is the parity oracle the tests pin against.

### Reproduce
```bash
PYTHON=/home/user/.venv-nio/bin/python make check          # gate, incl. 28 new guards
python3 scripts/nexus_bench.py --json bench.json           # the tables above
python3 -m orchestrator.cli loop --watch --uds runtime/bus.sock    # producer
python3 -m orchestrator.cli bus tail --socket runtime/bus.sock     # consumer, no disk
python3 -m orchestrator.cli archive verify --json                  # digest fast path
```
Metrics also logged in `.nio/nexus.md` (TRIAD Nº2 + summary + corrected Graveyard).

author: ismaelocaramelo
body:
## What

The Merchant Center loads its JavaScript in rounds. The browser only learns it needs the next set of files after downloading and running the previous set, so each round costs a full trip to the network.

This adds preload hints to the built page for the shell files (navbar, project container, menus) so the browser fetches them at the same time as the main file instead of waiting to discover them.

## Why this differs from the ticket

The ticket asked for `modulePreload: { polyfill: false }`. That setting adds no hints. I applied it, rebuilt, and compared the built page: the only difference was the main file's hash.

The actual reason there were no hints is that Vite only preloads files the main file imports directly, and ours imports none of them. Everything is loaded on demand. So the hints do have to be built, as the ticket says, just not with that setting.

## Measured

Integration, signed in, empty cache:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| main file | 2314 -> 3014 ms |
| translations | 3676 -> 4174 ms |
| shell files | 4185 -> **4629 ms** |

The app cannot render until both translations and shell files are in, so today the shell is what holds it up. That is roughly **455 ms** to recover, after which translations become the limit.

Two things I noticed while measuring. The trace showed 8 rounds rather than 3, and translations arrived before the shell rather than alongside it. And the biggest single cost is not a round at all: the main file takes 700 ms to download, then nothing happens for another 660 ms while the browser works through it. That looks like a bigger win than anything in this PR and has no ticket.

## Cost, and one file left out

The hints total **128 KB across 8 files**.

`application-shell-splitter` is left out on purpose even though it belongs to the same round. It is 1.2 MB on its own and drags in another 172 KB, so including it meant fetching 1.5 MB at high priority alongside the 2.3 MB main file, which could delay the very thing this speeds up. The trade-off is real: that file still gets discovered late, so the round does not fully collapse. Whether to add it back should come from a measurement on a throttled connection, not from an argument.

Custom Views also get these hints, since they build from the same package, even though they never render a navbar. Custom applications do use them. There is no reliable way to tell the two apart at build time. Flagging it rather than hiding it, and happy to put it behind a flag if you would rather.

## Not included

- The after measurement, which needs a signed-in session.
- `polyfill: false`. It is a browser support decision worth about 600 bytes, so it should not ride along quietly.
- The translations round. The language is only known at runtime, and the build emits about 52 language files for the 3 a session actually uses, so preloading them all would clearly make things worse. Needs its own ticket.

## Checks

- 20 unit tests. Typecheck and lint clean. `mc-scripts` 120/120.
- Playground build: 8 hints, correct CDN URLs, main file not duplicated.
- Custom View template still builds.
- Full suite green apart from the known `application-shell.spec.js` flake, which passes on its own.

If a shell file is renamed so only some names still match, the build fails and says which one, because otherwise the speedup would quietly disappear. Worth an opinion: `mc-scripts` is published, so that would fail other people's builds too. Say the word if you would rather it warned.

author: atwoodtm
body:
Fixes #69. The reported defect was a wrong count; investigating it turned up two more, one of them destructive.

`List` implements `IList<object>` over its elements **and** `IDictionary<string, object>` over the dynamic properties it inherits. A single public member cannot mean the right thing to both, and the three members that satisfy both interfaces at once had never been separated.

| Member | Through the dictionary interface | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Count` | reported the **element** count | Fixed |
| `Clear()` | **emptied the elements**, left properties intact | Fixed — worse than the reported bug |
| `IsReadOnly` | `false` | Correct as-is, no change |

## Count

Not only a wrong number. **LINQ special-cases `ICollection<T>`**, so `Count()` and `ToList()` over the properties read this value instead of enumerating — making counting and iterating the same sequence disagree. A `List` with no elements and two properties enumerated two pairs while `Count()` said zero.

## Clear — the one that wasn't in the issue

The public `Clear` empties the elements. Because it also satisfied `ICollection<KeyValuePair<string, object>>.Clear`, asking to clear the **properties** destroyed the list contents and left the properties untouched — the exact opposite of the request. That is data loss, not a wrong number.

Both now have explicit dictionary-side implementations. The public `Count` and `Clear` are unchanged, so anything using `List` as a list behaves exactly as before; only the dictionary interface, where the answers were wrong, changes.

## A third defect, found by mirroring

Writing `Clear`'s notifications meant reading `Dictionary.Clear` to match it, which is where this surfaced:

```csharp
var tKeys = Keys;      // a LIVE view over _dictionary
_dictionary.Clear();   // ...which this empties
foreach (var tKey in tKeys) OnPropertyChanged(tKey);   // so this iterates nothing
```

`Dictionary.Clear()` raised **no** `PropertyChanged` at all. A bound control was left showing properties that no longer existed. Copying that shape into the new code would have propagated it, so it is fixed with a `ToList()` and the reason recorded beside it.

## Verification

Established by construction rather than by reading. Before: dictionary count 3 against 2 enumerated entries; a dictionary-side `Clear` emptied the elements; `Dictionary.Clear` notified nothing. After: counts agree with enumeration, each `Clear` affects only its own side, and both raise notifications for every removed key.

0 warnings and 0 errors on both `netstandard2.0` and `net10.0` with `-warnaserror --no-incremental`; **636 tests passing**, 0 skipped, no filter.

Six tests fail when the three defects are restored in an isolated worktree. The test the coverage push wrote to pin the count inconsistency is flipped — it was explicitly marked as pinning a bug rather than blessing one, and now asserts the two agree.

## Behavior changes, for the release notes

- `((ICollection<KeyValuePair<string, object>>)list).Count` now returns the property count rather than the element count, and agrees with enumerating the same sequence.
- Clearing a `List` through `IDictionary` or `ICollection<KeyValuePair<,>>` now clears the properties instead of the elements.
- `Dictionary.Clear()` now raises `PropertyChanged` for each removed key, as it always intended to.

No public signature changed, so `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` needs no update — the two new members are explicit interface implementations.

author: adrians5j
body:
Follow-up to #823. That PR made merging a `release-announcements/X` PR the thing that publishes to Slack, which isn't obvious from looking at the repo and can't be undone once it fires. This writes it down.

Covers:

- The trigger split between the two workflows, and which merge causes which
- That merging the announcements PR **is** the send button
- Only `slack.md` and `social.md` exist now, `tweets.md` is gone and shouldn't come back
- Edit copy on the branch, never rerun the generator to fix wording, since it discards the reviewed text
- Verify bug descriptions with the PR author, because the changelog is generated and gets them wrong
- Copy conventions for the two files, including the `—` separator and shortcodes vs literal emoji
- The `announcements-published/<version>` tag guard and what it does and doesn't cover

Two hazards get their own callout, both hit during the 6.4.10 rollout:

1. For `pull_request` events GitHub reads workflow files from `master`, not the PR branch, so publish workflow changes have to land first.
2. A stale announcements PR is live ammunition. Merging one announces an old release to the community channel with an `@channel` ping, and the tag guard doesn't help since that version was never tagged. We closed five of these (795, 798, 800, 803, 805) rather than merging them.

Docs only, no behaviour change.

body:
## 배경

PR #59(품목코드 매칭) 병합 후 실제 파일로 재검증했더니 오히려 0/38로 매칭 건수가 줄어서 다시 보고받음. 사용자가 화면에서 직접 "사급 요청 추적" 탭을 열어 "두하"로 검색한 결과를 캡처해 보내줘서 원인을 바로 확인할 수 있었음: 매각내역의 사급처는 "(주)두하(3018537479)"(정규화하면 "두하")인데, 실제 미완료 발주는 전부 **"두하 생산관리"**로 등록돼 있었음. 사용자에게 확인한 결과 같은 회사가 맞고, 이런 식으로 뒤에 부서/구분 표현이 붙는 사급처 이름이 실무에서 흔하다고 함.

## 수정 내용

- 사급처 전체 표기가 정확히 일치하지 않으면, 첫 단어(회사명 부분)가 같은 등록 사급처가 있는지 한 번 더 찾아봄
- **다만 자동 처리는 하지 않음** — code-review에서 지적받은 위험 때문: 첫 단어만 같은 건 서로 다른 두 회사(예: "대성"↔"대성 물류센터"가 실제로는 남남인 경우)의 우연일 수 있고, 원자재 품목코드는 여러 회사가 공용으로 쓸 수도 있어 품목까지 맞아도 안심할 수 없음
- 대신 "확인 필요" 목록에 **후보 등록명을 구체적으로 알려주는 사유**를 표시(예: `사급처 표기가 등록된 발주("두하 생산관리")와 정확히 일치하지 않아 자동 처리하지 않음 — 같은 회사인지 확인 후 직접 처리하세요`) — 완전 자동화는 아니지만, 어느 발주를 찾아 확인해야 하는지 바로 알 수 있어 수작업 부담을 크게 줄임
- "주식회사 OOO"처럼 법인 표기 자체가 띄어써 있는 경우, 정규화하면 빈 문자열이 되는 "주식회사" 토큰을 회사명으로 잘못 쓰지 않도록 처리

## 검증

- `cssales.js` 시나리오 45개 전부 통과(사급처 부서 표현 관련 새 시나리오 4개 추가)
- 실제 업로드 파일로 재검증: 화면에서 확인한 실제 사례("두하 생산관리" / "Extadditive 003")로 재현했을 때 확인 필요 목록에 정확히 그 사유와 후보 등록명이 표시됨을 확인
- 기존 회귀 스위트(95개) — 이번 변경과 무관한 사전 존재 실패 8건 외 이상 없음
- `code-review` 스킬로 자체 검토 — 처음 구현은 첫 단어만 같으면 바로 자동 처리하는 방식이었는데, 리뷰에서 서로 다른 회사가 우연히 같은 첫 단어를 쓸 수 있는 위험을 지적받아 자동 처리를 하지 않고 후보만 안내하는 지금 방식으로 수정함

## 참고

이번 PR은 "부서 표현 때문에 사급처를 못 찾던" 문제를 완전 자동 처리가 아니라 "빠르게 찾아 확인할 수 있는 안내"로 해결합니다. 완전 자동화하려면 사급처를 회사 단위로 정확히 식별할 방법(예: 발주 등록 시 사업자번호도 같이 저장)이 있어야 안전하게 할 수 있어서, 이번에는 안전을 우선했습니다.
