author: keylormr
body:
## Por que

Produccion corre **2.3.6** y el repositorio tambien. Los doce PR de ayer estan en
`main`, pero **ninguno subio la version**. Desplegando asi, `/health` seguiria
diciendo 2.3.6 y no habria forma de saber si el despliegue entro — que es
justamente el problema que se resolvio poniendo la version de build en `/health`.

Estado de produccion al momento de abrir esto (`GET /health`): version 2.3.6,
base y Redis en `ok`, desvio de conciliacion en 0, y CoinGecko respondiendo
—plan `demo`, ultimo exito hoy, diez activos en cache—, asi que los precios de
cripto estan vivos.

## Minor, no patch

Hay funciones nuevas de verdad: entrar con nombre de usuario, ver y cerrar los
dispositivos con la cuenta abierta, y el canal de actualizacion de iOS.

## Lo que el chequeo atrapo

Los lugares que hay que mover a la vez ya **no son cuatro sino cinco**. El PR
#153 agrego `MARKETING_VERSION` y `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` al proyecto de iOS,
en las **dos** configuraciones. Sin `npm run check:version` el tag habria salido
con iOS marcando 2.3.6 — exactamente el defecto que ese script existe para
impedir, despues de que `package.json` pasara ocho versiones marcando 2.0.0
mientras la aplicacion publicada iba en 2.3.3.

## El changelog

En lenguaje de usuario: que recibe la persona, no como se hizo. Siete lineas que
cubren lo que de verdad se nota — el nombre de usuario, los dispositivos
conectados, la contrasena para cambiar el correo, las pantallas que dicen cuando
no pudieron cargar, los montos en su moneda, los cobros que avisan que no hay
convenio, y el aviso de version para iPhone.

## Verificacion

- `npm run check:version`: sincronizado en 2.4.0 (versionCode 13).
- Frontend: typecheck, lint y build en verde.
- Backend: build y pruebas de `appversion` en verde.

## Lo que NO hace este PR

No corta el tag ni despliega. Eso sigue siendo decision tuya. Cuando lo hagas:

- `RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` aplica las migraciones **057, 058 y 059**.
- `DEMO_LOGIN_ENABLED=true` solo mientras dure la demostracion.
- Despues del despliegue, `GET /health` debe responder `"version":"2.4.0"`. Si
  sigue diciendo 2.3.6, el despliegue no entro.

author: qchantel
body:
## Add Scoutee — remote MCP server for public procurement

Adds `servers/scoutee/`: a **remote** server (`type: remote`, `transport_type: streamable-http`), so no Docker image is built. Modelled on `servers/apify/`, which is the existing precedent for a remote server authenticated with an API-key **header** rather than OAuth.

### What it does

[Scoutee](https://scoutee.org) collects the public procurement notices published every day by official journals and buyer platforms across Europe (TED plus the national portals of 30 countries) and North America (SAM.gov, CanadaBuys, SEAO), deduplicates them into one row per notice, and exposes the result as a searchable index — 200,000+ notices, 87 sources, 32 countries.

Two tools, both read-only:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `search_tenders` | Full-text search over title, buyer and description, with filters for keywords (with cached translations per portal language), countries, source portal, estimated-value range, sort order, closed notices and freshness. Returns a page of notices, the total, a per-country facet and the caller's remaining quota. |
| `get_tender` | One notice in full by its Scoutee id: buyer, description, CPV codes, estimated value and currency, publication and deadline dates, documents link and the source URL where a bid is actually filed. |

`tools.json` is `[]` per CONTRIBUTING ("always an empty array for remote servers because they use dynamic tool discovery"), matching `servers/linear` and `servers/apify`.

### Authentication

Header API key, no OAuth:

```yaml
remote:
  transport_type: streamable-http
  url: https://scoutee.org/api/mcp
  headers:
    X-API-Key: "${SCOUTEE_API_KEY}"
config:
  secrets:
    - name: scoutee.api_key
      env: SCOUTEE_API_KEY
      example: sct_YOUR_API_KEY
```

The endpoint also accepts `Authorization: Bearer sct_...`, but `X-API-Key` is the documented form.

### Getting a test key

Sign up at https://scoutee.org, subscribe to the **Standard** plan, then open the workspace page → section **API** → create a key (`sct_...`). Keys are revocable from the same page; quota is 10,000 searches per hour. Happy to provide reviewer credentials through your Google form — just say the word.

### Links

- Documentation: https://scoutee.org/en/api-docs
- Pricing: https://scoutee.org/pricing
- Server docs repo: https://github.com/qchantel/scoutee-mcp
- Official MCP Registry entry: `org.scoutee/scoutee` (https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=scoutee)

### Validation

`go run ./cmd/validate -name scoutee` passes every check:

```
✅ Name is valid
✅ Directory is valid
✅ Title is valid
✅ YAML formatting is valid
✅ Commit pin not required (non-local server)
✅ Secrets are valid
✅ Config env is valid
✅ License validation skipped (remote server)
✅ Icon is valid
✅ tools.json is valid. Found 0 tools.
✅ Remote is valid
✅ OAuth dynamic configuration is valid
```

The endpoint is publicly reachable and `readme.md` links to live documentation.

author: dahlweid
body: Closes #178.  Two separable changes, and the second one is a judgement call I want read on its merits.  ## Part 1 — the coverage gap, re-measured  The issue's comment claimed no unit test reaches `#invalidateState`. I did not inherit that. I put an `appendFileSync` probe at the top of `#invalidateState (render-cache.mjs)` and ran the whole Office-free suite:  - **0 hits across 712 tests.** The claim holds. - **2 hits from `edit-invalidate-close.test.mjs` alone**, with the same probe still in place. That is the positive control, and it is the part that makes the zero mean anything — without it, "no output" is equally consistent with instrumentation that never ran.  The probe was removed before commit.  ### The fake is a Word host, not a fake `DocumentEditor`  The issue proposed a `DocumentEditor` fake. I did not build one, because it turns out not to be necessary: `DocumentReader` only ever calls `host.structure`, and `RenderCache.host` is already publicly assignable — `outline-interleave.test.mjs` establishes that precedent. So a fake host runs the **real** `DocumentEditor` and `DocumentReader` on top of it, and the queued unit of work under test is the product's own — read, edit, re-read, invalidate. No production code was widened for testability, and the addresses the edit resolves against are minted by the real structure map rather than invented.  ### One of these tests was the trap the issue documents, and I measured it being so  My first version of test 1 was the obvious shape: hold the queue open inside an outline handshake, start an edit, assert the edit "has not run yet". **It passed with `editDocument` bypassing the queue entirely.** The real editor does a stat, a hash, a snapshot and a full read before it reaches Word, and that outlasts any microtask turn count — so the assertion was passing on slack, which is exactly the "test that cannot fail for the reason its comment claims" family, and exactly what #178 exists to warn about. I would have shipped a test that looked like coverage of the ordering and was not.  Both tests now hold their gate **inside `host.edit`**. The window stays open for as long as the test likes, so a competing operation that is not queued has unbounded opportunity to run, and "it did not run" stops being a statement about timing. The reasoning is recorded in the test file.  ### Mutations verified red  | Mutation | `an edit holds the document queue…` | `a reopen cannot land between…` | | --- | --- | --- | | `editDocument` calls its operation directly instead of through `#enqueueDocumentOperation` | **red** — `an outline ran against the document while an edit was mid-flight inside Word` | **red** — `actual: ['openDocument','edit','closeDocument']` vs `expected: [… ,'openDocument']` | | `await this.#invalidateState(state)` dropped from `editDocument` | **red** — `actual: ['edit','outlineMarkup','outlinePositions']` vs `expected: ['edit','closeDocument','outlineMarkup','outlinePositions']` | green (honestly so — `open`'s own stale-key path still closes the document, so this mutant does not violate *this* test's claim) |  ## Part 2 — I accepted the choke-point guard, with the narrowing stated  **First, the correction to the brief was itself half-right, and I checked it before acting.** The kickoff claimed all four non-close sites throw `not_open`; the follow-up corrected that to three, and said `open()`'s status was an open question I had to settle. I had already found the discrepancy from the source before the correction arrived. Here is the answer:  **`open()` never reaches `#enqueueDocumentOperation` with `state.closing === true`.** Two independent reasons, either sufficient:  1. The closing branch **returns** (`return this.open(docPath)`). The outer invocation never falls through to the enqueue at all. 2. The recursive call re-derives state through `#stateFor`, and `close()`'s enqueued operation deletes the map entry as its *first* statement while `state.documentPending` resolves only after the whole operation — so the state `open` recurses into is freshly minted, with `closing: false`.  So a choke-point throw is unreachable from `open`, and the relocation is **not** a behaviour regression in that seam. The three throwing sites are a clean relocation: same code, same message, and the throw still happens before `state.documentPending` is touched, so nothing is enqueued.  I did it, and I removed the outer guards on `editDocument` and `revertDocument` so there is exactly one mechanism and no ambiguity about which one is load-bearing — the thing the kickoff explicitly did not want left unstated.  What did **not** move, with reasons:  - **`#require` keeps its `closing` arm.** `search`, `text` and `info` go through `#require` and then straight to the host without enqueuing anything. For them it is the only refusal there is, so removing it would be a real regression. `outline` is therefore doubly guarded — `#require` throws first — which is unavoidable and stated in the code. - **`open()` keeps its guard**, because it is a *different policy*: wait-and-reopen, not refusal.  **So the invariant is narrowed, not retired, and I have said so in the code rather than claiming more.** Two exemptions: `close()` opts out explicitly; `open()` never arrives with the flag set. What the change does buy is real — `open()`'s correctness stops being a property of every other caller and becomes a property of one function, so a future queued call site gets the safe answer by default instead of silently breaking `open()` from a distance.  One hazard I want on the record rather than buried: `open()`'s exemption is *by construction*, not explicit. If someone later refactored its closing branch to fall through instead of return, they would get a hard `not_open` where a wait-and-reopen used to be. That is a loud failure rather than a silent one — refusing is never the teardown-while-in-flight bug — and `a repeated close cannot delete a document reopened behind the first close` in `outline-interleave.test.mjs` goes red if it happens. Both facts are recorded at `open`'s guard.  ### Guard mutations verified red  - **Choke-point refusal disabled** → `an edit or revert cannot enqueue after a document starts closing` fails with `an edit or revert appended to a document's closing queue`, `actual: undefined` vs `expected: 'not_open'`. The relocated guard is load-bearing and already covered by the #177 test, which now tests the choke point instead of two inline guards. - **`close()`'s `allowClosing` exemption removed** → `close()` throws, `documentPending` never advances, `open()` waits on it forever and the file times out at ~102 s. The exemption is required, not decorative.  ## Verification  - `node tools/validate-extensions.mjs` — OK, 1 extension valid. - `node tools/check-citations.mjs` — OK, 73 probes resolve. - `node tools/check-citation-lines.mjs` — OK, no positional coordinate in any line it read. - Full Office-free unit suite, run with the glob: **722 pass / 0 fail** on the rebased tree. Accounted for exactly: **712** original baseline, **+2** the two tests added here, **+8** the `mutation-anchors.test.mjs` that arrived with `df5618d` (counted by running that file alone). No test was removed — extracting `deferred` and `turns` into `queue-probe.mjs` moved helpers without changing any count.  No Word or PowerPoint was started, and nothing under `test/integration/` was run.  ## Notes for the concurrent mutation-anchor work (#182) — resolved  **Settled now that #183 has merged as `df5618d` and this branch is rebased onto it.** The gate `node tools/check-mutation-anchors.mjs` passes here: **143 anchors across 4 harnesses, every one resolving exactly once**, and none of them is in `render-cache.mjs`.  That matters because this PR removes text a new anchor could have targeted: the inline `if (state.closing) throw …` blocks in `editDocument` and `revertDocument` **no longer exist**, the closing refusal now being a single site inside `#enqueueDocumentOpera

author: acehack
body:
fix(hygiene): the drift publication lint reported SHAPE as if it were liveness

`lint-drift-publication-lands` printed "ok: 2 drift publication lane(s) route via
PR, fail loudly, and probe capability" — naming `drift-sweep.yml` and
`drift-dashboard-cadence.yml`. Both are `disabled_manually` and publish nothing.

Its own origin is the argument. It was written because drift-sweep computed a
ledger and could not publish it for TEN DAYS behind 1,597 green runs. Every rule
it enforces reads the workflow FILE — so a lane that is correctly shaped and
switched off entirely satisfies all three and prints a bare "ok". That is the
same green over a frozen dashboard, one level out, committed inside the guard
against it.

Now reports enablement beside shape: the summary says "ok (SHAPE)", each lane
carries its recorded state, and when EVERY validated lane is disabled it says so
in a sentence — because a bare ok there reads as "drift publication is healthy",
which is the exact confusion this lint exists to end. Being disabled is a
legitimate choice (Aaron's size-and-cost reduction) and is NOT a failure here, so
the exit code is unchanged.

State is read from `github-settings.expected.json` rather than the Actions API:
this lint runs where network is not guaranteed, and that file is itself compared
against the live repo by `check-github-settings-drift`. That dependency is named
in the code rather than hidden — the reported state is only as fresh as that
check is green, which is strictly better than reporting nothing.

A missing expectation file yields NO states rather than defaulting to "active".
The dangerous default is the opposite one: absent data read as all-live would
restore precisely the reassurance this removes. Asserted.

NOTE ON WHAT THIS PRINTS TODAY: on this branch the expectation still records
those lanes as active, so no annotation appears yet. It starts reporting
`[disabled_manually]` once #16931 lands, which is the change that makes the
expectation true. The behaviour is proven here by falsifiers over synthetic
states rather than by waiting for that merge.

Verified: 26 tests pass, lint (TS) clean.

author: ernestasd
body:
## Kodėl

Paskutinė perpardavėjo laiško eilutė, kuri vis dar buvo mūsų.

Viskas žinutės viduje jau buvo jų — logotipas, spalvos, nuorodos, o nuo #298 ir vardas pašto dėžutės eilutėje. O adresas šalia jo skelbė `hello@orbetra.com`. Kiekviename aktyvavimo laiške, kiekviename slaptažodžio atstatyme, kiekviename pranešime.

Tai nebuvo atvaizdavimo klaida. `MAIL_FROM` yra **vienas procesui bendras** kintamasis (ADR-023), tad per-tenant siuntėjas buvo ne šiaip nesukonfigūruotas — jis buvo **neišreiškiamas**. 2026-09 auditas įvertino tai kaip paskutinį HIGH, kurį gali uždaryti pats kodas: W-12 ir W-13 reikalauja neutralaus domeno ir jokia kodo eilutė jų nepasiekia.

ADR-036, įgyvendintas taip, kaip nuspręsta, be nukrypimų: patvirtiname nuomininko domeną kaip DKIM tapatybę **mūsų** SES paskyroje ir tada nustatome `From` į jų adresą. Viena antraštė nepakeistame pristatymo kelyje — SES priima bet kokį `From` ant patvirtintos tapatybės — o ne antras pristatymo kelias.

## ★ Tai išeina INERTIŠKAI, ir tai yra esmė

IAM naudotojo, kurio tam reikia, dar nėra, tad `sesIdentityConfigFromEnv()` kiekviename dabartiniame diegime atsako `null`: keturi maršrutai grąžina 503, o kortelė sako, kad funkcija neprieinama. **Niekas nė vieno nuomininko laiškuose nepasikeičia**, kol nenustatyti trys env kintamieji.

Serverio SES **SMTP** kredencialai to negali — jie siunčia, bet nevaldo tapatybių. Reikia atskiro IAM naudotojo su keturiomis `ses:*EmailIdentity*` teisėmis (surašyta ADR ir README lentelėje). **Tai vienintelis likęs founder'io darbas.**

SMS šliuzas išėjo lygiai taip pat (ADR-032); alternatyva — funkcija, kurios niekas negali peržiūrėti, kol neatkeliauja kredencialas.

## Nepatvirtintas NIEKADA netampa neišsiųstu

Siuntimo kelias skaito `verifiedAt`, o ne `status`. Jie sąmoningai išsiskiria: tapatybė, kurios paskutinis `GetEmailIdentity` grįžo nelaimingas, pažymima `failed`, **kad nuomininkas MATYTŲ**, o jos DKIM įrašai tebėra paskelbti ir tebeveikia. Tyliai grąžinti tą perpardavėją prie mūsų `From` eilutės dėl laikino API atsakymo būtų būtent tas nutekėjimas, kurį čia uždarome.

O nuomininkas be patvirtintos tapatybės siunčia mūsų adresu, nes laiškas, siunčiamas kaip domenas, kuris už mus nepasirašė, krenta per DMARC ir nusėda šlamšte: klientas, kuris niekada nesužino, kad jo automobilis pajudėjo, yra blogiau nei `From` eilutė su mūsų vardu.

## Adresas paklūsta tam pačiam vartui kaip ir vardas

Tik white-label nuomininkas siunčia kaip kažkas kitas. `direct_*` klientas pirko MŪSŲ produktą ir mūsų tapatybė jam teisinga — net jei kokia nors pasiklydusi eilutė sakytų kitaip. Tai tvirtina testas, kuris **krenta**, kai vartus pašalini.

## `safeSender()`

Pakartotinai tikrina ties transportu — ne todėl, kad zod schema silpna, o todėl, kad tai **skirtingos garantijos**: eilutė, įrašyta prieš schemos sugriežtinimą, ranka paleistas SQL pataisymas ar būsimas kitas iškvietėjas apeina pirmąją ir neapeina antrosios.

Jis **ATMETA, o ne taiso** — skirtingai nei rodomas vardas, nėra „išvalytos" adreso versijos, kuri vis dar būtų ta pati dėžutė. O atmetimas krenta į platformos tapatybę, tad injekcijos bandymas kainuoja `From` eilutę, niekada — išsiuntimą.

## Du sarginiai suveikė, abu teisingai

`audit.spec` išvedžioja esybes iš repozitorijų šaltinių ir krito ties nepažymėta `sendingDomain` — iš čia keturios kalbos. Izoliacijos šlavimas atsisakė naujo kolekcijos maršruto, neturinčio nei fixture id, nei užrašytos priežasties; šis grąžina vieną objektą, parenkamą pagal JWT nuomininką, tad priežastis užrašyta, o cross-tenant atvejis tvirtinamas tiesiogiai.

## Sąmoningai NEPADARYTA

Per-tenant SMTP kredencialai, kuriuos ADR-036 atmeta (aklumas palaikymui, kai jų pačių tiekėjas ima stabdyti; svetimo gyvo kredencialo laikymas tiek, kiek gyvuoja klientas).

Founder'is vėliau atsakė „abu, DKIM numatytasis" — tas atsakymas **ankstesnis** už šio pagrindimo perskaitymą. DKIM yra numatytasis abiem atvejais, tad niekas išleisto nuo to nepriklauso, bet BYO SMTP nereikėtų statyti ant vieno pasirinkimo iš sąrašo, neturint tos kainos prieš akis. Pažymėta ADR — **verta jūsų sprendimo.**

## Antras commit'as — žinių bazė

Du straipsniai buvo teisingi, kai parašyti šįryt, ir tapo klaidingi dėl to, kas susiliejo po jų.

- **„Laiškai, kuriuos gauna jūsų klientai"** sakė, kad siuntimas iš savo domeno „jau planuojamas". Jis išėjo prieš valandą. Dabar tai instrukcijos + tai, ko iš tikrųjų reikia sunerimusiam skaitytojui: laukiant niekas nesustoja.
- **„Klientų paskyros"** vedė per kūrimą ir nė žodžiu neužsiminė, kad tai užrakinta. Po #306 perpardavėjas be patvirtinto hosto gauna 403 ties pirmu to sąrašo žingsniu.

Keturios kalbos. Du paketo sarginiai mane pagavo pakeliui: metaduomenų veidrodis atmetė santraukas, nebeatitinkančias straipsnių, o cross-link patikra atmetė „Savas domenas" ir „Ihre eigene Domain" taikiniui, kurį visa likusi KB vadina kitaip.

## §10 gedimų žemėlapis

Liečia **#13 — platformos tapatybė pasiekia perpardavėjo klientą**. Šis PR uždaro paskutinį to žemėlapio HIGH, kurį pasiekia kodas.

## Vartai

`api 601 · worker 633 · web 540 · db 181 · shared 199 · kb 42 · isolation 46` — visi 54 turbo darbai žali ant perbazuoto medžio.

Kiekvienas naujas testas paleistas prieš `main` (arba prieš pašalintus vartus, kur funkcija nauja) — praėjęs testas netikrina nieko.

연결된 채널의 최근 업로드와 조회수를 채널별 표로 보여줍니다. 상단바에 **「실적」** 탭이 생깁니다.

| 제목 | 업로드 | 공개 상태 | 누적 조회 | 평균 대비 | 판정 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- 기간 칩 **7 / 28 / 90일**, 채널 칩으로 필터
- **판정** — 채널 평균 대비 150%↑ 히트 / 80%↑ 보통 / 그 아래 부진
- 제목·채널명은 눌러서 새 창으로 열림

## 지속률은 뺐습니다
YouTube **Analytics** API 는 스코프가 다릅니다 (`yt-analytics.readonly`).
추가하면 **이미 연결해 둔 채널을 전부 다시 연결**해야 해서, 업로더분이 붙여둔 게 다 풀립니다.
나중에 얹을 수 있게 자리는 비워뒀습니다.

## 판단한 것들
- **비공개·예약은 조회수를 `null`** 로 두고 평균 계산에서도 뺍니다.
  `0` 으로 넣으면 방금 올린 영상이 평균을 끌어내려 **전부 「부진」** 으로 찍힙니다. 이 경우 판정은 「대기」입니다.
- **채널 하나가 실패해도 나머지는 그대로** 보여줍니다. 토큰 하나 만료됐다고 화면 전체가 비면 어디가 문제인지 알 수 없습니다 — 해당 채널 자리에만 오류를 띄웁니다.
- **미연결 채널**은 칩을 흐리게 두고 「유튜브 대시보드에서 연결하면 표시됩니다」 안내만 냅니다.
- **기간 필터는 화면에서만** 걸러 API 를 다시 부르지 않습니다 (쿼터 절약). 새로 받으려면 「지금 새로 조회」.

## 검증
- `tsc --noEmit`, `next build` 통과 (`/performance`, `/api/v1/performance` 생성 확인)
- 빌드된 CSS 로 렌더해 표·칩·배지 확인

> 현재 12개 채널 전부 유튜브 미연결 상태라, 연결 전에는 안내만 나옵니다.

developへ入れる前に各PRで行った自動レビューの判定です（#2448）。レビューの本文は表の下の折りたたみで読めます（#2488）。

<!-- issue-deck-review-detail:start issue=248 -->

> ## 総評: LGTM
>
> ## 変更内容の確認
> `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:148` の `ssh -p "${SSH_PORT}" "${USERNAME}@${HOST}"` にリモートコマンド `bash -s` を明示的に追加する1行の修正。Issue #248（guchi-apps/question#63起点）の原因分析（リモートコマンド無しの `ssh` はsshd側でログインシェルとして起動され、VPSの `/etc/profile.d/signaly_login_notify.sh` が読まれて本番デプロイのたびに誤ってSSHログイン通知が飛ぶ）に対して、対応案どおり `bash -s` を渡している。同一Issueに書かれている横断確認（`guchi-apps/myroom` の `deploy.yml:203` が同じパターンで解決済み）とも一致する。
>
> - **Issue要件充足**: 満たしている。差分は指摘された1箇所のみで、Issue外の変更は無い
> - **副作用の確認**: `bash -s` はログイン・非対話シェルになるため `/etc/profile`（および `/etc/profile.d/`）を経由したPATH等に依存する処理が無いか確認した。ヒアドキュメント内から呼ばれる `deploy/ensure_venv.sh`（`python3`・`.venv/bin/pip`）、`deploy/restart-service.sh`（`systemctl --user`）、`deploy/health-check.sh`（`curl`・`journalctl --user`）はいずれもシステム標準コマンドのみを使っており、ログインシェル固有のPATH拡張（nvm/pyenv等のshim）に依存していないことを確認した。PR本文に書かれている検証内容と一致する
> - **ヒアドキュメントの互換性**: `<< EOF`（クォート無し）のままなので、クライアント側変数展開と `\$` エスケープによるリモート側評価の挙動は変更前後で変わらない。`ssh` のリモートコマンドを変えただけで、渡す内容自体は変更していないため問題なし

> 特に無し。テストプランに「本番デプロイを1回通して確認する」とあるが、これは受動的な観察（通知が飛ばないことの確認）であり、ユーザーが能動的に実行すべき手作業ではないため、`71.manual-step` Issueの起票は不要と判断した。

author: randomcat4
body:
## Problem and resulting behavior

The finite-block tool bounds the full-subset Shannon entropy cost of deleting off-block DPP kernel entries. It gives a spectral bound, an explicit quadratic bound requiring a buffer on the block pinching B only, and the correct asymmetric Jensen-gap interval. Original K may be singular.

## Frozen theorem and independent verification

VERIFIED for the stated finite tool. A fresh GPT-5.5 xhigh context returned CORRECT for the theorem, both boundary families and the bounded exact-rational helper. It independently reran the 13 checks and both path examples. The verifier did not participate in creation or repair.

Audited candidate: `31143e0925f95e1c05b2165a71c0d541a20be3ef`. Current evidence commit: `27dda692856da210e23ae74ce267b813d3221822`. The frozen statement, proof, boundary derivations and helper source are unchanged; the later commit adds the audit and status metadata. See `research/T2/verifications/fresh_v1.md` and `research/T2/verdict.md`.

## Reproduction and actual coverage

Run `python3 research/T2/artifacts/demo_checks.py` (standard library). The helper uses exact rational arithmetic, finite-series logarithm enclosures, and outward rounding. Thirteen checks passed; path demonstrations at 8 and 64 coordinates completed; direct full-law crosschecks only at dimensions 2 and 4 (60 masses). The 64-coordinate case evaluates 384 block masses and encloses its Jensen gap in [4.812262390708765909, 5.974762390708765910] nats. The proof separately establishes a positive lower bound for every permitted path size and a broader finite-graph family.

Boundary contribution: ten exact-law checks and five floating scaling diagnostics; those diagnostics are not interval certificates. No random draws, large scan, GPU, or system package installation. Structural artifact validation passed. No Lean verification was performed.

## Limits and value

B1 disproves dimension-free total entropy continuity from operator norm alone; B2 disproves a universal quadratic constant without a fixed block spectral buffer. Neither refutes global DPP concavity. The positive-gap application is not a concavity counterexample.

The tool is a reusable consequence of standard entropy machinery. No entropy-rate, realification, Hessian, global-concavity or novelty claim. The exact helper is restricted to rational real-symmetric input with sufficient Gershgorin tests. README clarifies two reporting conventions noted by the verifier: external resource caps and one-block enumeration accounting.

Refs #2. First bounded milestone complete; kept Draft for review. No expansion into a new research unit or large scan.

author: vanzue
body:
## Summary

Prevent concurrent helpers from corrupting the append-only agent-pane session index.

During integration testing for https://github.com/microsoft/intelligent-terminal/pull/884, two helpers created sessions at the same time and their JSON records were interleaved at the byte level. The index then contained invalid JSON, so the affected live agent panes could not be resolved through the index.

This is a separate, main-based fix. It does not include the GetPaneContext optimization or change the index schema, runtime paths, duplicate handling, or historical records.

## Changes

- Serialize each complete JSON record and its newline into memory before writing, instead of streaming JSON formatting directly into the shared file.
- Hold an exclusive cross-process file lock across the append and any partial-write retries.
- Coordinate WTA readers with shared locks so a concurrent Windows byte-range lock does not make them read an incomplete index.
- Log shared-lock failures while preserving the existing graceful empty-map behavior.
- Add deterministic coverage for complete-record writes, short writes and error propagation, and 256 concurrent appends through independently opened file handles.

## Validation

- The deterministic regression fails before the fix because the first write contains only `{`, not a complete newline-terminated JSON record.
- Focused index tests after the final change: **13 passed**.
- Full WTA suite: **2,080 passed, 1 ignored**, before the final logging-only refinement; the focused suite was rerun afterward.
- Rust formatting and diff checks pass.
- All tests use temporary fixtures. No user index repair, settings changes, package deployment, or live-session migration is included.

The already-corrupted historical records are left untouched; this change prevents new interleaving.

author: techmefr
body:
Both external search drivers answered every search with an empty page while
reporting success, each for a different reason, and neither had a single test.
Found while verifying the version bumps in #1 against real servers, then
reproduced on Elasticsearch 8.17 and Meilisearch v1.11 -- the versions from
before that upgrade -- so both predate it.

Elasticsearch left `tenantId` to dynamic mapping, which types a first-seen
string as analysed `text` with a `.keyword` sub-field. A `term` filter on
analysed text matches nothing, so the tenant filter excluded every document,
including the caller's own. The field is now declared `keyword` before the
first document lands, which is what it is: an identifier to match exactly.
A collection created by the previous version keeps the mapping it was born
with -- Elasticsearch cannot retype a live field -- and has to be reindexed to
pick this up.

Meilisearch was handed documents carrying both `id` and `tenantId`, two
candidates ending in "id", so primary-key inference failed and the server
rejected every indexing task. The driver never read the task it enqueued, so
`index()` returned as a success on a write that had been refused, and the
collection stayed empty forever. The primary key is now named, every task is
awaited, and a task that ends in any state but `succeeded` raises
`MeilisearchTaskFailedException` rather than passing for success. `index()` is
therefore slower by the length of the task -- the cost of knowing whether the
write happened.

Neither failure leaked across tenants: both failed closed, which is also why
they went unnoticed for so long.

Both drivers now have integration specs that run against real servers, because
a mock would have agreed with every call these two got wrong -- the shapes were
valid, the client accepted them, and the failure was entirely in the server's
answer. Reverting either driver turns 12 of the 13 tests red.

The specs sit in `packages/<module>/test` rather than `src/runtime`, so they do
not ship to a project installing the module, and they run under their own jest
config (`test/jest-search.json`, `pnpm run test:search`) rather than the root
suite, which has no engines to talk to. A new `search-drivers` CI job runs them
with Elasticsearch and Meilisearch as services, on the same images the two
modules ship in their compose files.

author: dcotelo
body:
Fixes #344. Takes fix directions **(1)** and **(3)** from the issue, as it suggested.

## The bug

`seedDemoData` wrote both category lists absolutely:

```ts
cmds.push(["SET", AI_CATEGORIES_KEY, JSON.stringify(DEMO_AI_CATEGORIES)]);   // ["AI"]
cmds.push(["SET", CLASSIC_CATEGORIES_KEY, JSON.stringify(DEMO_CLASSIC_CATEGORIES)]);
```

The challenges are written per-field and keyed by id, so they survive and the admin panel keeps listing them — but `challenge-board.tsx` filters with `categories.includes(c.category)`, so anything under a dropped category is simply not rendered. On the live box that cost three authored AI challenges, 850 points, and the viewer's three solves of them, under a panel reading `1 category · 5 challenges`.

Master reset is not a way back — the Danger-zone copy correctly promises it *keeps* authored categories, so the list it keeps is the seeded one.

## The fix

**Union, not replace** (`unionSeedCategories`): the organizer's order verbatim, then any demo category not already present, matched case-insensitively — the same rule `setCategories` and classic's `importBundle` already use.

**Each seeded challenge is written under the spelling the union kept.** This is the half a surviving list alone would not have covered: seeding `"AI"` onto a board that spells it `"ai"` would store rows under a name absent from the list, which is exactly as invisible to the board's exact-match filter as before the fix. Same `canon` map `importBundle` builds, for the same reason.

**The pre-write read throws** rather than treating a failed `GET` as "no categories yet". That reading is how the same key was wiped through the import path in #261, and `upstashPipeline` does not throw on a per-command error — this path writes over the key it just read, so the two answers must not arrive as one value.

**A union over the 50-category cap refuses, writing nothing.** Trimming the overflow would orphan the demo challenges naming those categories — #344 from the other side — and storing an over-cap list would make `setCategories` reject every later category edit. Refusing loses nothing; the seed is a demo convenience.

## Saying so when it happens anyway (direction 3)

An organizer can still reach "challenges in no listed category" by removing a category by hand, or importing a bundle that spells one differently. So:

- `ModuleInventory` gains `unlisted`, counted by one shared helper for both boards on the **exact** match the board itself uses.
- The module panel renders an amber warning naming the count and what to do, and **opens the checklist** — the control that fixes it is in there.
- The status line appends `· 3 not on the board` and goes amber. It does *not* say "setup incomplete": every checklist step really was done, and sending the organizer back there would send them somewhere with nothing wrong.
- Nothing is claimed before the panel reports (`unlisted` undefined → silent), so a healthy board is never accused on first paint — the same rule the rest of this component already follows.
- The seed's confirmation copy names the authored content it touches. "Adds to" is now literally true, and it says the demo categories survive a master reset.

## Tests

- **`admin-store.seed.test.ts`** — 5 new cases: order-preserving union; no duplicate whatever the casing; **every seeded row's category is in the stored list**; a failed category read writes *nothing*; an over-cap union writes *nothing*. The pipeline-count assertion is now a shape assertion (reads are single commands, the last call is the write batch) so enabling another module does not mean editing a number.
- **`admin-module-setup.test.tsx`** — 5 new cases: silent until reported, the counts, the status-line suffix, the amber status line (asserted on the summary span — the per-step labels stay green, which is the point), and singular/zero.
- **classic + ai controls** — `unlisted` in the inventory, including the exact-match case.

Mutation-checked both halves: restoring the absolute `SET` fails 3 cases; removing only the `canon` lookup fails 1.

## Verification

- `pnpm exec vitest run` — **3431 passed**, 35 skipped
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm lint` — clean
- Live Lua/upstash suites against redis + srh at CI's pinned digests: **8 files, 38 passed** (`admin-store.ts` is a store, and those suites skip locally without the env vars)

## Not verified in a browser

The warning is asserted on rendered markup, not a live page: `/admin` needs an organizer session, and authenticating is off-limits for me — the same blocker recorded on #321.

author: rickfelix
body:
## Summary
The worktree cap (`MAX_WORKTREE_COUNT=40`) was only checked inside the three canonical creator scripts (`worktree-manager.js` `createWorkTypeWorktree`, `resolve-sd-workdir.js`, `qf-start.js`) that call `enforceWorktreeQuota()` before shelling out to `git worktree add`. Any other path that shells out directly bypassed the quota entirely — two such registrations landed at 48 and 49 against the cap of 40 on 2026-09-05.

Two-part fix, per the QF's own FIX text:
1. **`scripts/hooks/pre-tool-enforce.cjs` (ENFORCEMENT 12e):** this block already intercepts every `git worktree add` Bash command for the sibling-placement guard. Added one call to `enforceWorktreeQuota()` there, reusing the `repoRoot` already resolved for the sibling check, so every registration path meets the same count and is refused with the same error text (`quotaErr.message`, from `createQuotaExceededError`) a canonical creator would produce. Fail-open on any other internal error, matching the rest of this enforcement block.
2. **`.claude/commands/checkin.md`:** the `self_claimed_qf` recipe told a self-claiming worker to run a raw `git worktree add` directly (one of the QF's own candidate root causes). Changed to route through `node scripts/qf-start.js <qf>` instead — the canonical, already quota-enforcing QF entry point (mirrors `sd-start.js` for SDs).

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/unit/enforcement-worktree-add-sibling-guard.test.js` — extended with 3 new tests mirroring `tests/unit/worktree-reaper/qf-quota-relocation.test.js`'s established convention (source-order/static-content assertions for these top-level CLI/hook scripts, rather than spinning up 40 real worktrees): the call is wired into the ENF-12e block, blocks via `auditAndExit(_, 2, _)` with the quota error text on `WORKTREE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, and is fail-open on any other error. All 11 tests in the file (8 existing + 3 new) pass.
- [x] Existing live subprocess tests (`ALLOWS an in-tree git worktree add`, etc.) still pass — confirms the new quota check doesn't falsely block a normal add under today's real (well-under-cap) worktree count.
- [x] `tests/unit/worktree-reaper/qf-quota-relocation.test.js` (unrelated but adjacent) still passes.

author: chronosbvrx
body:
## Resumen del Cambio

Este PR resuelve de manera definitiva la regresión donde la herramienta de **Vacaciones** (y otros componentes montados) continuaba mostrando datos del tarjetón o trabajador anterior tras importar y confirmar un nuevo tarjetón.

### Acciones Realizadas
1. **Hook Canónico de Invalidación (`usePayslipInvalidation`)**:
   - Escucha el evento unificado de broadcast `nomina_payslip_updated`.
   - Incorpora debounce configurable (150ms por defecto) para evitar ráfagas o refrescos duplicados.
   - Invoca `router.refresh()` de forma segura con Next.js App Router (y fallback a prueba de fallos para entornos de test).
   - Admite callback local `onInvalidate` para componentes que manejan estado propio.

2. **Ruta del Servidor de Vacaciones (`src/app/(dashboard)/vacaciones/page.tsx`)**:
   - Forzada ejecución dinámica con `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` y `export const revalidate = 0` para garantizar que cada re-evaluación consulte `getWorkerContext()` sin quedar en caché RSC estática.

3. **Componente Asistente de Vacaciones (`VacationWizard`)**:
   - Conectado a `usePayslipInvalidation({ refreshRouter: true })`.
   - Implementa comparación de huella (`contextFingerprint`) sobre matrícula, nombre, último periodo, fecha de vencimiento, categoría, antigüedad, marca de continuidad y salario mensual integrado.

author: dkounal
body:
When the DB connection dies at the moment a transaction is started, TransactionBegin() leaks state in two independent places. Both leaks are permanent: from that point on every TRestBatch send on that storage fails, until the process is restarted. 

Leak 1 — the session flag is never released
TRestStorageExternal.TransactionBegin (mormot.orm.sql.pas:1924):

if (aTable = fStoredClass) and
   inherited TransactionBegin(aTable, SessionID) then
  result := fProperties.SharedTransaction(SessionID, transBegin) <> nil
else
  result := false;

inherited is TRestOrm.TransactionBegin (mormot.orm.rest.pas:2376), which sets fTransactionActiveSession := SessionID and returns True. If SharedTransaction() then returns nil, the function returns False — but the session flag stays set. Every later call is refused at the inherited check, so this storage can never begin a transaction again.

Leak 2 — the entry is registered before the transaction is started
TSqlDBConnectionProperties.SharedTransaction (mormot.db.sql.pas:3724) registers the entry inside the lock (SessionID, RefCount := 1, Connection), and only afterwards, outside the lock, runs Connect / StartTransaction. If that raises, the handler sets result := nil and swallows the exception. The entry stays behind with RefCount = 1, describing a transaction that was never started.

This is worse than an error. With leak 1 fixed but leak 2 present, the next transBegin for the same SessionID takes the "found" branch and simply inc(t^.RefCount), returning success — so the caller writes outside any transaction, silently. Note the exit in that branch: a nested begin never reaches the SQL, so only the registering call can fail this way.

## Summary

@samcantrill

Implement configured foreground-container deadlines with positive namespace settlement. The two existing managed process-group owners retain capacity until containment, not merely launcher exit. Timeout and unresolved cleanup reject worker outputs before reading them, and frozen timeout metadata retains its classification and durable outcome.

Independent implementation review and the expressly authorized cleanup-budget correction verification are complete, with no remaining findings. Refreshed develop includes PR #281; this phase's reviewed code delta is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Enabled timeouts use the verified built-in Linux/SingularityCE 3.10.4 PID-namespace path; unsupported selections fail explicitly.
- [x] Cleanup uses one non-renewable deadline; delayed and repeated containment cannot extend it, and forced KILL can only shorten it.
- [x] Managed group identity remains anchored through the final signal, followed by one reap and permanently observation-only settlement checks.
- [x] Capacity remains held while containment is uncertain; early worker success cannot override timeout or cleanup failure.
- [x] No enabled timeout adds no namespace/version restriction; unmapped CPU/RAM adds no runtime limit flags.
- [x] Fresh local gates, real-container acceptance and independent correctness verification pass.

## Implementation Notes

The direct runner stays in its inherited group and observes a creation-linked namespace-init pidfd. The existing legacy and resident managed owners share a private group handle, not a new supervisor. Public protocols, durable schemas, resource registries and StageContext owner values are unchanged.

The shared reliability reader accepts Mapping across frozen result metadata. Tests exercise normal/startup timeout, cooperating and TERM-resistant descendants, root-first exit, interruption, identity uncertainty/reuse, one-shot signaling/reaping, request-stop/shutdown, lease retention, and a real worker success file written before expiry.

Five deterministic deadline regressions failed before correction and pass afterward. Independent verification closes that finding at `6afbaef`. Upstream refresh `f1aaa9c` incorporates `43d02a1` without overlapping changed paths; the complete phase delta before subsequent docs updates is byte-identical across bases.

## Tests And Validation

Validated combined production/test revision: `f1aaa9c`; subsequent commits change roadmap metadata only.

| Check | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original correction / affected owners | 89 passed at `6afbaef`; independent closure | `build/cleanup-budget-targeted.xml` |

Final receipts and built distributions are preserved in the integration worktree under `build/stage-38-p3-f1aaa9c`; copied summary and composition XML checksums match the originals.

## Risks / Follow-Ups

- Runtime qualification is deliberately bounded to the evidenced foreground mode; other runtimes and injected runners are not admitted with enabled timeouts.
- Actual outer-owner death and hostile payloads are outside the ownership contract. Uncertain post-reap group presence conservatively retains capacity.

author: oc-jg
body:
`docs/ASSESSMENT.md` closed with a "Still open" list, which is a residue rather than a plan: no order, no exit criteria, and no distinction between work that is blocked and work nobody has chosen. `docs/ROADMAP.md` replaces it with seven milestones, each anchored to the file and line that shows the gap is real.

Docs only — no source or behaviour change. `test:contract` and `test:unit` pass (126 assertions).

## The four gaps it is built on

These came out of reading the tree rather than the docs, and they are the spine of the sequence.

**The primary input path is the only untested one.** `.ipt` now arrives as STEP — `src/app/main.js:61` routes an Inventor part through `parseSTEP`, the same function a dropped `.step` uses at `:67`. There is no STEP fixture anywhere in `test/`, so `src/geometry/step.js` has no automated coverage at all while both suites drive STL.

**B-rep faces are extracted and then thrown away.** `src/geometry/step.js:96` builds `faceGroups`, `:119` returns it, and nothing consumes it. That is why `corners` carries `weight: 0` (`src/rules/scoring.js:82`), and why the README and `src/app/bridge.js:9-11` both promise per-face draft that `src/analysis/mesh.js:9` still measures per triangle.

**The Inventor loop has no test.** `grep -i bridge test/*.mjs` returns nothing. The flagship feature is hand-verified only, against a dependency on a separate release cycle.

**Exports carry no build identity.** `src/export/json.js:11-13` records session and timestamp but not the build, so `src/rules/compare.js` — which caveats material, mode and check-set changes at `:51`, `:54`, `:59` — cannot raise the one that matters most: the rules moved, not the part. Findings have no stable ids either, so "point 4" in a factory's DFM reply is a position in a list rather than a handle.

## Milestones

| | Milestone | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| — | Release discipline (tags, CHANGELOG, lint, perf budget) | 2–3 d |
| R2.1 | Trust the STEP path | 3–5 d |
| R2.2 | Features, not triangles | 1–2 wk |
| R2.3 | The Inventor loop under test | 4–6 d |
| R2.4 | Numbers that get quoted (cycle time, cost) | 1 wk + a decision |
| R2.5 | Two-shot and FPC earn their weights | 1–2 wk |
| R2.6 | Findings that survive leaving the tool | 4–6 d |

Release discipline first because it is cheap and makes everything after it traceable. Then R2.1, which unblocks R2.2 and R2.3 — those two touch different directories and can run in parallel. Every exit criterion is a test, not the existence of code.

## Decisions that need a human

1. **`coolK`: half-wall or full wall?** (`src/core/materials.js:7`) A factor of four in every cycle time, and everything costed from it. Raise it at the start of R2.1, not when R2.4 comes up.
2. **Vendor the OpenCascade module for tests?** Gates the STEP fixture, and through it most of R2.1 and R2.2.
3. **`--vendor` as the committed default?** 900 kB of file size against two fewer third-party runtime loads and the SRI question.
4. **Does `corners`, once measurable, take weight from the other checks or widen the budget?** The eight default checks sum to exactly 100 today.

## Two things found on the way

- `test/offline.mjs:106` tolerates blocked `fonts.` requests, so the `--vendor` build — whose whole purpose is needing no network — still reaches for Google Fonts and silently falls back to system faces. A report sent to a supplier renders in a different typeface depending on their connection.
- `src/geometry/weld.js:169` sets `faceGroups: null` unconditionally. Harmless today because the STL path never had them, but it will bite whoever wires up R2.2.

The document also records what has been decided **against**, so it stops resurfacing as an oversight: a computed parting line, flow simulation, authentication on a localhost-only bridge, three.js past r128, and scoring melt against HDT.

`README.md` gains a short pointer, and `ASSESSMENT.md`'s "Still open" list is marked superseded while being kept as the record of where Phase 4 ended.

body:
Deux défauts signalés par Charlie sur l'écran de **Vente flash**.

## 1. « la facture à droite n'est pas parfaitement centrée »

`.dvf-feuille` est un article flex : son `flex-shrink` par défaut la ramenait à la largeur du cadre — **337 px mesurés** — pendant que son **contenu** restait à 794. L'échelle tourne autour de `transform-origin: top center`, donc autour du centre de la **boîte** : la facture sortait **97 px trop à droite**, rognée par l'`overflow: hidden` du cadre.

Le devis y échappait *par hasard* (la largeur minimale de son tableau retenait le rétrécissement), pas par construction — d'où la largeur forcée en JS côté vente, qui ne pouvait pas gagner contre un rétrécissement. `flex: 0 0 auto` retire la cause au lieu du symptôme.

| | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| marge gauche / droite | 97,0 / −97,1 px | −0,06 / −0,07 px |
| papier dans son cadre | 337,9 px pour 337,7 (débordant) | 337,9 px pour 337,7 (rempli) |

Vérifié aux trois positions de la poignée (78 %, 57 %, 30 %) et à l'échelle 1 en 1920 px : l'écart entre les deux marges ne dépasse jamais 0,1 px.

Deux corollaires :

- **la largeur A4 devient un jeton**, `--dvf-a4`, écrit une seule fois dans `devis-flash.css` — les deux écrans en tirent leur facteur d'échelle au lieu de recopier `794` chacun de leur côté ;
- **la gouttière est réservée des deux côtés** : la barre de défilement qui apparaît dès que le papier dépasse d'un écran mangeait ses 15 px à droite seulement, décalait la feuille d'une demi-barre et faisait osciller la mise à l'échelle (mesuré sur le devis : figée à 325,9 px de papier dans 337,7 px de cadre).

## 2. « à la fin je ne peux rien faire et émettre la facture est grisé »

Le bouton était désactivé sur **quatre** conditions et n'en disait **aucune**. La plus coûteuse — le **mode de règlement** — vit dans la carte « Fiscalité et règlement », **repliée par défaut** : on remplissait le client et les articles, on arrivait au bout, et le seul bouton de l'écran refusait sans un mot. La vente n'atteignait jamais le planning.

Les quatre `dire(...)` d'`emettreFacture` disaient pourtant chacun le leur — mais ils étaient **inatteignables** : un bouton grisé ne se clique pas.

Désormais :

- ce qui manque est **une seule liste** (`manquePourEmettre`), lue par le compteur de l'en-tête, l'infobulle du bouton et le clic — deux listes de champs obligatoires s'écartent l'une de l'autre sans que rien ne le dise ;
- le bouton ne se grise plus que sur un **fait** (facture déjà émise, émission en cours), jamais sur un manque ;
- le clic dit **tout** ce qui manque d'un coup, **ouvre la carte** concernée, y amène l'écran et pose le curseur dans le champ ;
- le message de réussite nomme le planning : « Facture NNN émise — la vente est au planning ».

L'invariant métier ne bouge pas : pas de mode de règlement et pas de ligne sans prix, pas d'émission (§4 du spec).

**Même traitement sur le devis flash**, à un clic de là : le nom du client y est dans une carte repliée elle aussi. Au passage, son bouton disait autre chose que son garde-fou (`dossierId && !repriseDe` contre `dossierId`) — après l'enregistrement d'une reprise il restait vivant et ne répondait plus.

## Vérification

- `npm test` vert — 157 vérifications, dont les nouveaux garde-fous sur la largeur de la feuille et sur l'état des deux boutons ;
- mesuré au navigateur sur le serveur local (1280×800 et 1920×1000), les deux écrans, avant/après ajout d'articles : aucune erreur console, papier centré à 0,07 px près.

⚠️ **Pas de merge sur `main` avant validation en local par le patron** — le service `web` est branché sur `main`.

author: jianxing-chen
body:
## Problem

CI is currently red on `main` and on open PRs (e.g. run [34116303775](https://github.com/54yyyu/zotero-mcp/actions/runs/34116303775): 25 failures — all of `tests/test_rate_limit_guard.py` across the 5-job matrix):

```
httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '429 Too Many Requests' for url 'https://api.zotero.org/users/1/items'
```

## Root cause

pyzotero 1.15 removed `TooManyRetriesError` (only `TooManyRequestsError` remains). The internal retry path then raises a raw `httpx.HTTPStatusError` on a persistent 429, which `find_existing_items` does not catch — the exact escape the `>=1.13.5` floor was added for (urschrei/pyzotero#352).

This is not hypothetical: with pyzotero 1.15.1 installed, all five rate-limit tests fail; with 1.14.x they pass (verified on both 1.15.1 and 1.14.0 locally, and in CI logs on both sides of the version bump).

## Fix

- Cap `pyzotero>=1.13.5,<1.15` in `pyproject.toml`, extending the existing floor's comment.
- Apply the same pin in the workflow's test-dependency install line: `pip install -e . --no-deps` skips pyproject's constraints entirely, so the unpinned install resolves 1.15.1 regardless of the cap. Also pinned `bibtexparser>=1.4,<2` there to match pyproject (v1-only API), for the same bypass reason.

## Notes

- The cap is a stopgap; a follow-up could adapt `find_existing_items`' error handling to 1.15's exception shape and lift it.
- With these two pins the full 5-job matrix goes green again (same fix verified end-to-end on my fork's identical workflow: [green run](https://github.com/jianxing-chen/zotero-mcp/actions/runs/34122584767)).

- `ivor.micallef@telenetgroup.be`
- `lode.lauwers@telenetgroup.be`

Branched from `master` after #10 merged, so this is a clean two-line addition rather than a re-run of the previous three.

Same three files as #10, because the allowlist has three representations that have to agree:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `allowed-emails.txt` | source of truth |
| `lib/allowed-emails.generated.js` | mirror the serverless API falls back to when it cannot read the txt |
| `share/auth-config.js` | client config the gate loads |

Written with the project's own `addAllowedEmails()` and `npm run build` rather than by hand, so the formatting matches what `npm run invites` produces.

## Testing

- [x] `allowed-emails.txt` holds all six, sorted, header intact
- [x] `share/auth-config.js` regenerated — "wrote share/auth-config.js 6 emails with Clerk key"
- [x] `lib/allowed-emails.generated.js` mirrors the txt exactly

## Risks & Considerations

- **This widens access for everyone**, not just the two people named — it is your gate, so flagging it rather than assuming.

- `share/auth-config.js` is a build artefact Vercel regenerates on deploy, so committing it is slightly redundant. Kept in sync so the checked-out repo matches what ships — happy to gitignore it instead if you would prefer.

author: ntdatt812
body:
TypeScript 6 reports this as an error:

```
Option 'baseUrl' is deprecated and will stop functioning in TypeScript 7.0.
  Specify compilerOption '"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"' to silence this error.
```

The repo pins `typescript@5.9.2`, so `npm run typecheck` is quiet today. An editor running a newer TypeScript flags it now, and it becomes a hard failure the moment the pin moves to 7.

## Why removing it rather than silencing it

`baseUrl` here only anchors `paths`, and `paths` has not needed it since TypeScript 4.4 — entries resolve relative to the tsconfig that declares them. That makes `"src/*"` → `"./src/*"` the only other change.

`"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"` would also make the message go away, but it buys one major version and has to be revisited. This makes the config correct instead.

## Why it is safe

`baseUrl` has a second effect — it lets bare specifiers resolve against the base directory — so removing it can break imports that quietly relied on that. Checked: there are no `from "src/…"`-style imports anywhere under `src/`, only relative ones and the `@/` alias.

Build and tests never read this setting at all. Both `vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` declare the alias themselves:

```ts
resolve: { alias: { "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src") } }
```

so the change is type-level only.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors before, 0 after**, with `@/` imports in **250 files** under `src/` still resolving — if the alias had broken, that would be hundreds of `Cannot find module` errors, not silence.
- Re-ran the same config under TypeScript **6.0.3**: the deprecation is gone, and no new diagnostic replaces it.

## `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests`

The Go cluster extends `config:recommended`, not `config:best-practices`, so it never had GitHub Action SHA pinning that every other repo gets. Adds it. `pinact` in the toolchain already pins on write; this makes Renovate keep the digests updated.

## `:automergePatch`

The `Go dependencies` group is `minor` + `patch`, but only `:automergeMinor` / `:automergeDigest` were extended — so a grouped PR containing any patch update would stall and never automerge. Add `:automergePatch` to close the gap.

author: edmonddantes
body:
Fixes the php-async issue #280: `fread()` inside a coroutine failing with
`Read of 18446744073709543424 bytes failed with async IO error` during an S3
upload, with the body arriving empty.

## What breaks

`php_stream_fill_read_buffer()` derives a target address and a length from
`readbuf`, `readpos` and `writepos`, hands them to `ops->read`, and credits the
result back to `writepos`. Upstream relies on that sequence being indivisible.
`php_stdiop_read()` parks the coroutine inside `ops->read`, so a second
coroutine reading the same handle derives the same address and the same length
from a state the first one has not finished updating.

Both reads then fill one buffer offset and both credits land on one `writepos`:

```
A: buf = rb+0, len = 8192  -> ops->read -> parks
B: buf = rb+0, len = 8192  -> ops->read -> parks     (same state, same address)
A wakes: writepos = 0    + 8192 = 8192
B wakes: writepos = 8192 + 8192 = 16384              (readbuflen is 8192)
```

Two consequences, both reproduced on Linux:

* data is lost and duplicated — 1024 distinct records out of 2000 in the
  regression test, while the byte count still adds up, which is why the S3
  upload saw a wrong body rather than an error;
* `writepos` passes `readbuflen`, so `readbuflen - writepos` wraps around zero
  and `ops->read` gets a length near 2^64. The async layer clamps it to
  `INT_MAX` and hands it to `uv_fs_read` against an 8 KB allocation: a heap
  overflow on Linux, and on Windows the failure from the issue.

## The fix

A per-stream lock covers the whole derive-read-credit sequence.
`php_stream_read()`, `php_stream_fill_read_buffer()`, `php_stream_get_line()`,
`php_stream_get_record()`, `php_stream_write()` and `php_stream_seek()` take it.
It is recursive for its owner, because the buffered API re-enters itself (a seek
emulated through reads, a userspace wrapper reading its own stream).

The lock is an event, and its callback vector is the queue of waiters in arrival
order. Releasing the lock invokes the head callback directly — no notify, so the
other waiters are not woken only to go back to sleep — and that callback takes
ownership inside the call, so a coroutine arriving between the release and the
wakeup finds the lock taken and queues behind instead of overtaking. The event
carries an order-preserving `del_callback` of its own: the core
`zend_async_callbacks_remove()` fills the hole with the last element ("order is
NOT preserved"), which would run the queue as a stack.

`php_stream` grows one pointer; owner, recursion depth and the queue live inside
the event. Nothing in `Zend/` is touched.

`fill_read_buffer` also refuses to call `ops->read` when `writepos` is past the
end of the buffer, so a residual accounting error degrades to a failed read
rather than to a read into unallocated memory.

With async off, outside a coroutine, and in scheduler context every lock call is
a no-op — synchronous behaviour is unchanged, and a stream no coroutine touches
never allocates the event.

## Use after free on close

A coroutine parked inside `ops->read` or `ops->write` can return to a stream that
is already gone: another coroutine closed the handle, `php_stdiop_close()`
deferred the free because the parked coroutine still held a pin, and the unpin on
the way out performed it.

The lock helpers therefore do not reach the lock through `stream->buffer_lock`
any more. `stream_buffer_lock()` hands the caller the lock itself and takes a
reference on it, so the lock outlives the stream, and its closed flag is what the
buffered paths test after every call that can park — instead of touching the
stream again.

`php_stream_write_buffer()` had the same defect on its own: after a close during
a parked write, its `out:` label read `stream->eof` and
`PHP_STREAM_CONTEXT(stream)` from freed memory. Verified with a poisoned free —
SIGSEGV in `php_stream_write_buffer` at the notify line, reached from `fwrite()`
in one coroutine while another closed the handle. Clean afterwards.

Three more paths of the same kind are closed:

* `php_stream_flush()` reaches the write-filter chain, which writes through
  `ops->write` and therefore parks. It now takes the lock and hands it down.
* `stream_seek_locked()` read `stream->writefilters.head` after that flush
  regardless of its outcome; it now returns -1 when the flush lost the stream.
* a persistent stream outlives the request, but its lock and the callback vector
  inside it come from the request allocator. The request-end pass over the
  persistent list drops the lock, so the next request builds its own instead of
  reading a dangling pointer.

## Tests

* `tests/io/085-shared_handle_concurrent_reads.phpt` (true-async/php-async#281):
  red before this change (`unique: 1024` of 2000), green after.
* `tests/io/086-close_during_io.phpt` (same PR): reads and writes while another
  coroutine closes the handle. Segfaults on the previous code under a poisoned
  free, green here.
* `ext/async` suite: 1298 tests, 3 failures, all three pre-existing and caused
  by relative includes that leave the tree because `ext/async` is a symlink.
* php-src `ext/standard/tests/file`, `ext/standard/tests/streams`, `ext/zlib`,
  `ext/phar`: 1825 tests, one failure
  (`ext/zlib/tests/filter_broken_object_options.phpt`), which fails the same way
  on a build from before this change.
* Stress: six coroutines over a 3.2 MB file of distinct records, byte-exact on
  every run; the randomised mixed-chunk fuzzer clean on every seed that used to
  corrupt.

## Not covered here

* `php_stream_flush()`, `_php_stream_copy_to_mem()`,
  `_php_stream_copy_to_stream_ex()` and `php_stream_passthru()` hold state across
  several locked calls without holding the lock themselves; `flush()` also
  reaches the write-filter chain outside the lock.
* `filter.c` reallocates `readbuf` when a filter is appended, and `cast.c`
  resets the buffer — both can still run while an owner is parked.
* Two coroutines reading one socketpair pass, but a variant with all data already
  in the kernel buffer hangs. That hang predates this change and is still open.

author: patrykomiotek
body:
## What

The documentation site still carried the old palette — crimson as `--ifm-color-primary`, and the pre-navy Ragen blue for the footer and hero heading. It now takes the navy scale from `ragen-website`'s `src/config/brand.ts` value for value, so the marketing site, `apps/web` (#931) and the docs agree.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| primary (light) | `#cb1d3d` crimson | `brand-600` `#394d9d` |
| primary (dark) | `#e85575` | `brand-300` `#9eabe0` |
| footer | `#252d53` (dead — see below) | `brand-950` `#1c244b` |
| dark page / surface | `#0f1117` / `#181a24` (dead) | `slate-950` / `slate-900` |
| body copy greys | `#555` `#666` `#999` `#aaa` | the website's slate ramp |

**Crimson is deliberately left out.** The design system rations it to the conversion CTA and small ornaments, and forbids it as a text colour in any form — and `--ifm-color-primary` *is* a text colour here: it paints links, the active sidebar item and the active table-of-contents entry. A documentation site has no conversion CTA, so crimson survives only inside the logotype asset. "If in doubt it is navy."

## Three colours that never rendered

Swapping the hex values in place would have carried these forward silently. Both are custom-property cascade traps, and neither is visible to typecheck, lint, or the build:

- **The footer.** It read `#252d53` in `:root`, but `footer: { style: 'dark' }` puts `.footer--dark` on the `<footer>` element, and Infima's rule for that class assigns all four footer variables **on that element**. A property set on the element beats one inherited from `:root` whatever the source order — so the footer had been Infima's grey `#303846` the whole time. The tokens now sit on `.footer`.
- **The dark surfaces.** `--ifm-background-color: #0f1117` and `--ifm-background-surface-color` were written under `[data-theme="dark"]` (specificity 0,1,0) while theme-classic sets them under `html[data-theme="dark"]` (0,1,1), which wins regardless of load order — so the dark theme had been Infima's `#1b1b1d`/`#242526`. The block is now `html[data-theme="dark"]`.

Logged as [a lesson](docs/lessons/a-custom-property-override-on-root-loses-to-the-element-that-owns-it.md), since `apps/web`'s `global.css` carries the same trap in a different form.

## Contrast was measured, not assumed

Two choices changed as a result:

- Light primary `brand-600` is 7.7:1 on white — fine as link text and under a white button label. Dark primary is `brand-300` (9.0:1 on the page, 8.0:1 on a card); `brand-600` reaches only 2.6:1 there.
- Because the dark primary is a *text* colour, it cannot carry a white button label — 2.2:1. The solid button therefore gets its own dark-mode rule using the website's dark-section pairing: `brand-600`, hovering to `brand-500`, both above 4.5:1. (The previous dark button was white-on-`#e85575` at 3.51:1, so this fixes an existing shortfall too.)

## Verification

Rendered in both themes and every token read back with `getComputedStyle` — which is how the three dead declarations surfaced. Confirmed after the fix: footer `#1c244b`, page `#020617`, surface `#0f172a`, navbar `#020617`, primary `#9eabe0`, button `#394d9d`, active sidebar item navy-on-navy-tint, body copy on the slate ramp. `npm run docs:build` and `npm run verify` are both green.

A `docs` entry was added to `.claude/launch.json`, which was missing despite the docs site being a first-class app on port 3400.

author: mozzy11
body:
Fixes [OGC-1192](https://uwdigi.atlassian.net/browse/OGC-1192).

**What changed**
- The order dashboard now lists the newest orders first and honours the requested page size, so a freshly saved environmental order shows up immediately (before: the oldest 21 samples, always).
- Editing a sample that has no patient (environmental orders) works instead of failing with a 500; the patient block is simply empty.
- Patient-scoped reports skip samples that have no patient instead of crashing, and reflex handling no longer assumes a patient.
- Reopening an environmental order from the dashboard (`?labNumber=`) loads it again, and its collection date keeps the day and month it was entered with.

**Why**
- The dashboard paged samples oldest-first with the system default page size, so nothing newer than the first page ever reached it — not a patient join, as the ticket suspected. Three separate code paths dereferenced the patient without a null check. The order page only read `?order=` and parsed backend dates before the site's date locale had loaded.

**How it was tested**
- New backend tests: dashboard newest-first / page size / environmental filter, SampleEdit on a patientless sample, patient report guard, reflex helper. New frontend test for loading an order from either URL parameter under both date locales. Full backend and frontend suites green; live check on a dev stack with a patientless environmental sample (dashboard, SampleEdit, order reload, ModifyOrder, patient report).

**Notes**
- §4 of the ticket (empty CONTAINER dropdown) is reference data, not code: that server has no `Sample Container` dictionary rows. They come from `volume/configuration/backend/dictionaries/environmental-site-dictionaries.csv`; a fresh dev install has all seven. On testing, check `dictionary_category` for `Sample Container` and reload the configuration with `force=true` if the file is newer than the recorded checksum (adjacent to OGC-1161).
- Deep links now wait for the site configuration before loading the order; if that request never completes the page stays blank rather than guessing the date order.

author: nikokiru
body:
## Summary

Promotes #287 to production.

The landing page's ranked panel becomes a **trio board**: every trio the model rates as a live chance at the next race, already-happened and brand-new ranked together, with the never-happened ones highlighted and the rest muted and carrying their history behind a hover/tap bubble.

Previously the panel listed only never-happened trios, so a visitor could not tell whether a trio they had in mind was missing because it already happened or because the model rated it too unlikely to list. On the current grid six of the ten likeliest podiums have happened before, and none of them were on the page.

## Changes

- #287 — Show already-happened trios beside the new ones on the landing page

## Testing

Verified on the feature PR before merge into `develop`:

- `pytest -q` — 728 passed, 1 skipped
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` — clean
- `PYTHONPATH=src python -m datalib.validate` — 16 datasets OK
- Chromium against a served `dist/`: 12 rows visible desktop / 6 mobile, bubble escapes the scroll container and flips above near the viewport bottom, no horizontal overflow at 390px, both themes

All 7 required checks passed on #287; this PR additionally runs CodeQL.

### Deployment note

`trioBoard` is an **optional** schema field defaulting to `[]`, and the builder falls back to the previous new-only list when it is empty. This is deliberate: `deploy.yml` builds `main` from committed data and this promotion's three-way merge keeps `main`'s newer `data/`, so the live site may run on a board-less `podigami.json` until the next automated data update lands — at which point the board appears on its own with no further action.

author: christ-roy
body:
Renommage des taches de ce banc d essai pour les rendre auto-porteuses.

## Pourquoi

Nomad nomme le conteneur d apres la **tache**, jamais d apres le job. Une tache
`db` ou `postgres` produit un conteneur `db-<alloc>` qu on ne peut rattacher a
aucun service en lisant Beszel ou `docker ps`. Sur le parc, `db` designait
4 jobs et `postgres` 8. C est ce que Robert voyait dans Beszel.

Regle : `nom_de_tache == nom_du_job`, ou `<job>-<role>`. Elle vit dans le
CLAUDE.md de nomad-veridian et est appliquee par `scripts/lint-nom-tache.py`.

## Comment

Par `scripts/renommer-tache.py`, jamais par un `sed` — un remplacement global
frapperait les commentaires, les chemins et les images. Le script ne touche que
`task "<nom>"` et `task = "<nom>"`, puis **compare le JSON que Nomad produira
avant et apres** et refuse si autre chose a bouge. Chaque appel a rapporte
`JSON identique par ailleurs`.

## Note pour le deploiement

Pour le garde-fou `taches-disparues` de `nomad-v`, un renommage est une
suppression plus un ajout : le refus attendu est legitime. L ecart doit etre
verifie comme etant **exactement** un renommage — une tache disparue pour une
tache apparue, dans le meme groupe — avant d assumer
`--force=taches-disparues`.

Et apres deploiement, **verifier que le banc se rendort** : Sablier ne rendort
pas ce qu il n a pas endormi (son balayage ne tourne qu a son demarrage, et un
job reveille par un deploiement n a aucune session a expirer). Mesure du
2026-09-07 : `cms-staging` est reste eveille indefiniment apres un deploiement
et a demande une reouverture de session par l ingress.

body:
## Problem

`github.com/urfave/cli/v2` is in maintenance mode; v3 is the actively developed line.

## Solution

Move `pkg/app` to `github.com/urfave/cli/v3` (v3.11.0). The API changes applied:

- `cli.App` / `cli.NewApp()` → a `cli.Command` struct literal
- flag `EnvVars: []string{...}` → `Sources: cli.EnvVars(...)`
- action signature `func(*cli.Context) error` → `func(context.Context, *cli.Command) error`
- `Run(args)` → `Run(ctx, args)`

`app.New()` now returns `*cli.Command` instead of `*cli.App` — the only signature change visible to importers of `pkg/app`. `app.Config()` is unchanged.

As a side effect, v3 drops three indirect dependencies that only the v2 docs generator pulled in: `cpuguy83/go-md2man/v2`, `russross/blackfriday/v2` and `xrash/smetrics`.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, plus `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` and `go build -tags nats ./...`
- `go test -tags=test ./...` — all packages pass
- `golangci-lint run` — no new findings
- `--help` output, flag defaults, env var names and `--version` are byte-for-byte equivalent to v2; `kine foo` still fails with `kine does not accept positional arguments, only flags`, and an unknown flag still prints usage and exits 1
- Started the binary against sqlite with `KINE_ENDPOINT` / `KINE_LISTEN_ADDRESS` / `KINE_METRICS_BIND_ADDRESS` set to confirm env-var sources still bind, and that shutdown on SIGTERM is unaffected

## Summary
Human-vs-AI Battleship ("Battle of the Bots") as a static Vite + React + TS app. Pure, Vitest-tested `engine/`, `ai/` (hunt/target with parity), `personality/` (Commander BOLT's lines, cooldowns, no-repeat pools) and `state/` reducer; React only in `ui/` (enforced by an oxlint import rule). 55 tests.

### Polish pass
- **Ships render as continuous hulls with silhouettes** — `Grid` overlays one `Hull` per ship, placed with `gridColumn/gridRow` spans on top of the cell buttons (all cells now have explicit grid positions so overlays don't displace them). New `ShipSilhouette` draws a top-down SVG outline per `ShipKind` (carrier deck + island, battleship turrets, cruiser, submarine with conning tower, destroyer) in `currentColor`, rotated 90° for vertical ships so the bow points up; the hull is still visibly divided into its N squares (dashed dividers) and shows per-square ✕ damage, a short label (incl. `DD` for the destroyer) and a `title` tooltip. The same silhouettes appear in the placement fleet list ("Carrier · 5 squares") and the Fleet HUD. Drag still works via the hull (`onShipPointerDown(ship, cellUnderPointer)`); during a drag the hulls become `pointer-events-none` so `elementFromPoint` hit-tests reach the cells.
- **Enemy board is the focal point** — larger cells (`size="lg"`) with a glowing active frame during the player's turn; own board is `size="md"`, a tappable mini-map (`compact`) on small screens, and shows a red scanning sweep while BOLT aims. Hint bar sits directly above the enemy grid.

- **Pacing** — `AI_THINK_MS = { miss: 500, hit: 750, sunk: 1300 }` instead of a flat 900 ms; the player can tap a cell during BOLT's turn to **queue** the next shot (`QueuedShot{coord, turn}`; fires when the phase returns to `playerTurn` and is discarded once `state.turn` advances).
- **Commander readability** — bubble moved from the top banner to directly under the enemy board on desktop and a fixed bottom dock on mobile; larger text, `LINE_VISIBLE_MS` 3800 → 5500.
- **Sink banner fix (Devin Review)** — newest sink wins: `playerSeq = 2·playerShots − 1`, `aiSeq = 2·aiShots`; previously `lastPlayerShot` always took priority and hid subsequent AI sinks.

author: oliverlaz
body:
### 💡 Overview

`CallState` declared every piece of state three times: the `BehaviorSubject`, a bare `x$: Observable<T>` placeholder carrying the JSDoc, and an assignment in the constructor. Understanding one field meant jumping between three regions ~200 lines apart, and adding one meant touching all three. This collapses it to one subject/observable pair per field, then takes the two performance wins that fall out of it.

### 📝 Implementation notes

- Three module-local helpers keep each declaration to a single line. `subject()` is overloaded so the seeded and empty cases stay honest at the type level: `subject<T>(initial)` yields `BehaviorSubject<T>`, `subject<T>()` yields `BehaviorSubject<T | undefined>`. `duc()` and `shared()` replace the constructor-local `distinctUntilChanged` closure and the six hand-spelled `shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: true })` calls.
- Every observable is now a field initializer, which leaves the constructor holding only the event handler map (215 lines -> 98). The map has to stay in the constructor: it references private arrow-function fields declared further down, so as a field initializer it would capture `undefined` and those events would silently stop updating state.
- The 18 `undefined` entries in `eventHandlers` existed purely as a compile-time guard. They are replaced by an `UnhandledEventType` union in the new `src/store/types.ts`, enforced with `satisfies CallStateEventHandlers`. This keeps the "a newly introduced event fails to compile until it is triaged" guarantee and adds two more: a stale name in the ignore list, and an event that appears in both lists, now also fail to compile. All three are verified by perturbing the source, not assumed.
- `RxUtils.getCurrentValue` no longer wraps its argument in `combineLatest`. That wrapper landed in #1095 to replace `pipe(take(1))`, whose problem was resolving with the *first* rather than the *last* synchronous value; a bare `subscribe` already has that property. It now also reads a `BehaviorSubject`'s value directly instead of subscribing.
- The 27 getters backed by a plain `asObservable()`/`duc()` pair read their subject so they take that fast path. The eight backed by transforming pipelines (`participants`, `rawParticipants`, `localParticipant`, `remoteParticipants`, `dominantSpeaker`, `pinnedParticipants`, `hasOngoingScreenShare`, `ownCapabilities`) still read their observable, since those pipelines change the value.
- `call.state.getCurrentValue()` and `call.state.setCurrentValue()` are removed in favour of calling `RxUtils` directly, which is what `stateStore`, `DeviceManagerState`, `SpeakerState` and `Call.ts` already do.

### 📈 Benchmarks

Measured with the existing `bench/` harness against this branch's merge base, median of 7, three full runs agreeing within ~2%.

| exercise | before | after | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| read a scalar field (`state.callingState`) | 248 ns | 12 ns | **20.2x faster** |
| six setters, one of which reads a getter | 366 ns | 128 ns | **2.9x faster** |
| `updateFromCallResponse` | 900 ns | 633 ns | **1.42x faster** |
| participant patch, 10-participant call | 1.1 µs | 791 ns | 1.36x faster |
| participant patch, 50-participant call | 2.2 µs | 1.8 µs | 1.21x faster |
| read `state.participants` | 919 ns | 754 ns | 1.17x faster |
| `updateFromSfuCallState`, fan-out, subscribe churn | | | flat |
| bundle, minified / gzip | 456.6 kB / 133.2 kB | 453.7 kB / 132.8 kB | -2.9 kB / -0.3 kB |

Two caveats measured rather than waved away. Scalar writes look ~1.1x slower in the harness, but those totals are sub-millisecond and therefore display granularity; at 2M writes across 9 interleaved rounds the real delta is 14.31 -> 14.47 ns, i.e. flat. Heap per `CallState` instance is genuinely ~250 bytes (~1%) larger; the harness reports +8%, but that number is cold-start attribution, and repeating it with the order swapped gives a stable ~0.9%.

### ⚠️ Breaking change

`call.state.getCurrentValue()` and `call.state.setCurrentValue()` are removed. Use `RxUtils.getCurrentValue()` and `RxUtils.setCurrentValue()`, both already exported from `@stream-io/video-client`. Nothing in this repo outside `CallState` itself used them and no docs reference them.

One further intentional behavior change: `RxUtils.getCurrentValue` on a **completed** `BehaviorSubject` now returns its last value instead of `undefined`, because it reads the held value rather than subscribing (RxJS does not replay to subscribers of a stopped subject). Nothing in the SDK completes a `BehaviorSubject` (the only `.complete()` in the monorepo is `IceTrickleBuffer.live`, a plain `Subject`), and there is a test pinning the new behavior. Every other shape was verified identical: `ReplaySubject` at buffer size 1 and 2, finite `windowTime`, completed and errored subjects, plain `Subject`, `AsyncSubject`, `of(1,2,3)`, `EMPTY` and `throwError`.

### ✅ Verification

`yarn lint:ci:all`, `yarn test:ci:client` (82 files, 1168 passed, 1 skipped), `yarn test:react-native:sdk` (22 suites, 130 passed), `yarn build:client`. `react-bindings`, `react-sdk` and `react-native-sdk` all typecheck against the rebuilt client. The generated `CallState.d.ts` is unchanged apart from the two removed members, so all 35 observables keep their exact public types.

🎫 Ticket: https://linear.app/stream/issue/REACT-1106/callstate-clientstate
