author: yonatankarp
body:
The four copies of `capture3_with_timeout` read a child's output with a bare
`stdout.read`, which runs to EOF with no bound, so a child that never stops
writing is read into the test process in its entirety. The timeout does not
help: it bounds how long the child lives, not how much it emits in that time.

Read with a cap instead — `read(limit + 1)`, close the stream when the result
exceeds the limit, and raise `FixtureCaptureOverflow` at the join.

```ruby
CAPTURE_LIMIT_BYTES = Integer(ENV.fetch("FIXTURE_CAPTURE_LIMIT_BYTES", "8388608"))
class FixtureCaptureOverflow < StandardError; end

def bounded_capture(stream, limit_bytes)
  bytes = stream.read(limit_bytes + 1) || ""
  stream.close if bytes.bytesize > limit_bytes
  bytes
end
```

## Why the overflow is raised on the success path, not inside the reader thread

This is the part of the change that will look like it can be simplified, and it
cannot.

`Thread#join` re-raises a thread's exception exactly as `Thread#value` does. The
timeout path joins both readers before raising `FixtureTimeout`, so an exception
raised from inside a reader would surface *there*, in place of the timeout — the
more informative diagnosis would be masked by the less informative one. Verified
rather than assumed:

```
value re-raised: IOError: boom-value
join re-raised: IOError: boom-join
```

So `bounded_capture` returns the bytes and the main thread decides. The success
path is the only path that consumes the output; the timeout path discards it.

That masking is pre-existing and unreachable today — no fixture in the repository
produces a reader that outlives the kill, which is what #473 is about. Not fixed
here.

## Why a raise rather than an `oversized` flag

#474 framed the cap as needing an `oversized` signal threaded through four call
sites. It does not, and a flag would be worse than no signal: a fourth tuple
element is silently dropped by every existing `_stdout, stderr, status =`
destructuring, so it would be a signal that cannot fail. Raising keeps the
helper's 3-tuple contract and no call site changes.

`capture_limit_bytes:` is a keyword with a default so the new case can inject a
small limit without touching the environment.

## Why 8 MiB, and one shared environment input

Measured rather than reasoned about. All four were instrumented to print
`bytesize` per capture and run: **59 captures, largest 6151 bytes**, every stderr
empty (immich 16, max 6151; audiobookshelf 27, max ~5034; ntfy 8, max 2127;
beszel 8, max 1514). 8 MiB is over a thousandfold headroom and small enough that
eight concurrent captures cannot matter.

One shared `FIXTURE_CAPTURE_LIMIT_BYTES` rather than four per-check prefixes: the
right playbook timeout depends on how long one fixture takes and the right memory
bound does not. It also keeps the constant line inside the identical surface
instead of adding four divergent ones.

## The exception handling is deliberately untouched

#474 proposed a bare `rescue IOError` returning `""` as the cheaper half. It
would be a regression. `report_on_exception = false` (#475) suppresses the
*report* of a dying reader, not the propagation, so a genuine IO failure still
surfaces at `Thread#value` on the success path where the values are consumed.
Silencing it there would turn a broken capture into empty output —
`pin-protected-input.rb` gets away with it only because it threads a `failed:`
flag through to a `capture_failed` result field, which is exactly the caller
plumbing that makes the "cheap" version expensive.

## Byte identity, and why the case is duplicated

The helpers were byte-identical after #475 (`c9bd119c3f08d3fb18ba23fe40d88eac`,
one distinct digest across four). They are again, per region:

| region | digest | distinct across four |
|---|---|---|
| `capture3_with_timeout` | `fe91a879b3fc9db89c9d95407c3c7a49` | 1 |
| `bounded_capture` | `0c6ab8a15bf8c57e1e9f27f5950d423c` | 1 |
| `terminate_process_group` | `7ea8fb8ab8758929493dbddc025495eb` | 1 |
| limit comment + constant + error class | `6383c2c754caa9970f4316111ca9ff50` | 1 |
| the new case | `fa27dd403f49c1791c751a5d9c915e2a` | 1 |

The case is in **all four** files rather than centralised because nothing in this
repository enforces that identity — it has been established by hand five times
across #464, #468, #470, #474 and #475, and is filed as #478. Until that guard
exists, a cap exercised in one file could be dropped from the other three with
nothing red.

`tests/immich_configured_password_test.rb` carries the canonical docstring and
keeps it; two clauses were appended so its claim that `pin-protected-input.rb` is
"differently hardened rather than better" survives the four bounding their reads
too. Confirmed by extracting every removed line from the diff and filtering to
comments: one comment line removed across all four files, and it is the line
extended in place.

## Proving the cap bites

Two plants, both red, and **both fail as `FixtureTimeout` rather than "no error
raised"** — `yes` never stops writing, so an uncapped read never ends. A reader
who expects the obvious failure mode and sees a timeout will suspect the case is
flaky rather than working; it is working.

```
# plant A: bounded_capture reads to EOF (cap removed entirely)
FAIL a capture past its limit was not refused as an overflow: #<FixtureTimeout: Ansible fixture timed out after 10 seconds>

# plant B: capped read kept, only `stream.close` removed
FAIL a capture past its limit was not refused as an overflow: #<FixtureTimeout: Ansible fixture timed out after 10 seconds>
```

Plant B is the one worth keeping in mind before anyone drops the close as
redundant, given `popen3` closes the pipe in its own ensure. Without the close
the producer keeps writing, fills the pipe, blocks, and `wait_thread.value` never
returns — so the overflow is only reported after the deadline. **The close is
what lets `wait_thread.value` return promptly**, and it is therefore covered by
the assertion rather than decoration.

No timing assertion anywhere. The case asserts an error class; the `10` is a hang
bound, not a budget (#462).

## Cost

Same machine, interleaved, back to back.

| check | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| ntfy | 6.65 / 6.66 / 6.73 user, 13.24 / 12.33 / 13.09 wall | 6.57 / 6.73 / 6.80 user, 12.81 / 12.11 / 12.78 wall |
| beszel | 7.16 user, 11.76 wall | 6.98 user, 11.24 wall |
| beszel `--self-test` | 7.13 user, 11.47 wall | 7.25 user, 11.97 wall |
| immich | 18.21 user, 29.06 wall | 17.87 user, 28.25 wall |
| audiobookshelf | 81.32 user, 23.70 wall | 80.68 user, 23.11 wall |

Inside noise; three of five are faster on the branch. No precise delta is quoted
because these files boot ansible 16 and 27 times and the resolution does not
support one.

The first ntfy pair printed base 16.05s against branch 25.19s — a +9.1s that
would have blown the ten-second budget. `user` was flat (7.14 → 7.30) and CPU%
dropped 60% → 40%; three interleaved rounds afterwards put the branch
consistently equal or slightly faster. That is contention, not work, and it is
the discriminator CLAUDE.md's fourth `static` occurrence paid for: a cost that
moves when the load moves is a wait.

## Verification

```
ruby tests/ntfy_verify_execution_test.rb                     exit=0
ruby tests/beszel_password_preservation_test.rb              exit=0
ruby tests/beszel_password_preservation_test.rb --self-test  exit=0
ruby tests/immich_configured_password_test.rb                exit=0
ruby tests/audiobookshelf_initial_scan_behavior_test.rb      exit=0
ruby tests/policy_test.rb                                    exit=0
ruby tests/policy_ci_test.rb                                 exit=0
ruby tests/gate_manifest_coverage_test.rb                    exit=0   # 156 declared checks, all of them run
ansible-playbook -i inventory/local.yml site.yml --syntax-check   exit=0
ansible-lint --strict                                        exit=0
```

Routing: `static=true`, `suites=[]`. Note that the bare `classify_changes.rb`
i

author: panyaasanee
body:
NOT a claim. Round `kq4m8t`'s own lock (`pf_bridge#1771`) is already released and merged. This adds only what arrived AFTER the unlock — the `ADVERSARY_PENDING pirate-force-server#1064` result — into that round's own record, per the house rule. Two files, no code, in either repository.

**The result is not clean, and the automerge marker has already been removed from `pirate-force-server#1064`'s body** (verified by GET) so the reaper will not land it on first green. Same move this lane made on `#991` and LANE-B made on `#922`. The marker must not be restored until D1/D2/D5/D6 are answered, and that instruction is written into `#1064`'s body itself.

Every finding was re-measured by this lane with its own commands before being accepted, and one was declined.

## Three findings that sink the design's central claim

- **D1 — `slot_id = n_EQUIPTYPE` is a *kind*, not a *slot*, and the column cannot hold it.** Re-measured on the committed table:

```
974 rows | n_EQUIPTYPE > 255: 650 | max: 524288
n_EQUIPSLOT   24 -> n_EQUIPTYPE [8, 16, 64]   <- three kinds, ONE physical slot (classes 4/16/32)
n_EQUIPSLOT 16384 -> n_EQUIPTYPE [1]
```

  `store.equip_item` refuses `slot_id` outside `0..255`, and migration 015 sized that column to `ItemAttr+0x39` — a bit index `0..31`. The chosen namespace is arithmetically incompatible with its column for **650 of 974 rows**. And in the future this lane's own docstring describes, equipping type-8 then type-16 writes **two rows for one physical slot**: the swap migration 015 exists to make becomes an accumulation. 🔴 The suite **kills** `slot_id = equip_type.bit_length() - 1` — the number a real `+0x39` encoder wants — and lets three wrong ones through.

- **D2 — the premise is false, and the crosswalk is in this project already.** `tools/pf_equip_attack_behavior_extract.py` does `n_SLOT_RHAND - 2200000` → `EQUIPMENT_BASE` row → `n_EQUIPTYPE`, and it is the tool that **produced** the table the module depends on. All five classes re-derived by hand and matched. So "there is no `template_id -> n_EQUIPTYPE` table anywhere in this repository" is false in the module docstring, the commit message, the round file, the PR body **and the RE ticket this round sent to LANE-K**. The "one item per class" limit was a limit of this lane's search, not of the repository. Bound kept: the `-2200000` base is proven for the `2200xxx` weapon family only.

- **D5 — the headline claim does not survive a relog.** `list_equipped_items` has no caller anywhere, while `ItemAttrState.raw_u8_39` — the literal `+0x39` byte — is already persisted and already emitted in the StartGame BackpackAttr (`inventory.py:508`). Equip, relog, and the wire sends `255`, which `RE-280`'s sentinel makes the client read as "not worn". "The equip outlives the session" is true only of a row nothing reads.

## Also accepted

**D6** `production_allowed = True` adds a measured 5.01s stall on the single-threaded dispatch path under write-lock contention (uncontended 0.002s) — "no `return`" is true about the return value and false about time. **D4** the write line is dead for 4 of 5 classes in production, because `INITIAL_BACKPACK` is issued to every class and holds only class 1's weapon, and no test imports it. **D7** eleven surviving mutants that the round file's 7/7 table contains none of — three sharing one root cause (`CLASS_UNDER_TEST = 1`, where `class_id`, `n_EQUIPTYPE` and `bit_length` are all 1), plus `CONSOLE_PREFIX`/`WROTE` compared against themselves and `REASONS = frozenset()` turning the ASCII census into a zero-iteration PASS. **D8/D9/D10** recorded.

## Declined, with a measurement

**D11's first half** ("the round file's §7 has no body") is a timing artifact — the reviewer opened the file while only its first half was on disk. §7 carries the full-suite line (`13670 passed, 401 skipped, 0 failed, 37606 subtests` on `40a94c4`) and the preflight result. D11's second half stands and is paid here.

## The negative results, which are stronger than this round's own evidence

Fail-closed **held against everything**: a raising `__eq__`, a raising `identity` property, a generator dying mid-iteration, a missing store, a missing keyword, and `KeyError`/`ValueError`/`RuntimeError` from the store — nothing escaped `fire()` and every case wrote zero rows. No duplicated predicate. No stale pins: every number is derived at import or read from a sha-checked table. Skip census green with no new skips, module source pure ASCII, and the write lock is taken by winning `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` rather than by writing.

## A false sentence corrected before it costs owner machine time

`notes_to_chief/20260907_1955_LANE-DB-TO-K-CORRECTION-value32-ticket-has-a-false-grep-line.md` asks LANE-K to hold this round's RE ticket off the capture bus. Beyond D2, two committed reports already answer half of it: `reports/PF_RE_V130_*` records the right-hand `+0x39` index as **3**, and `reports/PF_RE_V123_*` says op=5's `value32` comes from `n_EQUIPSLOT`. The ticket's own nonclaim is dead — the item that produced `value32 = 8` is `EQUIPMENT_BASE` row 2, whose `n_EQUIPTYPE` is **1**, not 8. The `GT-301` letter sent in the same round is unaffected; its measurements hold.

## The question the design never answered, which is the root of D1/D2/D5

**What reads `character_equipment.slot_id`, and in which numbering does that reader expect it?** Until a reader exists it is not opaque, it is undefined, and four numbers are equally defensible for one Gladiator blade: `n_EQUIPTYPE` 1, `n_EQUIPSLOT` 16384, the wire's `value32` 8-or-16, and the `+0x39` index 3 already committed here. Next round answers that in one sentence, starting from "who reads it", before touching a line of code.

author: dcbaugher
body:
Standing ecosystem-map maintenance for the 2026-09-07 scan. One slot touched:
**Distribution-free uncertainty quantification**, MAPIE entry. Both changes are
category (b) — an existing entry is now wrong or omits a capability change.

## What changed, and the evidence for each

### 1. The "requires torch" con is wrong, and it is a routing con

The entry read:

> the v1 API is a rewrite; most tutorials on the internet target the dead v0
> classes. The newer conditional-conformal features require torch, so
> "lightweight" holds only on the classical path.

torch is not what they require. Read from the 1.5.0 wheel on 2026-09-07:

- `mapie/conditional_conformal_prediction.py` imports `numpy`, `scipy.optimize.linprog`
  and scikit-learn. It imports no torch. Grepping every `.py` in the distribution for
  `import torch` returns five files, none of them on this path — they are
  `experimental/conformity_scores/bounds/utils.py`, two `risk_control/` modules and
  two test modules.
- The solver arrives through a lazy `_import_cvxpy`, whose own message is
  `ImportError: cvxpy is required for ConditionalSplitConformalRegressor. Install it
  with: pip install mapie[conditional]`.
- Measured in an environment with **no torch installed**:
  `ConditionalSplitConformalRegressor(estimator=..., feature_map=...)` conformalizes on
  200 points and returns intervals, once `cvxpy` is present and nothing else is.

The `conditional` extra *does* declare `torch>=2.0` beside `cvxpy==1.9.1`, so
`pip install mapie[conditional]` genuinely pulls a deep-learning stack — which is why
the old con was written and why it is not a careless error. But that stack is packaging
metadata the code path never imports, and the distinction is the whole decision: a
reader who needs conditional coverage installs a convex solver, not a framework. This
page was routing them away on the second. Recorded as a dated `{note}` beside the entry
rather than as a silent edit.

### 2. The v1 rewrite dropped Mondrian

- `mapie/mondrian.py`, exporting a class `MondrianCP`, ships in the **0.9.2** wheel.
- **Nothing** matching `mondrian` — file, class or export — is in the **1.5.0** wheel.
- Stratum-conditional coverage in v1 means `ConditionalSplitConformalRegressor`, whose
  signature takes a `feature_map: Callable` rather than a group label, so a v0 Mondrian
  user is porting rather than renaming.

Both wheels were downloaded from PyPI and their file lists, `METADATA` and module
imports read on 2026-09-07. Reported as read from the distributions, not from the
documentation site. Added as a con, on the page's own logic: the capability a reader
comes to a slot for can be the one an upgrade removed, and a map that only records
arrivals decays in one direction.

This one bears on [#281](https://github.com/enginbio/engin-suite/issues/281), which
names Mondrian as the deliberately-*not*-taken route for the stratified-coverage gap.
The decision is unaffected — the argument there is about a misspecified noise model, not
about tool availability — but a reader following that thread to this page would

author: michiiik
body:
**Not a match.** This only edits the `#ifdef NON_MATCHING` branch of `func_84362084`, so the build is unaffected: `.text` / `.rodata` / `.data` of `build/src/fragments/battle_engine/battle_engine_34A420.o` are byte-identical before and after (verified with `objdump -s`; only `.mdebug` line numbers move).

### The "2 instructions short" reading was a tooling artifact

`tools/probe_one.py` treats every `/* off addr word */` comment line in the target `.s` as an instruction. `func_84362084.s` opens with a `.section .late_rodata` block holding two jump tables and a pile of float/double constants — 32 of those lines have an 8-hex-digit word and are counted. So the reported `target=1591` is really **1559** text instructions, and the old candidate at "1589" was **30 instructions too long**, not 2 short. That is why three unrelated width/literal hypotheses all landed on the same number.

### What actually changed

* **`case 6:`/`case 7:` display-list blocks** (both `for (x…19)` passes) index their triangles with the loop counter itself — `for (j = 1; j < 2; j++)` then `j + 0 … j + 10` — not `j * 1 + 1` / `j * 4`. The wrong multipliers made IDO build ten strength-reduced induction variables per block and spill six of them. Fixing this removes ~28 instructions and brings the count to within ±2 of the target.
* Dropped the `sp1BC` and `if (var_s2) {}` scaffolding — `0x1BC` in the target is a loop counter slot, and the `if` produced a stray `move`.
* Reordered locals so the frame layout matches: the target leaves an unused 8-byte hole between `sp1B4` (`0x1B4`) and `sp1A0` (`0x1A0`), i.e. `var_s2` and `vtx` are declared between them and both got registers.

### Remaining gap

The target keeps the display-list pointer in `$fp` for the whole function (`or $fp, $a0, $zero` in the prologue, `move vN, $fp` / `addiu $fp, $fp, 8` per command). IDO spills it here and reloads it once per basic block instead. That single decision accounts for essentially all of the remaining ~45 `or`-vs-`sw`/`lw` differences, and downstream for the `case 6/7` blocks still being strength-reduced rather than collapsed to straight-line code (the target has no back edge there at all). Ablation shows the tipping point is the combined pressure of the `case 8` and `case 2/4` vertex-build blocks: deleting either one makes IDO put the pointer in a register.

author: christ-roy
body:
Renommage des taches de ce banc d essai pour les rendre auto-porteuses.

## Pourquoi

Nomad nomme le conteneur d apres la **tache**, jamais d apres le job. Une tache
`db` ou `postgres` produit un conteneur `db-<alloc>` qu on ne peut rattacher a
aucun service en lisant Beszel ou `docker ps`. Sur le parc, `db` designait
4 jobs et `postgres` 8. C est ce que Robert voyait dans Beszel.

Regle : `nom_de_tache == nom_du_job`, ou `<job>-<role>`. Elle vit dans le
CLAUDE.md de nomad-veridian et est appliquee par `scripts/lint-nom-tache.py`.

## Comment

Par `scripts/renommer-tache.py`, jamais par un `sed` — un remplacement global
frapperait les commentaires, les chemins et les images. Le script ne touche que
`task "<nom>"` et `task = "<nom>"`, puis **compare le JSON que Nomad produira
avant et apres** et refuse si autre chose a bouge. Chaque appel a rapporte
`JSON identique par ailleurs`.

## Note pour le deploiement

Pour le garde-fou `taches-disparues` de `nomad-v`, un renommage est une
suppression plus un ajout : le refus attendu est legitime. L ecart doit etre
verifie comme etant **exactement** un renommage — une tache disparue pour une
tache apparue, dans le meme groupe — avant d assumer
`--force=taches-disparues`.

Et apres deploiement, **verifier que le banc se rendort** : Sablier ne rendort
pas ce qu il n a pas endormi (son balayage ne tourne qu a son demarrage, et un
job reveille par un deploiement n a aucune session a expirer). Mesure du
2026-09-07 : `cms-staging` est reste eveille indefiniment apres un deploiement
et a demande une reouverture de session par l ingress.

Ticket ROB-60.

author: karim-sidibe
body:
## Symptôme

Depuis l'admin (Tarifs & accès), impossible d'enregistrer un prix : « ✗ Prix invalide » sur 50000 XOF, 50000 XAF et 77,00 EUR — alors que ces montants sont parfaitement valides.

## Diagnostic

« Prix invalide » est le **texte de repli du client** quand l'erreur n'est pas une réponse de l'API — la requête n'atteignait donc jamais le serveur. Reproduit en local : le préflight CORS répondait

```
access-control-allow-methods: GET,HEAD,POST
```

Sans option `methods`, `@fastify/cors` n'annonce que les méthodes « CORS-safelisted ». Or l'admin appelle l'API **inter-domaines** (admin.declick.digital → api.declick.digital) : le navigateur bloquait donc tous les **PUT / PATCH / DELETE** après préflight. La route des prix (`PUT /payments/products/:id/prices/:currency`) est la première à l'avoir révélé ; étaient également touchés, sans avoir encore été exercés inter-domaines : révocation d'un cadeau, édition de compte, suppression de webhook… (**7 PUT, 9 PATCH, 16 DELETE** dans l'API).

## Correctif (`server/src/app.ts` — 4 lignes)

Liste explicite des méthodes au registre CORS : `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS` (commentaire expliquant le piège du défaut safelisted).

## Vérification (serveur réel)

- Préflight PUT et DELETE : `access-control-allow-methods: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS` ✓
- Parcours complet reproduisant les captures : création du produit puis **prix 50000 XOF ✓, 50000 XAF ✓, « 77,00 » EUR ✓** (7 700 centimes) — données de test nettoyées.
- `npm test` (server) : 298 verts. Typecheck OK.

## Déploiement

Rebuild API uniquement (`up -d --build api`). Après déploiement : re-saisir les prix dans Tarifs & accès — ils s'enregistreront.

body:
## Fix

Kanban-enabled interactive profiles receive the assigned-worker protocol even when they have no assigned task. Tool visibility was widened to support orchestrators, but prompt initialization and its fallback still treated `kanban_show` as worker identity.

Both paths now require a task binding and canonical dispatcher ownership as well as the tool. The decision remains session-static. Interactive board access stays available, while delegated children and non-owning cron contexts do not receive worker instructions.

This adapts the fix from #102857 to current main's split modules, credits its contributor, and adds real initialization/prompt/cache regression coverage. It is a salvage candidate for the same issue, not a separate fix to merge alongside #102857. Related alternatives: #64186, #68608, #95857. Afterward, `kanban_show` and `kanban_list` remain available and worker guidance is absent. author: richarddli
body:
Closes #9.

Every invocation made four Open-Meteo requests, and the shared `_get` helper retried a timeout or 5xx immediately, once, with no delay, jitter, `Retry-After` support, or memory across runs.

## What changed

**`retry.py` (new)** — `Retry-After` parsing (delta-seconds and HTTP-date; missing, malformed, or already-elapsed values fall back to local backoff), `RetryPolicy`, and `RetryState`, the durable cooldown record. A record written by a clock ahead of ours is ignored rather than parking the CLI.

**`cache.py` (new)** — versioned entries under `~/Library/Caches/weatherodds` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/weatherodds` elsewhere, `WEATHERODDS_CACHE_DIR` overrides). Atomic writes (temp sibling + `os.replace`, temp removed on failure); anything unreadable, mismatched, or of an unknown schema is a miss. Forecasts are gzipped — about 30 KB per five-day model, against multiple megabytes raw.

**`fetch.py`** — `_get`/`fetch_*` replaced by a `Session` with injectable clock, sleep, and jitter:

- A hit within six hours issues no requests at all, forecast *or* metadata. The key covers the model, location, horizon, units, and every other parameter that shapes the response, derived from the request itself.
- Timeouts and 5xx get at most three attempts with capped exponential backoff plus jitter, inside a 20-second wait budget. Ordinary 4xx are not retried.
- A rate limit is never retried in place. It records a cooldown that outlives the process and suppresses forecast and metadata calls alike until its deadline — `Retry-After` if usable, else 60s doubling per consecutive rate-limited invocation, capped at six hours.
- When a refresh fails, a cached forecast up to 48 hours old that still covers today is served, marked stale.

**`cli.py` / `render.py`** — `--refresh` (skips the cache, never the cooldown), a `Next attempt at 14:32 EDT (in 42m)` message instead of an interactive terminal sleeping, staleness notes, `(cached)` in the header, and a `cache` block in `--json`. Days already past at the location are dropped before the horizon is applied, so a forecast reused across local midnight still shows N days from today.

## Review fixes (second commit)

Two defects found reviewing the first commit, each with a test that fails without the fix:

- `gzip.decompress` raises `zlib.error`, not `BadGzipFile`, when a cache file's header is intact but its body is damaged in place. A fuzz of single-bit flips produces it about a quarter of the time. It escaped `_read` unhandled, so the CLI printed a traceback instead of refetching.
- Reading a cooldown back clamped it to the module default, so a policy with a longer cap was let back on the wire early.

## Verification

65 tests, 0.19s, no live API calls — mocked transport, clock, sleep, and jitter throughout. Covers cache keys and expiry, corrupt entries and atomic writes, the retry and time budgets, `Retry-After` in both forms, cooldown persistence across sessions, stale fallback, and optional ECMWF failure. `conformance/dump_reference.py --check` still passes. Also run live: first invocation 1.76s, second 0.26s and marked `(cached)`.

author: gmelodie
body:
The `/perf/1.0.0` server handler reads an 8-byte big-endian size field and sends that many bytes back. The variable held that count but was named `uploadSize`, which names the wrong direction: it is the size of the server's response, not of the client's upload.

This renames it to `responseSize`, and renames `uploadSizeBuffer` to `sizeBuffer`. No behaviour changes.

An earlier version of this PR also capped the size to a configurable maximum. That is wrong: the spec gives the client the size, up to max uint64, and a server-side cap makes the server send a short response with no error, which produces a wrong throughput number for the client. Dropped.

Perf spec: https://github.com/libp2p/specs/blob/master/perf/perf.md

author: pgermosen
body:
## Summary

Several open PRs have had sections of the pull request template deleted outright rather than filled in (missing `## Summary`, `## Type of change`, `## Checklist`, sometimes all three). Nothing currently catches this, so it only surfaces if a reviewer happens to notice.

This adds a CI check that fails when the PR body is missing a required section header. `## AWS Compatibility` is intentionally excluded from the check since plenty of PRs (chores, refactors, non-AWS-behavior fixes) legitimately have nothing to say there.

There is no grandfathering: this applies to every open PR immediately, so a currently open PR missing one of the required sections will start failing on its next push, edit, or reopen until the description is fixed up.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (`fix:`)
- [ ] New feature (`feat:`)
- [ ] Breaking change (`feat!:` or `fix!:`)
- [x] Docs / chore

## AWS Compatibility

N/A: CI workflow change only, no AWS-facing behavior.

## Checklist

- [ ] `./mvnw test` passes locally
- [ ] New or updated integration test added
- [x] Commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)

body:
The bounded controller could ACK an inadmissible batch, forget unresolved work during cleanup, or create a second scale set through another state directory. Worker journals could become unrecoverable after approval expiry, skip a failed directory sync on reopen, and start without the required bridge attachment. This correction addresses the six reproduced PR25/28 findings tracked by #30 and #1.

The controller durably retains work evidence from every statistics and runner observation and refuses unsafe effects and stale-zero cleanup, validates single-job acquisition before ACK, and holds a permanent OS-account-scoped admission pin across directories and restarts. Both journals separate immutable ownership from explicit, durable inspect/cleanup-only authority renewal, retry directory synchronization, and authorize each operation under an exclusive lease. Worker startup requires exactly one bridge. Adjacent regressions cover unexpected job-kind messages, case-folded JSON fields, raw authority changes and unsupported account lookup builds.

Original findings: [batch admission](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/25#discussion_r3949077092), [observed work](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/25#discussion_r3949077101), [cross-directory cap](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/25#discussion_r3949077105), [renewed recovery](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/28#discussion_r3949487028), [directory sync](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/28#discussion_r3949487039), [bridge attachment](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/28#discussion_r3949487047).

Author full `make check` passed on exact `a9fb8de3199a4627f532024e5381e0ba30d2b478`, integrated with main92b2062: both modules, tagged commands, executable build, race, vet, dependency/license and configured root vulnerability checks. Fuzz explicitly skipped because no targets exist. Meaningful red commits and working-tree-only qualifications are recorded in `docs/evidence/g01-audit-corrections.md`.

Final independent review reproduced further evidence loss on the earlier cad9 head despite its external clean verdict. Red commits `5c853eb`, `f1c94ec` and `5dbfa75` preserve those cases. The correction records intent before each work-bearing read, then persists its category before further effects. Validated create/session identities share the result with the category. Demand permanently blocks cleanup; running/acquired/runner counts, negative or missing required statistics and observed runner presence quarantine effects. Later zero/nil responses cannot clear evidence, including after result-write failure and actual private journal reopen. Counts never establish ownership.

The subsequent external P1 [invalid owned-set observation](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/37#discussion_r3950272982) was reproduced before correction: red `b29f3ba` covers 30 invalid-to-valid transitions across inspect/pre-JIT/pre-ACK with fresh Driver or actual file reopen. The final fix moves ID/name/group/ownership-label validation into the durable read result. A later matching-zero response cannot clear failed ownership proof. The intentional DisableUpdate-drift empty-cleanup control is preserved.

Independent review had approved the shared work-evidence implementation at94e4eff, and earlier full reviews covered the unchanged admission/renewal/worker/integration. Final independent Astra xhigh review approved exact a9fb8de: all28 preserved ownership failures now pass with file reopen, earlier/adjacent regressions pass three race repetitions, and full tagged G01 tests/vet pass. Hosted CI also passed. External Codex completed review of exact a9fb8de at 2026-09-07T13:56:53Z with an [explicit clean verdict](https://github.com/1XP-AI/gh-runnerd/pull/37#issuecomment-5571698918). The ownership finding has reproduction/fix evidence and is resolved. Independent review, hosted CI and final external review are complete. Original threads remain open until verified integration. No live resource or actual account admission directory was created.

Scope is the permanent controller-UID scale-set experiment cap. Independent worker commands remain limited per journal; integrated/global worker and production fleet admission are still blocked. Old ambiguous journal formats are retained and refused, never silently migrated. A fixed private OS-account-home directory and supported native account lookup build are explicit operator prerequisites in the guides.

author: sg-devstudio
body:
## O quê / Por quê

O CI estava vermelho em **todo PR aberto**, sem que ninguém tivesse mexido em nada. Dois problemas, um imediato e um estrutural.

- Spec: n/a

### 1. Imediato — `qs` vulnerável nas Functions

O passo `npm audit --omit=dev --prefix functions` passou a falhar com 3 vulnerabilidades *moderate* em `qs`, dependência **transitiva**: `firebase-functions` → `express@4.22.2` → `body-parser` → `qs`.

- [GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx) — array-limit bypass via bracket-key comma parsing
- [GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) — DoS via attacker controlled `isBuffer`

`npm audit fix` não resolve sozinho: `express@4.22.2` é o topo da linha 4.x e ainda depende de um `qs` vulnerável. A saída é um `overrides`, seguindo o padrão que `functions/package.json` já usa para `uuid`.

### 2. Estrutural — a auditoria travava o caminho de todo mundo

O passo `Validar Functions e dependências de produção` juntava duas coisas de natureza diferente:

| | o que verifica | determinístico? |
|---|---|---|
| `require('./functions/index.js')` | código do repo | sim — depende só do diff |
| `npm audit` | serviço de advisories, em tempo real | **não** — o veredito muda sozinho |

Como estavam no mesmo `run`, a auditoria derrubava o passo inteiro. O último CI verde do `main` é de 18/08; as advisories acima são posteriores. Resultado: o mesmo commit que passava em agosto reprovava em setembro, e todo PR de app ficava vermelho por um motivo que nada tinha a ver com ele.

Agora `Validar Functions` fica sozinho e segue bloqueando, como deve. A auditoria vira **job próprio**, que imprime o relatório completo — moderate e low continuam visíveis no log de todo PR — e reprova **apenas em severidade alta**, que é risco real em produção.

## Como verificar

Comportamento da nova política, medido na base **sem** o bump do `qs` (ou seja, com os 3 *moderates* presentes):

```
npm audit --omit=dev                        → exit 1   # política antiga: o que travava
npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high     → exit 0   # política nova: não trava mais
npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate → exit 1   # controle: o gate reprova quando deve
```

A terceira linha importa: mostra que `--audit-level=high` não é "sempre verde" — o gate por nível funciona, só subiu o limiar.

Nesta branch, com o bump aplicado:

```bash
npm ci --prefix functions
npm audit --omit=dev --prefix functions   # found 0 vulnerabilities
node -e "const f=require('./functions/index.js'); if(!f.gerarFlashcards || !f.lembreteEstudo) process.exit(1)"
```

Como `qs` é dependência de **produção** das Cloud Functions, validei compatibilidade em runtime, não só a auditoria:

- `express@4.22.2` declara `qs ~6.15.1` e recebe `6.16.0` — bump minor, mesmo major
- `qs.parse('a[b]=1&c=2&d[]=3&d[]=4')` → `{"a":{"b":"1"},"c":"2","d":["3","4"]}`
- o query parser do Express carrega normalmente
- `require('./functions/index.js')` expõe `gerarFlashcards` e `lembreteEstudo`

## Checklist

author: abic
body:
The desktop application (#21) was built to be the platform's first wide consumer, and this branch is the harvest: everything the app consumes that the C ABI and the JNI binding could not yet provide, plus the bugs the wiring shook out. Five commits, each standing alone.

## Sync crosses the C ABI

`cb_sync_open` puts the worker over the host's transport; `cb_sync_request_all`/`_request_book` ask for work; `cb_sync_next` drains typed per-book reports (a position outcome, seven mark counts, strings borrowed until the next call); `cb_sync_close` joins. `cb_library_set_sync_targets` and two getters record a book's services. Entry points exist in every build and decline without the `sync` feature, so the header stays one file everywhere; `CB_CAP_SYNC` says whether they mean it.

Two decisions, both learned from the app. **No credential surface**: a host transport is the host's networking and authorizes its own requests — smaller than the Rust path, whose per-book credential loop exists only because the bundled transport is credential-less. And **the transport must write**: reconciling marks is POST/PUT/DELETE, so the host-transport ABI grew `cb_http_send_fn` and `cb_http_response_add_header` — a Web Annotation container speaks its concurrency in `ETag` and `Location`, and the old marshaling dropped every response header. A get without a send is refused at open; the finalizer runs exactly once on every path, declines included.

## The bug the live test caught

A real C host (compiled `-Werror` against the golden header) drove shelf → session → sync against a live mocklib, planted a mark as "another device" — and adoption came back zero. Not an FFI bug: `chapbook-annotations` read `selector` only as an array, while the model permits a lone object, which is exactly what webanno writes. Every single-selector mark in a listing failed serde and was **silently skipped** — a container full of another device's highlights looked exactly like an empty one. Fixed with a shape-branching deserializer (an untagged enum would let `Selector::Other` swallow arrays); the regression test was reverted against the fix to confirm it fails without it. After the fix the C host reports `1 adopted`, and a second run is idempotent-zero.

## Android was shipping a broken loader

The binding builds with `cbz` and `pdf` and exposed no waker, no poll — so an image book opened to its placeholder and nothing could ever carry the decoded pages to a redraw. The emulator verifications were EPUBs, which lay out synchronously, which is why five rungs never noticed. `setWaker`/`pollLoaded`/`hasPendingLoads` land with the reference wiring in the demo (post → poll → repaint), **verified live on the emulator**: the comic's first page rendered where the placeholder used to sit forever, and a volume-key turn brought the second page in through the loader.

## The rest of the catch-up

- **Session events cross both boundaries**: `cb_session_next_event` and the JNI `drainEvents` — loads landing and failing, the position moving, the book finishing. The desktop app used this on day one; a failed comic page is now a status line instead of an unexplained placeholder.
- **Android settings** catch up from "cycleTheme and nothing else" to the full model — the flat scalar setter that preserves the font family (the C ABI's lesson, kept), the family on its own calls, the picker's family list — plus the `spineLen`/`pageCount`/`bookKind` accessors a title bar needs.
- **Android sync**, over the platform's own networking: the binding still bundles no TLS on purpose (webpki-roots would ignore user CAs and network security config), so `SyncTransport` is a Kotlin interface over whatever client the app has, write half included, exceptions crossing as transport failures. `SyncWorker`, typed `SyncReport`s, and the library's sync-target calls complete the Kotlin surface.
- `chapbook-sync` re-exports what a caller constructing an engine must name (`Device`, `HttpMethod`, the `HttpClient` family, `UreqHttp` behind `ureq`); PLATFORM's Backend section now describes the reach as it is.

## What this deliberately leaves

The selection/highlight/link block is still Rust-only on both boundaries — the one remaining gap between the desktop reader and what a C or Kotlin host can build. It freezes Contract-tier shape for the most gesture-heavy part of the reader, so it gets its own design pass rather than riding along here.

## Verification

Full gate (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, workspace tests) green; ffi feature matrix including the new sync-without-ureq device shape (added to CI); golden header regenerated twice, additive both times, C-compile checks passing; `build-jni.sh` linkage and symbol gates green for both Android ABIs; Kotlin compiles; the C host ran live against mocklib; the comic fix verified live on the emulator.

author: sykosyber
body: ## Problem and result Closes #137 Returning people still met a sidebar dashboard. The agreed product direction is the Application Runtime plant in `main-interface-1(1).html`: one core application, inbound queue, sent receipts, blocked questions, context tiles, live state, and an autopilot control. After this change, `/` is that plant, wired to existing Relay records. Held jobs sit in Up next, blockers in Stuck, outcomes in Sent, and the selected job occupies Core while remaining visible in its lane. Context tiles open Profile, resume extract, style rules, and Tools. Tools name **Simplify, Notion, and Obsidian** (plus WebMCP and application limits) instead of Greenhouse/Lever/Indeed OAuth. Autopilot writes the existing application policy (`enabled` + `review=all` when toggling on) and loads the next Held job. It does not accept wording, POST to an employer, or call `begin`. Accept exact draft stays on the job. Ready jobs link to `/applications` for a permit. Find more jobs opens the existing import dock. Stuck jobs select into Core without opening a dialog, so BlockerReview stays usable. **Answer the open question** opens the blocked modal. Inspect always states that fit is a heuristic match, not a qualification score. The activity log no longer duplicates polite save notices. Core facts list **evidence** as hit and miss counts from compared gates. There is no match percentage and no `evidenceFitPercent` helper. Plant chrome lives in `app/runtime.css`, imported by the plant shell, not in `app/globals.css`. Enabling Autopilot or saving Tools with Enable checked posts the saved job allowlist when one exists. Eligible workspace ids are used only when nothing is saved yet. More than 100 eligible ids with an empty allowlist still fails closed without a POST. A workspace viewer switch clears policy, Autopilot, and style counts immediately (same as expiry) so a Tools save cannot POST the previous owner's version. Expiry also forgets the selected job id. Changing tiles remounts modal private state. Policy/profile GETs run only after a successful workspace refresh binds a viewer. Each reply is applied as it arrives, so a 401 is not blocked by a hung peer fetch. They expire on 401 before parsing JSON, clear tile state, and ignore delayed responses. A different viewer on those GETs clears the previous owner's private fields and reloads. Autopilot serializes writes on the latest policy version; catch/finally and Tools continuations ignore expired or replaced sessions. The workspace does not read `sessionRef` during render (React Compiler). Autopilot disable uses the saved bounded job list. Tools uses the same **Approval setting** as Applications. Modal private state unmounts on close, expiry, and confirmed viewer switch. Cancelled in-flight profile GETs still apply a later 401. Helpers await `processAuthorizedGet` so malformed JSON cannot escape. Dirty-editor `confirmLeave` guards **Approve and send** and modal **Open Your facts**. ## Evidence - Extra High [5134997722](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5134997722) on `8aceb62`: remaining P1s (enable allowlist, viewer-switch tiles) and P2s (`selectedRef` on expiry, `key={which}`) are fixed. That is peer review of those findings, not deployment approval. `workspace.tsx` size is deferred to a follow-up. - GitHub CI [34157843489](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/actions/runs/34157843489) **succeeded** on head `8aceb62`, including Quality and release build and Integration (browser). A duplicate cancelled run ([34157843042](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/actions/runs/34157843042)) left a failed aggregate CI check; it is not the required run. - Local on `8aceb62` (clean tree): `pnpm lint`; `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm test` (**462** unit tests, 0 failed), including saved `[job-a, job-b]` + 101 Held enable staying two ids, and viewer switch clearing tiles while `loadRuntimeContext` is still pending; `pnpm public-copy:check`; `pnpm test:e2e` (**59** Chromium journeys, 0 failed). - Extra High [5134851711](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5134851711): deleted `evidenceFitPercent`, Core shows hit/miss counts, plant CSS is in `app/runtime.css`. Rebased onto `origin/main` (`bc557f2`). - Extra High [review 5134780808](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5134780808) on `20bfa86` **cleared all four findings** from [5134623904](https://github.com/SyberLabs/relay/pull/138#pullrequestreview-5134623904). - Security, data migration, and rollback impact: no new tables, statuses, or gateway routes. Imports remain evidence-only. Public copy is unchanged because Relay still does not POST to employers. ## Review - [x] One issue owns this scope; unrelated changes are separate. - [x] Tests exercise the changed behavior, including failure paths. - [x] No credentials, personal applications, or private research are included. - [x] Extra High session-expiry, fit-%, CSS split, enable-allowlist, and viewer-switch findings are addressed with compiled regressions; that is not a full review of the UI rewrite. - [ ] A maintainer other than the author will approve. - [x] Public capabilities, integration limits and lead-engineer credit match `docs/public-copy.json`; run `pnpm public-copy:check` and follow `docs/PUBLIC-COPY.md` when these change. Ready for human review. Do not merge until a maintainer other than the author approves. Mapping spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-application-runtime-plant-design.md`. Does not implement #135 arm/heartbeat send or #136 combined QA.

body:
Renommage des taches de ce banc d essai pour les rendre auto-porteuses.

## Pourquoi

Nomad nomme le conteneur d apres la **tache**, jamais d apres le job. Une tache
`db` ou `postgres` produit un conteneur `db-<alloc>` qu on ne peut rattacher a
aucun service en lisant Beszel ou `docker ps`. Sur le parc, `db` designait
4 jobs et `postgres` 8. C est ce que Robert voyait dans Beszel.

Regle : `nom_de_tache == nom_du_job`, ou `<job>-<role>`. Elle vit dans le
CLAUDE.md de nomad-veridian et est appliquee par `scripts/lint-nom-tache.py`.

## Comment

Par `scripts/renommer-tache.py`, jamais par un `sed` — un remplacement global
frapperait les commentaires, les chemins et les images. Le script ne touche que
`task "<nom>"` et `task = "<nom>"`, puis **compare le JSON que Nomad produira
avant et apres** et refuse si autre chose a bouge. Chaque appel a rapporte
`JSON identique par ailleurs`.

## Note pour le deploiement

Pour le garde-fou `taches-disparues` de `nomad-v`, un renommage est une
suppression plus un ajout : le refus attendu est legitime. L ecart doit etre
verifie comme etant **exactement** un renommage — une tache disparue pour une
tache apparue, dans le meme groupe — avant d assumer
`--force=taches-disparues`.

Et apres deploiement, **verifier que le banc se rendort** : Sablier ne rendort
pas ce qu il n a pas endormi (son balayage ne tourne qu a son demarrage, et un
job reveille par un deploiement n a aucune session a expirer). Mesure du
2026-09-07 : `cms-staging` est reste eveille indefiniment apres un deploiement
et a demande une reouverture de session par l ingress.

Ticket ROB-60.

author: artvsmark
body:
## Что не определено

Спецификация говорит «просуммировать по сессиям, попадающим в окно» и не говорит главного — **что именно суммируется**: итог сессии или её приращение за окно. Правил связи ровно два, и они дают разные числа. Выбор неверного даёт цифру, которая выглядит правдоподобно и врёт.

## Решающее наблюдение — не рост

Рост между двумя замерами предсказывают **оба** чтения: и итог сессии, и расход за текущее окно растут, пока окно идёт. Вывод из него был бы догадкой — ровно тем, от чего заведено правило **178**, которое родилось здесь же.

Решающее одно — поведение **через сброс окна**:

| наблюдение | ответ |
|---|---|
| расход **упал** | число за окно, суммируется напрямую |
| **не упал** | итог сессии, расход за окно считается разностью |
| сброса **не было** | **не различить** |

Третий исход полноценный, а не неудача (039). Команда, отвечающая на данных, которые ответа не несут, — это и есть та самая правдоподобная ложь.

## Погрешность названа вслух

Вердикт печатает, на чём основан: сколько сессий сопоставлено, у скольких сменилось окно, сколько из них упало, сколько сессий было только в одном замере. Без этих чисел «за окно» неотличимо от «за окно, по одной сессии из ста».

`cost_usd` в счёт не идёт: производная по чужой формуле, и её поведение через сброс ничего не говорит о природе исходных чисел.

## Что это меняет для задачи

Замер по-прежнему требует окна с реестром — у облачного его нет, — но теперь он **сведён к одной команде**, а не к процедуре в тексте задачи:

```
claude-code-usage-meter probe --before ДО.json --after ПОСЛЕ.json
```

Развилка, её цена и что делает `report` до ответа записаны в `docs/spec.md` прямой фразой: шаг 2 больше не утверждает того, что не установлено.

`preflight` — 16 из 16.

Closes #101

## R233 — 자기유사 예측 탭: 한 조건에 알림 셋 · '0건'과 '12건'이 한 화면

R229 가 남긴 자리. 절 지도를 다시 재니(2026-09-07 · 삼성전자 · 렌더 안정 뒤) 차트 절은 1,070px 로 이미 짧고 **점수 요인 절이 3,672px** 였다. 그 기본 탭에서:

- 20일 표본 부족 **한 조건에 알림이 셋** (거래 회피 · 표본 통제 · 확률 미표시 · ~300px)
- 엔진의 `match_count` 는 **20일 지평**의 수인데 화면은 '유사패턴 표본 0건'이라 세 번 말한 뒤 아래 그래프는 60일 표본 **12건**을 그렸다 — 둘 다 맞는데 어느 지평인지 없어 모순으로 읽힘
- 20일 관찰 타일 여섯 칸이 전부 '산출 불가' (~330px) · '기간 간 방향 일치도' 두 번 · 7단계 설명 상자 늘 펼쳐짐

### 고친 것 (표시 전용 · 값·판정 불변)
- `ui_kit.horizon_counts_line(hz)` — 지평별 표본 수 한 줄 ("5일 195 · 10일 11 · 20일 0 · 40일 0 · 60일 12 · 120일 3")
- 게이트 알림 **하나** (엔진 사유 · 20일 지평 기준 명시 · 지평별 한 줄 · 회피 권고 문장)
- 7단계 설명은 접는다 (내용 그대로) · 빈 20일 타일 여섯 → 문장 하나 · 중복 타일 제거

| | 전 | 후 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 점수 요인 절 | 3,672px | **2,976px** (−19%) |
| 표본 게이트 알림 | 3 | 1 |

다른 절 높이 불변. 계산 파일 불변.

### 덤 — §249·§250 은 전체 회귀에서 한 번도 안 돌았다
요약·`sys.exit(0)` 블록이 §248 뒤에 있어 파일 끝에 붙인 §249(R232 · 19건)·§250 이 그 뒤에 있었다. 사전 점검은 절을 마커로 떼어 돌려 초록불이었고, 단서는 전체 실행 수가 안 는 것(4,522 → 4,522)뿐. 블록을 끝으로 옮기고 **자기 뒤에 절 머리가 있으면 실패**하게 했다(본 절 머리 수를 `scanned=` 로 찍는다). CLAUDE.md §6 한 줄.

### 검증
- 사전 점검(§108 · §244 · §250) 통과 → 전체 회귀: **4,549건 · 실패 0 · 건너뜀 0** (앱 서버 내리고 · 요약 블록을 옮기자 4,522 → 4,549 = §249 19 + §250 7 + 가드 1 — 그 27건이 여태 안 돌던 것이다). 계산 파일 불변.

author: johnnyt
body:
Implements ADR-0004's amendment of 2026-09-07 (E1-E4): the compiler
replaces a composite with its expansion at the Resolve stage, and a
finding raised inside that expansion is reported one level up against
the composite and the param that produced it.

## What changed

**E1 - the expansion happens at Resolve.** `resolve/2` now answers a
*list* of resolved nodes, because a composite answers its expansion,
which is spliced in place of it. Stages 3-6 read a tree with no
composite in it and are unchanged. A member that is itself a composite
expands here too, so the replacement is complete before the stage ends.

**E2 - state ids come from the expanded ids.** Nothing was added: the
members are ordinary blocks with ids minted by the declaration, so
decision 3 derives their state ids the way it derives every other one.

**E3 - the one-level-up rule.** The Resolve stage builds an expansion
index alongside the tree - every block inside an expansion, to the
composite it came from and the param key to blame. Every reported
finding is re-anchored through it before `in_document_order/2` runs, so
the finding names the composite block and the param's key, or the
composite with no key when no single param is to blame. The provenance
map is never rewritten: every span keeps the expanded block that
emitted it, which is what keeps the Source tab and a fixture run at the
engineer's altitude.

**E4 - byte identity.** A document holding a composite compiles to
bytes identical to the same document with that composite expanded in
place, and the provenance maps are equal too. The test builds the
expanded document from `Composite.expand/2` itself, which is what the
Expand operation will put in the document.

## Provenance

Edits the file map did not name, both forced by the bead:

- `lib/statifier_blocks/compiler/finding.ex` - one row of the stage
  table gains `:composite_expansion_failed`. `Composite.expand/2` raises
  on a broken declaration and ADR-0004 decision 1 forbids `compile/3` to
  raise, so the raise becomes a `:resolve` finding against the composite
  block. The same code carries the case where the document root is a
  composite whose subtree answers more than one top-level block: ADR-0001
  decision 1 gives a document exactly one root, so there is nowhere to
  splice the rest, and refusing beats silently dropping members.
- `structure_document/3` in the compiler - the Structure stage walks a
  `Document.t()` rather than the resolved tree, so a document holding a
  composite is handed the expanded tree instead. Without it E1's third
  consequence ("Config and Structure see the members") is false for
  every structural check: a sabotage run confirmed the arity violation
  inside an expansion goes unreported. A document holding no composite is
  passed through untouched rather than rebuilt, so no existing compile
  changes.

`lib/statifier_blocks/composite.ex` is untouched: the expansion contract
is read as it was built, not widened.

## What is NOT decided here

A member whose type is at `current_version` 2 carries `type_version` 1
from the declaration, so `Palette.resolve/2` takes the migration path on
every expansion. The Resolve stage does **not** stamp the current
version, deliberately: the document an author gets from Expand holds
those same blocks at the same version, so stamping only in the compiler
would make the composite and its expansion take different paths and put
E4's byte-identity obligation at risk. Reported for a record ruling
rather than settled here.

## Tests

Ten tests in `test/statifier_blocks/compiler/composite_expansion_test.exs`,
over two composites in the two canonical example domains plus one whose
declaration is wrong where no param can be blamed. Byte identity is
asserted for a single-member and a two-member expansion; both attribution
arms, the document-order placement, the raise-becomes-a-finding case, and
both provenance keys are asserted. Four mutations were run against the
implementation and each turned the tests they name red.

Full gate green; the headless job (`STATIFIER_BLOCKS_HEADLESS=1` compile
plus test) run locally and green. The new test file is pure and carries no
`ensure_loaded` wrapper.

body:
fix(schemas): revert in-place edit, cut 1.1.0 instead (correcting PR #35)

PR #35 edited stateless-calculation-{request,result}/1.0.0/schema.json
in place to widen rateJurisdiction/bucket for Scottish. That was wrong:
these two schemas ARE referenced by a RATIFIED compatibility manifest
(rule-packs uk-sa/2025-26/1.0.0/compatibility-manifests.json,
resolutionPolicy "exact_id_and_hash_only",
engineImplementation.{request,result}SchemaHash) — confirmed by
recomputing the canonical-JSON SHA-256 of the PRE-edit files and
matching it byte-for-byte against the manifest's pinned hashes. The
schema's own header comment claiming "not yet referenced by the
compatibility registry" was stale/wrong for these two files (it was
accurate for pdf-box-mapping/reviewed-pdf-renderer-build, the other
two schemas that comment described). #35 silently invalidated that
ratified pin.

Reverts 1.0.0 to its exact original content (byte-identical, hash
re-verified against the manifest). The Scottish-inclusive widening
now lives at a new 1.1.0 version directory instead of mutating 1.0.0
— matches this manifest's own "exact_id_and_hash_only" discipline:
schemas are versioned artifacts, a shape change needs a new version,
not an in-place edit. 1.1.0 is not yet referenced by any ratified
manifest entry; that ratification stays a separate, later, owner
decision, same as 1.0.0's original ratification was.

author: saculo
body:
Creates the task branch at preflight, before the pipeline's first write of anything.

§7.4 had preflight check out the *base* branch, then implement and qa modified the working tree and each step committed its artifacts — with the branch not created until `step-push`, step 5 of 7. So the pipeline did its work on the base branch, contradicting the "never work on the base branch" rule the project ships in `templates/PROJECT.md`. Found by running TASK-008, whose artifact commits had nowhere correct to land.

## Acceptance criteria

| id | criterion | |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | §7.4 creates the task branch during preflight, after the tree and dependency checks pass and **before** any artifact or source write | ✓ |
| AC-2 | §4.6's "delivery-pipeline artifact commits land on the task branch" is reachable — no step commits a task artifact while the base branch is checked out | ✓ |
| AC-3 | `step-push`'s responsibilities are restated for a branch that already exists: it pushes and opens the PR, and its adoption rules still cover a resumed run | ✓ |
| AC-4 | The spec states what preflight does when the base is behind its remote **or** when the base is ahead of it — the second had no defined outcome and stopped TASK-008 at push | ✓ |

Verified by qa 4 of 4 (`QA.md`, 2026-09-03T19:10Z). Review `passed`, lenses correctness + design (`REVIEW.md`, 2026-09-03T20:30Z).

## Changes

One file, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, in six components:

1. **Branch creation as an ordered act inside `step-preflight`** — a `▸ CREATE THE TASK BRANCH` act between checks (b) and (c). An act rather than a fifth check, because lettering it would reletter (c) and (d) and break every citation to them.
2. **Check (b) rewritten** — it said "base up to date with origin", which the new base-ahead row contradicts. It now points at §7.4.2 for the branch point instead of assuming one, and admits the task's own branch so a resumed run from implement onward passes.
3. **§7.4.3's premise** — planning is checked "before any work *and on the task branch*, which preflight created before (c) ran".
4. **§4.6's commit-location rule** — now headed *the dispatching workflow decides the branch, not the artifact's type*, so a `PLAN.md` backfilled at preflight travels with its PR instead of being stranded on the base.
5. **§7.4.2's branch rows re-keyed to preflight**, with adoption still resolving for a resumed run.
6. **Base divergence** — two new rows on `git rev-list --left-right --count @{u}...HEAD`: ahead-only branches from `origin/<base>`; ahead-and-behind blocks `branch-conflict`. No new `blocked_reason` value minted.

## Deviations

`deviation: minor` — component 6 was determined during design rather than specified by the plan; the plan named the gap, not the resolution. Nothing outside `REQUIREMENTS.md` was touched, and no `blocked_reason` vocabulary was added.

## Known follow-ups, filed not fixed

- **F-1 (minor, not required)** from review: check (b) still requires a clean tree, while source stays uncommitted until push — so a resume between implement and push blocks on `dirty-tree`. Deferred deliberately; now filed as **TASK-065** after it deadlocked this task against TASK-046.
- `TASK-020` implements this change in `skills/task/` — this PR is the specification half (D-019).

author: ffelipesimoes
body:
# 🎯 fix(authz): permitir acesso a observabilidade e menus administrativos para usuários com papel `owner`

## 📋 Resumo das Alterações
Esta PR corrige a verificação de permissões tanto no backend quanto no frontend para que usuários com papel de `owner` (proprietário de organização) tenham acesso completo às páginas de Observabilidade (`/company/settings/instance/observability`), menus administrativos da barra lateral e abas de configurações, resolvendo o bloqueio onde o sistema exigia estritamente a flag `instance_admin`.

---

## ✨ Principais Funcionalidades

### 🗄️ 1. Autorização no Backend (`instance-settings` & `access`)
- Atualizada a função `assertCanManageInstanceSettings(req)` em `server/src/routes/instance-settings.ts` para permitir atores cujo membership role seja `owner` ou `admin`.
- Endpoint `GET /api/cli-auth/me` em `server/src/routes/access.ts` atualizado para fundir as memberships de `req.actor` e `accessSnapshot`, garantindo que papéis resolvidos em sessões e ambientes de nuvem não sejam descartados.

### 📊 2. Reconhecimento Robusto no Frontend (Sidebar e Menus)
- No `Sidebar.tsx`, `Sidebar.production.tsx`, `SidebarAccountMenu.tsx`, `SidebarAccountMenu.production.tsx`, `SidebarCompanyMenu.tsx` e `SidebarCompanyMenu.production.tsx`, a verificação de administrador foi expandida para checar se o usuário possui papel `owner` ou `admin` em qualquer membership (`boardAccess.memberships.some(...)`), além da empresa selecionada.
- Adicionada a aba `Observability` em `CompanySettingsNav.tsx` com roteamento e detecção automática de tab ativa.
- Adicionado botão "Instance Observability" na página de Organizações (`Companies.tsx`) para usuários com papel `owner`.
- Atualizados os gates `ToolsAdminGate.tsx` e `AdvancedToolsRoute.tsx` com a mesma checagem resiliente.

---

## 🗃️ Arquivos Criados/Modificados

### Arquivos Modificados
- `server/src/routes/instance-settings.ts` - Atualizado `assertCanManageInstanceSettings` para aceitar `owner` e `admin`.
- `server/src/routes/access.ts` - Atualizado `/cli-auth/me` para consolidar `memberships` do ator autenticado.
- `server/src/__tests__/instance-settings-routes.test.ts` - Adicionado teste unitário validando acesso de atores `owner` à rota de observabilidade.
- `server/src/__tests__/cli-auth-routes.test.ts` - Adicionado teste validando consolidação de memberships em `/cli-auth/me`.
- `ui/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` - Checagem `isAdmin` atualizada para verificar `owner` em qualquer membership.
- `ui/src/components/Sidebar.production.tsx` - Checagem `isAdmin` sincronizada para produção.
- `ui/src/components/SidebarAccountMenu.tsx` - Menu de conta com checagem para exibir item de observabilidade para `owner`.
- `ui/src/components/SidebarAccountMenu.production.tsx` - Menu de conta de produção atualizado.
- `ui/src/components/SidebarCompanyMenu.tsx` - Menu superior de empresa atualizado com checagem de `owner`.
- `ui/src/components/SidebarCompanyMenu.production.tsx` - Menu superior de empresa de produção atualizado.
- `ui/src/components/access/CompanySettingsNav.tsx` - Adicionada a aba `instance-observability` no topo das configurações.
- `ui/src/components/access/CompanySettingsNav.test.tsx` - Testes atualizados para a nova aba `instance-observability`.
- `ui/src/pages/Companies.tsx` - Botão "Instance Observability" liberado para `owner`.
- `ui/src/pages/tools/profiles/ToolsAdminGate.tsx` - Permissão resiliente para donos e administradores.
- `ui/src/pages/tools/AdvancedToolsRoute.tsx` - Permissão resiliente para donos e administradores.

---

## 🔄 Fluxo de Funcionamento

```mermaid
graph TD
  A[Usuário Autenticado] --> B{Possui papel Owner ou Admin?}
  B -->|Sim| C[Libera Menu Admin no Sidebar]
  B -->|Sim| D[Exibe Aba Observability em Configurações]
  B -->|Sim| E[Autoriza GET /api/instance/observability - 200 OK]
  B -->|Não| F[Apenas Funções de Membro/Operador]
  E --> G[Visualização das Métricas de Computação e Simulação de Custos de Tokens]
```

---

## 🐛 Correções Implementadas

### 1. Bloqueio 403 Forbidden na API de Observabilidade
- **Problema:** Usuários com o papel `owner` recebiam status `403 Forbidden` ao consultar métricas globais de computação em `/api/instance/observability`, pois `assertCanManageInstanceSettings` exigia estritamente `isInstanceAdmin`.
- **Solução:** `assertCanManageInstanceSettings` agora reconhece `membershipRole === "owner" || membershipRole === "admin"`.

### 2. Ocultação dos Menus Administrativos na UI
- **Problema:** Usuários autenticados como `owner` não visualizavam os links de administração e observabilidade caso `selectedCompanyId` não estivesse definido ou caso não possuíssem a flag isolada `isInstanceAdmin`.
- **Solução:** Checagem expandida com `boardAccess?.memberships?.some(...)` para cobrir usuários `owner` em qualquer contexto de navegação.

---

## 📈 Benefícios Alcançados
- ✅ Acesso imediato dos proprietários às ferramentas de gestão de custos e consumo de recursos.
- ✅ Eliminação de erros 403 indevidos para os donos das instâncias/organizações.
- ✅ Navegação fluida com aba de Observabilidade presente na navegação contextual de configurações.

---

## 🧪 Testes e Validação
- ✅ `server/src/__tests__/instance-settings-routes.test.ts`: 52 testes aprovados (incluindo o novo teste para `ownerActor`).
- ✅ `server/src/__tests__/cli-auth-routes.test.ts`: 11 testes aprovados (incluindo consolidação de memberships).
- ✅ `pnpm check:token-gates`: 100% aprovado sem violações de tokens de design.
- ✅ `npx tsc -p server/tsconfig.json --noEmit && npx tsc -p ui/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: 0 erros de tipagem TypeScript.

---

## 🔒 Compatibilidade
- ✅ Totalmente retrocompatível com instâncias `local_implicit` e usuários `instance_admin` existentes.

## Summary

The `/services` and `/providers` lists stopped looking like a different product from the rest of the site. Reviewed on dev against the landing page and a provider's page, three parts of last week's refresh were inconsistent; this branch replaces them with the site's own parts. Nothing from the heading row down changes.

- **Header.** The standard `SiteHeader` every other page renders, with the centred Explore / Services / Providers pill and the current page lit. The `search` variant is removed and the file restored byte-for-byte.
- **Search.** The landing hero's `ServiceSearch` bar sits under the header. It gained a destination, a placeholder and an accessible name, so `/providers` searches business names and says so.
- **Categories.** One row of chips in the filter pills' own style, "Todas" first and filled navy when chosen, keeping the strip's scroller, edge fades and arrows. The band and the underline are gone.
- **Missing photos.** The site's own placeholder, the pale-blue tile with the brand mark the landing cards use. `BrandTile` and `public/brand/tie-pattern.svg` are deleted.
- Thirteen orphaned locale keys deleted; a new `searchLabelProviders` in all eight; a comment sweep so the prose no longer places the search in the header.

## The bug the whole-branch review caught

The first plan told the bar to navigate to a bare `?q=`, so submitting a term on a narrowed list silently dropped the category, the filters, the city and the sort, while every other control on those pages composes with `browseSearch(current, …)` / `directorySearch(current, …)`. The page now hands the bar its own URL builder; the home page's hero still starts a fresh search; a discriminated union makes a half-configured bar unrepresentable. Verified in a browser: searching inside a category plus a filter keeps both and resets the page, and an emptied box clears the term without clearing the filters. The spec revision now states the rule.

Also fixed: the navy container that showed behind a loading or failing photo, a phone price line that was clipped, and several stale comments.

## Verification

- apps/frontend/web: 2432 tests in 198 files, locale parity gate 112, typecheck, lint (one pre-existing warning), `bun run build`.
- packages/frontend 92, packages/shared 261, packages/backend 2078; all typechecks clean.
- Four task reviews, a whole-branch review, one fix round and a scoped re-review, all clean.
- Both pages rendered at 1440 and 390 against a local worker before and after the fix round.

## Known, pre-existing, not fixed here

- The shared header's "Sign in" wraps to two lines on narrow phones; reproduced on the landing page, so it belongs to the header every page uses.
- A photo that 404s before hydration keeps the browser's broken-image glyph over the placeholder.
- The catalogue query's `total` still counts rows its list drops, so the services page shows fewer tiles than "found".

author: christ-roy
body:
Renommage des taches de ce banc d essai pour les rendre auto-porteuses.

## Pourquoi

Nomad nomme le conteneur d apres la **tache**, jamais d apres le job. Une tache
`db` ou `postgres` produit un conteneur `db-<alloc>` qu on ne peut rattacher a
aucun service en lisant Beszel ou `docker ps`. Sur le parc, `db` designait
4 jobs et `postgres` 8. C est ce que Robert voyait dans Beszel.

Regle : `nom_de_tache == nom_du_job`, ou `<job>-<role>`. Elle vit dans le
CLAUDE.md de nomad-veridian et est appliquee par `scripts/lint-nom-tache.py`.

## Comment

Par `scripts/renommer-tache.py`, jamais par un `sed` — un remplacement global
frapperait les commentaires, les chemins et les images. Le script ne touche que
`task "<nom>"` et `task = "<nom>"`, puis **compare le JSON que Nomad produira
avant et apres** et refuse si autre chose a bouge. Chaque appel a rapporte
`JSON identique par ailleurs`.

## Note pour le deploiement

Pour le garde-fou `taches-disparues` de `nomad-v`, un renommage est une
suppression plus un ajout : le refus attendu est legitime. L ecart doit etre
verifie comme etant **exactement** un renommage — une tache disparue pour une
tache apparue, dans le meme groupe — avant d assumer
`--force=taches-disparues`.

Et apres deploiement, **verifier que le banc se rendort** : Sablier ne rendort
pas ce qu il n a pas endormi (son balayage ne tourne qu a son demarrage, et un
job reveille par un deploiement n a aucune session a expirer). Mesure du
2026-09-07 : `cms-staging` est reste eveille indefiniment apres un deploiement
et a demande une reouverture de session par l ingress.

author: gestionewebstudio-beep
body:
Sintesi

Questa PR impedisce ai percorsi Shopify di cancellare o alterare silenziosamente dati locali VestiFlow.

Il vecchio percorso di disconnessione distruttiva è stato riprodotto su PostgreSQL reale: movimenti e giacenze passavano rispettivamente da 2 a 0 e da 1 a 0. La PR protegge lo stesso perimetro e chiude ulteriori cancellazioni emerse durante il collaudo.

Modifiche principali

La disconnessione Shopify resta disponibile e non cancella dati locali.

La funzione purge è temporaneamente sospesa in tutte le sue combinazioni.

Nessuna funzione Shopify elimina prodotti, varianti, giacenze o movimenti VestiFlow.

Nessuna funzione Shopify elimina clienti o ordini VestiFlow.

La sincronizzazione non elimina una sede, nemmeno quando risulta vuota.

Una location scomparsa da Shopify non disattiva e non scollega automaticamente la sede VestiFlow.

Sono state censite tutte le 21 relazioni verso Location, comprese le relazioni Cascade e SetNull implicite.

Le guardie statiche impediscono di reintrodurre cancellazioni Shopify su location, clienti, ordini, catalogo e inventario.

Un payload ordine con line_items vuoto o assente non viene più interpretato come un ordine senza righe: aggiornamento sospeso, righe e impegni conservati, errore registrato.

Le cancellazioni delle righe realmente rimosse da un ordine continuano a funzionare in modo mirato e idempotente.

Comportamento temporaneo

Finché non sarà disponibile lo storico dei collegamenti, una location Shopify non più esistente viene conservata con il proprio identificativo e segnalata in errore.

È un comportamento deliberatamente conservativo: evita di perdere l’unica traccia del collegamento e impedisce riagganci automatici errati.

La purge verrà sostituita successivamente da operazioni non distruttive basate sullo storico dei collegamenti.

Collaudo

PostgreSQL locale reale, con bersaglio isolato e verificato.

518 scenari di integrazione in 29 file.

2.502 test API.

2.086 test frontend.

1.315 test componenti.

author: akashshivanand
body:
`visibleDocuments` ended with `.map((d, i) => ({ ...d, n: i + 1 }))`. It reads as a convenience — renumber the filtered list so it displays 1..n with no gap — and it was data loss, because **`n` is what uploads are keyed by.** The same document therefore had a different key on every branch.

## The failure, concretely

**AVYAY's Rent Agreement** is document **10** on the new-project branch and **6** on renewal — and the renewal branch lists only **nine** documents. An applicant who attached it as a new project and then switched to renewal had that upload keyed `10` against a list with no tenth slot: not misattributed, **gone**. Where both lists are long enough the file survives and silently re-attaches to whatever now sits in that position, which is worse, because nothing looks wrong.

## The fix

`n` is identity and is returned unchanged. The **display** number is the render position and belongs to the renderer, which has the index — both list sites now show `i + 1`.

**The rendered output is identical by construction**: the old code assigned `n = i + 1` and displayed `d.n`, so the same values appear on screen. What changes is only the key.

## Verified in a browser

Signed in, attached a probe file to the one document both NAPDDR branches ask for, then switched Case Type:

| | Displayed as | Counter |
|---|---|---|
| New project | `5. List of Beneficiaries — previous year` | 1 / 12 |
| → switched to renewal | `1. List of Beneficiaries — previous year` | 1 / 6 |

**The document moved from slot 5 to slot 1 and the upload came with it.** Under the old code that file was keyed `5`, and position 5 on the renewal branch is *"Provisional / unaudited audit report"* — so it would have been shown as a different document entirely.

Also confirmed on the same pass: renewal renders `Step 10 of 11` with 8 documents, 2 marked OPTIONAL and a mandatory denominator of 6; new project renders `Step 9 of 10` with 12, none optional. Both match the captured live portal.

## Tests

- **272 pass.** The NAPDDR renumbering test is replaced by two that assert what actually matters:
  - the one document both branches ask for keeps the **same `n`** while sitting in a **different position** on each — this fails under the old code;
  - **every scheme's declared document numbers are unique** — the invariant the whole upload store rests on, and one nobody had written down.
- The AVYAY parity tests asserted the *displayed* list, so they map with the index now.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean · all repo gates pass.

## Scope

This predates the NAPDDR branch work (#363) and already affected **AVYAY and SMILE**, which have forked document lists of their own. NAPDDR's fork made it reachable on a third scheme, which is how it was noticed.

author: deboal
body:
`dma::run` advanced the clock without telling the timers or the PPU, so **every cycle spent moving data was invisible to both**. The timers ran slow by exactly the transfer time — while the link, which measures a transfer against that same clock, did not.

Nothing looks wrong in a single-player game: everything is late together. In a linked one the two clocks disagreed, and they disagreed most on the screens that move the most data — which is exactly where a linked game does its heaviest work.

The game's link driver demands nine cable transfers in every frame and gives up when it gets eight. Walking two players to the trade machine:

| | frames short of nine |
|---|---|
| before | **257** |
| after | **11** |

(The remaining eleven are my frame-bucketing straddling a boundary, not real shortfalls.)

## Two more, both found building the tool to reproduce it

- **A save state has to carry the transfer in flight.** It did not, so restoring one mid-exchange left the cable half-way through a word it would never finish, and the game's link driver gave up. Appended after the existing fields and read with defaults, so states written before this still load — no version bump.
- **`Cable` measures its quanta against a clock of its own**, and steps each machine until it reaches the grid. Replace the machines' state wholesale and they arrive already far past a grid still sitting at zero, so the loop that steps them "until they catch up" never runs them at all. Nothing crashes; they simply stop. `rebase` aligns the grid to the machines.

## Tooling

The headless driver can now drive the two units with **different buttons** (`--script-2`) and **snapshot both machines mid-session** (`--snapshot-out` / `--snapshot-in`). Completing a trade needs the first; the second turns a two-minute walk into a fifth of a second, which is the difference between guessing at this and testing it. Both were flagged as missing when the link work landed.

## Health readout

The strip showed slack and stalls — and idling to stay level with a partner is neither, so a session crawling along behind a backgrounded tab reported perfect health while nothing moved. It now reports the rate the session is actually advancing at, which cannot be fooled that way, and the overlay says when a partner's window has gone behind another one.

## Checks

107 core tests (both new ones verified to fail without their fix) and 41 browser checks, all green.
