author: flavioneto11
body:
`operate.json` is the page an operator opens at three in the morning — the authoritative configuration reference, the deployment shapes, and the honest inventory of what is not wired. It only spoke English. This adds `internal/ui/assets/docs/operate.pt.json` beside it.

One new file. Nothing else is touched.

## Structural parity

Verified by a script that walks both documents together:

- same top-level keys in the same order; `area` copied unchanged
- 12 sections, same order, same keys per section
- table shapes identical: 4x12, 3x28, 4x7, 2x15 — 190 cells, every row the same width
- 23 examples, same order, same keys per example (the five that carry no `note` still carry no `note`)
- 2 gaps, both `status` values copied

## What was copied byte for byte

**All 23 `code` strings and all 23 `output` strings.** These are `docker compose`, `helm`, `psql` and shell an operator copies under pressure, and observed transcripts captured from a running farm. A translated command does not run, and a translated transcript is no longer the evidence this page claims it is. The `docker run` block embedded in the section 7 *body* is checked separately and is also byte-identical.

Also verbatim: every `lang`, every `source` citation, every gap `status`, every environment variable, role and service name, every Go/SQL/Helm identifier and file path, and the domain vocabulary the schema and the API speak — lease, fence, devpath, holder, slot, hub, quarantine, artifact, pool, tenant, queue, role, heartbeat, grace, backoff. Table columns of variable names, default values and source locations stay English because they are typed verbatim into a shell or a manifest.

## What the translation preserves beyond the words

The prose here says what a thing *prevents*, not what it does, and the causal clause is the point of the sentence. "SIGTERM drena o trabalho e não libera nada" keeps the reason attached: a control plane that released its leases on the way out would turn every rolling deploy into destroyed work.

Emphasis is load-bearing and lands in the same place — `**Nada.**`, `**Validada, depois ignorada.**`, `NADA CONSTRÓI NENHUM DOS DOIS`, `SE RECUSA a iniciar`.

The admissions are not softened. The `met` in code / `unverified` in practice rows still read that way, the table row that says `farmd node` cannot currently start still says it (the English file's own internal tension is reproduced, not tidied), and the gap recording that `internal/node` and `internal/topo` have never met a phone keeps its full force.

## Verification

`node check.js` — 276 checks, 0 failures, PARITY OK:

```
code strings byte-identical:   23/23
output strings byte-identical: 23/23
headings: 12  bodies: 12  labels: 23  notes: 18  bullets: 44  table cells: 190
```

The checker also flags any prose string still identical to English (67 remain, each one an intentional keep listed above) and runs an English-residue heuristic over every translated field. Both are clean.

`go build ./...`, `go test ./internal/ui/` and `go test ./...` all pass. `assets/docs` is embedded as a whole directory, so the file ships automatically; `TestDocsRegisterMatchesREQUIREMENTS` reads `requirements.json` by exact name and is unaffected.

## One judgement call to confirm

`verified` — the provenance record, not rendered by the UI — was translated rather than copied, matching what a sibling area unit does so the eight files stay consistent. Every command, path, commit hash, byte count, exit code and quoted refusal string inside it is preserved verbatim and checked against a list of 43 literals. Say the word if the coordinator would rather it stay English; it is one field and reverting is a one-line change.

Browser check skipped per instructions — the per-language docs loader is not on `main` yet, so nothing fetches a `.pt.json` path today.

body:
## Objective
A0b big-job seam: **staged (thirds) billing** for long jobs. Deposits already existed and work; the genuine gap was the middle stage. A >2-week job is now: deposit up front (existing) → **one midpoint progress invoice** → final that credits both. No installment-schedule engine — "thirds" is just deposit + one progress invoice + final.

## Files changed
- `db/migrations/177_invoice_kind_progress.sql` — widen `invoice_kind` CHECK to allow `'progress'` (additive, reversible, idempotent).
- `apps/web/lib/invoices/progress.ts` — pure `thirdOfTotalCents` + `clampProgressAmountCents` (staged invoices can never exceed the total).
- `apps/web/app/api/v1/jobs/[id]/progress-invoice/route.ts` — `POST`; creates a draft progress invoice (defaults to ⅓ of the estimate total, clamped to the remaining balance), estimate-linked so the final credits it.
- `apps/web/lib/invoices/db.ts` — `loadCreditedInvoicesForEstimate`: one shared loader crediting `deposit` **and** `progress`, replacing 4 inline `invoice_kind = 'deposit'` queries (convert route + `final-invoice.ts` ×3) so every final-invoice path credits the same set.
- `apps/web/app/app/jobs/[id]/{page.tsx,NewProgressInvoiceButton.tsx}` — "Progress billing" card + one-tap ⅓ button on open jobs with an approved estimate.
- backlog: TASK-120 In Progress; merged TASK-123/124/125 → Done.

## Correctness
The crux is that the final invoice must credit progress invoices, never double-bill. `reconcileFinalInvoice` already sums a credited-invoice array and clamps to the total; the fix routes all four final-invoice paths through the shared loader.

## Gate results
- `progress.unit.test.ts` (6) ✓, `progress-credit.integration.test.ts` (2) ✓ — final credits deposit + non-void progress, void excluded, stages + balance = project total.
- All 155 invoice unit tests ✓, `typecheck` ✓, `lint` ✓ (pre-existing warnings only).
- Migration verified against the dev DB: single `invoices_invoice_kind_check` widened to include `progress`.

## Risks / follow-up
- Estimate detail view still lists only deposit/final (display-only); progress invoices surface on the job page. Can extend later if wanted.

body: nav_back_url() now prefers the explicit returside over the session nav stack (report filters survive Tilbage), with a bare-script guard, and honours a luk.php returside first so a popup's Luk actually closes. Popup semantics move from the user preference to a popup=1 request flag: menu.php's window.open links carry it, nav_push() skips only flagged requests, luk.php closes on either, and varer/modtagelse/historikkort/ pos_ordre set their luk.php returside on the flag instead. luk.php: returside sanitised via new central nav_sanitize_returside() (reflected XSS / open redirect fixed), unlock SQL cast and whitelisted, blocked-close fallback goes to the returside instead of the login page. Print pages (udskriv/formularprint/koekkenprint) are excluded from the nav stack; dedup compares path only and keeps the newest query; nav files are deleted on logout plus an age-based sweep. update_iframe() tags iframe navigations with inframe=1. Same-PR link fixes: debitorkort Historik/Opgaveliste and ansatte header icons now pass urlencoded, id-carrying retursides; kladdeliste hands its GET returside to the topline and casts exitDraft. ## What are the changes about? Provide a brief explanation of the changes you have made ## What are the changes about? Work package 1 of the return-link audit (Requirements_return_link_fixes_EN.md, 2026-09-03) — the navigation infrastructure everything else builds on: - **`nav_back_url()` priority flip:** the explicit `returside` now beats the session nav stack (report pages render from POST, which the stack never records — filters survive Tilbage), with a guard that keeps the stack entry when the returside is a bare script name and the stack holds the same script with a query (the id). A `luk.php` returside is honoured before the stack, so a popup's Luk actually closes. - **Popup flag (1.3):** popup semantics move from the user *preference* (grupper USET box2) to a `popup=1` request flag. menu.php's window.open links carry it; `nav_push()` skips only flagged requests (popup-preference users get a working nav stack for the first time); luk.php closes on either preference or flag; varer/modtagelse/historikkort/pos_ordre set their luk.php returside on the flag so inline/iframe use no longer dead-ends. - **luk.php hardening (1.5):** returside sanitised via new central `nav_sanitize_returside()` — fixes a reflected XSS / open redirect; root-relative paths still accepted. Unlock SQL params cast/whitelisted. Blocked-close fallback now goes to the returside instead of the login page. - **Print pages (1.2):** udskriv/formularprint/koekkenprint are excluded from the nav stack (back can never re-print); dedup compares path only and keeps the newest query. - **Cleanup (1.7):** nav files deleted on logout + 48h age sweep. Per-tab stacks remain a documented limitation. - **iframe flag (1.6):** `update_iframe()` tags navigations with `inframe=1` centrally. - **Same-PR link fixes required by the flip (1.1):** debitorkort's Historik/Opgaveliste links and ansatte's header icons pass urlencoded, id-carrying retursides (previously id-less, masked by the stack); kladdeliste hands its GET returside to topLineFinans (never plumbed before) and casts exitDraft. **Manual test (done on ssl12):** filtered report → kontokort → Tilbage returns the filtered report; print → back → list, back again never re-prints; popup-preference kassekladde popup closes on Luk; `luk.php?returside=https://evil.example` and `">x` inert; iframe back/Luk never shows the login page; logout removes the session's `temp/nav_*.json`; debitorkort Historik/Opgaveliste round-trips to the same customer. WP-2–6 follow as separate PRs per the spec. `finans/bogfor.php` untouched; no DB schema changes. ## Have you checked the following? - [x] I have updated relevant documentation at https://github.com/DANOSOFT/saldi/wiki - [x] I have checked that i am not linking to any external resources such as external style- or JavaScript-files, that could compromise stability - [x] I have read and understood the developer guidelines https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GOmomtvKf21OV2VWNOIPweDi4gJHpMCK5qXzrPrypUc/edit?usp=sharing ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Improved return navigation so pages preserve the correct record, list, search, sort, and popup context. - Popup windows now close or return to the appropriate originating page more reliably. - Improved iframe behavior by preserving embedded-page context. - Secured return links by rejecting unsafe destinations and safely handling navigation parameters. - Navigation history now handles reloads, filtering, printing, and logout cleanup more consistently. - **Security** - Added validation and escaping for return URLs and related navigation values to prevent unsafe redirects or markup injection.

author: mjun0812
body:
## Overview and Background

The Ruff configuration in generated projects now selects five more rule families, formats code examples inside docstrings, and no longer carries ignore entries for rules that were never enabled. Previously the `ignore` list contained COM812, COM819, G004, ISC001, ISC002, Q000, Q001 and Q002 even though the COM, G, ISC and Q families were not in `select`, so those lines suggested behavior that did not exist. Common pytest, comprehension, and performance mistakes also went unreported.

## Related Issues

None

## Implementation Approach

- Added families: `C4` (flake8-comprehensions), `FURB` (refurb), `PERF` (perflint), `PT` (flake8-pytest-style), `TC` (flake8-type-checking). Each targets a class of issue the existing set did not cover, and none conflict with the Ruff formatter. Only stable rules in each family are enabled because `preview` stays off.
- Removed the eight ignore entries whose families are not selected. Entries for selected families (ANN, B, D, E, PTH, RUF, SIM) are untouched.
- `[tool.ruff.format] docstring-code-format = true` formats fenced or doctest code in docstrings with the same style as the source.
- Comments in the `select` list are re-aligned for the four-letter codes; no other formatting changed.

## Changes

- `template/pyproject.toml`: `select` gains C4, FURB, PERF, PT, TC; `ignore` drops COM812, COM819, G004, ISC001, ISC002, Q000, Q001, Q002; new `[tool.ruff.format]` table.

## Impact

- User-facing: `ruff check` in generated projects reports more issues. The example package and tests in the template pass without changes.
- Compatibility: projects updating from the template may see new findings after `copier update`; most rules in the added families have auto-fixes (`ruff check --fix`).
- The lockfile, CI, Docker, and devcontainer are unchanged (Ruff is already at 0.16.6).

## Validation Results

Rendered the new `pyproject.toml` into a generated Python 3.10 project and ran Ruff.

```bash
uv run --frozen ruff check .                 # All checks passed!
uv run --frozen ruff format . --check        # 7 files already formatted
uv run --frozen ruff check . 2>&1 | grep -i warn   # (none: no unknown or deprecated rule codes)
```

body:
## Problem

The root `CLAUDE.md` says **`cva` 1.0 beta everywhere** — shadcn generates
`class-variance-authority`, and the standing instruction is to swap the import and wrap the
args into its object form after every `shadcn add`.

`proto-lab` was the last holdout. Six files still imported
`class-variance-authority` and called the old string-first API.

## What changed

- **10 call sites across 6 files** move to the object form:
  `cva('base', { variants })` → `cva({ base: 'base', variants })`
- **Dependency swapped**: `class-variance-authority` 0.7.1 out, `cva` 1.0.0-beta.9 in — the
  exact version `@ui/kit` and every other app already pin.

Files: `frame/variant-bar.tsx`, and `protos/001-session-progress-board/parts/`
`roadmap-list.tsx`, `session-rail.tsx`, `task-group.tsx`, `tickets-today.tsx`,
`context-residency.tsx`.

Nothing else moved. The app uses no `VariantProps`, no `defaultVariants`, no
`compoundVariants`, so the migration is the call shape and nothing more — no types to rewrite,
no behaviour to reason about at the call sites.

## Why this was left out of #47

#47 standardised every manifest, and it would have been easy to swap the dependency there and
call it done. I did not, because the dependency is the small half: the six files call the old
two-argument API, and changing the package without changing them produces classes that compile
and render wrong. That is app logic, so it earned its own PR.

author: topi-banana
body:
## Summary

`jals-hir` ships signature-only stubs for `java.lang` and `java.io` so that a reference to `String`
or `IOException` resolves. They are *bones*: no bodies, and nothing to run — the wasm backend says
so in as many words when a compile reaches one, *"a wasm host has no `java.base` to supply the
rest"*.

This adds that `java.base`, as a second native package on the seam #319 built. Fifty-two Java files
— `String`, `StringBuilder`, every wrapper, `Character`, `Math`, `System`, `Class`,
`java.io.PrintStream`, and twenty-four exception classes — compiled into the same module the project
is, behind **ten** host functions. Those ten are exactly the operations Java cannot express and a
dependency-free `no_std` crate can. Everything a program calls is the Java half.

```java
// examples/hello_world_java_base
System.out.println(new String(HELLO));                       // -> Hello, world!
System.out.println(Double.toString(Math.sqrt(value)));       // -> 1.4142135623730951
catch (NumberFormatException failure) {
    System.err.println(failure.toString());                  // -> java.lang.NumberFormatException: 12x
}
```

Related issue: N/A. Follows #319.

## What changed

### `jals-javac` — three refusals the backend made on valid Java (`a6fe3dc`)

Each is independently reachable and none needed a native package to hit; all three were found by
compiling one, because a `java.lang` is the first input large enough to reach them all. Split into
its own commit for that reason.

| where | what was wrong |
| --- | --- |
| `wasm/lower.rs` | An `int` literal past `i32::MAX` was refused as out of range. Every legal spelling of one is past it — JLS §3.10.1 admits `2147483648` as the operand of a unary minus (which wraps it back to itself, and is how `Integer.MIN_VALUE` is written), and a hexadecimal, octal or binary literal denotes its low 32 bits outright (`0xFFFFFFFF` is `-1`). Both the expression lowering and the constant-initialiser fold now take the low 32 bits; `i64` already read its own out-of-range spellings this way. |
| `wasm/lower.rs`, `wasm/encode.rs` | `==` over two references pushed two `anyref`s at `ref.eq`, which takes `eqref` — so the module failed validation with *"expected subtype of eqref, found anyref"*. That is what `String.equals(Object other) { if (other == this) … }` compiles to. A nullable `ref.cast` to the new `HeapType::Eq` narrows first; it always succeeds, since every reference this backend creates is a `struct.new` or an `array.new`, and staying nullable is what keeps `null == null` answering true rather than trapping. |
| `wasm/lower.rs` | `Lowering::overriders` sorted with a comparator that is not a total order: three classes where one extends another and the third is unrelated compare as `a < b`, `b == c`, `a == c`. Rust's sort detects the intransitivity and **panics**, so a dispatch with enough overriders aborted the compile. Ordering by depth in the class chain is the property the sort actually wants and is transitive by construction. |

### `jals-native` — the package (`50fa8fa`)

| area | what is there |
| --- | --- |
| `java/java/**` (52 files) | The Java half, one public type per file. `String` is a `char[]`; `Math.sqrt` is Newton's iteration over a mantissa reduced into `[1, 4)` with an exact-residual (Dekker) correction, which agrees with the JDK on every input tried but `Double.MAX_VALUE`. |
| `src/packages/java_base.rs` | The ten bindings and the `SystemHost` seam. `Decimal` re-lays `core`'s scientific form into Java's (`1.0` where Rust writes `1`, `1.0E-4` where Rust writes `0.0001`, `Infinity` where Rust writes `inf`), so the shortest-round-trip digits come from `core` and only the layout is ours. |
| `jals-cli`, `jals-lsp`, `jals-playground` | Each host builds its own `SystemHost`. `jals` sends `System.out` to stdout and `System.err` to stderr through `Shell` — which gains `plain_bytes`, the stderr counterpart of `machine_bytes`, because a module decides where its own line breaks are. The playground joins both into the Run pane; the language server discards, since it instantiates nothing. |
| `examples/hello_world_java_base` | A CI cell of its own, running `jals build` then `jals run --invoke describe -- 2`, then `fmt --check` and `lint`. |

Four properties are load-bearing, and the crate/README/CLAUDE.md docs state each:

- **A package's Java outranks a stub per FQN, so a type it declares must be a superset of the
  stub's members.** A member the stub had and this does not is one that disappears from analysis
  for every project that selects it — a regression with no diagnostic.
- **`java.lang.Object` is not declared and must not be.** It is the backend's `anyref`, and
  `Layout::class_ref` answers for it *before* it consults the struct table — so a declared `Object`
  would be one question with two answers, silently: a class that writes no `extends` gets no
  `Object` struct prefix, so a field on it would exist on some instances and not others.
- **One package publishes two Java packages**, and the JDK's own module name is why: `System.out`
  is a `java.io.PrintStream` in the stub this shadows, so a `java.lang` that superseded `System`
  without `java.io` beside it would be a `System` whose `out` had no type left.
- **What a project still cannot write is the backend's gap, not the package's** — a string literal
  (`String s = "x"`) and an autoboxing conversion (`Integer n = 1`). Until those land, a constant
  string is spelled as a `char[]`, which is what every constant in this package's own Java looks
  like.

Deliberately absent, each because of what the target is rather than as an omission: `Enum`,
`Record`, `Iterable` (needs `java.util.Iterator`), reflection, `Math`'s transcendentals, and full
Unicode case mapping. Each class says so where it declares what it *does* answer.

## Invariants

Neither the lexer, the parser nor the formatter is touched. One invariant from CLAUDE.md is in
scope and holds: **all project and artifact enumeration is deterministic.** The overriders fix
replaces an intransitive comparator with a stable sort by class-chain depth, and unrelated classes
keep their `layout.structs` order, which is a `BTreeMap`'s — so a dispatch chain is the same at
every compile. `NativePackageSet::select` already orders by registry name rather than by manifest
order, so selecting `java.base` does not depend on where it is written in `[build]
native-packages`.

## Testing

| file | what it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `jals-build/tests/java_base.rs` (new) | The three claims a review would otherwise take on trust. **It compiles** — every one of the 52 files is lowered, since a library input has every body lowered rather than only the reachable ones. **It supersedes what it shadows** — two indexes are built and their member sets diffed per FQN, so a lost stub member fails with its name. **It runs** — the renderings, parses, arithmetic, `System.out`/`System.err` split, and a `throw` from inside the package caught by the project are asserted through a module the engine actually executed. A fourth test pins the two remaining backend gaps **as failures**, so closing one fails this test and says which line to delete. |
| `jals-native/tests/package.rs` | The Rust half driven without an engine, over the `FakeHost` already there: the two streams stay apart until each flushes, the clock is the host's, the bit casts round-trip, and a rendering is written into the array the *module* allocated. |
| `jals-native/src/packages/java_base.rs` | `Decimal`'s unit tests: Java's renderings for thirteen values plus `NaN`/`±Infinity`, the `0.1f` case that proves a `float` is not rendered at `double` width, the buffer-length bound, and what a Java type suffix does to a parse. |
| `jals-javac/tests/wasm_lower.rs` | One pinned body per backend fix. These assert the emission without an engine, so they still run in CI's `wasm32-wasip1` cell, which has neither a JVM nor a wasm engine. |

Gates run locally, all green: `cargo fmt --all --che

author: vincent-pochet
body:
> Follow-up of #6314 and #6320.

## Context

`events:recover_pay_in_advance_fees` is very slow on an organization with a very large `events` table. It scanned the whole ingestion-time window for the organization, and no index carries the event code alongside the time, so every event ingested in the window was visited just to test its code. It also counted those candidates up front to show a total, walking the window twice before printing anything.

## Description

- Bound the window on the event `timestamp` rather than `created_at`, and walk one subscription external id at a time, so each lookup is served by an index leading on `external_subscription_id`. Cost now follows that subscription's events inside the window rather than everything the organization ingested.
- Drop the up-front count, so the header and progress appear immediately. Progress is reported per subscription, which gives back a total to measure against.

Timestamp is also the axis a pay-in-advance fee is billed against — its period comes from the event timestamp, and the cached aggregations it chains through are ordered by it — so replaying in timestamp order per subscription is closer to the original processing than ingestion order was.

## Behavior change to be aware of

- `FROM`/`TO` now bound the event timestamp. An event ingested during an outage but timestamped outside the window is no longer in scope; widen `FROM` to reach backdated ones.

author: tsukasai
body:
## Summary

Fixes #444 (critical): inside `$'...'` (ANSI-C quoting), brush-parser's tokenizer strips a backslash-newline pair the same way it does outside quotes, but bash's own ANSI-C decoding does not treat `\`+newline as a recognized escape there and keeps the raw newline. shguard trusts brush's decoded value, so recursing into it as a nested script (`bash -c $'...'`) let a `#` comment swallow a real command bash still runs on a separate line: `bash -c $'echo x #\<newline>rm -rf /'` reached `Allow`.

## Fix

Took the issue's own suggested "cruder fallback": `parse()` now fails closed to `Ask` whenever the raw command contains both `$'` and a literal backslash-newline anywhere, rather than a precise per-span comparison inside `convert_word`. This over-Asks when the two substrings are unrelated elsewhere in the same command, which is the safe direction here.

## Testing

- `cargo test`: 1532 lib tests + all integration suites, 0 failures.
- Repro from the issue body now returns `Ask` instead of `Allow`.
- False-positive controls confirmed unaffected: `$'...'` with no continuation, and a continuation with no `$'...'` elsewhere.

body:
## ① 買収前の店舗数

表を「買収前」「買収後」の 2 枚に分けた。

| 買収前 | トライアルHD | 西友 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 店舗数 | **343店**（2024年6月期） | **242店**（2024年12月期） |
| 売上 | **7,179億円** | **4,835億円** |

単純合算で **585店・1兆2,014億円・営業利益426億円**。買収後は **621店・1兆3,471億円**。
**店舗数 +36店、売上 +1,457億円**で、足し算より上に出ているのが見える。

## ② 「同じものがいくらか」なのに同じものを比較していない

**指摘のとおりだった。** 番組が測ったのはくるみパン259円／カツ丼299円／野菜詰め放題430円で、**別々の品目**。

- 節の題を **「いくらで買えるのか」** に直した
- **「なぜ『同じ商品を横並び』が作れないのか」** を新設

| 店 | 値段の公表 | なぜ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| オーケー | **チラシを出さない** | **EDLP だから。** 販促費・値札の貼り替え・人の張り付きが要らない。その削減ぶんが価格に回る |
| ロピア | 店舗ごと・その日ごと | 精肉の仕入れが相場で動く。全店共通の定価をとっていない |
| 肉のハナマサ | **公表している** | プロが仕入れに使う。値段が分からないと発注できない |
| 西友 | **公表している** | 駅前の一般客向け。チラシで来店を作る |
| 業務スーパー | 公表している | ただし**自社製造品が中心で、他店に同じ商品が無い** |

**公表しない理由が、そのまま各社の安さの型になっている。** そのうえで、同じ土俵の数字として
ハナマサの **100gあたり89円**（実物の値札）を位置づけ直した。

各社の公表物から同一商品の横並びが取れるかは **`t070`（#410・マージ済み）で調べに行っている。
ただし Mac 側のタスク実行が 15:21 UTC で止まっていて、まだ結果が返っていない。** 取れたら表を足す。

## ③ ドンキの売上を同じ棒に並べていた

**指摘のとおり。** 2兆2,467億円は総合ディスカウントストアかつ**グループ全体**の数字で、
食品スーパーとしての売上ではない。神戸物産の 5,517億円も **FC への卸額**。

売上の横棒は**並べてよい4社だけ**（トライアルG／オーケー／ロピア／まいばすけっと）にして、
この 2 社は **「並べてはいけない2社」**として理由つきの表に分けた。

## ④ 「買った」→「買収」

見出し・カード・アイキャッチの文言・本文・`description` をすべて統一。

## ⑤ 買収のソース

[トライアルHD「西友の株式の取得（完全子会社化）に関するお知らせ」](https://trial-holdings.inc/news/release/67c7e56725df23ba67b568c5/)／
[同「経営統合が完了」](https://trial-holdings.inc/news/release/686382439f0b7297ddd48fb7/)／
[流通ニュース](https://www.ryutsuu.biz/strategy/r030512.html) を本文のすぐ下に置いた。
**買収額 3,826億円**、KKR 傘下から85%・ウォルマート傘下から15% という内訳も足した。

## ついでに直したもの

`.cmp-table` は `white-space: nowrap` なので、**説明文の列があると右端で切れて横スクロール送りになる。**
描画して見つけた。折り返す `.prose-table` を足して 3 つの表に当てた。

## 検査

`check-article-ux.py` / `check-md-bold.py` 通過。アンカー全解決。「西友を買った」の残存 0。
売上の棒から PPIH が消えていることを HTML で確認。該当セクションを描画して目視確認した。

author: ruckus000
body:
A 275-agent adversarial review of the live support inbox raised **86 findings and refuted 50**. The 38 survivors collapsed to 20 distinct issues, and the sign-off was **"no, not as is"** - four defects to fix first. This is those four, plus one approved follow-on and the dead code.

**Two of the four were mine from earlier in this PR.**

## B4 - the `Re: (no subject)` fix never fired

The earlier commit in this PR taught `buildReplySubject` not to emit a parenthetical placeholder, with a property test across `null`, `''`, `'   '`, `'Re:'`. All passed. **None of them is what the caller sends.**

`support_inbox_threads.subject` is NOT NULL, so the ingest stores the literal `'(no subject)'` and `parent?.subject ?? thread.subject` resolves to that *string*, never to null. Confirmed in production - threads 3 and 4 hold `'(no subject)'` while their message rows hold NULL:

```
buildReplySubject(null ?? '(no subject)')  =>  "Re: (no subject)"
```

The fix was unreachable for the exact case it was written for, and the test passed honestly while proving nothing. The placeholder is now single-sourced as `SUPPORT_THREAD_NO_SUBJECT` in `packages/shared`, imported by both the ingest that writes it and the reply path that must treat it as absent.

Making the column nullable was rejected: it needs a migration plus three UI fallbacks (empty link in `InboxDashboard`, empty `<h1>` in `ThreadView`, untyped null through `inbox.ts:90`).

## B1 - a NUL byte permanently poisons the durability invariant

Postgres rejects U+0000 in `text` (22021) and `jsonb` (22P05). Neither is 23505, so `persistInboundEmail` rethrows and the route 500s - **the branch whose entire premise is that the failure is transient.** It isn't: Forward Email 421s, the sender's server holds and retries for 24-72h failing identically, then hard-bounces. Nothing is diagnosable, because the route deliberately logs no body.

Stripped at the boundary rather than in `readString`, because the quarantine path writes the whole payload into `raw_payload` (`jsonb`) and neither reader runs there. Two passes are needed: a raw `0x00` byte, and a backslash-u **escape**, which is six ordinary characters until `JSON.parse` decodes it. Placed strictly after signature verification, since the HMAC covers the bytes as sent.

## B2 - `html_body` stored as the literal string `"false"`

mailparser sets `html: false` (not undefined, not `''`) when there's no HTML part, and `readString` stringified it. Every plain-text-only sender wrote the word `false`, which sanitizes to a truthy string - so the console offered "Show original HTML" and rendered a word nobody sent. The pre-existing optional-fields test *omits* `html` rather than setting it false, so it exercised `undefined`.

## B3 - the idempotency key ignored the payload it protects

Per Resend's docs, a key lives 24h; a duplicate payload replays without sending, a **different** payload under an existing key returns 409. Subject, `In-Reply-To`, `References` and quoted text all derive from the parent - so a repeated short reply ("Thanks!") after new mail arrived changed the payload but not the key, throwing a 500 for 24 hours. The parent id is now in the key.

## F1 - the thread sort key was the sender's

`occurredAt = email.sentAt ?? new Date()` fed `last_message_at`, which the inbox orders by. A `Date:` of 1970 buried a thread permanently outside the 14-day fallback window; 2099 pinned it. Now our clock - a **net deletion**, since the backwards-move guard existed only because the value could be sender-supplied. `sent_at` still records the sender's claim.

## Deletions - ~130 lines, zero behaviour change

Headed by `api/admin/inbox/[threadId]/route.ts`: zero callers, and the only place in the feature where **unsanitized attacker HTML crossed the network**. Also `HtmlMessageFrame`'s grow-to-fit effect (dead by spec - `contentDocument` is null under an empty sandbox), `ReplyComposer`'s unused `mailbox` prop, two type guards with no importers, and `allowRemoteImages`, whose only consumer was its own test.

Three comments described things that do not exist, including one pointing at "migration 0067" when it is 0068 - and `0067_cron_runs.sql` exists and is unrelated, so it actively misdirected.

**Deliberately kept:** `ResolvedMailbox.unresolved` (5 reviewers wanted it gone) is the only field distinguishing a real alias match from the fallback in the cross-domain spoofing test; deleting it makes that test vacuous. Its comments were corrected instead. `data-blocked-src` stays - nothing renders it, but it is the only place a blocked tracker URL survives into the document.

**Explicitly not done:** recomputing the stat cards unfiltered. The proposed fix moves `.eq('status')` into JS, making `.limit(500)` apply *pre*-filter - it would silently drop closed threads from the table. That trades a cosmetic quirk for missing rows.

## Verification

Revert-check per `.claude/rules/verification.md` on each fix - the failure message names the defect:

```
B1  the expected string prints with the surviving NUL escape still in it
B2  expected 'false' to be null                                    (x2)
B3  expected 'support-reply:42:1aa7b1c1...' not to be 'support-reply:42:1aa7b1c1...'
B4  expected 'Re: (no subject)' to be 'Re: your message to PropertyPro'
```

B4's property test **now** reddens under revert; it did not before, because its array lacked the one value production supplies. That is the whole lesson.

226 tests pass, all 29 guards pass, typecheck clean, admin build succeeds. F1 carries no unit test - the service has no mock harness and building one for a two-line net deletion isn't proportionate; it is covered by the live check.

body:
Levels used to need 1000 XP while Mochi handed out ~10 at a time, so the bar felt frozen. This makes leveling cozy and alive.

**Faster curve (200 XP per level)**
- Shared curve in UserProgress.levelForXp (client) and levelForXp (mochi_chat) so the app, Mochi, and the bar always agree.
- Mochi default award 10 -> 25 and is told to be generous (20-50 big moments, 10-20 small wins).
- Saved XP totals stay, so levels jump once (e.g. 450 XP goes L1 -> L3).

**Auto XP for daily moments**
- Mood 20 (1/day), journal 30 (2/day), garden visit 10 (1/day), star drop 15 (3/day).
- Caps live in the same progress-doc transaction (dailyXp map): no extra reads, no rules change.
- A normal cozy day earns ~45-75 XP, so a level lands every 2-4 days.

body:
## O que muda

Fecha o buraco da auditoria: o embarque/desembarque em **texto livre** que menciona uma cidade da rota onde **não paramos** (Bacabeira, Santa Rita, Entroncamento, Colombo, Miranda, Matões) faz a reserva nascer **`pendente`** — não ocupa vaga, o cliente é avisado que vamos verificar, e a **equipe recebe um alerta**.

- **`domain/cidades.js`** (novo, puro): `classificarLocal(texto)` → `"atendida" | "intermediaria"`, `foraDaAreaPadrao(textos)`. Listas são fallback; aceitam override de `settings`. Cobertura 100%, mutation 91%.
- **`App.jsx`**: passa a usar `foraDaAreaPadrao` — a heurística inline duplicada (`CIDADES_INTERMEDIARIAS` + `contemCidadeIntermediaria`) saiu (AGENTS.md §2, fonte única). `CIDADES_ATENDIDAS` saiu de `constants.js` para `cidades.js`.
- **Bot** (`_shared/whatsappService.ts`): `mencionaCidadeIntermediaria()` lê `settings.intermediate_cities` (já existe no banco, fallback embutido); `enqueueAreaReviewAlert()` enfileira `notifications` com `template_key: "reserva_fora_de_area"`.
- **Bot** (`_shared/conversationEngine.ts`): `finalizeReservation` classifica desembarque + detalhe + bairro **antes** de criar a reserva, manda `status: "pendente"` + `pendingReason`, dispara o alerta interno. A mensagem "vamos confirmar" já existia e agora de fato acontece.
- **e2e**: novo caso — desembarque "perto do posto em **Bacabeira**" → `rpc_create_reservation` chamado com `p_status: "pendente"`. 16 specs verdes (chromium + mobile).

Nada de migração — `settings.served_cities` e `settings.intermediate_cities` já estão semeados.

## Por quê

Closes #6

## Como testar

- **Painel** (aba Reservar): escolher desembarque "Outros locais" e escrever algo com "Bacabeira"/"Santa Rita" → aparece o aviso "ficará pendente"; a reserva entra como pendente (não conta vaga, aparece no contador de pendentes da Agenda).
- **Bot** (quando as Edge Functions subirem): responder o desembarque com uma cidade intermediária → resposta "vamos confirmar" + linha em `notifications` (`select payload from notifications where template_key='reserva_fora_de_area'`).
- `cd frontend && npm run test` (91) · `npm run test:e2e` (16)

## Checklist

- [x] Lint / Knip / Arch — verdes (76 módulos)
- [x] `npm run test` 91/91, cobertura do domínio 100%/98%
- [x] `npm run test:mutation` 91,3% ≥ break 75 (cidades.js entra no mutate)
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` 16/16
- [x] Reserva pendente **não** ocupa vaga (`p_status: "pendente"` → RPC cria passageiros como 'cancelado', igual frete/encomenda)
- [x] Fallback humano preservado — alerta interno + reserva revisável na Agenda

author: eshelton328
body:
Adds the ALEC shower-presence companion as a routed 64 × 56 mm, four-layer PCB and a circular 116 mm diameter × 54 mm enclosure fit prototype. Native KiCad, editable Blender, STEP parts, schematic previews and populated-board renders are included in the board/enclosure READMEs and root catalog.

Routine service is through the screw-fastened rear cover. The three-AA holder opens toward that cover, with POWER, RESET and BOOT alongside it on the rear of the PCB. A fixed internal carrier keeps the cells, wiring and board installed when the cover is removed. The LD2410C faces the opposite, outward side; the presence LED and membrane-covered battery/pairing button remain accessible outside. USB retains its front-side location and reviewed signal routing, so inserting a flashing cable may still require carrier/PCB removal.

The electrical design retains the ESP32-S3, RV-3028 RTC and reviewed TPS63070 converter cells, including their short capacitor connections and switch-node copper. GPIO16 enables radar 5 V, GPIO17/18 provide UART, GPIO4 receives presence and GPIO11 controls default-open TMUX1511 signal isolation. A C&K 1101M2S3CQE2 provides the hard battery disconnect; a Littelfuse 046701.5NRHF fuse sits near the battery connector. All 88 electrical components have explicit prototype ordering candidates. USB is data-only, with no AA charging path.

S1.1 changes three control footprint placements/faces and affected routing from S1; electrical topology and values are unchanged. An ordering audit corrects C29 to the 0402 Murata GRM155R71C104KA88D for its existing footprint, with no geometry change. The assembly imports the actual populated PCB, MPD BH3AAW holder and Hi-Link LD2410C geometry. It has a solid PC radar face, proposed rear O-ring seal and external mounting-cradle interface. The radar uses a nominal 12.4 mm front gap and 3.6 mm PC wall. PCB/radar/button/LED/mount/control coordinates are checked against the mechanical interface file.

Validation performed locally:

- KiCad 10.0.1: zero ERC/DRC violations, zero schematic-parity issues, zero unconnected items; JLCPCB advanced four-layer profile passes.
- Saved-copper coverage: 277 pad nodes across 60 nets. All 47 independent schematic interface assertions, eight rear-service assertions and layout intent checks pass. USB signal copper matches the prior S1 geometry.
- Python: 127 passed, one Docker-dependent integration module skipped. Negative tests include UART swap, isolation/fuse bypass, forward-facing service button inward-opening holder and stale BOM substitution. A new BOM check verifies 88 component MPNs against native sources and 27 selected capacitor package codes.
- CadQuery 2.8.0: valid solids and 19 selected nominal solid/approach intersection checks pass, including control access with the holder and carrier installed. All 88 electrical footprints resolve to 19 local STEP models.
- Free ngspice: 27 passive input-inrush cases regenerated using the revised 78.1 mΩ summed battery trace resistance, plus 72 battery-source and 12 lumped thermal sensitivity cases. These are bounded screens, not converter-switching/EMI or junction-temperature qualification.
- Blender renders regenerated and visually reviewed; delivered sources, models and reports are bound by the evidence hash manifest.

[Full S1.1 test report](https://github.com/eshelton328/the-forge/blob/codex/alec-sensor-design/boards/alec-sensor/TEST-REPORT.md) · [Enclosure/render gallery](https://github.com/eshelton328/the-forge/blob/codex/alec-sensor-design/enclosures/alec-sensor/README.md) · [PCB/schematic gallery](https://github.com/eshelton328/the-forge/blob/codex/alec-sensor-design/boards/alec-sensor/README.md)

The sensor CI regenerates electrical/power evidence, checks the rear-service contract and separately rebuilds nominal CAD. Standard board CI discovers `boards/alec-sensor`; the old study path redirects to the new sources. The board, sensor/SPICE, mechanical, Python and openEMS fixture checks passed on `2578d07`. CI for the latest C29 ordering/metadata correction is pending. The correction preserves native geometry and circuit values exactly; the committed metadata-change evidence binds retained renders and simulation results to that unchanged geometry.

The immediate goal is a small paired engineering PCB order: `alec-main`, `alec-controls`, `alec-front` and `alec-sensor`. The user reports a working breadboard and detection through a plastic food container. Final enclosure work is deferred while we prepare the electronics for bench testing; supplier parts, placement, stackup and assembly preflight remain open. See the [prototype order plan](https://github.com/eshelton328/the-forge/blob/codex/alec-sensor-design/boards/alec-sensor/PROTOTYPE-ORDER.md).

Keep this as a draft engineering prototype pending order-package review. There is no implemented sensor firmware, measured battery endurance, physical parasitic/thermal qualification, validated water-only rejection or ingress rating. Scheduled sensing is the proposed default: illustrative assumptions yield about 11.6 hours continuous versus 22 days at 30 minutes awake daily. Manufacturing stackup/process, effective capacitance, fuse/switch inrush, wet detection, seal tolerances, carrier retention and manufacturing splits remain open. In particular, the carrier plate has only 0.61 mm nominal clearance to PCB screw heads; physical access, cell extraction, clip creep and tolerances require samples. No manufacturing order or physical qualification is implied.

author: ashokhein
body:
Competition desk Wave 3. 22 commits on top of `main`.

## What changes for an organiser

**The competition page gains a live in-play band.** Fixtures currently being
played, and what is up next, surfaced at the top of the competition rather than
found by opening each division. Served by a new
`/api/v1/competitions/[id]/desk` route.

**The stage card stops being a rail.** W2 gave each stage a
`md:grid-cols-[1fr_280px]` split — a 280px control rail beside a body with
nothing in it. Measured at 1280, each active stage rendered a **163px void out
of a 262px card (62% empty)**, because the rail's height set the card's. The
rail is retired; controls stack under the body and the card is sized by its
content. Void after: **1px**.

**The body now answers the question the card was raising.** A counts line —
scheduled / in play / done — replaces the progress bar, which encoded those
same three numbers as a width nobody could read. Zero counts are omitted
rather than printed as "0 in play"; a stage with no fixtures renders no
progress section at all. Each stage carries a **"View N fixtures"** control
that filters the run sheet to that stage.

**Auto-schedule leaves the fixtures page.** Scheduling belongs to the Schedule
page, which already owns the full `AutoScheduleMode` flow. The fixtures page
keeps the unscheduled count as a *fact* and links to where the action lives.

**Required court tags** become one button and a dialog instead of a wrapping
field.

**The run sheet's group headers stick again.** They were pinning to their own
card rather than the viewport, because two ancestors carried `overflow-hidden`
— a `sticky` element pins to its nearest scroll container — so on a long list
the headers scrolled away. Sections also gained vertical separation.

**Phones.** The desk unifies on one breakpoint (`md`, not `sm`), run-sheet rows
become two deliberate lines instead of a groomed shrink, and the stage's edit
controls fold into a bottom sheet below 768. One DOM, branched — no second
phone tree; ≥768 is unchanged.

## Verification

- **Unit: 14650 total / 14583 passed / 0 failed / 67 pending**, full suite from
  `apps/web` with `DATABASE_URL` and `PLACEMENT_SERVICE_HOST` both set (without
  them 3,539 tests silently skip). All 1151 suite paths confirmed inside the
  worktree.
- `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors**, re-run after the rebase.
- ESLint: **0 errors** (146 pre-existing warnings, none in the changed files).
- Locales: 11 new keys present in all four dictionaries, `i18n-keys.ts`
  regenerated; the two retired keys have zero remaining references. Tests
  assert the four locales are not the same English string copied four times.
- Visually signed off by the owner per screen at 320 / 390 / 430 / 768 / 834 /
  1280.

Three earlier full-suite failures (`credits-monthly-cron`,
`org-posts-digest`) were **environmental** — two carried this repo's
`STACK_TRACE_ERROR` timeout signature, both files are untouched by this branch,
both are green in isolation (34/34), and the suite then passed 0-failed at a
*higher* machine load than the run that produced them.

## CI note

`e2e.yml` triggers on push to `main` only, so **this PR gets no automatic e2e
run** — smoke is the only automatic signal here. Given how much of this wave is
seven-width layout behaviour, e2e is being dispatched manually against this PR
via `workflow_dispatch`.

## Not fixed here

`.btn-primary` renders 2px shorter than `.btn-ghost`/`.btn-danger` —
`globals.css` gives the latter two a `border` and the former none. Repo-wide
blast radius, filed rather than changed inside a desk wave.

author: imcbeth
body:
Prometheus's `ruleSelector` is `matchLabels: {release: kube-prometheus-stack}`. A rule without it is created **successfully**, appears in `kubectl get prometheusrule`, reports no error — and **never loads**.

**Three occurrences:**
- **2026-07-31** — `velero-alerts`, dormant **198 days** (#848). The alerts that would have caught 16 days of silent backup failure.
- **2026-09-07** — **six more** at once (#896).
- **2026-09-07** — a **seventh, found by this check**: `pvc-mount-monitor-alerts`.

REFERENCE.md has carried this gotcha since the first occurrence and it recurred twice anyway. Documentation alone is demonstrably insufficient.

Adds `scripts/validate-prometheusrules.sh` as a pre-commit hook — scans **by content, not filename**, so it finds rules embedded in multi-doc manifests. Verified both directions: passes clean, exits 1 naming the file on violation.

### The seventh matters more than the count

**`PVCMountReadOnly` has had zero rules loaded this entire time.** The remediator itself was unaffected — #753 deliberately rewrote it to query monitor pods directly rather than Prometheus alerts, precisely so it wouldn't depend on the monitoring stack. But that means **the human-facing notification never fired**. Had the remediator stopped working, nothing would have said so.

That's F7 (dead-man switch) restated from a different angle.

My earlier audit missed it because it globbed `*alerts*.yaml`; this rule lives inside `pvc-mount-monitor.yaml` next to the DaemonSet. Scanning by content is why the script caught it.

author: gloiiire
body:
Trois décisions de l'auteur du 7 septembre, prises par l'outil de sélection.

## Les noms d'idoles reçoivent la couche des Shemot

**Merumath, Barisat, Nahon, Zucheus, Joavon** passent de `==…==` à `[[…]]` et reçoivent chacun leur fiche. Par cohérence, les deux toponymes du slavon les suivent — **Fandana** et le fleuve **Gur** —, et **Ora / Oron**, deux formes du nom de [[Haran]], deviennent des alias vers sa fiche plutôt que d'en avoir une.

**59 marques converties, 7 fiches neuves.**

J'avais argumenté l'inverse : un nom qu'un artisan transfère d'un bloc à l'autre n'est pas un **Shem** au sens du §3.2. **L'arbitrage retenu est meilleur**, et les fiches le disent — le nom reste un nom propre, et le lecteur doit pouvoir le toucher **pour comprendre pourquoi il ne porte rien**. Une couche qui refuserait ça le laisserait devant un mot coloré sans recours.

## `'irin` garde son apostrophe, et la fiche prend son nom

`lexique/irin.md` → `lexique/'irin.md`. Le §2.9 gagne son exception écrite : il ne légifère que sur l'hébreu, et `'irin` est de l'**araméen**, où l'apostrophe marque le ayin initial que la règle hébraïque laisse tomber. Seul terme du corpus dans ce cas — d'où la règle écrite plutôt que sue.

## Les `**elohim**` fabriqués gardent le mot

Confirmé sans changement. L'hébreu emploie *elohim* pour le Créateur et pour les dieux d'une maison sans marque qui les sépare ; en ajouter une trancherait à la place du texte. **C'est cette indistinction qui rend possible « n'est-il pas l'Elohim de ses elohim ? »** Les marqueurs « à confirmer » tombent.

## Ce que le contrôle a attrapé — dans ce que je venais d'écrire

```
**à la lettre**   **avait**   **déjà tombé**   **Shemot**
[[Rivqah]]        [[Ya'aqov]]
```

Quatre gras d'emphase et deux Shemot sans fiche, **dans les sept fiches elles-mêmes**, écrites dix minutes plus tôt.

C'est la troisième fois cette semaine que ce contrôle me reprend moi. **Il n'a jamais servi à surveiller quelqu'un d'autre.**

## Contrôles

```
0 termes inconnus · 0 marqueurs déséquilibrés · 0 mots d'or sans fiche
0 Shemot sans fiche · 0 liens livrés qui n'ouvrent rien
```

author: inf-1oop
body:
## Summary

Adds a second reward model to `VanaPoolEntity` alongside the existing APY drip: a **Synthetix-V3-style linear STREAM**, selectable **per entity** with a maintainer switch. An entity vests its `lockedRewardPool` into `activeRewardPool` either by the current continuous-compounding APY drip (unchanged) or by a scheduled linear stream. Per-staker rewards, bonding, and forfeiture are untouched — this changes only how an entity moves locked → active.

**Draft:** the core (Phases 1–3 of the plan) is complete and tested; views, interaction-policy decisions, and the full-lifecycle integration test remain (see Remaining below).

## What's here

- **Storage foundation** — `RewardModel { APY, STREAM }` (APY = 0, so the upgrade is behaviour-neutral) and a `RewardSchedule` struct (active entry + one queued follow-on), appended to `Entity`. Layout verified unchanged via `forge inspect` (Entity is mapping-held).
- **`_vestStream`** — linear vesting math ported from Synthetix `RewardDistribution.updateEntry`, minus per-share/D18 scaling (VanaPool vests raw wei into the pooled `activeRewardPool`). Preserves the interval when `totalShares == 0`; promotes the queued entry when the active one ends.
- **`processRewards`** branches on `entity.rewardModel`; APY path character-identical to today.
- **`updateEntityRewardModel`** — maintainer-only switch, settles the outgoing model before flipping (conservation-verified both directions).
- **`distributeRewards`** — the scheduling API: Synthetix replace/queue semantics, funded by `msg.value` and/or locked residue, with an escrow check (`InsufficientRewardFunds`) so every scheduled reward is backed by locked funds. Owner-or-maintainer gated, STREAM-only, `start >= now`.

## Deliberate design choices

- **Zero-shares vesting preserves the interval** (matches Synthetix `updateEntry`, not its pool→vault trickle drop) — rewards vest to whoever holds shares when they return, never into a zero-share pool.
- **Cancelled/displaced remainders stay funded in `lockedRewardPool` as residue** (our in-protocol adaptation; Synthetix returns them to an external distributor). No funds leave the protocol.
- **`distributeRewards` is privileged** (owner/maintainer) while `addRewards` stays permissionless and additive — a stranger can donate but cannot cancel or defer an entity's schedule.

## Testing

Foundry, scoped `foundry.toml` (viaIR, mirrors hardhat settings). 22 tests across three suites — vesting math (linear, timing-invariance, zero-shares, instant, queue cycle, conservation fuzz), the model switch (conservation, settle, access), and scheduling (install, replace-on-overlap, queue, escrow, guards, end-to-end vest). Harness-based, since the switch/schedule/vesting paths touch only entity storage + pure math.

## Remaining (tracked, not in this draft)

- Views: `entityRewardSchedule`, model-aware current-rate/APY, runway.
- Interaction policy: `returnForfeitedRewards` → residue in STREAM mode; the paused-entity `processRewards` gap (affects both models); optional `topUpQueuedRewards`.
- Full-lifecycle integration test through the real proxy + VanaPoolStaking + treasury, including the `msg.value > 0` funding path (unit tests used residue).
- `EntityInfo`/`entities()` view does not yet surface the new fields.

## Notes for reviewers

- After pulling: `git submodule update --init` (forge-std).
- `foundry.toml` here scopes `src` to `contracts/vanaStaking`; it will conflict with the deposit branch's scoped config on merge — main should get a single `src = "contracts"` version.
- UUPS upgrade of `VanaPoolEntityImplementation` only; `VanaPoolStaking` untouched.

author: vaibhavtiwarigithub
body:
## Why

Free-tier Function Storage (10 GB) hit 100%. Function Storage bills the bundle of every function in **every retained deployment**, so the cost is `deployments × functions × bundle size`.

Attribution across the team:

| Project | Retained deployments | Functions each | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **financeos** | hundreds (back to 2026-07-24, at 7–19/day) | 11 Node + 1 Python | ~all of the 10 GB |
| hardware-ai-hub | 7 | 3 Node | negligible; unlinked duplicate of home-ai |
| home-ai | 3 | **0** (fully static) | zero |
| fin-nudge | 1 | 1 Node | negligible |

A large share of those financeos deployments are previews nobody looks at. The parallel-worktree rule in `CLAUDE.md` pushes `worktree-agent-*` branches, and each one built a full 11-lambda preview — three landed within 156 seconds of each other on 2026-07-24.

## What changed

One key in `vercel.json`:

```json
"ignoreCommand": "if [ \"$VERCEL_ENV\" = \"production\" ] || [ \"$VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF\" = \"main\" ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi"
```

Builds on `main`, or whenever `VERCEL_ENV=production`. Skips every other ref.

## Verification

Vercel's exit-code convention is **inverted from intuition** — `0` *ignores* the build, `1` *continues* it — so a wrong guess silently stops production from deploying. Direction confirmed against Vercel's own `vercel.json` documentation, and the command was executed across all seven branch/env combinations before commit:

```
VERCEL_ENV   VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF        exit  result
production   main                          1    BUILD
production   worktree-agent-a258f...       1    BUILD
preview      main                          1    BUILD
preview      worktree-agent-a258f...       0    skip
preview      worktree-agent-ac016...       0    skip
preview      claude/function-storage...    0    skip
<unset>      <unset>                       0    skip
```

Production is tested **first and independently of the branch name**, so it cannot be skipped even if the ref check is wrong. `crons` (4) and `functions` (`api/py/*.py`) asserted unchanged after the edit.

## Trade-off

**PR branches no longer get preview URLs.** To get one: push to `main`, or drop the key temporarily. This PR's own branch is the first thing the change skips.

## Not in this PR

- **The Python bundle.** `api/py/ic.py` pulls `statsmodels` + `scipy` + `numpy` (~250–300 MB of site-packages) to call `sm.OLS(cov_type='HAC')` and `spearmanr`. Its own docstring says it exists to cross-check the TS implementation — a verification oracle, not a money-path dependency. It is the largest per-deployment item, but slimming it changes numerics and needs its own architecture gate.
- **Deleting the existing backlog of deployments.** This session had no Vercel write access (the MCP server exposes no delete tool; no CLI, no token), so a dry-run-by-default cleanup script was handed over to run locally instead. This PR stops the bleeding; it does not reclaim what is already stored.

## Scope

No agent, schema, cron, scoring, or money-path change. `WORK_LOG.md` updated. No `docs/arch/` chapter owns build-trigger policy — per `00-index.md` the update rules cover agents, schema, providers, schedules, env vars, safety gates and the learning loop, none of which this touches — so no chapter was edited.

author: jdfalk
body:
## What
Compresses the SQLite activity `details` column with **pure-Go zstd** so the log is comparable in size to Pebble's compressed footprint — fixing the disk blow-up that forced the SQLite re-enable rollback on 2026-09-07.

A class of `change` rows carries multi-MB `details` blobs (iTunes `ApplyITLOperations` dumps). Pebble stores the activity keyspace block-compressed; SQLite has no transparent text compression, so raw JSON ballooned `activity.sqlite` past 30 GB. SQLite has no built-in text compression, so this is application-level.

## How
- Central codec `encodeActivityDetails` / `decodeActivityDetails` (`klauspost/compress`, no cgo — matches the `modernc.org/sqlite` driver choice).
- Stored as a **tagged BLOB**: 1-byte format tag (`0x00` raw, `0x01` zstd) + payload. Below a threshold, or when compression doesn't shrink, the value stays raw → stored size never exceeds original+1. A **legacy untagged raw-JSON** value (leading `{`/`[`) still reads back, so a pre-change DB loads unchanged.
- Applied at **all 5 boundaries**: `rowArgs` write, `RecompactDigests` UPDATE write, `scanEntries` read, `commitDayDigest` existing-digest read, `RecompactDigests` read.
- Schema: `details TEXT` → `details BLOB` (prod DB was wiped; recreates fresh).

### Why only `details`
Every other column is queried/indexed/searched (`tier/type/level/source/operation_id/book_id/ts` in WHERE+indexes, `summary` via `instr()` search, `tags` via `json_each()`, `src_key` is the unique index) and is tiny. `details` holds ~all the bytes; compressing the rest would break querying for no gain.

## Tests
- Codec: 9.6 MB-shaped blob compresses hugely + round-trips; tiny payload stays raw (no growth); empty→nil; legacy untagged JSON reads verbatim; high-entropy payload falls back to raw.
- Store-level: a large `details` is stored as a compressed BLOB (`<< raw`) and reads back byte-for-byte through the normal query path.
- All activity/backfill tests green under `-race`.

## Follow-ups filed (todo.d)
- Activity-log **reset feature** (multi-confirm, audit who/when/source-IP durably, mask-by-default UI + unredacted export, runs as the `audiobook` service user).
- **Reauth/passkey reverify** gate before unredacted export and destructive resets.
- **Full-app-database reset**, gated on that reauth.
- **Re-enable SQLite** after verifying the compressed on-disk size (separate deploy step; SQLite stays OFF on prod meanwhile).

author: lexgub-peru
body:
PR nuevo: el #8 ya está fusionado y no puede seguir trabajo. Esta rama parte del `main` actual.

## 1. La marca: se elimina el gallo

Se probaron tres direcciones antes de decidir, renderizadas a 44, 28, 20 y 14 px sobre marfil y sobre navy:

| Dirección | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| **A** — wordmark puro `LEXGUB \| PERÚ` | Aguanta de 44 a 14 px. Lee como marca jurídica seria. |
| **B** — wordmark + gesto abstracto (cresta / perfil heráldico / pluma) | Los tres colapsan por debajo de 20 px: leen como garabato, mancha y hoja. |
| **C** — monograma LG | Funciona; el filete se ensucia a 16 px y hubo que afinarlo. |

**Decisión: A para el logotipo, C afinado para favicon y avatar. Sin isotipo figurativo.** Un símbolo que no aguanta el tamaño de una pestaña del navegador no es una marca, y era exactamente el problema señalado: literal, caricaturesco, desproporcionado en móvil.

Especificación fijada:

- **LEXGUB** — Source Serif 4, peso 700, interletrado 0,095 em.
- **Filete** — regla vertical dorada, 3 % de la altura de mayúscula.
- **PERÚ** — Source Serif 4, peso 600, interletrado 0,175 em, 80 % de la altura de LEXGUB.
- Proporción del lockup: **8,2 : 1**.

Las letras van como **trazados**, generados desde la propia Source Serif 4 con fontTools. Un logotipo con `<text>` cambia de forma si la tipografía no está instalada —un PDF, una tarjeta, LinkedIn— y baila mientras la fuente carga. Un único archivo sirve sobre fondo claro y oscuro: «LEXGUB» hereda `currentColor` y «PERÚ» toma `--brand-peru`.

Archivos en `public/brand/`: `lexgub-wordmark.svg` (maestro), `lexgub-dark.svg`, `lexgub-light.svg`, `lexgub-mark.svg` (monograma en caja), `lexgub-monogram.svg` (letras sueltas). Favicon actualizado.

## 2. Cabecera y navegación

Corrige tres defectos reales:

- **`.navbar` estaba declarada en seis bloques** con `min-height` contradictorias (68, 72, 66, 58 px). Ahora hay una sola declaración, a 68 px (62 px por debajo de 700 px).
- **La marca se aplastaba hasta 0 px.** Sin `flex: 0 0 auto`, la barra la comprimía antes de dejar desbordar los enlaces (`white-space: nowrap`), que acababan pisando el logotipo. Reproducible a 1280 y 1440 px.
- **El cajón se ocultaba por encima de 861 px mientras la hamburguesa seguía visible hasta 1240 px**: entre esas anchuras el menú no abría nada.

Además: nueve destinos en la barra —el máximo que cabe a 1260 px junto a la marca, el buscador y el CTA—, y el **cajón pasa a estar disponible en todas las anchuras** con el mapa completo del sitio, en tres columnas desde 900 px. Ninguna ruta depende ya de que quepa arriba. El disparador del buscador pasa a solo icono por debajo de 1440 px.

En móvil el lockup mide 21 px de alto → **172 px de ancho, el 48 % del ancho útil a 390 px**.

## 3. Radar normativo

`/radar` es una línea de tiempo de normas, modificatorias y jurisprudencia **ya incorporadas al compendio**, agrupadas por año, filtrables, cada una con su fecha y su enlace oficial. 59 entradas, todas contrastadas con fuente oficial identificada.

`app/data/radar.ts` no consulta ninguna fuente externa ni infiere fechas: hereda de cada ficha su marca `verificacion` y deja sin ordenar lo que no puede interpretar, en lugar de inventarle fecha.

Convivía con una implementación previa del Radar como selección curada de píldoras por categoría. Se conserva la línea de tiempo —crece sola conforme crece el compendio, mientras que la selección por categoría solapaba con `/pildoras`— y de la otra se conserva el aviso «Criterio editorial del Radar», que advierte sobre régimen transitorio y versión vigente.

## 4. Portada

- Titular de 33,6 a **30,4 px en 390 px**, medida de 20ch, interlineado 1,09.
- Entradilla condensada de seis a cinco líneas, medida de 58ch.
- Búsquedas frecuentes en pastillas, no en enlaces subrayados.
- **Retrato del fundador en óvalo con filete dorado**, contenido a 168 px.
- Se retira el bloque `<style>` embebido en `app/page.tsx`: era una séptima capa CSS que además apuntaba a clases de marca (`.lgBrandMark`, `.lgBrandName`, `.lgBrandCountry`) que ya no existen. Su intención está recogida en `globals.css`.

## 5. Limpieza

Eliminados: dos sistemas de marca huérfanos (`.lexgubBrand*` de V4 y `.lgBrand*` de V5), el componente `.navAssistant` (sin uso) y el bloque `.homeRadar` (huérfano desde la reescritura de la portada). Radios y sombras más discretos: la jerarquía la marcan el filete, el color y el espacio.

## Verificación

**Build:** `✓ Compiled successfully` · `✓ Generating static pages (54/54)`. TypeScript limpio.

**Responsive:** Playwright en **390, 412, 430, 768, 1024 y 1440 px** sobre once rutas. **Cero desbordamientos horizontales.**

Puntos de corte reales: ≥1440 buscador con etiqueta · ≥1260 enlaces en la barra · ≥900 cajón en tres columnas · ≤700 marca a 21 px · ≤560 el CTA se repliega.

## Lo que no se tocó

No se alteró ningún dato normativo ni jurisprudencial. No se añadieron normas, artículos, resoluciones, modificatorias ni fechas. Sin login, testimonios, clientes, cifras ni afiliaciones. Sin escudos ni logos de entidades públicas. El aviso de independencia sigue en el pie y en las franjas de fuentes.

## Pendiente

- `AGENTS.md` y `CLAUDE.md` los regenera `next dev`; quedan fuera de este PR por no ser parte del rediseño.
- El retrato sigue siendo la imagen de biblioteca aportada; si llega la versión definitiva basta sustituir `public/marvyn-gallo-retrato.webp`.

No fusionar sin revisión.

body:
Adds internal coaching-staff assignments to the validated dated Structured Schedule. 

Head Coach and Super Admin can assign one Primary Coach and optional Assistant Coaches to scheduled training sessions, while Coach and Assistant Coach receive a read-only My Assigned Sessions view showing only their upcoming responsibilities. 

Assignment changes preserve audit history by deactivating previous rows rather than physically deleting them. 

Sessions with active staff assignments are protected from recurring-template synchronization so an operationally staffed session cannot be silently moved or removed by a later Class Template change. 

Member-facing Schedule data remains unchanged and does not expose coaching assignments. No QR/session linking, Training Program/Log linking, exception management or punctuality logic is introduced.

Includes a targeted TypeScript typing fix for assistant coach IDs in the session-assignment API. No runtime behavior, database schema or assignment logic is changed.

author: rodohasarrived
body:
## Summary

No Meridian behavior changes. This appends the 2026-09-07 scheduled pass to
`docs/architecture/security-master-extensibility-review.md`, re-read against `193afa1a` — 238 commits
after the 2026-09-01 baseline.

**Re-verified as still open:** A1 (the cash-flow resolver's alias list still lacks `currentCouponRate`,
the key `DirectLoan` declares; `principalBasis` still falls back to `100m`), A3, A4, N4/N5, and the
deferred quartet. Also records what the range *did* close on its own terms: `SecurityTermsProjectionRegistry`
is the declarative projection pattern this document asked for twice, covering 2 of 26 classes and
staging the remaining eleven hand-written writers deliberately — noted so it is not later read as the
quartet's closure.

**Seven new findings (C1–C7)**, from walking each declared capability outward to the consumer that
must honour it, rather than from the consumer inward:

| # | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| C1 | No issuer entity. `IssuerId` returns nothing repo-wide; issuer is free text denormalized per security. `Lei` and `Cik` — which the enum's own doc comments call entity identifiers — are carried in the per-security identifier namespace because there is no entity table. "Issuer concentration" exists only as a `RiskModelHints` prose string, twice, with nothing implementing it. |
| C2 | Credit rating and sector/industry have no canonical home. The only place to record a rating is the operator override overlay, whose contract states it never amends canonical terms. The shared taxonomy catalog declares five vocabularies; none is sector or rating. |
| C3 | `InstrumentTypeDescriptorCatalog` is a second per-asset-class capability matrix restating `SecurityAssetClassCatalog` facts in different types. It is in no parity guard and already disagrees on identifier spellings. |
| C4 | No route exposes the terms schema or asset-class catalog, so both clients hardcode four divergent vocabularies — including a details tracker offering five non-canonical class names and bucketing 26 classes into three field-visibility sets, and a CSV hint advertising eight importable classes where the server permits two. |
| C5 | Six classes marked `SupportsCashflowScheduleByDefault: true` can never project one — `Repo`'s `endDate`, `CommitmentGuarantee`'s `expiryDate`, `PrivateFundInterest`'s `navDate` and `RealEstateHolding`'s `valuationDate` are not maturity aliases; `MoneyMarketFund` and `CashSweep` declare no terminal date. Fails silently. |
| C6 | `SecurityMasterAmortizationLedgerBridge` cites the cost-basis service's lot filter and omits its `AmortizesTowardPar` gate. Latent, not live — the bridge has no production caller. |
| C7 | `DirectLoan` reaches the accounting slice only through vendor aliases: its canonical name is absent from `IsFixedIncome` and its catalog entry declares no `AccountingInstrumentClass`. |

Priorities from the pass, in order: model the issuer (unblocks C2); add a parity guard binding
capability flags to the engines that must honour them (closes C5 and C7 and would have caught A1 in
August); serve the terms schema over HTTP (retires three hardcoded UI vocabularies); guard or collapse
the second capability matrix; fix the amortization bridge's filter.

Scheduled institutional-requirements review of the Security Master architecture, in the cadence this
document has carried since 2026-08-12. Prior passes had covered identifier-to-entity modeling,
classification reference data, and the catalog-to-client path only indirectly; this pass reviewed

author: alexphaus
body:
## Why it was empty

The section asked the agent for a lesson with **a real, working URL** — the single thing a model is least able to supply. It either invents the link (breaking invariant 2) or, told not to, returns nothing. Told not to, it returned nothing.

There was a second hole underneath: `selectLesson` only fires when a finding carries a `topic`, and `BOTTLENECK_TOPIC` had no entry for `drafted` or `sent`.

```js
matched: undefined, drafted: undefined, sent: undefined,   // ← your bottleneck
replied: 'writing cold openers that get replies',
```

**`sent` is the most common bottleneck in this product** and the one your account has sat on for weeks. The state that most needed something to say produced silence by construction.

## You're right that it's dead UI — but loosening the URL rule is the wrong fix

Dead links are how this section first failed (you hit it yourself: *"when you click one it shows empty"*). The fix is to stop asking the web for something the ledger already knows.

`growthEdge()` computes the capability in priority order:

1. **From your calls** — a topic in the decision record you acted on 3+ times where the metric it named never moved. Repeating something that doesn't work is the most expensive gap there is, and nothing but the record can see it.
2. **From your funnel** — the bottleneck stage as a capability. Every stage has one now.
3. **From your matches** — the top demand term your offer doesn't cover.

## What you'll see

```
GET BETTER AT                            from your funnel

Sending what you have already written
  · 33 of 33 stopped at drafted.

TRY THIS WEEK
Send five before you open anything else, and log what came
back. Nothing above this line improves until something
leaves the queue.
```

One bounded experiment for the week, not a reading list. Evidence citing a number from rows you created. `null` only for an account with nothing measured yet — a real empty state instead of a permanent one.

Note the evidence line deliberately **doesn't restate the bottleneck card above it** — it counts what's stuck rather than what got through. That's the same duplication that made Today feel heavy.

A lesson with a real URL still renders underneath when one exists. It's no longer the reason the section is there.

## Verification

`tsc` clean · **13 suites** pass, including one asserting every funnel stage produces an edge (so nothing can fall through to silence again) · build green · shot at 390×844 in your exact state.

## One thing I'd push back on

"Learning is growth" is true, but an article you don't read isn't growth — and a generic one fails the survival test in `DIRECTION.md`: it needs none of your state, supply or ledger, so Claude with a search box does it better. What passes is *"you have done this four times and the number never moved."* That's the version worth having.

## 何を直したか
期限前に担当者へ届く **1:1 の催促（期限リマインド・確認ループ）** が LINE でしか届かなかったのを、担当者が Slack / Discord / Telegram 等で紐付けている場合にも届くようにしました。

関連: #632（タスク詳細の時刻指定リマインドの同じ是正）。互いに独立で、どちらから入れても動きます。

## 原因
担当者の紐付け（合言葉）は全チャネルで成立するのに、送信処理（`/api/cron/due-reminder-sender`）が LINE 専用の `findLineAccountByIdLookup` で鍵を読んでいたため、Slack 等の担当者は `no_route` として **黙ってスキップ** されていました。

## 変更点
- 宛先解決の鍵読み出しを、全チャネル対応の `findAccountForSecretaryPush` に差し替え（disabled / 資格情報欠落は従来どおり `no_route`）
- `sendSecretaryPush` が非LINEアダプタの失敗時に `status` / `permanent` を載せた `SecretaryPushError` を投げる。Slack は `channel_not_found` 等の論理エラーでも HTTP 200 を返すため、これが無いと恒久失敗が一時扱いになり **再claim→再送を無限に繰り返す** 穴があった
- sender の恒久/一時判定は `permanent` を優先し、無ければ従来の LINE の status 判定（LINE の挙動は不変）
- プラン機能一覧の文言から「LINE個別配信」を外す（機能キー `line_direct_dm` と Pro ゲートは据え置き）

## 動作上の注意
- 非LINEでは確認ボタン（[完了した][対応中][明日また確認]）は付かず、本文（altText）だけが届きます。Slack のボタン対応は別PR
- 非LINE送信は事務所自身のアカウント経由のため、共通LINEの送信枠は消費しません

## テスト
- sender: Slack DM 配信 / 資格情報欠落→no_route / disabled→no_route / permanent:true(HTTP200)→push_failed_permanent / permanent:false→再試行（5件追加）
- secretaryPush: 例外に status/permanent が載る（2件追加）
- 関連 suite 全て pass・tsc OK・eslint OK

### SUMMARY
Resolves code-scanning alert #2674 (zizmor/self-repository, note severity).

`superset-translations.yml` referenced the in-repo `setup-backend` composite
action with the legacy workspace-relative syntax
(`uses: ./.github/actions/setup-backend/`). GitHub now supports a dedicated
["self-repository" syntax](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-reference-same-repository-actions-with-self-repository-syntax/)
(`uses: $/...`) for same-repo actions/reusable workflows, which zizmor
recommends because it isn't subject to runtime filesystem state (it can't
be swapped out by an earlier step cloning something into that path) and is
treated as a pinned reference for "fully pinned" policy enforcement.

Also bumps the `zizmor` version pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` from
1.25.2 to 1.30.0 (the first release that understands `$/...` refs — the
old pin fatal-errors trying to parse the new syntax, e.g. `malformed 'uses'
ref: missing '@<ref>' in $/...`). 1.30.0 is also the version GitHub's
code-scanning zizmor integration already runs, so this keeps local
pre-commit in sync with CI.

Only the one flagged line/instance is changed; three other `./`-style
local action refs remain in this same file (and many more exist
repo-wide) as separate open code-scanning alerts (#2671, #2672, #2673,
etc.) not covered by this PR, to keep the diff scoped to alert #2674.

author: mgrossmann
body:
The symbol was entered **before** the constant body was scanned, so the only
lengths available at that point were the explicit modifier or the fallback 1.
Wherever the length is implied by the nominal *value* it was therefore 1:

| symbol | constant | IFOX00 | as370 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CC` | `C'ABC'` | 3 | **1** |
| `XX` | `X'FFFF'` | 2 | **1** |
| `EE` | `3C'AB'` | 2 | **1** |

Silent, rc 0, and the wrong length is then used by every expression that reads
it. `F`, `H` and `A` were right because their implied length is fixed; `CL7`
was right because it is explicit; `B'1010'` agreed by coincidence, being one
byte anyway.

The C, X and B arms now define the symbol after the body scan, from `emit` —
which is already the length of **one** constant, and that is what `L'` is:
`L'` of `3C'AB'` is 2, not the field's 6. The P/Z arm already did this. The
move is safe because the scan touches neither `lc` nor any symbol.

## The tests were built to fail on this

`amp_fold` and `amp_selfdef` pinned their single remaining difference to
exactly the `L'` byte — 104 and 99 — and were written to **fail** once those
matched, so the defect could not be repaired unnoticed. It worked: both now
report `differs at []`. They move into the byte-identity loop, together with
`tests/len_attr.s`, the oracle committed with the issue — eight symbols holding
all three ways a length is decided, so a repair that fixes only one group
cannot pass.

## Measured

5,528 `MVSBLD` modules against the recorded IFOX00 decks, baseline `e502f71`:

```
as370 == IFOX00 : 3640 -> 3735   (+95, none lost)
rc 0            : 4339, unchanged
decks changed   : 240
                   229 closer to IFOX00
                    10 unchanged in distance
                     1 further — IRBMFINP, 3 bytes, each inside a run already
                       carrying 14 wrong bytes within eight either side
```

## One correction to the distance measure itself

Distance here is the **address-keyed section image**, not the card sequence.
The card-based measure — the one from #168 that went into `retest.py` — called
eight modules worse, and seven of those were its own artifact: it charges a
full card for a card-count difference.

`IFNX4S` is the clearest case. Its section length went `0x196` → `0x1ad`, which
is exactly IFOX00's. The deck therefore grew by one TXT card, and a card-count
metric read a **corrected length** as a regression. By image it went from 402
differing bytes to 382.

Worth propagating: a fix that changes a section's length will keep tripping the
card measure, and the module that looks worst under it may be the one that just
became right.
