body:
## 1. Real company names were live on the site

The CRM motion piece shipped in PR #22 is a screen recording of the demo tenant. The deal cards name **Sunrise, Oakmont, Cedarhurst, Brightview, Discovery and Thrive Senior Living** — with amounts, close dates, a named owner, and two of them sitting in **Closed Won**.

The data behind those cards is invented. That is not what a visitor sees. "Closed Won — Discovery Senior Living, $88,400" on a public marketing page reads as a signed customer, and those six are among the largest operators in TNX's actual target market. It also publishes an apparent book of business to competitors and to MIX.

**Fix:**

- The video is **rebuilt from scratch in code** rather than recorded. Every account is invented — Havenwood, Larkspur, Windrow, Copperline, Fernbrook, Tidewater, Northgate, Clearwater, Sandhill, Ridgeline, Marbury — and the owner is "Alex Morgan".
- The board UI carries a persistent **"Sample data"** badge, so a single frame lifted out of context still can't be read as a customer list. That is the durable part: the problem was never the numbers, it was that a still frame of a real-looking pipeline named real companies.
- The old `crm-value.v2.mp4` and its poster are **deleted**, not merely unreferenced — the file stays fetchable at its public URL otherwise.
- The homepage keeps a sanitized static dashboard shot (KPI figures and stage totals only; no account names in frame).

The beat is unchanged: account data lands on a deal, a next step is set, the deal moves Proposal → Negotiation, stage totals and the weighted figure settle, and the Partner Hub agent reports what it did. 1920×1080, 10s, silent, 1.36 MB.

## 2. The unsourced statistics

| Was | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "roughly 40 million analog lines in service across the US" (industry estimates) | **15.0 million**, down from 27.2M three years earlier, with the FCC report linked | The FCC's own count as of 30 June 2025. The site overstated the market ~2.7×, and DataRemote publishes the correct figure. The real number is the better argument: ~4M lines a year disappearing. |
| `40+` Agents live | tile removed | A placeholder that shipped — the code comment beside it said so. A hedged number reads worse than no number. |
| `25+` Years in telecom | `25+` **Years of founder experience** | Sat unattributed beside company stats, so it read as the company's age. It's Carter's experience. |
| `50%` Typical line-cost cut | **$85 → $25** Typical line cost, per month | Contradicted `/tools/pots-roi-calculator`, whose defaults imply ~71%. Neither figure was sourced. Now the homepage and the tool agree, and the number is specific rather than round. |
| /about body + meta | attributes the 25+ years to the founder | Same issue as the tile. |
| "2–5 business days" | "5–10 business days" | Per Carter. |

The stats strip goes from four tiles to three. Calculator dollar constants are untouched — those are a pricing decision.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — 80/80 routes prerendered, 23 shells patched
- [x] `/`, `/platforms/crm`, `/about`, `/ai-workforce`, `/pots-replacement` at 1440 and 390: zero console errors, zero 4xx, no horizontal overflow, no broken images
- [x] `grep -ril` for all six operator names across `src/`, `public/` and `dist/` — no matches

## Follow-up for Carter

Rename the accounts inside the CRM demo tenant. Right now any future screenshot or recording of it reproduces this, and the next person to grab one won't know to check.

author: chadaibbhot-git
body:
## Problem

#4035 wired the recorded registration deposit into `LedgerView.DRepRegistration` / `DRepRegistrations`, and the gouroboros v0.204.0 bump it carried made `common.DRepRegistration.Deposit` a `*uint64` so absence is distinct from a recorded zero.

Absence is not inert on that path. `conway.UtxoValidateCertificateDeposits` fails closed on it:

```go
// gouroboros v0.204.0, ledger/conway/rules.go
if registration.Deposit == nil {
    return DRepDepositStateInconsistentError{Credential: c.DrepCredential}
}
```

```
registered DRep credential has no recorded deposit: type 0 hash <...>
```

That is the correct default for gouroboros — the reference ledger's `DRepState` carries a non-optional `drepDeposit`, so a registration without one is internally inconsistent and there is no refund to compare against. But it means a DRep that reaches this state deterministically rejects its own deregistration block, and a node that reaches that block stops making progress.

**Dingo can produce that state.** `ledger/governance/processing.go` calls `InsertDrepIfAbsent(..., active = true, ...)` on the vote-replay recovery path when a valid DRep vote proves the credential exists on-chain but the metadata row was lost during recovery or bootstrap. That writes a row in `drep` and **no `registration_drep` row at all**, so `GetDrepLastRegistrationDeposit` returns nil. The DRep is active, is deregisterable, and has no recorded deposit.

This is the follow-up @chrisguiney asked for in his review of #4035, which dispositioned the three-states-collapsed-to-one issue as non-blocking there and named this exact path:
https://github.com/blinklabs-io/dingo/pull/4035#discussion_r3945923931

> `ledger/governance/processing.go:306` calls `InsertDrepIfAbsent(..., active=true, ...)` on the vote-replay recovery path, and that writes only the `drep` table. It leaves an **active** DRep with no `registration_drep` row [...] Not a blocker [...] Better as a follow-up issue than as growth in this PR.

The store side landed in #4035 already returns `*uint64`, so this is purely the view's answer for the nil case.

## Change

`ledger/view.go` only, +59/-2. A recorded deposit is passed through unchanged; when nothing is recorded, the view reports the DRep deposit under the current era and protocol parameters instead of the absence.

That value is not invented. `currentDRepDeposit` runs the current era's `CertDepositFunc` over a `RegistrationDrepCertificate` — the same function `ledger.calculateCertificateDeposit` runs on the certificate write path — so the fallback equals what a registration applied now would have recorded. Era and parameters are read from a single published consensus snapshot so they cannot be torn apart.

Two things it deliberately does not do:

- **A recorded zero stays authoritative.** A zero `dRepDeposit` is a legitimate configuration; folding zero into the unrecorded case would refund the current parameter and reject a valid deregistration. This is the same distinction `LedgerView.StakeCredentialDeposit` keeps for the stake analogue (#3829).
- **Absence is still reported when the current era charges no DRep deposit** (pre-Conway, or parameters that do not belong to the era). gouroboros fails closed there rather than being handed an invented zero refund. Whether an era has a DRep deposit is decided by asking the parameters for one (`drepDepositParams`, the same capability `conway.UtxoValidateCertificateDeposits` asserts), not by inferring it from what the era's `CertDepositFunc` returns: `CertDepositShelley` through `CertDepositBabbage` have no `*RegistrationDrepCertificate` case and fall through to `default: return 0, nil`, so inference yielded a fabricated zero. Fixed in 1174ea92 after @chrisguiney caught it in review; the original revision of this description claimed the guard without it existing.

## Tests

`ledger/drep_deposit_unknown_fallback_test.go`, reusing #4035's existing fixtures (`drepRefundTestPparams`, `drepDeregistrationTx`, `seedImportedDrep`). Assertions are on the validation outcome through `conway.UtxoValidateCertificateDeposits` and `eras.ValidateTxConway` with a real `*LedgerView` over a real database, not on the helper's return value.

The unrecorded case is seeded through `InsertDrepIfAbsent` itself rather than by hand, and the helper asserts that path really does leave no registration row — if recovery ever starts writing one, the test says so instead of silently measuring nothing.

- `TestDrepDeregistrationFallsBackToCurrentDepositWhenUnrecorded` — the regression
- `TestDrepDeregistrationRejectsWrongRefundWhenUnrecorded` — the fallback is not a licence to accept any refund (0, +1, and a negative amount all still rejected)
- `TestDrepDeregistrationPrefersRecordedDepositOverFallback` — recorded and parameter values are deliberately different, so the two answers give opposite outcomes
- `TestDrepDeregistrationKeepsRecordedZeroAuthoritative`
- `TestDrepRegistrationsFallBackForUnrecordedDeposit` — the plural view has its own absence path
- `TestDrepRegistrationReportsAbsenceInAPreConwayEra` — the era guard, on a *published* Babbage snapshot, first asserting that era's deposit function really does answer zero-without-error
- `TestDrepRegistrationReportsAbsenceWithoutAPublishedSnapshot` — the other absence branch, asserting the fixture leaves the snapshot unpublished

Each is load-bearing. Removing the fallback fails 3; ignoring the recorded value fails 5 (including two of #4035's own); removing the `drepDepositParams` guard fails `TestDrepRegistrationReportsAbsenceInAPreConwayEra` and leaves the unpublished-snapshot test green, which is the discrimination the earlier single test did not have.

The substitution is also logged at WARN with the credential and the value used, so a node serving a fabricated deposit is distinguishable from one serving a recorded one.

## Verification

Rebased on `main` at c6488d37 (#4035).

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./...`, `go build -tags dingo_extra_plugins ./cmd/dingo` | pass |
| `go vet ./...` | pass |
| `golangci-lint run ./ledger/...` | 0 issues |
| `gofmt -l ledger/` | empty |
| `go test ./ledger/...` | pass, all 9 packages (`ledger` 102.5s) |
| `go test -race ./ledger/` | pass, 405.2s |

Related: #4035, #4055, #3829

author: adi-stefan
body:
## Problem

Every scenario of `huTraceability.feature` fails in CI with

```
ERROR: column "link_basis" does not exist
  Position: 67
```

Seen on `new_dawn_uat` build `5.175-new-dawn-uat.43189` (2026-09-04) and on every attempt of the merge PR https://github.com/metasfresh/metasfresh/pull/25802 — e.g. https://github.com/metasfresh/metasfresh/actions/runs/34118864067/job/101770302980 (10/10 scenarios; `tests=375 failures=10` in the JUnit XML, nothing else red).

`link_basis` is a new OUT column of `m_hu_trace_report()`, added by `5821840_sys_M_HU_Trace_Report_GraphPairing.sql` (from https://github.com/metasfresh/metasfresh/pull/25719). That script sits **directly in** `backend/de.metas.handlingunits.base/src/main/sql/postgresql/system/`, not in the module's `70-de.metas.handlingunits/` subfolder.

The `db-images` job aggregates migration SQL with

```bash
find backend -path "*/src/main/sql/postgresql/system/*/*.sql"
```

which requires exactly one intermediate folder. A script placed flat in `system/` matches nothing, is neither copied into `migration-sql/` nor counted, and its migration **silently never reaches the `metas-db` image**. Real `find` over `origin/new_dawn_uat`: **13 734 of 13 738** system scripts matched. The four dropped ones:

| script | consequence of being dropped |
|---|---|
| `de.metas.handlingunits.base/.../5821840_sys_M_HU_Trace_Report_GraphPairing.sql` | `m_hu_trace_report()` has no `link_basis` -> all 10 huTraceability scenarios red |
| `de.metas.banking.base/.../5753800_sys_gh30431_C_Payment_SingleView_AllocatePayments_Process.sql` | "Zahlung-Zuordnung" launcher missing on the C_Payment single-document view |
| `de.metas.payment.esr/.../5818570_sys_AD_Message_ESR_InvoiceAlreadyPaid.sql` | AD_Message missing -> raw key shown in `ESR_ImportLine.MatchErrorMsg` |
| `de.metas.purchasecandidate.base/.../5798910_sys_gh29155_remove_InterceptorEnabled_...sql` | obsolete interceptor kill-switch SysConfig not removed |

This is not a one-off: on the hotfix branches flat `system/*.sql` is still the norm (1 145 such files on `vampire_textbook_hotfix`), so every script ported up from a hotfix branch lands where this glob does not look. `vampire_textbook_hotfix` CI is green on the same 10 scenarios (build `5.175-vampire-textbook-hotfix.43275`) precisely because its `cicd.yaml` has no such glob - it builds the migration-tool image from the Maven dist.

## Change

1. `git mv` all four flat scripts into their module's existing `NN-<module>` folder. Apply order is unaffected: `GloballyOrderedScannerDecorator` sorts by the sequence number in the **filename**, folder-independent.
2. Fail `aggregate-sql-from-source` loudly when any script sits directly in `system/`, so a misplaced script is a red `db-images` job in minutes rather than an invisible missing migration.

## Verification (local, before this PR)

Against a throwaway container built from the DB image the failing profile5 job itself pushed (`metasfresh/metas-db:5.175-merge-intensive-care-hotfix-109-to-new-dawn-uat-tmp.43298-postcucumber-profile5`):

- **RED reproduced**: 13 876 `AD_MigrationScript` rows, **no row for `5821840...`**; `pg_get_function_result(m_hu_trace_report)` has no `link_basis`; replaying the step def's exact query (`M_HU_Trace_Report_StepDef.java:249-252`) gives `ERROR: column "link_basis" does not exist` with the caret at char **67** - the same position CI reports.
- **GREEN after the move**: `workspace_migrate` applied the script from its new folder (`Evaluated 1 / Applied 1 / Ignored 0`, 42 ms, recorded as `projectName=70-de.metas.handlingunits`); `link_basis` present; the same query now returns a result set.
- **No re-apply risk**: a full apply of the branch's 13 738 scripts against that image evaluated all of them and applied exactly **3** - the other three formerly-flat scripts, each for the first time, cleanly. On a CI-aggregated DB the folder change is a first-time apply, not a duplicate.
- **Packaging fix, with the real CI command**: after the moves the glob matches **13 738/13 738** (`5821840...` included) and the new guard returns empty. Guard exercised both ways: with a planted stray script it exits 1 and names the file; with none it exits 0.

Sets up biome as a CI gate and brings `./src` into compliance.

**1. Formatting gate** (`d1aafb5`)

| Function | Before | After |

body: ## Summary by cubic Makes the Mise toolchain lock-free, renames `workspace_root` to `repository_root` and `declared_repositories` to `subprojects`, and removes private-dependency token minting from the docs and release workflows so tools always resolve to current releases and CI no longer needs a workflow-scoped token. **Behavior changes** - Deletes `mise.lock`; every tool resolves to the newest published release at setup time. - Mise staging validates the root launcher fleet instead of a committed lock. - The LOC cap ceiling moves from config to `c.Infra.LOC_CAP_MAX`. - Drops the public `FlextInfraUtilitiesIteration` export. - Adds `config/codegen-overrides.yaml` and `config/codegen.gen.yaml`; bypass managed-file policies are forbidden and `make gen` is the single regeneration verb. - Bumps the package version to `0.12.0rc0`. - Received agent-hook projections are untracked and excluded from lint and type-check surfaces. - The codemod provider index skips unimportable and data distributions instead of failing. - The duplication gate maps each duplicate to its real file owner. - Tool floors are clamped to cooldown-eligible releases. **Migration** - CLI option `--workspace` becomes `--repository`. - `WorkspaceSpec.declared_repositories` becomes `subprojects`. - Generated Makefiles and templates now use `REPOSITORY_ROOT` instead of `WORKSPACE_ROOT`. - Two codemod rules rewrite the retired `Tests.mapping` and `declared_repositories` call sites. Written for commit ae7bf324cd6e4232bd76f5495e42dfa03688b76f. Summary will update on new commits.

author: eykonai
body:
No migration. Frontend + one lib file.

## What this does

A button per approved community next to each Reddit draft in `/admin/newsjack`. It opens **Reddit's own compose window with the draft already in it** — you review and hit post.

## Why not the API publish path you asked about

Reddit stays draft-only, and the reasons have got stronger rather than weaker:

1. **The account can't reach r/OSINT until it clears the age-and-karma gate** — months out. A publish path built today is one that cannot be used, which is exactly the trap the brief records for TikTok: *"a publishing path built before the audit would look exactly like a working one and reach zero people."*
2. **Automated marketing posting is commercial use of the Reddit API**, requiring approval and a paid agreement.
3. **The failure mode is invisible.** A shadowbanned post reads as published in our queue, renders correctly in our own logged-in view, and reaches nobody — the master pattern, on the one channel where it's hardest to detect.

A prefilled compose URL sidesteps all three: **no API** so no terms question, **you post as yourself** so there's no bot to shadowban, and **a human stays at the gate**, which the SOP requires anyway. It also works *today* in any community the account can post to — which is the whole karma-building window, not just after it.

## Design decisions

**One link per approved community, no inference.** The artifact validates its subreddit against the allowlist at assembly then discards it, so a draft doesn't carry its destination. Emitting one link per approved entry gives a single button today and a choice if the allowlist grows. Inferring the target would be a stored assumption that silently goes wrong the day a second community is approved.

**Never a truncated body.** Measured against real drafts:

| | |
|---|---|
| Reddit body, mean / max | 2,052 / 2,643 chars |
| URL-encode expansion | **1.57×** |
| Largest real draft as a URL | **~4,150 chars** |
| Guard | 8,000 (common proxy header limit) |

So every current draft gets full prefill; the fallback is a guard, not a common path. Over the limit, the link carries the **title only** and the body goes to the clipboard — because a silently shortened post is one that ships without its limits paragraph or its affiliation disclosure, the two things the artifact exists to carry.

**The label says "Open in r/X", not "Post".** It hands over a compose window; it does not publish. A button claiming more than it does is the composer-badge gate again.

**Targets computed server-side**, for the same reason `publishTarget` is — only the server sees the allowlist and it shouldn't ship to the client.

**Flair is surfaced beside the button, not encoded.** Reddit's prefill can't set flair without an internal id we don't have, and pretending otherwise would post into a community missing the tag its rules require.

- [ ] Click it — Reddit compose should open with title and body populated

## Note

With the allowlist at one approved entry, this renders one button. If r/OSINT were ever downgraded to `comment-only` or the allowlist emptied, it renders none — which is the correct state, not a defect.

author: kefaro
body:
## Causa

El backend pasa a emitir una cookie de refresh distinta por tipo de sujeto (`vet_refresh_system` / `vet_refresh_employee`) porque consola y tenant comparten la misma API: con una sola cookie de refresh, la sesión de una app pisaba la de la otra y ambas expulsaban al usuario cada 15 minutos.

## Cambio

- `POST /auth/refresh` exige ahora `{ type }` en el cuerpo; `authApi.refresh` recibe el tipo de sujeto y lo envía.
- `auth.store.ts`: `refreshSession` no llama a la API si no hay sesión conocida en memoria (evita una llamada sin `type`).
- Contrato (`api/openapi.json`) y tipos generados (`src/types/api.generated.d.ts`) sincronizados con el cambio del backend.
- Tests unitarios nuevos en `tests/unit/http-client.spec.ts`: el refresh manda el `type` de la sesión, y sin sesión conocida no se llama a `/auth/refresh`.

## Verificación

- `npm run quality` completo en verde, incluido `api:check` y `typecheck`.
- `vitest related`: 473 tests en verde.
- Ningún gemelo TR-02 tocado.

## Dependencia

Requiere desplegar antes el PR del backend, rama `fix/cookie-refresh-por-tipo-de-sujeto` de `vetsoftware-backend`. Sin ese despliegue, `POST /auth/refresh` seguirá sin aceptar `{type}`.

author: simon-yhkim
body:
**R32-LEGAL-01 여섯 번째 조각.** `src/lib/ops/recommend.ts` 는 세 번째로 많이 인용되는 파일(18건)이고, 그 인용들이 이 문서의 **하중을 받는 주장 둘**을 떠받칩니다 — 저널 텍스트가 LLM 프롬프트에 절대 안 들어간다는 것, 그리고 추천이 위키 스냅샷만 프로파일링한다는 것.

| 인용 | 주장 | 그 자리에 실제로 있는 것 |
|---|---|---|
| `:5-9,138` | "이 경로는 `includeRecords` 를 안 넘긴다" | `:5-9` 은 계약이 맞지만 **`:138` 은 탭 전환과 쿼터에 관한 캐시 주석** |
| `:137-157` | "추천이 위키 스냅샷을 프로파일링한다" | **캐시 TTL 과 `resetOpsRecommendCacheForTests`** |
| `:6-10` | 인용된 계약 문구 | 그 문구는 `:7-8` 두 줄 |

**첫째가 이름을 붙일 만합니다.** 저널 기록이 정말 프롬프트에서 빠지는지 확인하러 간 사람이 **캐시 메모**를 읽게 됩니다. 그걸 정하는 호출 — `exportUserWiki(userId, { bodyCharLimit })`, `includeRecords` 없음 — 은 **90줄 떨어진 `:235`** 에 있고, 이제 문장이 그것을 인용합니다.

## ⚠ 변이 검증이 **제가 직접 만든 구멍**을 찾았습니다

Round44 에서 "모든 앵커의 범위가 그 심볼을 담는다" 검사를 **인접 범위 판**으로 갈아끼웠습니다 — 같은 줄이 네 범위를 네 주장에 인용하는 531행에서 거짓양성 여섯이 나왔기 때문입니다.

**갈아끼운 게 틀렸습니다.** 인접 검사는 **문서가 심볼 이름을 인용 옆에 적었을 때만** 발동합니다. 문서가 `fenced as untrusted` 라고 **소문자 산문**으로 쓰면 앵커 `UNTRUSTED` 는 **한 번도 코드와 대조되지 않습니다.** 표가 거짓이어도 아무도 모릅니다.

둘 다 되살렸습니다. **다른 명제이기 때문입니다:**

```
표 vs 코드   — 표가 참인가 (문서와 무관)
문서 vs 표   — 문서가 그 표와 어긋나지 않는가
```

## 그리고 구멍처럼 보였지만 아닌 것 하나

같은 앵커에 대한 첫 변이 시도는 `<UNTRUSTED>` **여는 태그만** 바꿨습니다. 그러면 `</UNTRUSTED>` **닫는 태그가 인용 범위 안에 남으므로** 울타리는 여전히 그 자리에 이름이 있고, **가드가 조용한 것이 옳았습니다.** 두 태그를 다 옮기도록 고쳤습니다.

## 기록해 둔 한계

**문서가 심볼 이름을 인용 옆에 적지 않은 인용은 경로·줄범위 가드만 덮습니다.** 변이 5번은 문서가 이름을 적는 자리를 노립니다 — 이 가드가 실제로 볼 수 있는 자리입니다. 없는 능력을 있다고 적지 않기 위해 이 한계를 그대로 남깁니다.

```
npm run verify   exit 0 · 666 suites / 7,529 tests · lint 0 errors
변이 6/6 · MUTATION_VERIFIED
```

**4번은 코드 쪽을 움직입니다** — 이것이 문서 검사가 아니라 양쪽 대조임을 보입니다.

author: smallfoi
body:
Пункт go/no-go из плана запуска (Фаза 5).

## Как проверял

**Прод не трогал** — там живые тестеры, а нагрузочный прогон по боевому серверу это самому себе устроить отказ обслуживания. Воспроизвёл его условия: отдельная временная база, **gunicorn с прод-конфигурацией** (3 воркера, `DEBUG=0`, реальные секреты, `X-Forwarded-Proto`), объём «мы взлетели» — 5000 пользователей, 40 000 забегов, 40 000 транзакций, 3000 территорий PostGIS.

Пустая база врёт: N+1 на девятнадцати строках неотличим от идеального. Для сравнения масштаба — у лидера рынка РФ около 40 тысяч активных в месяц.

## Что нашлось: одна ручка клала бы весь сервер

**`/v1/clubs` делал 5061 запрос к базе и отвечал 1.9 секунды.**

N×M: километры считались вызовом на **каждого участника каждого клуба**, и суммировались в Python вместо базы.

Воркеров на проде три. Значит **три одновременных открытия списка клубов занимали бы весь сервер на две секунды** — приложение вставало бы для всех, включая тех, кто просто отправляет забег.

| | Было | Стало |
|---|---:|---:|
| Запросов к базе | 5061 | **3** |
| Время ответа | 1952 мс | **42 мс** |

Тот же дефект на карточке клуба (вклад участников в челлендже) — тоже починен.

## Тесты на число запросов, а не на время

Время на ноутбуке ничего не говорит о проде и плавает от прогона к прогону. Число запросов одинаково везде и растёт вместе с данными — по нему и видно то, что убивает сервер.

Отдельный тест **удваивает данные и требует, чтобы число запросов не изменилось**.

## Результат прогона после починки

| Одновременных | rps | p50 | p95 | Ошибок |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5 | 127 | 19 мс | 112 мс | 0 |
| 25 | 127 | 143 мс | 526 мс | 0 |
| 50 | 125 | 237 мс | 1152 мс | 0 |
| 200 | 117 | 860 мс | 5178 мс | **0** |

Запись (отправка забега) при 50 одновременных: 126 rps, p95 417 мс, ноль ошибок.

**Главный вывод для go/no-go: система не падает, а деградирует плавно.** Ноль ошибок, ноль таймаутов, ноль пятисоток даже при 200 одновременных.

Потолок ~125 rps достигается уже при пяти одновременных — это упор в процессор на трёх воркерах. В людях: одно открытие приложения = 7 запросов → ~18 открытий в секунду. Для пяти тысяч пользователей запас многократный.

## Прибрано

Временная база и роль удалены, скрипты прогона удалены, рабочая база не тронута (проверено).

Отчёт: `docs/LOAD_TEST.md`. Пункт в `LAUNCH_PLAN.md` отмечен.

**647 тестов** зелёные (+6).

author: titouanmathis
body:
Removes every `vi.mock` and `vi.useFakeTimers` from the suite.

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `vi.mock("../src/ssh.js")` ×3 | one shared `SshIo`, injected into `deploy`, `destroy`, `setup` |
| `vi.mock("node:child_process")` in agent | `DdevRunner` on `startProject` / `stopProject` / `getProjectInfo` |
| `vi.mock("node:child_process")` in CLI | `CommandRunner` via `ExecOptions.runner` |
| `vi.useFakeTimers()` in db tests | `Clock` on the four functions that read the time |

One `SshIo` rather than three interfaces: the field `destroy` and `setup` don't use costs less than two more near-identical shapes.

## Why it's worth more than removing the mocks

A fake that *answers probes* lets the real control flow run. `setup`'s decisions — whether Node is recent enough, whether the apt prerequisites are present, whether the npm prefix is already on root's PATH — are now exercised instead of stubbed.

That paid off during the conversion. One test had two `io = fakeServer(...)` assignments in a row, the second silently discarding the non-root uid its assertion depended on:

```ts
io = fakeServer({ "id -u": "1000" });                              // discarded
io = fakeServer({}, (command) => command !== "sudo -n true");
```

The mock-based version passed while testing nothing.

## `run` is now actually tested

It's the seam everything else replaces, so its exit-code handling was only reachable through a mocked `execFile` and was never exercised. Exported and tested against real processes:

```ts
await expect(run("sh", ["-c", "exit 3"], 5000)).rejects.toThrow(/exit code 3/);
```

## Coverage: `utils/db.ts` was at 2.85%

The persistence layer behind scale-to-zero, with no tests at all. 23 now, aimed at the boundaries that decide behaviour rather than the happy path:

- **`updateProjectAccess` must not clobber a status set elsewhere** — otherwise a start in flight is reset to `running` by a request arriving on the waiting page
- **`setProjectStatus` must leave `last_access` alone** — otherwise stopping a project looks like activity and defers the next sweep
- **`getIdleProjects`** treats a project used *exactly* at the cutoff as active, and ignores anything not `running`
- **`cleanOldLogs`** keeps an entry exactly at the cutoff

439 tests, typecheck and lint clean.

body:
## Qué

Al adjuntar fotos a una visita (flag `mediaVisitas`) ahora hay **dos botones explícitos**:

- **Cámara** → `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">` (abre la cámara del dispositivo, una foto por apertura).
- **Galería** → input actual (`accept="image/*" multiple`, sin `capture`), abre el chooser del SO (Google Photos en el Redmi 11).

Ambos comparten el mismo pipeline (`captureImage` → preview → `AttachMediaToVisit` al registrar). El usuario conserva **ambas opciones** en todo momento.

## Por qué

En Android (Xiaomi Redmi 11) el input sin `capture` abre solo la galería de Google Photos **sin CTA de cámara**. No se podía sacar una foto en el momento.

## Alcance

- Solo UI: `src/ui/components/MediaGallery.tsx` + tests (`tests/ui/media-gallery.test.tsx`, `visit-detail-screen.test.tsx`).
- No se toca dominio ni application.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-foto-camara-o-galeria-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-07-foto-camara-o-galeria.md`

## Riesgo / probar en teléfono

`capture="environment"` puede no abrir cámara en algunos dispositivos/PWAs instaladas. Probá en el preview (móvil): botón **Cámara** debe abrir la cámara trasera, botón **Galería** debe seguir abriendo el chooser de fotos. Si la cámara no responde, el plan documenta el fallback a `getUserMedia` (mismo patrón que la nota de voz).

author: jrochub
body:
This changes traversal for no-axis integer and boolean sums with integer
accumulators. Contiguous arrays use a flat physical scan. Arbitrary layouts
up to rank four normalize negative strides, order dimensions by stride magnitude
and coalesce contiguous dimensions. Higher-rank arbitrary layouts retain the
existing iterator. Per-element casts and accumulator selection are preserved;
the optimized path uses wrapping LLVM addition without no-overflow flags.

Floating-point/complex inputs, floating or boolean accumulators and explicit-axis
reductions keep their existing path. This is related to the layout performance
problem in https://github.com/numba/numba/issues/9819, but does not fix its
floating-point reproducer or request closing that issue.

Validation on the final source: 536 tests passed and three skipped across
`numba.tests.test_array_reductions` and `numba.tests.test_array_methods`.
Six added test methods cover 372 combinations. A separately constructed
Python-integer oracle passed 640 additional cases. These are differential
validation results, not an external audit. Repository-config lint reports no
new issues.

On one host, controlled before/after trials measured 13.6× for int64 transposed
and 28.4× for int32 Fortran-layout sums; an ad-hoc public-image processing
pipeline improved 1.49×. One int64 sliced control was 7.8% slower. These compare
patched against unpatched Numba, not NumPy; no multi-machine result is claimed.
All 22 cases, raw trials, exactness checks, earlier failed diagnostics and
reproduction instructions are in the
[evidence branch](https://github.com/JROChub/numba/tree/evidence/integer-sum-memory-order/benchmarks/integer_sum_memory_order).

author: chelseakr
body:
## What was wrong

The exit-gate table in `docs/BETA-ROADMAP.md` has a dependency column, and it
keeps saying the same four things: **External jurisdiction. External reviewers.
External recruitment. External partner.**

Every matrix behind those gates is prepared. The validators exist, the fixtures
exist, the records refuse to lie about their own state. What does not exist is
people, and the repository had **no issue templates at all** - so there was no
route in for any of them.

Portfolio-wide, measured today: 69 open issues carry `help wanted`, 5 carry
`good first issue`, and **all 54 repositories already have the
`good first issue` label defined**. The infrastructure is not the problem.

## What changed

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/partner-jurisdiction.md` - for #114, the root of
  twelve blocked roadmap issues (#115 through #126). It states what step 1
  actually asks (an authoritative local source package **and** a named
  conflict-resolution authority) and, just as importantly, what it does not
  ask: no money, no contract, no applicant data, no integration, no
  endorsement. It says `stop` is a real supported outcome, because the roadmap
  says so. "An introduction is a complete contribution."
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/screen-reader-session.md` - scoped to **one page**,
  15 to 40 minutes.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`
- `docs/HELP-WANTED.md` and a CONTRIBUTING section.

## Where this deliberately does not overstate

This is the part worth your eye.

**The session template tells a volunteer, up front, that their session cannot
promote a row in `docs/MANUAL-VALIDATION.md`.** That record is bound to an
exact deployed commit and deployed URL, and both are `null` because no run has
been executed against a frozen deployment. So a volunteer's session is real
evidence and a source of filed defects, but it is not a completed matrix row
until you fill that lock.

I could have left that out and gotten more sessions. Someone who spends an
afternoon and then finds their work could not be recorded where they expected
does not come back, and this portfolio's own DevRel note is about exactly that
failure mode.

Also:

- No page is described as a five-minute job.
- Spanish is described as explicitly review-pending and outside any beta claim,
  matching the roadmap.
- The screening-form section asks the question that actually matters: whether
  the **unknowns and questions for staff** are announced as clearly as the
  answers, because if that framing is visible only to a sighted reader then the
  tool is quietly more confident in a screen reader than it is on screen.

## The question this raises rather than settles

Credit means being named in a public file. Both templates offer an anonymous
option and neither invents a policy about what a credit line may say instead of
a legal name. `docs/HELP-WANTED.md` notes that sibling repos have answered this
in opposite directions and says it is your call, possibly counsel's.

## Verification

Documentation and issue templates only. No source, no data, no rule, no
evidence record touched.

Ran locally: `tests/test_manual_evidence.py`, `tests/test_beta_gate.py`,
`tests/test_conformance.py` - **156 passed**. All 21 manual rows still read
`not_run` and nothing here claims otherwise. #114 stays open.

*Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed before submission.*

author: patrickserrano
body:
## The problem

Both the drift audit and the doctor probe resolved `releases/latest` and ran **that** lacquer against the project's files. So every lacquer release retroactively marked all sixteen repos as drifted, and a one-line comment fix upstream became a fleet-wide re-sync just to get CI green again.

The cost of improving lacquer scaled with the size of the fleet. That is backwards.

It also inverted what the check means. **Drift should mean "someone hand-edited a file the lacquer owns."** Being *behind* is not drift — it is a normal, deliberate state that `lacquer audit` already reports as its own category, and that a sync resolves when someone chooses to run one.

## The fix

`.lacquer.lock` already records the version each project synced with:

```json
{ "version": "1.15.1", "files": { ... } }
```

That is the only version whose output can meaningfully be compared against these files. Both steps now read it instead of asking GitHub what is newest.

## The doctor probe had the sharper version of the same bug

It ran the **newest** lacquer's probes against the config the project synced from an **older** one — a pairing that exists nowhere and that nobody chose. Not hypothetical: merging a new probe upstream once turned every project's CI red simultaneously, because each was still carrying the config the previous version had shipped.

## What is preserved

- Fail-closed on both sides: the audit still reports `result=fail` and never exits non-zero (so a finding cannot suppress the lint/test results on the PR that needs them); the probe still **must** fail, because a probe that silently did not run is the exact failure it exists to catch.
- A missing lock is now an **explicit failure** on the probe rather than a silent pass, and a warning-plus-drift-failure on the audit.
- The version is shape-checked before it can reach `ref:` or a download URL, exactly as the resolved tag was.
- Plain `grep`/`sed` on one scalar field rather than `jq`, which is not guaranteed on the self-hosted Mac.

## Side benefit

No network call, no redirect to parse, and none of api.github.com's 60-requests-per-hour unauthenticated budget — which every runner behind one NAT address shares.

Verified: `gofmt` clean, `go build` OK, `go test ./...` **0 FAIL**, extraction checked against a real `.lacquer.lock`, and `grep -rn "setup-go|go build" profiles/*/workflows*/` still empty.

body:
## Root cause

Post-#4490–#4492 holiday-gate sweep left two routes with real side effects on NYSE holidays (Labor Day 2026-09-07):

1. **largo-morning-brief** — dual-band EventBridge (13:25/14:25 UTC) still lands 9:25 AM ET on holidays. inEtWindow alone does not exclude NYSE holidays → web-push to opted-in members with a fake open brief.
2. **thermal-discord EOD recap** — isThermalEodRecapDue is time-only (16:00–16:30 ET). eodDue=true bypasses the RTH skip → session-close Discord recap on a closed market.

## Fix

- largo-morning-brief: isTradingDayEt(sessionDay) after inMorningWindow, before buildLargoMorningBrief; force=1 bypasses (same pattern as nighthawk-morning-confirm).
- thermal-discord-eod: isTradingDayEt(todayEt(now)) inside isThermalEodRecapDue before the 16:00–16:30 ET band check.

## Evidence

- npx tsx --test src/app/api/cron/largo-morning-brief/route.holiday-gate.test.ts — GREEN
- npx tsx --test src/lib/thermal-discord-breach-state.test.ts — GREEN (includes Labor Day 4:10 PM ET → false)

Two routes only. Trading-day morning brief + EOD recap behavior unchanged.

Awaiting Claude peer review.

author: kefaro
body:
## Causa

El backend pasa a emitir una cookie de refresh por tipo de sujeto
(`vet_refresh_employee` / `vet_refresh_system`) porque tenant y consola
comparten la misma API y una sola cookie `vet_refresh` se pisaba entre
apps, expulsando de las dos cada 15 minutos.

## Cambio

- `POST /auth/refresh` ahora exige `{type}` en el cuerpo en vez de leer una
  cookie sin distinguir sujeto.
- `authApi.refresh` recibe el tipo de sujeto y lo envía.
- `authStore.refreshSession` toma el tipo de la sesión en memoria o del
  storage; si no hay tipo conocido, limpia la sesión sin llamar a la API.
- Contrato (`api/openapi.json`) y tipos generados
  (`src/types/api.generated.d.ts`) sincronizados con el cambio del backend.

author: m-guchi
body:
## 対応Issue

#3

## 概要

在庫を正本として管理し、購入・消費・廃棄・訂正・取消を追跡できる永続モデルを追加します。

設計の柱は3つです。

1. **在庫の実体は`StockLot`**（同一商品・同一期限・同一保管場所のかたまり）。期限や保管場所が違えば別ロットになります。
2. **数量の増減は`InventoryTransaction`にappend-onlyで積む。** 既存行のUPDATE・DELETEは行わず、取消は「符号を反転した`REVERSAL`行を足す」ことで表します。この形にしてあるため、現在数量は`quantityDelta`の**単純合計**で復元でき、取消済みの行を除外する処理が要りません。`StockLot.quantity`はその合計を保持する集計値で、正本は履歴のほうです。
3. **他家庭のデータを参照できないことをDB制約で担保する。** 家庭に属する全モデルへ`@@unique([householdId, id])`を置き、子から親への参照を`[householdId, 親Id]`の複合外部キーにしました。`householdId`が違う行はそもそも外部キーを満たせません。`access.ts`の`scopeToHousehold()`がアプリ側の入口の担保、この複合外部キーがDB側の最後の砦という関係です。

## Issue #2 との調整

計画レビュー（G1）の指摘を受けて実装方針を変更しました。#2 と #3 が並行して同じ空スキーマから初期マイグレーションを作っており、**両方が入ると`Household`が二重に作られて`prisma migrate deploy`が落ちる**状態でした。

Issue #2 本文の「後続: データモデル」に従い、**利用者と家庭の境界は #2 を正本**としています。

- `Household`・`Member`の定義を #3 から落とし、#2 の`Household`・`HouseholdMember`を再利用
- 初期マイグレーションを取り下げ、#2 のマイグレーションの上に積む**2本目**に作り直し
- テーブル名を #2 に合わせて PascalCase へ揃え（`@@map`を外した）
- `src/lib/db.ts`・`scripts/setup-db.sh`・`tsconfig.json`・テスト周りは #2 のものを使用
- `prisma/seed.ts`の投入先を、開発用ログインが入る家庭（`dev-household-own`）に変更

判断の記録は #3 のコメントに残してあります。

## 実装内容

### スキーマ（`prisma/schema.prisma`）

| モデル | 役割 |
| --- | --- |
| `Category` | 家庭ごとのカテゴリ。親子関係を持てる |
| `Product` | 商品マスタ。内容量・食数・使用回数・防災判定用の属性を持つ |
| `ProductAlias` | レシート・バーコード・AIが返した表記ゆれを商品へ寄せる別名 |
| `Barcode` | JAN等のバーコードと商品の対応 |
| `StorageLocation` / `StoragePosition` | 保管場所と、その中の詳細位置 |
| `StockLot` | 在庫の実体。数量・単位・賞味期限・消費期限・開封日を持つ |
| `InventoryTransaction` | append-onlyの入出庫履歴。購入・消費・廃棄・訂正・取消 |

- **数量は`Decimal(14,3)`と単位（`UnitCode`）の組**で持ちます。小数の食数・使用回数・容量をそのまま扱えます。
- **防災判定用の属性**は`temperatureZone`（常温/冷蔵/冷凍）・`requiresHeating`・`requiresWater`・`emergencyRole`を列として持ち、将来の追加は`disasterAttributes`（JSON）へ逃がせます。
- `HouseholdMember`へ`@@unique([householdId, id])`を追加しました。入出庫履歴が記録者を`[householdId, memberId]`で参照するために必要で、これにより**他家庭のメンバーを記録者にした履歴を作れません**。

### ドメイン関数（`src/lib/inventory/`）

- `units.ts` — 単位と次元、換算、合算。**個数系の単位（個・パック・本…）は商品ごとの入数が分からないと互いに換算できない**ため、`sumQuantities()`は換算できない組み合わせを黙って合算せず`UnitConversionError`を投げます。合算できないものも落とさず並べたい場面用に`groupSummableQuantities()`も用意しました。
- `ledger.ts` — 履歴からの数量再計算（`computeLotQuantity`）、取消行の組み立て（`buildReversal`。取消の取消と二重取消を拒否）、集計値と履歴の突き合わせ（`verifyLotQuantity`）、種別と符号の矛盾検出（`assertDeltaSign`）。

### seed（`prisma/seed.ts`）

`pnpm db:seed`で、`pnpm db:seed:dev`が作る「開発用の家」へ在庫のサンプルを投入します（6ロット・13履歴）。
**数量は`StockLot.quantity`へ直接書かず、`computeLotQuantity()`で履歴から組み立てています。** 実装と同じ経路を通るため、集計値と履歴がずれたseedを作れません。取消・訂正の例も含めてあります。

### その他

- `.github/workflows/claude-conflict-resolve.yml`の`verify-commands`に`pnpm test:unit`を追加（#2 が`ci-fix`・`pr-repair`の2つだけ直していたため）
- `CLAUDE.md`にデータモデルの設計方針、`README.md`にseedの手順を追記

## テスト内容

### 単体テスト（`pnpm test` = lint + typecheck + test:unit）

```
ℹ tests 69   （#2の36件 + 今回の33件）
ℹ pass 69
ℹ fail 0
```

今回追加した33件は、単位換算（L↔mL・kg↔g）、換算できない単位の合算拒否、小数の誤差なし加算（0.1+0.2=0.3）、履歴からの数量再計算、取消による数量の復元、二重取消・取消の取消の拒否、種別と符号の矛盾検出、集計値のずれ検出をカバーしています。

`pnpm lint`・`pnpm typecheck`・`pnpm build:ci`もすべて成功しています。

### 実DBでの確認（ローカル MySQL 8.0 / `app_stockly`）

`pnpm db:migrate:deploy` → `pnpm db:seed:dev` → `pnpm db:seed` を実行したうえで、**越境が実際にDBで拒否されること**をSQLで確認しました。

```
-- 1. 他家庭の商品を参照するロット
ERROR 1452 (23000): Cannot add or update a child row: a foreign key constraint fails
  (`app_stockly`.`StockLot`, CONSTRAINT `StockLot_householdId_productId_fkey`
   FOREIGN KEY (`householdId`, `productId`) REFERENCES `Product` (`householdId`, `id`) ...)

-- 2. 指定した保管場所の配下にない詳細位置を参照するロット
ERROR 1452 (23000): ... CONSTRAINT `StockLot_householdId_storageLocationId_storagePositionId_fkey` ...

-- 3. 他家庭のメンバーを記録者にした履歴
ERROR 1452 (23000): ... CONSTRAINT `InventoryTransaction_householdId_memberId_fkey`
   FOREIGN KEY (`householdId`, `memberId`) REFERENCES `HouseholdMember` (`householdId`, `id`) ...

-- 4. 同じ履歴の二重取消
ERROR 1062 (23000): Duplicate entry 'dev-household-own-seed-tx-egg-2'
  for key 'InventoryTransaction.InventoryTransaction_householdId_reversesTransactionId_key'
```

集計値と履歴の合計が全ロットで一致することも確認しました（小数を含む`9.500`も一致）。

```
id                      unit    stored_qty  computed_qty  result
seed-lot-alpha-rice     PACK    15.000      15.000        OK
seed-lot-egg            PIECE   8.000       8.000         OK
seed-lot-gas-cartridge  PIECE   5.000       5.000         OK
seed-lot-milk           BOTTLE  1.000       1.000         OK
seed-lot-toilet-paper   ROLL    9.500       9.500         OK
seed-lot-water          BOTTLE  11.000      11.000        OK
```

seedを2回流しても件数が変わらないこと（冪等）も確認済みです。

## 確認方法

画面の変更はありません（在庫UIは後続Issue）。DBで確認する場合は次の順で実行してください。

```bash
cd /home/guchi/apps/stockly-worktrees/issue-3
pnpm install
pnpm db:migrate:dev      # 2本目のマイグレーションが適用される
pnpm db:seed:dev         # 開発用ユーザーと家庭
pnpm db:seed             # 在庫のサンプルデータ
pnpm db:studio           # 中身を見る場合
```

## 注意点

- **DBスキーマの変更のため、`22.merge-confirm-required`に従いユーザー確認なしにマージしないでください。**
- **このPRは #2（PR #17）がマージ済みであることを前提にしています。** すでに`develop`へ取り込み済みで、差分は #3 の範囲だけです。
- 複合外部キーが効くことのCIでの自動検証は、`lint-and-build`にDBが無いためこのPRには入れていません。#18 として切り出しました（このPRでは実DBでの手動確認と実行ログで担保しています）。
- `HouseholdMember`へ一意キーを1つ追加しています（`@@unique([householdId, id])`）。既存データに重複が無ければそのまま適用できます（`id`が主キーなので重複しません）。

author: stephnangue
body:
Stacked on #607. Last of the stack.

The suite alongside this one covers the same shape over a KV read. This one exists because until #607 no other kind of source could be a chaining source at all, so the machinery's driver-independence was true in principle and untested in fact.

### Both subject sources, because only one of them mints anything

Under `agent_identity` the agent's inbound token is forwarded and Warden signs nothing. Under `warden_identity` Warden mints an assertion — and that is the only path on which the audience and resource claims are derived, so a suite covering just the first would leave the resource derivation added in #607 with no coverage anywhere.

That row captures the token the exchange receives, checks it is not the agent's own, verifies it against the published JWKS, and asserts both claims. Verification rather than decoding: an account that could not verify the assertion would reject it, so decoding alone could pass on a token nothing real would accept.

### The stub

One listener serves both legs, routing on the target header, and derives each payload from the id it was asked for. That is what lets the templated row prove *which* secret was read rather than merely that a read happened — the value arriving upstream names it.

The control row asserts on the header a declared field would occupy, not on some inert key: a field no extractor maps could never appear whatever carriage did, so asserting its absence would pass against an implementation that copied the whole payload.

### Verification

Run against a live three-node cluster. Six tests pass; the full e2e suite passes across all twenty packages, including `e2e/rotation`, which matters given #604 changed rotation behaviour.

Writing them caught a real bug in my own first draft: `ensureEnv` clears the upstream recorder, so two subtests under one parent call shared a request count. The call now lives inside each subtest, with a comment saying why.

author: aparajon
body:
The CLI sends the ID token as its bearer credential but schedules refresh using the access token's lifetime. Different lifetimes can leave it sending an expired token or refreshing too early. Login and refresh now cache the ID token's `exp` value, and existing OIDC profiles read that claim on load so they adopt the correct lifetime automatically.

```text
Before                           After
ID token -> bearer credential    ID token -> bearer credential
Access expiry -> refresh time    ID expiry -> refresh time
```

Numeric expiry values support fractional seconds and exponent notation. Login and refresh reject missing, malformed, or out-of-range expiry values. A malformed cached token triggers a refresh when possible; failed refresh preserves the existing cache. The local clock only schedules renewal. This upholds AZ-3: no client-parsed claims establish identity, and `pkg/auth/oidc.go` still verifies every bearer token before granting access.

<details>
<summary>Login error when the provider omits exp</summary>

```text
log in to https://issuer.example.com: read login ID token expiry: id_token must contain a positive exp claim
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Refresh warning when the provider omits exp</summary>

```text
could not refresh the token for profile "default" (run `schemabot login`): read refresh ID token expiry: id_token must contain a positive exp claim
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Warning when a cached ID token omits exp and cannot be refreshed</summary>

```text
read cached ID token expiry for profile "default" (run `schemabot login`): id_token must contain a positive exp claim
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Warning when a refreshed token is past by the local clock</summary>

```text
refreshed ID token for profile "default" is already expired according to this computer; check the local clock and the provider's ID token lifetime
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Warning when an expired token cannot be refreshed</summary>

```text
token for profile "default" is expired or about to expire according to this computer and cannot be refreshed; check the local clock or run `schemabot login`
```

author: yunosukeyoshino
body:
## Summary

Implement ADR 0001: External skills from different sources can share an upstream name and still coexist as sibling directories under `~/.agents/skills/`.

The identifier is `{owner}--{name}` (e.g. `vercel--next-best-practices`), not `/` and not a single `-`. Agents only scan a single-depth folder, and both GitHub owners and skill names already use kebab-case, so `--` is the flatten that can be split again.

### Behavior
- No collision → keep the short upstream name
- Collision with Custom / Vendor / other External / an already-active directory → `{owner}--{name}`, or `--as <alias>` / `--prefix`
- Lock key is the deploy name; `installSkill` is the upstream name passed to `skills add --skill`
- After rename, `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name:` matches the folder

### Coexistence (the actual goal)
The skills CLI always writes the upstream folder. Deploy now stashes any pre-existing upstream directory, installs that one skill, moves the fresh copy onto the deploy name, syncs frontmatter, then restores the stash. `search/` and `second-owner--search/` both remain on disk.

### Also in this PR
- Collision mapping uses `lock.vendor` (not `lock.vendor.skills`) and does not treat an already-active name as non-colliding
- Same-source re-add skips instead of creating a duplicate `owner--name`
- Web install/add-to-deck pass `{deployName, upstreamName}` from mapping instead of parsing the `owner--` prefix
- CLI: `--prefix`, kebab-case / no-slash alias validation, TTY options (namespace / alias / Vendor fork / skip), unlink dangling agent links for the upstream name
- Source detail matches candidates via `installSkill`, so a namespaced skill is not listed as both installed and importable

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run format:check` — pass
- `bun run test` — **358/358 pass**

author: chelseakr
body:
## What was wrong

`check --json` is machine readable and it is this tool's own shape, so anyone gating a document in CI writes an adapter first. SARIF is the shape those surfaces already read.

## What changed

`check --sarif` emits a SARIF 2.1.0 log. It is a serialiser: it reads a finished `RunReport`, changes no conclusion, and leaves the exit code exactly as `ExitCode` documents it. `--json` and `--sarif` together is a usage error, because they are two shapes of one report.

The work is not the serialisation. It is **not losing the fail-closed contract in the translation.** SARIF's natural shape is a list of problems found; this tool's central claim is about the checks it could *not* decide. A log carrying only deviations would say the same thing for a clean label, an unreadable one, and a run that checked nothing at all.

| what the run concluded | where it lands |
| --- | --- |
| a deviation | a `result` at level `error` |
| a conforming check | counted in `invocations[0].properties`, no result |
| a registered check that is not implemented | `toolConfigurationNotification` at `note`, with its registered reason and blocker |
| an implemented check that could not be decided | `toolConfigurationNotification` at `error` |
| an unreadable document | `toolExecutionNotification` at `error`, and no results at all for that file |
| an advisory | `runs[0].properties.advisories`, never a result |

Three of those rows carry the argument.

**A conforming check emits no result and is still counted**, so the denominator is visible. Otherwise "we found nothing" and "we looked at nothing" render identically.

**The two kinds of not-evaluated are separated by severity rather than merged.** A check this tool has never implemented is a documented, permanent property of the catalog: it appears in every run, and raised as an error it would make every run scream and get muted within a month, which is how a real signal dies. A check that *is* implemented and still could not be decided on this document is the other thing entirely, and it is the case this repository refuses to let read as a pass. Both carry `properties.implemented`, so the distinction never depends on reading the level.

**`executionSuccessful` is false when nothing was checked.** SARIF uses that flag for "the tool failed to complete", and finding a deviation is not that, so a deviation keeps `true`. But a run over zero documents reporting success with an empty results array is, to every consumer, a clean run. Exit code 3 exists here precisely because an empty denominator is never a pass.

Advisories stay out of results and notifications entirely, under ADR 0013: an advisory carries no status, is in no count and reaches no exit code, and emitting one as a result would score it.

## Two findings worth more than the feature

**The log validates against the real schema, and the schema would not have caught the defect this issue is worried about.**

Measured today against the OASIS errata01 schema (`https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/errata01/os/schemas/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json`, 112,768 bytes, draft-04), for the deficient fixture: **0 errors.**

The issue cites qfer-preflight #14 as the reason to validate in the gate. That defect was a wrong `ruleIndex`, an index resolving to a different rule than `ruleId` names. That is well-formed SARIF by every structural rule in the specification, and a consumer shows the reader the wrong requirement with the right identifier printed beside it. No schema catches it. `test_every_rule_index_resolves_to_the_rule_its_id_names` does, and it resolves every reference in both results and notifications.

**The `$schema` URL that circulates in tooling is dead.** `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oasis-tcs/sarif-spec/master/Schemata/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json` returned **404** when measured on 2026-09-07: the specification repository moved its schema and dropped the `master` branch. This log uses OASIS's own address, and a test pins it against the dead one by name so a copy-paste back fails. Nothing fetches a `$schema`, so a broken one is a contract that rots with no test noticing.

## What I did not do, and why

The issue's "Done when" asks the log to validate against SARIF 2.1.0 **in the gate**. It validates, but the committed gate is structural rather than a schema run, because that would mean vendoring the 112 KB OASIS schema into this repository, and redistributing an OASIS specification artifact carries its notice requirements. That is your call, not an agent's. `tests/test_sarif.py` states the gap in its module docstring rather than leaving a reader to assume the schema runs. If you want it vendored, it is a small follow-up: the file, a provenance line, and swapping `_REQUIRED` for a `Draft4Validator` run.

`_REQUIRED` meanwhile pins the required keys of every object this serialiser emits, so a key dropped or retyped fails.

## How it was verified

Full suite: **975 passed**, 3 skipped (pre-existing, no calibration census committed). Coverage 98.67% against a 96% floor; `sarif.py` at 99%. `ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy` and `scripts/check_no_dashes.py` all clean.

Six negative controls, each committed first, baselined with `git hash-object`, sabotaged, asserted changed, asserted the sabotaged file still parses, run with `__pycache__` cleared under `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, then restored and re-hashed:

| sabotage | expected red | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `_LEVEL_UNDECIDED_IMPLEMENTED` `error` to `note` (the two kinds merged) | the could-not-look level | 1 red |
| `executionSuccessful` hardcoded `True` | the nothing-checked case | 2 red |
| `ruleIndex` hardcoded to `0` | the index-resolves check | 1 red |
| the not-evaluated filter inverted (the unevaluated half leaves the log) | the catalog-completeness checks | 3 red |
| advisories dropped from `run.properties` | the ADR 0013 fence | 1 red |
| unreadable documents dropped from the execution notifications | the unreadable-is-not-clean checks | 2 red |

All six restored to their exact baseline blob hashes.

The `ast.parse` step is there deliberately: a sabotage that leaves a file unparseable turns the suite red on a collection error, which reads exactly like a control firing and is not one. Asserting the mutated file still parses is what separates "the guard fired" from "I broke the file".

All six controls fired on their first run, which is worth stating plainly rather than leaving implied.

## Scope

Part of #42. Uploading to code scanning stays out of scope, as the issue says: the tool writes a log and stops.

*Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed before submission.*

A line in either holding section had to carry a number saying which project it was of, so writing down an idea meant deciding whose work it was first.  That is backwards: the holding sections are where a thing goes precisely because nobody has decided that.

A held line with no number is now stored with its project as tbd and rendered back as it was typed, no number invented for it.  Giving it a number in the document is how it joins a project, which is the same gesture as moving it into the goals of the period.

Since it is not reached through a project, it says whose it is itself: mc.changes writes the lead of a goal that has none, from whose document it was in.  Without that it would belong to nobody, appear in no document, and be dropped by the next sync for not being in one.

A goal of the period still needs its number.  That is work somebody is doing, and the project is what says who.

author: eldad8802-prog
body:
A business arriving at Dubiz usually brings years of invoices and receipts that another system issued. It should be able to keep that history here. What it must not get is history that looks like Dubiz issued it.

## Why this is not a BillingDocument

`BillingDocument` means one thing: Dubiz produced this document. It carries a number drawn from Dubiz's own sequence, an issuance snapshot and legal hash, a Dubiz-rendered and sometimes cryptographically signed PDF, and it is the table the uniform (מבנה אחיד) export files with the Israeli Tax Authority. The export selects `status: ISSUED`, `documentType != QUOTE`, by issuance date — so a foreign invoice stored there would not merely be mislabelled, it would be **filed**.

So this is a separate table with a separate vocabulary, and the separation is enforced rather than described.

## What is deliberately absent

- **No status, no issuance state.** Copying that vocabulary is how a historical record starts being treated as an issued one.
- **No line items.** The import contract that would produce them does not exist yet, and the detail is preserved in the original artifact. An empty table now would be persistence with no producer.
- **No structured payments.** Reusing `BillingReceiptPayment` would assert Dubiz saw those payments.
- **No `allocationNumber`.** Only `originalAllocationNumber` — a number somebody else obtained, which Dubiz never requested, validated or reported.

## Tenant isolation is structural, not remembered

The Document and reversal references are composite foreign keys through `(businessId, id)`, so a cross-tenant reference cannot be written at all — not "is checked and rejected", but has no representation. RLS is enabled and forced, with SELECT and INSERT policies only, and the grants agree with them: the migration revokes the UPDATE and DELETE that this project's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` hands to `app_runtime` on every new table.

`Document` is changed by one added index and nothing else. No column, no behaviour, no existing query.

## The uniqueness rule that is deliberately missing

Business + source system + type + original number looks like an identity, and it is indexed as one. It is **not** a unique constraint. A corrected re-export, a document with no number, an owner relabelling which system a batch came from, and two prior systems both numbering an invoice 1001 are all legitimate — and a database rule would turn each into an import failure the owner cannot resolve. Duplicate policy belongs to the import contract, which can show the owner what it found and ask.

## Evidence

**Real PostgreSQL 17.11 — 42 checks, 0 failed.** The migration file itself is applied statement by statement and then interrogated through a role that is **not** superuser and **not** bypassrls, which the battery asserts before trusting a single result. The `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` hazard is reproduced before the migration runs, and CI confirms the new table really does arrive holding UPDATE — otherwise the REVOKEs would be proving nothing.

Covered: forced RLS, policy shape, privileges, isolation in both directions, insert-into-another-tenant, insert with no tenant context, immutability, cross-tenant artifact and reversal links, many-to-one artifact sharing, self-reversal, retention under delete, provenance fading, accepted duplicate identity, decimal fidelity, and zero billing rows throughout.

**25 structural firewall checks, no database.** Field vocabulary, relation targets in both directions, expand-only migration, schema/migration column agreement, and zero consumers.

**11 negative proofs, all passing.** Each mutates the migration itself — unforced RLS, no RLS, an open read policy, an open insert policy, the REVOKEs removed, the identity index made unique, the composite FK reduced to one column, RESTRICT turned to CASCADE, the self-reversal guard removed, a foreign key into `BillingDocument` — and the eleventh adds a `status` field to the schema. Every mutation is confirmed to have applied before its result is believed.

Two of these earned their keep during the run. `INSERT ... RETURNING` asks the SELECT policy about the row it returns, so an open INSERT policy was being masked by the read policy; the rejection cases now insert without RETURNING, so only the policy under test can refuse.

Full regression green: TypeScript, production build, lint unchanged at 370 problems before and after, the data-transfer and documents suites, the tenant, Prisma-centralization, admin-boundary, import-ledger, account-deletion and pilot-RLS guards.

## Migration

One, expand-only, **not applied to production**. No `BillingDocument` change, no sequence touched, no data written, no dependency on any database's current state.

## Follow-up in its own PR

Adding `historicalFiscalDocument` to `RETAIN_MODELS` is application code, and the migration-first guard keeps application code out of a PR carrying a migration. It follows immediately. Nothing can reach the model in the meantime: no purge set names it, and the firewall asserts that.

## Out of scope

Analyze, Preview, Execute, import UI, history UI, export, reporting, learning, OCR. Nothing consumes this model.

body:
Six commits of client iteration on where the two brief figures live and
what their box looks like. Reviewing this commit by commit will show
the figures move twice — the diff against `main` is what landed.

## Where they ended up

Under §2's «مسرعة أعمال متخصصة أطلقتها منصة بدار…» paragraph, as a
2-up pair inside the sticky split's own column. That paragraph is where
the brief actually says «تمكين **21** شركة ناشئة … عبر برنامج مكثف»,
so the pair answers the sentence directly above it.

The `.stat-row` band under the hero is gone. §3 على ماذا ستحصل is back
to its five benefit cards and its `nth-child(4)` centring, unchanged
from `main`.

## The route it took (all client instructions, Sept 2026)

| | |
|---|---|
| `632f9be` | figures out of the hero band, into the §3 grid as cards |
| `1f3898a` | gave them Building2 / Target marks |
| `6d666c9` | moved them again, to under the عن المشروع paragraph |
| `6efc0ac` | dropped the marks |
| `f1f5e23` | rebuilt the box so it is actually visible |
| `d4e6b1d` | trimmed it back down 15% |

The note on `FigureCard` records that the marks were tried and removed,
so nobody re-adds one as a "missing" icon.

## Why the box is not `band-tile`

It was, and it read as almost nothing. Measured: `#0f2325` on a
`#081a1a` page behind a `#1b2e31` hairline — a 7% lift and a border you
cannot see. That restraint is right for the three sector cards below it
(a row of equals, where the box is a container and the copy is the
content) and wrong for two figures whose whole job is to be seen.

So: a teal wash pooling at the reading corner, a `brand-300/25` ring
that is actually visible, a soft bloom behind the numeral, and a
`brand-300` bar down the inline-start edge — the same gesture the
paragraph above already uses, which is what makes the pair read as that
sentence's figures rather than as two cards that happen to follow it.

`FigureCard` rather than `IconCard`: a figure is not an icon, and the
number needs display scale, which that component's icon slot cannot do.
The count-up and `formatNumber` came across from `StatRow`, so the
digits still animate and still render Western.

## Also in here

- **`auto-rows-fr` now starts at `sm`** on §3's grid. Levelling row
  heights is what puts side-by-side cards on one baseline; in the
  single column below `sm` there is no row to level, and it was
  stretching every card to the tallest.
- **A dead transition removed**: `transition-[box-shadow,--tw-ring-color]`
  asked the browser to animate an unregistered custom property, which it
  cannot do. The ring *is* a box-shadow, so one property covers both.

## Verified

- `npm run lint` clean, `npm run build` clean
- `grep -c supabase dist/shell.html` → `0`
- 1280px and 390px: cards 324×126 and 358×~120, no horizontal scroll,
  §3's five cards still centre their trailing row

`/programs/usus-syria` stays noindex — unchanged by this branch, and

author: alexander-turner
body:
## What & why

Move the `workflow_dispatch` that re-fires a push or scheduled scan out of its own `relay` job into `discover`'s last step. Neither event can resolve directly — claude-code-action rejects both — so the scan re-dispatches itself, and as a separate job that dispatch waited for a runner of its own to make one `gh` call. On #168 that hop cost 7m04s of queue.

`discover` runs on every trigger, so the step's `if:` is now the whole loop guard: it admits `push` and `schedule` only, so the dispatched run reaches the step and does nothing.

## Security boundary impact — the part worth signing off

`discover` gains `actions: write`, and a job's permissions cover every step in it. That scope used to sit in a one-step job whose whole body was a fixed `gh workflow run`. It now co-resides with `discover.py` — 1279 lines that read pull request metadata the author controls. No route from an author exists today: the checkout names the default branch, and the dispatch step is gated off `pull_request`. What grew is the blast radius of a future defect in that script, from read-only scopes to "dispatch any workflow, cancel or re-run any run, delete artifacts". That is the price of the runner saved.

Write scope also forces the staging change: `test_resolver_ref.py` refuses a write-scoped job that clones the resolver unpinned, so `discover` now checks out this repository's default branch and runs `resolver-dir.sh`. In THIS repo that script short-circuits on the self-repo branch and serves the checked-out tree, so the `ref:` is the whole control; the pin bites only in a consumer. A consumer also needs both resolver scripts beside the workflow, and a repository whose token policy caps at read gets a 403 at the dispatch step.

## Review focus

Read the dispatch step's `if:` against the `on:` block in `auto-resolve-conflicts.yaml` — the two halves of the loop guard, and no one screen shows both. Least sure of: the checkout's `ref:`, since `actions: write` is safe only while every tree the job stages is one no pull request author writes.

## How it was tested

- `tests/test_auto_resolve_any_base_branch.py` — 20 passed. Non-vacuity, per new invariant: moving the dispatch step above the scan reds only `test_the_dispatch_step_reads_a_scan_that_already_ran`; adding `github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'` to resolve's `if:` reds only `test_every_trigger_either_dispatches_or_resolves`.
- 516 passed across the four `_gha_if` consumer suites, after extending its context roots with `needs` and `vars`.
- `actionlint` clean. `zizmor --offline --persona=auditor`: 4 low findings before, 3 after.

## Decisions made

- A failed dispatch fails `discover`. On a push or schedule there is no pull request to comment on, so it surfaces as a red job — what a failed `relay` did.
- The gate tests drive `tests/_gha_if.py` instead of a local evaluator: it substitutes whole context paths, where a bare `str.replace` is corruptible by a longer path sharing a prefix.

## Proposed guards

The workflow arm of `test_resolver_ref.py::test_every_clone_of_the_resolver_pins_it` now inspects zero clones — `discover` held the last workflow-level `git clone` of `${RESOLVER_REPOSITORY}`, and every resolver clone is behind `resolver-dir.sh`. It still asserts that a write-scoped job was read, so it passes vacuously rather than reporting that its subject is gone. A clones-seen non-vacuity assert, matching the one the script arm already carries, would catch that.

body:
## Why

Stape's tracking audit on 2026-09-07 scored aungmyintoo.com 45/100. GA4 loaded straight from Google's hosts, so ad blockers dropped it and Safari ITP capped the `_ga` cookies at 7 days. amoOS sprint 122, tasks 1907 to 1910.

## What

- `app/t/lib.js` serves gtag.js from this origin, cached for one hour.
- `app/t/g/collect` forwards hits to GA4 with the visitor IP (`_uip`) and browser headers, then re-emits `_ga` and `_ga_*` via `Set-Cookie` with a 400-day Max-Age. Because the response comes from the same host and IP as the page, Safari honours the full lifetime.
- `GoogleTag` component replaces the `@next/third-parties` `GoogleAnalytics` and points gtag's `transport_url` at `/t`.

No new dependencies. `@next/third-parties` is now unused and can be removed in a follow-up.

- `GET` and `POST /t/g/collect` return 204 and set both `_ga` cookies with `Max-Age=34560000`, `Domain=aungmyintoo.com` on the production host and host-only elsewhere.
- Cookie values containing `$` pass through unencoded.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## To verify after deploy

- GA4 DebugView shows page_view from the proxy with the correct country (confirms `_uip` is honoured).
- Safari: `_ga` expiry moves to about 400 days after one page view.

author: famesjranko
body:
## What & why

Five behaviour-level quality fixes from the pre-release code audit, one commit each:

- **Every .env write goes through the blessed atomic writer.** Three surviving `sed -i` writers truncated in place, so an interrupt mid-write could corrupt .env. The writer single-quotes values, so the two raw-line readers of the stage marker became quote-tolerant in the same change.
- **A failed fail2ban fallback-unit write is no longer reported as success.** The install path swallowed the write failure and then restarted a unit that was never written.
- **Logging helpers now contract `return 0`.** Eight call sites use the `cmd && log_ok || log_warn` idiom and depended on an emergent return value; the contract is now explicit and commented.
- **One table owns the compose profile mapping.** Four independent implementations existed; the updater's copy expanded unquoted and broke on profile names with spaces. The updater and launcher now derive from the canonical function; the Stage 1 plan renderer deliberately stays separate (it runs before .env exists) with a comment saying why.
- **The undocumented `--wipe` flag is gone.** Fully destructive, zero callers, absent from usage/docs/tests; its unreachable teardown arms went with it.

## Linked issue

Pre-release audit findings; no tracking issue.

## How it was verified

- [x] `bash -n` is clean on changed shell scripts
- [x] `./tests/check.sh` passes (fast, unit, and wizard tiers — 333 wizard assertions)
- [x] Compose still validates (the default check renders it with `.env.example`)
- [x] New behavior is covered by a test — stage marker flips via the blessed writer and the wizard probe matches; fallback-write failure drives the honest-warning path; log_ok return pinned; profile expectations derived from the canonical table, not hardcoded
- [x] Docs updated (structure doc's stale full-wipe reference fixed)
- [x] No `.env`, live `config/<service>/` files, or generated NVIDIA patch/download trees committed

author: tmustafiz
body:
Closes #74

## What

Legacy / hybrid Spring apps wire beans in XML. This lands those beans and their `<property ref>` / `<constructor-arg ref>` wiring in the **same** `(:Bean)` graph as the annotation-wired beans from #73, so the injection graph is complete.

### Parser — `SpringXmlParser`
- stdlib `xml.etree`; registered ahead of `ConfigFileParser`; `can_handle` matches only `.xml` files whose **root element is `<beans>`** (not `pom.xml`, not arbitrary XML).
- One `SpringXmlBean` per `<bean>` (inner beans get a generated `<Class>#<n>` id): `class`, `scope`, `parent`, `factory-*`, `primary`, `abstract`, `lazy-init`, aliases (`<alias>` + extra `name` tokens), `depends-on`.
- Wiring: `<constructor-arg ref>` / `<property name ref>`, `<ref bean>` / `<idref>`, inner `<bean>`, `<list>` / `<set>` / `<array>` / `<map>` of refs, and the `p:` / `c:` shortcut namespaces. `${key}` placeholders in `value=` captured.
- File-level `<context:component-scan base-package>`, `<context:property-placeholder location>`, `<import resource>` and distinct non-`beans` namespace elements (`aop:*`, `tx:*`, `util:*` — recorded, modelled later) stored on the `ConfigFile` (`format="spring-xml"`, four new list fields).
- One `Section` + `Chunk` so `search` finds "where is bean X wired".

### Writer
- `(:ConfigFile)-[:DECLARES_BEAN]->(:SpringXmlBean)` intermediate nodes, per-source reconcile (mirrors `ConfigProperty`). New `spring_xml_bean_id` constraint.

### Resolver — `SpringXmlResolver` (third post-directory-ingest pass, after `SpringBeanResolver`)
- Projects each `SpringXmlBean` → `(:Bean {defined_in:'xml', stereotype:'XmlBean', name, scope, primary, abstract, bean_type})`.
- `(:CodeEntity)-[:IS_BEAN]->(:Bean)` when `class` resolves to an ingested type.
- Refs resolved by **name or alias against both XML and annotation beans** → `(:Bean)-[:INJECTS {via:'xml-constructor'|'xml-property', property}]->(:Bean)`. Unknown ref → `stereotype:'XmlBeanStub'` bean keyed by the ref name (per the issue's "stub Bean keyed by id"); ambiguous → `Bean.unresolved_injections` (JSON), never guessed.
- `${key}` in a `<property value>` → `(:Bean)-[:BINDS]->(:ConfigProperty)`.
- `<import resource>` and `<context:property-placeholder>` → `(:ConfigFile)-[:IMPORTS_CONTEXT {kind:'import'|'property-placeholder'}]->(:ConfigFile)` (best-effort path match against ingested files).
- Rebuilt from scratch each run (`defined_in:'xml'` beans + `IMPORTS_CONTEXT` edges dropped first) → idempotent. Pure `_assemble(...)` unit-tested without Neo4j.
- Added to all three `IngestionPipeline` construction sites in `cli.py`.

## Verification

- `uv run ruff check .` → All checks passed!
- `uv run ruff format --check .` → 171 files already formatted
- `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 uv run pytest -q` → **330 passed** (12 new in `tests/test_spring_xml_parser.py`)

## Limitations

- No containerised Neo4j in CI: the resolver's Cypher isn't exercised end-to-end; the pure `_assemble` logic is. Same limitation as the #73 / #70 resolver PRs.
- `<import resource>` / property-placeholder path resolution is best-effort (strips `classpath:` / `file:`, skips `${…}`, matches by resolved path → suffix → basename).
- Cross-file `<alias>` (aliasing a bean defined in another context file) is not resolved; same-file aliases and multi-`name` tokens are.

body:
The user reports that Update preview keeps showing the old clip after Mark In and Mark Out. Existing tests checked stored bounds but stubbed the media player, so they did not cover the visible refresh.

This removes form batching from the timestamp controls so externally received marks and manual edits use the same live widget state. Update preview remains an explicit button. The player key now includes the displayed source bounds, forcing a fresh player when the applied range changes. Marks and unrelated reruns keep the same key and preserve the playhead until the trim is applied.

Validation: 97 targeted tests passed across preview marks, timestamps, and UI state. The extended regression applies both marks and clicks Update preview before saving or navigating, checks the new generation bounds and player duration/token/key, and confirms stable player identity on subsequent reruns. The prior implementation fails the new player-key assertion. git diff --check passed; published and tested trees match.

Limitation: the exact user-visible failure has not been reproduced in a real browser. A synthetic video and local test app were prepared, but the cloud browser refused the local URL with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT. This is a targeted fix for stale form/player state, pending real playback confirmation.

Manual check: on this branch, seek and Mark In, seek later and Mark Out, click Update preview without Save timing first, then verify the displayed video starts at the marked moment and has the shorter duration. Check manual timing edits and candidate switching too. Await Sourcery review and playback confirmation before merging.

## Summary by Sourcery

Refresh the preview player when users apply updated clip marks while preserving state until the range is explicitly updated.

Bug Fixes:
- Refresh the preview player with the newly applied Mark In/Out range when Update preview is clicked, preventing stale clip bounds and duration from remaining visible.

Enhancements:
- Keep timestamp controls synchronized with live marks and manual edits while preserving the existing player and playhead across marks and ordinary reruns.
- Reset the media component only when the applied source bounds change, while retaining stable identity for acknowledgements and unrelated reruns.

Tests:
- Expand preview UI and component coverage to verify applied bounds, player identity, duration, source replacement, metadata handling, and playhead preservation.

Sourcery follow-up: added real Streamlit component identity/payload assertions without mocking preview_player, plus execution of the actual JavaScript source-replacement handler. These verify the transport and component protocol; the simulated media element does not establish real video decoding or visible playback.

## Why
QuickLaunch was an empty WPF shell that offered no usable launcher experience and had no protection against common startup/runtime failures. This PR turns it into a focused, keyboard-first Windows launcher with a calmer modern UI.

## What changed
- Replaced the blank window with a polished dark overlay and clear keyboard hints.
- Added `Ctrl + Space` global hotkey, tray access, Escape-to-hide, and Enter-to-launch behavior.
- Added searchable built-in actions for Calculator, Notepad, Settings, File Explorer, Desktop, and Downloads.
- Added Start Menu shortcut discovery with guarded filesystem access.
- Added safe process launching and user-visible failure feedback instead of crashing.
