author: i-rocky
body:
Three presence-membership correctness defects. Grouped because they overlap in
`ClusterCmd::PresenceSubscribe` and `ChannelState`, and would collide as separate
patches.

Closes #55
Closes #56
Closes #63

## #55 — the cluster presence cap was a check-then-act across nodes

`cluster_presence_capacity` read `HLEN presusers` and `HEXISTS presusers <user>`, and the
bridge committed the join with `PRESENCE_JOIN_LUA` several round trips later. Nothing
reserved the slot in between, so N nodes admitting a new distinct user at the same instant
each read room and each committed — overshooting by up to N−1, permanently, since the count
never falls back on its own. The comment above the check claimed the Redis count of record
made the probe authoritative; that is true only within one node, whose bridge drains
serially. It is deleted.

`PRESENCE_JOIN_LUA` now takes the cap and decides it itself:

```
KEYS[1]=presusers KEYS[2]=presinfo KEYS[3]=presmembers
ARGV[1]=user_id ARGV[2]=user_info ARGV[3]=member_token ARGV[4]=max_members
```

A new distinct user is weighed against `HLEN presusers` and committed in the same script.
Returns `-1` when the cap rejects — having written nothing, which is what lets the bridge
report the rejection without unwinding any cluster state — else the user's new refcount
(`1` = `first_for_user`). A negative `ARGV[4]` is uncapped, which is what the non-clustered
`RedisAdapter::subscribe` path passes (its cap is enforced node-locally in `ws::subscribe`,
which has a rejection channel; `SubscribeOutcome` does not). `cluster_presence_capacity` and
its probe are gone.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the same 4004 `LimitReached` `subscription_error`, the same
undo of the worker's inline node-local join, and a second connection of a user already on the
roster still admitted with the channel full.

**Test** — `cluster_presence_cap_is_atomic_across_nodes` (`tests/redis_cluster.rs`): roster
pre-filled to `CAP − 1`, then eight distinct users race the last slot across two adapters
(two nodes), all in flight together. Exactly one is admitted and `HLEN presusers` lands
exactly on `CAP`.

## #56 — still a real defect after the reconciler; now structurally gone

**Verdict: reduced, not fixed.** The membership reconciler that landed on master
re-subscribes any `msg` key the node has local members for, so the missing `SUBSCRIBE` is
repaired on its next tick rather than never. But that tick is up to
`PYLON_REDIS_PRESENCE_HEARTBEAT_SECS` away (default **25s**), and Redis pub/sub has no
replay: every `member_added`, `member_removed` and channel event published in that window is
lost outright, for every connection on the node, with nothing logged. The evidence is in the
regression test — it has to *step the reconciler aside* to observe the defect at all, and
with the reconciler in play the same test passes even with the bug present.

Fix: `node_first` is a one-shot token, so the bridge spends it before the admission verdict
rather than after. `cluster_subscribe` splits into `cluster_sub_channel` /
`cluster_unsub_channel` (the pub/sub lifecycle) and `cluster_membership_join` (the occupancy
write); `cluster_subscribe` is now the composition of the two and is unchanged for every
other caller. The presence arm takes the edge up front and hands it back — a matching
`UNSUBSCRIBE` — only when the rejection leaves the node with no members for the channel.

Taking the pub/sub edge first (rather than the whole of `cluster_subscribe`) is deliberate:
it means a rejected join never writes `occ`, so there is no transient over-count, no
compensating `cluster_unsubscribe`, and no interaction with the vacate CAS or a lost
`channel_occupied`.

**Test** — `capacity_rejected_presence_join_keeps_the_node_subscribed`
(`tests/cluster_bridge.rs`): drives the interleaving directly through `ClusterHandle` rather
than racing it — the rejected joiner's command carrying `node_first = true`, fired ahead of
the admitted joiner's carrying `false`, which the bridge drains FIFO. Asserted on `PUBSUB
NUMSUB`, gated not slept. A warm-up channel's own `NUMSUB` gates the reconciler's immediate
first tick so its member snapshot provably precedes the presence connections, and the
heartbeat is set to an hour so there is no second tick.

## #63 — the roster served a departed connection's `user_info`

`ChannelState` kept one `user_info` per distinct user, seeded by that user's first
connection; `remove` only decremented the refcount. Once the seeding connection left, the
roster advertised a value **no live connection had ever presented**, to every later
subscriber and every REST presence query, for as long as any other connection of that user
remained.

**Semantics chosen: the roster carries the user's OLDEST LIVE connection's `user_info`.**

First-wins was never wrong as a deduplication rule over live connections — the defect is that
it outlived the connection it deduplicated to. Stating the rule over *live* connections keeps
the add-side behaviour byte-identical (the roster goldens are unchanged, including the case
where a second connection of the same user presents different `user_info` and must not leak
into the roster) while repairing the remove side. Last-writer-wins was rejected: it changes
the add-side contract and has the same defect one step over — the newest writer can be the one
that leaves. Re-deriving by scanning `subscribers` was rejected as non-deterministic with
three or more live connections. `PresenceUser` therefore keeps that user's connections in join
order, and the entry moves to the next-oldest survivor on departure.

**The cache interaction.** `user_info` can now change without the user set changing, and the
memoised `subscription_succeeded` frame was invalidated only on a set change. Re-deriving
without matching invalidation gives the worst of both: `users` is correct and the served bytes
are stale. A roster generation is everything the encoded frame depends on, so `reseat_user_info`
takes the cached frame — and only when the value actually differs, so the memoisation stays
exactly as tight as the generation it tracks. This is pinned in both directions: a changed
value must produce a new frame, an unchanged one must keep sharing the old `Arc`.

**Tests** (`src/channel/state.rs`): `roster_reseats_user_info_when_the_oldest_connection_leaves`
(the issue's trigger, plus the cache and `members()` views),
`roster_follows_join_order_across_successive_departures` (three connections, deterministic
ordering), `identical_user_info_survivor_keeps_the_cached_roster_frame` (the memoisation is not
loosened).

**Known limitation, called out in the changelog:** the cluster (Redis) roster has the same
first-writer-wins shape in `presinfo`, and re-deriving there needs `presmembers` to carry
per-token `user_info` rather than just the user id. Out of scope here; only the node-local
roster is re-seated.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo clippy --locked --lib --bins -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --locked` — all clean,
  zero warnings.
- Cluster suites (`redis_cluster`, `percore_cluster_presence`, `cluster_capacity`,
  `cluster_bridge`, `--test-threads=1`): 52 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite with MySQL / Postgres / Mongo / Redis: **828 passed, 0 failed** across 31 binaries.

**Negative controls** — each fix reverted in isolation, its test confirmed failing, then restored:

| reverted | observed failure |
| --- | --- |
| the `cap >= 0` guard in `PRESENCE_JOIN_LUA` | `exactly one of 8 concurrent racers may take the last slot: left: 8, right: 1` |
| the pub/sub edge moved back after the verdict | `Redis never reported >= 1 subscriber(s) on …:msg:app:{presence-deaf} within 5s (last saw 0)` |
| the `reseat_user_info` call | `roster must carry the survivor's info: left: {"name":"Old"}, right: {"name":"New"}` |
| **only** the `roster_frame.take()` inside `reseat_user_info` | same stale `{"name":"Old"}` — served from the memoised frame whil

author: ghostwolf101
body:
Round 7 of the ongoing independent-audit passes. Five confirmed findings:

1. **High** — `.github/workflows/squad-alteration-gate.yml` spliced `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` (fully attacker-controlled — the PR's source branch name) and `github.base_ref` directly into `run:` bash blocks via `${{ }}`. GitHub Actions performs this substitution as a raw text splice into the step script *before* bash ever runs, so the existing double-quoting did not protect against it — a crafted branch name (e.g. containing `"; $(...)`) breaks out of the quotes and executes as a real shell command. Independently reproduced the injection mechanism with a crafted payload. Fixed by routing both values through `env:` and referencing them as `"$HEAD_REF"`/`"$BASE_REF"` in the scripts — the standard, GitHub-recommended mitigation for this exact vulnerability class. Low real-world risk today (single-owner repo, no external collaborators per its own governance doc) but a live landmine for the day a second collaborator gets push access, which the governance doc already anticipates.

   Note: this workflow was adopted from `auernyx-agent-mk2`'s `mk2-alteration-gate.yml` pattern, and mk2's copy has the identical bug (confirmed by diffing the two). Out of scope for this PR (SQUAD-only per this round's audit), but flagged here so it isn't lost — same fix should land there too.

2. **Medium** — The same workflow's `auto-authorize` job treated being merely *assigned* to a PR or *requested* as a reviewer — neither implies any actual involvement from that person — the same as a real approval. Confirmed with a scenario: an outside actor requesting review from the one allowlisted login got `is_allowed=True` with zero involvement from that person. Fixed by dropping assignee/requested-reviewer logins from the authorization chain; only actual approvals and self-authorship by an allowlisted login now count. (Still logged/printed for visibility, just no longer authorizing.)

3. **Medium** — `format_local_resource_line()` labeled a record with no phones/urls at all as `"Local (**verified**): ... — contact info **not yet verified**"` — a self-contradicting line. Reproduced against the real committed Montrose County VSO record (no `verify_before_production` flag, no contact info, only a free-text `source_hints` note the enforced gate doesn't read). Fixed: `"(verified)"` is no longer claimed when there's no contact info to back it up.

4. **Low** — 7 of 9 division CLI tools (`BUSINESS_OPPORTUNITY`, `LEGAL`, `MEDICAL_DISABILITY`, `TOXIC_EXPOSURE`, `TRANSPORTATION`, `VA_BENEFITS`, `WOMEN_VETERANS`) crashed with raw Python tracebacks on malformed JSON or a missing `--file` path — their payload loading had no exception handling. The other 2 division CLIs (`nonprofit_search_cli.py`, `intake_gate_cli.py`) already handled this correctly, proving the fix pattern exists in-repo; applied that same pattern to the remaining 7. Not reachable from production — manual/ops tools only.

5. **Low** — `tools/qa/validate_nonprofit_registry.py` stops *scanning files* once it hits `--max-failures` findings, but always printed the full candidate file count as if it had scanned everything — undercounting the real disclosed backlog. Now reports the actual files-scanned count and flags explicitly when it stopped early. Also logged in `KNOWN_GAPS.md` (not fixed here — separate root cause, doesn't undercount anything, so out of scope for this pass): the invalid-JSON branch's `continue` skips the `--max-failures` check entirely, found incidentally while writing this fix's test.

New tests: `test_alteration_gate_workflow.py`, `test_division_cli_error_handling.py`, `test_qa_registry_scan_count.py`, plus additions to `test_local_resources.py`. Full suite: 347/347 passing.

body:
## The problem

The GitHub Analytics images render as broken alt text. All three are hobby deployments on shared Vercel instances:

| Image | Host | Why it breaks |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Stats | `github-readme-stats.vercel.app` | Shared public instance runs against a GitHub API quota that is routinely exhausted. This card used the heaviest options — `include_all_commits` **and** `count_private`. |
| Top Languages | `github-readme-stats.vercel.app` | Same instance, same quota. |
| Contribution Graph | `github-readme-activity-graph.vercel.app` | Same pattern. |

This is a recurring failure mode, not a transient blip, so pointing at the same URLs again would not fix it.

## The fix

**Removed the GitHub Analytics section entirely.** GitHub already renders a contribution calendar natively on the profile page directly beneath the README, so the activity graph was duplicating something that can't break. The stat cards add little sitting next to six flagship project cards with real test counts.

**Self-hosted the remaining decorative assets**, so nothing outside GitHub can take down the top of the profile:

- `assets/banner.svg` replaces the `capsule-render` header and footer — same gradient and wave treatment, rendered and visually checked.
- `assets/tagline.svg` replaces `readme-typing-svg.demolab.com`, keeping the typing animation with self-contained SMIL that loops indefinitely.

**Dropped the `komarev` profile-view counter** — same fragility class, and a view count is weak signal next to the rest of the page.

## Result

External image dependencies are now just `img.shields.io` and GitHub's own CDN, down from five third-party services.

## Note on the animation

The first version of `tagline.svg` had a real bug: the loop driver animated the root element's `visibility` on `loop.end`, which does not restart child animations — it would have played once and then left blank space. Each element now carries its own `repeatCount="indefinite"` animation keyed across the full 16s cycle. A validator checks every `values`/`keyTimes` pair for equal length and strictly increasing times, which is how the last line's duplicate `1.0000;1` endpoint was caught.

author: tdoublep
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Description

The attention backend kept two dicts of compiled kernels, keyed on the values each factory baked as closure constants. Dynamo already caches compiled code per code object and guards on strictly more than those keys covered, so a dict hit was never a guarantee the call would not recompile — the warmup recorder's "already recorded" check was claiming a guarantee it could not honour.

The kernels are now plain module-level functions taking those values as arguments, compiled once each, with `__init__` picking the compiled or eager one. That drops both dicts, both accessors, both factories, `_maybe_compile` and `SpyreAttnBucket.key`, plus three flags that were redundant with an argument Dynamo already guards on (`store_out` is `out is not None`, `needs_gather` is `query_row_ids is None`, `has_alibi` is `alibi_bias_tiles is not None`).

No behaviour change intended.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/attention/test_spyre_attn_recorder.py tests/runtime/test_spyre_attn_bucketer.py -m "not upstream"` — 59 passed, 5 skipped.
- The recorder tests now count Dynamo's `unique_graphs` instead of dict length, and reset Dynamo per test so an earlier test's graphs cannot mask a recorder that compiled nothing.

author: qeude
body:
## Related issue

Closes #

## What changed

- `no-view` commands declaring `interval` (`90s` / `1m` / `12h` / `1d`, clamped to 1 min) re-run headlessly on schedule with `launchType: Background`.
- `updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle })` implemented (was a no-op): per-command override persisted in `extension-data`, shown in launcher search; `null` clears back to the manifest; a subtitle restating the extension name is dropped since the row already shows it.
- Launcher row: antenna dot while refresh is on (slashed twin when off), orange warning with the error as tooltip on background failure; the ⌘K menu gains Enable / Disable Background Refresh plus Refresh Now.
- Settings › Extensions › command: Background refresh toggle with last refresh + last error.
- Scheduler: a single loop, batched close ticks, deterministic per-command phase, exponential backoff to 24 h, timeout inside the interval, never preempts a running command (a manual run aborts a tick in flight), no toasts / HUDs / alerts from background runs.
- New `ext-refresh-test` harness; `ExtensionRefreshPolicy` holds every pure decision (parsing, due dates, backoff, subtitle fallback, indicator state).
- Tolerant `extension-data` decoding (new `ext-storage-test`): files predating a key keep their data instead of resetting the extension — this also fixes upgrades, where the pre-`metadata` files would otherwise have been wiped on first launch.

## Memory footprint

Verified with `footprint` (Activity Monitor's metric), same protocol on both sides.

| Profile | before (main) | after (PR) |
| ------- | ------------- | ---------- |
| Normal user, extensions off | 30 MB | 30 MB |
| Power user, extensions on + refresh ticking | 30 MB | 32 MB |

Nothing for normal users; ~2 MB transient during a tick, discarded with it.

## Demo

![Background refresh in launcher search](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qeude/tinycast/pr-assets/docs/assets/extension-background-refresh.png)

*Caffeinate Status showing its live `✖ Decaffeinated` subtitle plus the refresh dot. After-state still; no before clip (headless test run).*

## Drawbacks

- `menu-bar` intervals parse but never schedule (menu-bar commands don't run).
- A tick never preempts a running command; it waits for the next due slot.
- Minimum interval clamped to 60 s (Raycast documents 10 s in one place, 1 m in the manifest reference).
- No Extension Diagnostics equivalent; background errors surface in Settings and the row tooltip.

## Tests & validation

- New `Tests/ext-refresh-test.swift` (interval parsing, due dates, backoff, jitter, timeout, subtitle fallback/dedup, indicator state, `LaunchType` raw values); full suite 60/60 green, `lint.sh` clean, Debug build with zero new warnings, `Model/` purity grep empty.
- Live E2E on the Dev channel with the real Coffee extension: the `1m` manifest interval parsed, background ticks rewrote the subtitle (`✔ Caffeinated` / `✖ Decaffeinated`), dot + warning states appear in the launcher row (see Demo). Genericness proven with a synthetic second extension (counter + subtitle advancing across ticks, then removed).

author: firedmosquito831
body:
## What was broken

On a machine with **no Python at all**, `scripts/install.sh` and `scripts/install.ps1` were one implicit download away from failing. They installed `uv` and then ran `uv tool install --python 3.14.0` and hoped: no interpreter was ever provisioned as a step of its own, and nothing stopped uv from binding the tool environment to a **system** Python that happened to match the version.

Four smaller gaps came with it:

| Gap | Before |
|---|---|
| POSIX without `curl` | `curl is required. Install it first, then rerun this installer.` — true, and useless: it never says how. |
| The uv floor | `MIN_UV_VERSION`/`$MinUvVersion` existed but neither script said what it was for or where it came from. |
| Proxies, execution policy, desktop prerequisites | Stated nowhere. |
| `uv` on PATH | `install.sh` called a bare `uv` after installing one — which only worked because it had just pushed `~/.local/bin` onto its own PATH. |

## Mechanism

`uv tool install --python 3.14.0` *selects* an interpreter; it does not guarantee it *provisioned* one. Python discovery walks PATH before it considers uv-managed builds, so on a machine that has an unrelated 3.14 the tool environment silently binds to it, and on a machine that has nothing the install depends on an implicit download the user never sees named. The curl message was the generic `require_command` text, which cannot name a package because it does not know which command failed.

## The fix

- **Python is provisioned, first.** `uv python install --no-bin --no-registry <version>` runs as its own step before the tool environment is built, and `uv tool install --managed-python` forbids a system interpreter. `--no-bin` and `--no-registry` keep it to a self-contained interpreter under `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`: no `python` shim on PATH and, on Windows, no PEP 514 registry entry. Both flags exist at the `0.11.0` floor (checked against `crates/uv-cli/src/lib.rs` at that tag).
- **`require_curl`** replaces `require_command curl`: it picks the install command from the package manager actually present (`apt-get`, `dnf`, `yum`, `zypper`, `pacman`, `apk`, `brew`, `pkg`, generic fallback), prints it, and exits 1. curl is the one thing the script cannot bootstrap, because it is what fetches everything else. On Windows there is no equivalent gap — `Invoke-RestMethod` ships with PowerShell.
- **The uv it installed is run by absolute path.** `install.sh` pins `uv_bin`; `install.ps1` pins `$script:UvPath` and resolves it through `Resolve-UvPath`. Both closing messages now tell the user to open a new terminal if a command is not found.
- **Both headers state the contract**: the uv floor and that it tracks `[tool.uv] required-version`; that `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` are honoured by curl/irm and uv; and which desktop prerequisite each package carries (WebView2 bootstrapped by the Windows Setup `.exe`, `webkit2gtk` in the Linux `.deb` `Depends`, nothing on macOS). `install.ps1` records that the published `irm ... | iex` one-liner runs under the **default execution policy** — policy applies to script *files*, not to text executed in the session — and gives the `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File` form for a saved copy.

Coding agents are still not installed by either script; the existing contract test that greps for every agent package name is unchanged, and a new one asserts the same from the other direction.

## Version: 6.57.0 (MINOR, not PATCH)

Python provisioning is a **capability the installers did not have**. A machine with no Python is now a supported starting point rather than a coincidence. `packaging/npm/package.json` pinned equal; `uv lock --offline`.

## Verification

Fresh-machine simulations in scratch profiles on both platforms — `UV_TOOL_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`, `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, `APPDATA`, `LOCALAPPDATA`, `XDG_*` all scratch, and a child PATH carrying a symlink to every command **except** `uv` and every `python` (dropping whole directories would take `curl` and coreutils with them, which is not what a fresh machine looks like):

**Windows**, via the published scriptblock form under PowerShell 5.1 launched with `PSModulePath` cleared:

```
where uv      -> [Could not find files for the given pattern(s).]
where python  -> [Could not find files for the given pattern(s).]
where python3 -> [Could not find files for the given pattern(s).]
confirmed: no uv, no python on this PATH
==> Ensuring uv 0.11.0 or newer is installed
uv is not installed; installing the current standalone uv.
Verified uv 0.12.10.
==> Installing Python 3.14.0 through uv
+ C:\tmp\mcc-pr1-sim\home\.local\bin\uv.exe python install --no-bin --no-registry 3.14.0
Downloading cpython-3.14.0-windows-x86_64-none (download) (21.2MiB)
Installed Python 3.14.0 in 2.46s
Installed 41 executables: fcc-anthropic-oauth-login, ... my-claude-code
+ C:\tmp\mcc-pr1-sim\uv-tool-bin\mcc-server.exe --version
My Claude Code 6.56.0 is installed and verified.
```

**Linux**, in WSL, same shape: `cpython-3.14.0-linux-x86_64-gnu` in the scratch python dir, 41 commands in the scratch tool bin, `my-claude-code 6.56.0`. And the gap it cannot fill, with a PATH holding only `apt-get`:

```
==> Checking installation prerequisites
error: curl is required and was not found.

curl is the one thing this installer cannot install for you -- it is what
downloads uv, Python and the My Claude Code release wheel.

Install it with:
  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y curl

Then run this installer again.
exit=1
```

**CI**: a new `install-smoke.yml` job repeats the Linux half on a bare `ubuntu-latest` runner on every push/PR that touches `install.sh`, and asserts the interpreter came from uv, that no `python3` appeared on PATH, that `mcc-server --version` answers, that the real home was never written to, and that the missing-curl path exits 1 with the `apt-get` command named.

**Machine diffs empty on both sides**: HKCU `Run`, `HKCU\Software\Python`, the Start Menu, the real `~/.local/bin`, `~/.fcc` mtimes and the WSL home are unchanged, and `~/.mcc` does not exist on either.

Static contract tests in `tests/scripts/test_installers.py` cover every new line of script text (they run on all platforms; the PowerShell runtime cases skip off Windows), plus two new runtime cases on the POSIX harness for the ordering and for the failure path when the Python download fails.

`uv run ruff format` / `ruff check` / `ty check` all clean. `pytest -q --ignore=tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py`: **10215 passed, 59 skipped**.

## Residual risks

- The smoke job installs the latest **published** release, so it proves the script and not this branch's wheel. A release that has not happened yet cannot break it; a broken wheel shows up in `wheel-e2e` instead.
- The per-distro curl hints for `zypper`/`pacman`/`apk`/`pkg` are asserted statically; only `apt-get` is exercised end to end.
- `--managed-python` and `--no-registry` were read out of uv `0.11.0`'s CLI source rather than run against a `0.11.0` binary. The simulations ran against `0.12.10`, which the script installs when nothing is present.
- `HTTPS_PROXY` is documented as honoured by curl/irm/uv rather than tested — there is no proxy in this environment to test against.

## Not done (other PRs)

Everything else in the README install spec — the section reorder, the shortened README, the npm/npx runtime detection, the capabilities tables — is out of scope. The only README change here is the three lines in the install section that had become untrue, plus the prerequisites paragraph they imply.

author: jeffsteinbok
body:
Implements #13.

| Tier | Gets |
| --- | --- |
| Free | Connect a real mailbox. Every rule in plain language. Diagnostics, including the rules that quietly stopped working. |
| Pro — one-time $2.99 | Edit, create, delete, reorder, enable/disable. |

### The gate is one list

Every path that mutates the mailbox calls `requirePro()` in
`RulesListViewModel`, so the set of paid actions is that file's guard
statements and nothing else. When it refuses, it raises the paywall and returns
false; callers just return.

Opening the editor is gated at the entry points rather than at Save — filling
in a whole rule and only then being told you can't have it is the trick this
app shouldn't play. Reorder asks on the way in for the same reason, instead of
after a drag.

### Entitlement

Read from `Transaction.currentEntitlements`, not a cached flag, so it survives
a launch with no network — a paid user on a plane must not find the app locked.
`Transaction.updates` is observed so an Ask-to-Buy approval unlocks without a
relaunch. Restore is present because 3.1.1 requires it and its absence is the
most common IAP rejection.

### Testing

`App/Rulebook.storekit` drives the whole purchase flow locally with no App
Store Connect round trip — select it in the scheme's StoreKit configuration.

`-demo` runs unlocked (that's how the App Store screenshots are taken);
`-demo -locked` runs the same seed with the entitlement enforced, which is how
the gate gets exercised without buying anything.

### Not done here

- The IAP product in App Store Connect (`net.steinbok.Rulebook.pro`)
- Listing copy still describes a $2.99 paid app — #14
- Disabled controls don't yet carry a Pro badge; right now the paywall is the
  first signal that an action is paid

author: khorezmshakh12
body:
## What

Hardens every entrance animation from the motion pass (#21, #25) so **content is never left invisible by a stalled animation**. This is the fix for the production login outage (password field + submit button rendered at `opacity: 0` and never animated in).

## Rule

An entrance animation may never gate the visibility of real UI. If framer's engine doesn't run to completion, the element must still be visible.

## Changes (18 files, −17 net)

| File(s) | Fix |
|---|---|
| `page-transition.tsx` | whole-app wrapper: `initial={{opacity:0}}` → **`initial={false}`**. A client navigation can no longer strand a page blank. Only `exit` still fades. |
| `auth-card.tsx`, notification badge, sidebar "new" dots, theme-selector check, chat recording indicator | `<motion.*>` → plain element + CSS `animate-*` class (runs even if JS stalls; existing `prefers-reduced-motion` media query already disables it) |
| `market-view` tabs & grid, `income-kpi-strip` cards, `mission-card`, `goal-card`, `news-list`, `milestone-rail`, `salary-note-form`, `telegram-connect-section`, `staff-message-item`, `message-bubble` | `initial={{opacity:0,…}}` → `initial={false}` |
| `course-lessons-table.tsx` | non-collapsible table now renders in a plain `<div>` (was inside `AnimatePresence` + `accordion` height animation that could hide it); collapsible mode keeps the accordion, gated on the real toggle |
| `motion.ts` `staggerContainer` | `initial: {}` → `initial: { opacity: 1 }`, `opacity: 1` in `animate` — a stagger container always resolves to visible |

No behaviour change beyond removing fragile hidden resting states. No new deps. Guarded dirs untouched.

## Verify

`npm run verify` (`tsc --noEmit && eslint && next build`) — **green**.

Not visually verified on authenticated routes (no test login available). The changes are conservative *removals* of fragile animation state, so the failure mode is "less animation than intended," not breakage.

## Deploy note

Production is currently pinned to the pre-motion Cloud Run revision `persons-staff-app-00095-jx4`. Merging this triggers a Cloud Build deploy that creates a new revision and routes 100% traffic to it (`cloudbuild.yaml` has no `--no-traffic`), which lifts the pin automatically. Verify the live site right after; re-pin to 00095 if anything is wrong.

author: clhodapp
body:
Publication prep for ch-zsh-config, ahead of flipping it public.

## Diligence

The history is six commits, all from the 2026-09-04 re-creation. A
diff scan of every commit for secrets, tokens, LAN addresses, session
links, personal or work references, and private repositories found only
the workflow token references and the copyright line. The one file ever
removed was the ghostel shell helper (an MIT shell function). Inputs are
caisson and nixpkgs; the test flake's are all public. `LICENSE` is MIT
with SPDX headers throughout, and GitHub detects it.

## Changes

- **README.** It still described `enableGhostelIntegration`, which #1
  removed. That paragraph now lists the options the module actually
  has. A CI paragraph and a "Binary cache" section (the three
  substituters and keys a consumer needs) are added, as in
  clhodapp/ch-emacs-config and clhodapp/merman.
- **CI.** The single generic `check.yml` becomes the three-file set the
  other public repos run: `check.yml` (main's copy: cached store, the
  two-hop trusted build for pull requests, the priority-pruned union
  entry, push to the `clhodapp` cachix cache from the `cachix`
  environment), `check-pr.yml` (the request's own copy, builds only when
  `.github/` changed), and `cache-cleanup.yml`. Timeouts are 30 minutes;
  the check is an evaluation plus a `zsh -n`.
- **Roots loop.** This flake exports `checks` but its `packages` output
  is empty, so the loop that roots every check and package now skips an
  output the flake does not provide (matching Nix's "does not provide
  attribute" error) and still fails on any other evaluation error. The
  same change belongs in the other two copies for uniformity; this is
  the first repo where it matters.

actionlint passes on all three workflows; `nix flake check` passes
locally; `nix fmt` is clean. Because this changes `.github/`,
`check-pr` builds it, and the first `main` run after merge is the first
push to the cache.

author: emodv
body:
## Why
PR #2 improved scoring credibility but merged with no automated checks. A diagnostic product should not ship scanner changes without verifying that the TypeScript project still compiles and the production bundle still builds.

## Change
- Add GitHub Actions CI on every pull request and push to `main`.
- Use Node 22 and deterministic `npm ci` installs.
- Run the existing TypeScript lint/typecheck command.
- Run the production build.
- Add read-only permissions, concurrency cancellation, and a 10-minute timeout.

## Expected impact
Turns build/type safety from a manual assumption into a repeatable release gate and reduces regression risk before traffic acquisition begins.

## Verification
The workflow itself should execute on this pull request. Merge only after the GitHub Actions run succeeds.

Prevents today's outage class from recurring, and finishes the migration left half-applied.

## Why

The Dockerfile started `uvicorn` alone, on the documented reasoning that `create_all()` builds the schema at startup so migrations were optional. **That reasoning is wrong.** `create_all` creates missing *tables* but never ALTERs an existing one, so a migration that adds a *column* is silently never applied.

The founder dashboard 500'd on every lead query for ~50 minutes today:

```
psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column leads.client_since does not exist
```

while `alembic upgrade head` simultaneously refused to run, because `create_all` had already made the tables it wanted to create:

```
psycopg2.errors.DuplicateTable: relation "org_services" already exists
```

**No deploy in this service's history had ever applied a migration.** Shipping schema-dependent code with no schema step is the real bug; today's commit just exposed it.

## The change

```dockerfile
CMD ["sh", "-c", "alembic upgrade head && uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8000}"]
```

- **`&&` is deliberate.** A failed migration aborts the boot, which on Render fails the *deploy* rather than taking the site down — the previous version keeps serving until it's fixed. Fail-fast is the safe direction.
- **Safe on every boot.** Each migration is guarded by an inspector check (`af892ea`), so re-running against an up-to-date or `create_all`-drifted database is a no-op.
- `HEALTHCHECK` start-period 20s → 60s to cover the step.

## Also fixes the half-applied state

Production is currently stamped at `z9s0t1u2v3w4`, applied out-of-band to stop the bleeding. Booting with this change applies the remaining `aa0t1u2v3w4x` and `bb1u2v3w4x5y` and returns `alembic_version` to head.

## Caveat

Assumes a single instance (Render `numInstances=1`). If this is ever scaled out, the migration must move to a release/pre-deploy step so two containers can't race the same revision. Noted in the Dockerfile.

author: deea222
body:
Independent of the #77-#83 stack; branches off `main` and touches none of its files.

Importing `emuToPx` off `./core` - one multiplication - cost a consumer **817 bytes** minified. At v0.2.0, before the refactoring, it cost **182**.

`src/ooxml/image.ts` had picked up three module-level reads of the shared namespace table where it used to hold URI literals:

```ts
const PICTURE_URI = NAMESPACES.pic;
const WP_NS = NAMESPACES.wp;
const A_NS = NAMESPACES.a;
```

A property access at the top level is a possible side effect, so a bundler keeps it, which keeps `NAMESPACES`, which keeps `ooxml/names.js`, which imports `R_NS` and `W_NS` and so keeps `ooxml/xml.js`. None of it is reachable from `emuToPx`. Reading the table where the values are actually written takes the leaf back to **182 bytes** and leaves `image.js` as the only module a consumer keeps. No URI literal came back into the file; `ooxml/names.ts` is still the one place they are written.

Six other names were paying the same toll: `pxToEmu` 829 to 194, `toImageExtent` 1055 to 420, and off `./commands` `IMAGE_FILE_ACCEPT` 842 to 207, `imageFilesIn` 956 to 321, `fittedExtent` 2788 to 2148, `readImageFile` 4530 to 4033.

## The guard, which is the point of the PR

`leafImportSize.test.ts`'s 2048-byte budget did not catch this, and could not have: it was set against a bundling collapse that cost 22 kB, so a 4.5x growth sat comfortably inside it. A byte budget is the wrong instrument for a module that should not be there at all.

The test now asks esbuild for a metafile and asserts the **module graph**: `emuToPx` off `./core` keeps `dist/ooxml/image.js` and nothing else, `downloadDocx` off `.` keeps its two. Putting the three constants back fails that assertion and names the two modules that arrived, while the byte budget still passes at 817. I reproduced both directions.

The `emuToPx` budget also comes down from 2048 to 1024, which is the ratio the `downloadDocx` row already used. The budget's remaining job is weight taken on inside `image.js` itself; the graph assertion is what guards this class.

## Verification

`pnpm check` 137 files / 5,657 tests, `pnpm test:package` 40. The corpus is untouched - this changes where a string is read, not what is written, and no fixture or snapshot moved.

I measured the leaf myself before and after, and confirmed the module list both ways.

## Sweep

Every other module-level read of an imported object was checked against what it actually pins. Three in `docx/comments/*` were left alone: nothing reaches them except `importDocx`, `exportDocx` and `onlyCommentsChangedBy`, which are 84-113 kB and call into `names.ts` themselves. `linkCommands.ts`'s `docxSchema.marks.link` is droppable whole under the package's `sideEffects` field.

author: thirtysixthspan
body:
# The tab-close path walks the dispose registry

## What

`closeTabResources` released each of a tab's resources by calling a different manager by hand in a fixed sixteen-line sequence. It now walks `MANAGER_DISPOSE_ORDER` calling each manager's own `closeTab(label)` where defined, with the order-sensitive exceptions stated explicitly around the walk (the deferred workspace release, the conditional remote release, `deleteBusy`, `forgetPersisted` before `deleteAgentState`, the last-tab database close, and the `tab:removed` emit). Six managers gain a thin `closeTab` delegation; the plan's per-manager releases already existed on the other five.

## Why

A new per-tab resource was a line someone had to remember in a hand-maintained checklist — the shape the lifecycle principle retires — and the close-release signature carried test-era scaffolding (a map-or-number union, an optional queue map, a legacy tab-count parameter) that no production caller ever passed. The registry walk makes "a natural closeTab method defines it" the guarantee, asserted in a test instead of promised by review.

author: alexroessner
body:
Closes the root cause behind #112.

## The problem

CI recalculates workbooks **in the runner** and discards the result. `final-public-evidence-release.yml` recalculates twelve committed instances and rejects `total_errors != 0`; `flagship-validation.yml` recalculates `.flagship-build/*.xlsx`, which are freshly built. In both cases the recalculated bytes are thrown away, so the file a reader downloads is whatever the builder wrote — and openpyxl does not evaluate formulas.

**Thirty of the fifty-four committed public-case workbooks stored no results at all**, including six of the twelve in the final-public evidence release set. It is a regression, not a standing condition: `02_Corporate_Finance/instances/public_microsoft_2024.xlsx` was `198/198` at `c87c705` and `0/198` at `f5c0219`.

## Why it is not cosmetic

`tools/weekly_refresh_check.py` is the repository's only scanner for *cached* formula errors. It loads `data_only=True`. When no formula carries a stored result there is nothing for it to look at, so it reports the workbook clean.

I did not want to assert that from reading the code, so I ran the repo's own tool against a planted control:

| file | formulas | cached | `IS!F5` | `weekly_refresh_check.py` |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| A: `public_microsoft_linkedin_2016.xlsx`, unmodified | 194 | 194 | `=E5*(1+Assumptions!C5)` | clean |
| B: **A** with `IS!F5` set to `=1/0`, really recalculated | 194 | 194 | `=1/0` | **71 CELL ERROR(S)** |
| C: **B** round-tripped through openpyxl | 194 | **0** | `=1/0` | clean |

B and C carry byte-identical formulas and the same defect. The scanner finds 71 errors in one and reports the other clean. So the negative it produced on those thirty files was evidence of nothing.

Three checks I expected to share the problem do **not**, and I want to be explicit rather than leave it implied: `validate_model_inventory.py`, `validate_reconciled_models.py` and `workbook_engineering.py` all load `data_only=False`, but each is deliberately scoped to *literal* typed-in error strings and is named for exactly that (`literal_errors`, `literal_excel_error`). They are correct as written and unaffected.

## What this adds

`tools/verify_recalc_persistence.py` — a **presence** check that fails closed. It reports four outcomes separately rather than one boolean, because they are four different facts and only one is a defect:

```
ok            formulas present, results stored
empty_cache   formulas present, NO results stored          <- the failure
no_formulas   nothing to evaluate; states so rather than passing quietly
unreadable    the file could not be opened at all
```

`no_formulas` exists so that "no errors in a workbook with nothing to evaluate" can never render as the same green tick as "no errors in 198 evaluated cells". A partial cache is reported with its ratio and treated as ok — a formula can legitimately evaluate to blank, so a missing individual result is not evidence; a file where *nothing at all* evaluated is a different claim, and it is the one worth gating.

The workflow is deliberately **not path-filtered**. #112's regression arrived through a case rebuild, not through an edit to any file a filter would have named, and a gate that only fires on the files someone thought of is a gate that stops firing.

## The fix to the corpus

All thirty workbooks recalculated in place — every one `status: success`, `total_errors: 0` — with their receipts, the case ledger, the dataset catalogue and the WTI storyline's pinned workbook hash refreshed to match.

One note from doing that: `docs/storyline/public_wti_april_2020/provenance.json` pins `linked_public_case.workbook_sha256`, and **nothing updates it when the workbook changes**. `build_wti_storyline.py --check` — the command the published artifact's own footer tells a reader to run — verifies the series and cards hashes and that the HTML matches the render, but not that the pinned workbook hash is still the workbook's. Only `tests/test_wti_storyline.py` caught it. Same shape as the ledger/snapshot link #104 wired up; I have left it alone here rather than widen this PR, but it is worth owning.

## Verification

Run on macOS with real LibreOffice 26.2.5.2 and Python 3.12, then re-run **against the committed ref in a detached worktree** rather than my working tree:

- **530 tests pass** (522 existing + 8 new) at `4fbfa03` in an isolated worktree
- New gate: **54/54 ok, 0 empty_cache**, 13,940 of 13,952 formula cells carrying a result
- Green: receipts `--check`, model inventory, public-case status, forecast registry (11 forecasts, 0 overdue), builder parity 27/27, workbook engineering, final public evidence `--validate --require-instances`, standards conformance `--run-checks`, storyline `--check`

**The gate was mutation-tested rather than assumed.** A gate that cannot fail is theatre, so:

| mutation | applied at | result |
|---|---|---|
| `elif cached == 0:` → `elif False:` (fail-open) | line 105, printed back | **2 tests red** |
| `return sorted(paths)` → `return []` (empty enumeration) | line 74, printed back | **1 test red** |

Both were applied by line number and restored byte-identically (`diff -q` clean, zero markers remaining, suite green after each). The test file also carries a control asserting the positive fixture genuinely stores results, so the suite cannot pass vacuously if the corpus ever regresses again.

## Files

`tools/verify_recalc_persistence.py` (new), `tests/test_recalc_persistence.py` (new), `.github/workflows/recalc-persistence.yml` (new), `standards/public_cases/index.json`, `standards/metadata/catalog.jsonld`, the two `docs/storyline/public_wti_april_2020/` files, and 30 `.xlsx` + 30 `.receipt.json` pairs.

Flagging the list because the thirty workbooks are the collision surface — if you have anything in flight that rebuilds a public case, this will conflict with it and I would rather land after you than over you.

author: teknium1
body:
Explicit deny rules now follow executable paths through supported shell prefixes instead of matching only the beginning of the complete command.

- Extend the existing quote-aware detection owner to project each executable command and its basename; keep literal-path candidates, whole-input globs, and argument paths.
- Recognize launcher option operands, assignments, leading redirections, compound commands, ordinary conditional/loop transitions, shell `-c` payloads, and literal `env -S` payloads. Query-only `command -v`/`-V` operands stay data.
- Keep parsing on the original quote state. Normalize inter-word whitespace without collapsing quoted argument whitespace; apply existing text normalization only after executable positions are known.
- Keep the deny-before-yolo/mode-off ordering and empty-list behavior. Document supported normalization, all-backend enforcement, and the distinction between a command policy and an OS capability sandbox.

Root cause: full-string `fnmatchcase` cannot use the detector's command-position markers as independent executable candidates, and those candidates previously retained paths and launcher prefixes.

## Validation

**Live repro:** current-main baseline `869228cab4a8276d3b4c78da9d9939670c47bd0f` misses `/usr/bin/sudo`, `env sudo`, and a shell payload containing the absolute path. The fix blocks them with `user_deny` before approval-mode bypasses.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Two retained invariant tests | 2 failed on baseline | 2 passed |
| Real registry → terminal → local backend dispatch, five executable path/prefix forms | 0/5 blocked; inert fixture executed 5/5 | 5/5 blocked before execution |
| Quoted-prose dispatch control | Passed | Passed |
| Focused approval, deny, hardline, mode-parity and override files | — | 413 passed across 5 files |
| Ruff, Windows-footgun scan, compat-pointer scan, subprocess-stdin scan, diff check | — | Passed |

The reproducible dispatch harness is `evals/approval_deny_dispatch.py`. It creates a disposable `HERMES_HOME`, clears inherited credentials, and uses an owned inert executable named `sudo`; its PATH also routes the terminal's NOPASSWD probe to that fixture. No privileged payload is executed. Broad suites and independent review are left to CI/review, not claimed as locally verified.

## Review-blocker validation

Review baseline: `aa0263b971bde25ef812ea6f5cab1bcddbef9271`. The same two invariant tests were expanded, not supplemented with additional tests: **2 RED**, then **34/34 green** for their complete file.

- Reuse the shared comment-aware scanner in execution-flag segmentation, so commented-out shell payloads are not recursively promoted.
- Split literal `env -S` strings into argv, append the unconsumed argv, and quote each argument before reusing command-position detection. Do not independently promote the trailing argv to an executable.

**Live repro:** real registry → terminal → local backend, fresh credential-free process and temporary HOME/HERMES_HOME; GNU coreutils 9.7 `env`, owned inert sudo fixture, approval mode off.

| Review case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `env -S 'printf %s; sudo -n id'` | Incorrectly blocked | Executes printf only; output `sudo;-n;id;` |
| `env -S printf SAFE` / `env -S git status` | Not denied; reached execution | Both blocked by their exact deny rules |
| `echo ok # ; bash -c '<owned sudo> -n id'` | Incorrectly blocked | Output `ok`, exit 0 |
| `env -S 'printf %s' 'sudo -n id'` | Incorrectly promoted trailing data | Prints literal argument, exit 0 |
| Actual shell `-c`, including under `env -S`, and execution after comment newline | Blocked | Remain blocked |
| Quoted prose and `env -S printf BENIGN` | Allowed | Remain allowed |

Expanded live harness: **14 cases verified: 9 denied executions, 5 successful benign controls**. No privileged binaries or model/API calls. Broader focused validation: **586 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed across 12 files**, including execution-flag segmentation, hardline, approval mode/outcome parity and CLI approval tests. Ruff, Windows-footgun, compat-pointer, subprocess-stdin and diff checks passed.

Host qualification: the first focused run had one real-binary fixture failure because the host default `sort` is uutils 0.8.0 and does not exercise GNU `--compress-program` semantics. Re-running all 12 files with an owned PATH symlink to `/usr/bin/gnusort` 9.7 passed; no test or production predicate was patched or skipped to obtain that result. The existing `ag` binary test is skipped because that binary is absent. Full-suite and CI status are not claimed here.

## GNU env late-review repair

Addressed @andrexibiza's [20:54 review](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/105330#pullrequestreview-5135190765), reproduced against `e5c719038a0cbe5ecc53859b6e5591404607ed32`.

- Keep parsing in `approval_detection`: GNU literal split-string escaping is not `shlex` escaping. Unquoted `\_` separates argv; double-quoted `\_` stays a space; `\c` and word-initial comments terminate the split string. Single-quote and escaped-data semantics are retained.
- Skip `env -a` / `--argv0` operands without promoting the marker to an executable. Preserve separate and attached forms.
- Expand the same two invariant tests and the production-dispatch eval; `--verify` now asserts actual deny errors or exact benign output.

**Live repro:** GNU coreutils 9.7, registry → terminal → local backend, disposable credential-free HOME/HERMES_HOME, approval mode off. `env -S 'printf\_SAFE'`, `env -a marker printf SAFE`, and `env --argv0 marker printf SAFE` previously executed and printed `SAFE`; now their exact deny rule blocks before execution. Across 13 newly covered denied spellings, baseline allowed 10 and blocked 3; the fix blocks all 13. The two argv0-data false positives now print `BENIGN` successfully.

Validation repeated after clean rebase onto `4810074d73d9419dc82545202d595507a73f4f0e`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Two expanded invariants | 2 RED on review baseline; complete file 34 passed |
| Real dispatch, old and new cases | 33 verified: 22 denied executions, 11 successful benign controls |
| Approval/deny/execution-flag/hardline focused files under shared serial test lock | 597 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed across 13 files |
| Native GNU grammar differential | 600 deterministic payloads, 394 valid GNU argv results, zero mismatches (including invalid grammar rejection) |
| Ruff, Windows-footgun, compat-pointer, subprocess-stdin, diff checks | Passed |

The focused test run uses the previously qualified GNU `sort` PATH fixture; `ag` remains absent. Independent read-only review found no blockers and separately differential-probed the literal grammar. No full-directory/full-suite or new-head hosted-CI claim is made here.

Scope stays **literal executable-and-argument split strings**. Native probes confirm `${NAME}` expands in GNU env; this projection intentionally does not evaluate it because a remote backend's environment is not the approval process's environment. Escaped and single-quoted variable text remains literal. Dynamic expansion, clustered launcher options, and options inside the split string are explicitly unmodeled in the threat-model documentation; this is command-policy normalization, not a capability sandbox.

## Scope and contributor credit

Related to #104308; source report by @neosun100. Adapted command-position, bounded-segment and launcher-option work from @embwl0x in #76063 (earlier #76037 by @proofoftom), plus executable-basename normalization from @RohithPariki in #104338. Both implementation contributors are retained in commit co-author metadata.

Read the full #104338 diff/review thread first and swept #76063, #78521 and #86711 plus fresh path/wrapper/deny duplicates. This is a slim current-owner adaptation, not a wholesale cherry-pick of the old monolithic parser. #78521's git-global-option semantics and #76063's broader case-pattern parser are not included; #86711's blanket white

author: aghermida
body:
## Summary
- The nextcloud-addon service had no authentication at all. `manifest.json`/`catalog`/`meta`/`stream` accept a base64-encoded WebDAV config as a URL path segment with no validation against a known/allowed Nextcloud instance — anyone who found the subdomain could supply an arbitrary WebDAV url+credentials and have the server connect to it, effectively an open relay and SSRF vector into the host's local/Docker network.
- Adds a required `NEXTCLOUD_ADDON_ACCESS_KEY` env var and a `requireAccessKey` middleware (constant-time comparison) gating every route behind a shared secret path segment (`/:accessKey/...`), including the setup page. A missing/wrong key returns 404.
- `/media` (the file-streaming proxy) is intentionally left out of this gate — it already requires its own HMAC token that can't be forged without `NEXTCLOUD_ADDON_SECRET`.
- Updated the setup page to derive the access key from the current URL path when generating the manifest URL, and updated the README's env var table and route list.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm -F nextcloud-addon exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`
- [x] Built and ran locally, confirmed: no key / wrong key -> 404 on `/manifest.json` and `/`; correct key -> 200 on both
- [ ] Deploy to VPS with a new `NEXTCLOUD_ADDON_ACCESS_KEY`, reinstall the addon in Stremio using the new setup-page URL

Sul suo «CORRETTO procedi» ho misurato la popolazione **prima** di scrivere la cura, e il numero su cui la voce poggiava non regge.

| età | 0 | 1 | 2–11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 | 17 | 18 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

author: unxmaal
body:
Bundled per the review-bottleneck note. Three issues, each with its own commit.

Closes #27
Closes #6
Closes #29

## #27 — a broken stage must refuse early, and stop refusing when fixed
`upscale-seedvr2` crashes inside mflux, and the crash is in **stage two**, so discovering it cost a full diffusion run per case.

The version pin is the design. A flat "broken" flag would still be refusing a year after mflux ships the fix and nobody would find out, because the guard removes the evidence. It refuses the versions it was measured broken against (mflux 0.19.1 / mlx 0.32.2) and lets a newer stack through. A test fails if the installed versions drift off the pin while the issue is open.

Three `lh discover` defects fell out of this, all the same shape — the tool describing the repo as it was months ago:
- all nineteen workflow primitives reported "no runner yet", months after three got one
- `methods()` hardcoded two entries and cited #18 as why it was short; #18 is closed
- BROKEN was not a state, so `upscale-seedvr2` printed as `measured` — it *has* been measured, 0/3, precisely because it crashes

## #6 — the server was disabling the model's own repetition penalty
mlx_audio's `SpeechRequest` defaults `repetition_penalty` to 1.0 and forwards every non-None field. Chatterbox's own `generate()` defaults it to **1.2**. Going through the HTTP server silently disables the penalty the model ships with: sending nothing is not the same as letting the model decide.

Five cases at `lang_code="fr"`: three ran to **exactly 48.00 seconds**. An identical duration across three different sentences is a token budget being exhausted, not sentences ending. At `repetition_penalty=1.2` the same three came back at 9.92s, 5.40s, 4.28s.

**Scope, stated plainly: it does not reproduce on `lang_code="en"`.** Short, medium and long English through the accent voice all returned 0.25–0.36 s/word with and without the penalty. English is the path that matters here and English was never broken. This guards a failure that was observed, it does not fix one that is currently biting.

## #29 — the obvious fix broke rendering
Adding `--user-data-dir` made chrome write the screenshot and then hang forever, so every render cost the full 60s timeout. The tell was rc=124 *with the PNG present*.

Ruled out, all still hang: `--no-first-run`, `--no-default-browser-check`, `--disable-extensions`, `--no-sandbox`, `--disable-search-engine-choice-screen`, `--headless=old`, pre-creating the directory, a profile under `$HOME`. It is the flag itself. So we poll for the screenshot and terminate.

Second trap, found by a test that should have taken 0.3s and took 30: stderr must not be a PIPE read after terminating — chrome's grandchildren inherit the write end and hold it open.

Render is **2.2s, down from a 60s timeout**.

## Two things you should push back on if you disagree

**The five `fr-*` tts cases are now out of scope** given "we do not do work on any french language voices or models". I did not delete them: removing cases changes the corpus, and `comparable()` will then refuse to rank any future tts run against every past one. Your call whether that trade is worth it.

**#24 is labelled `priority:high` but its remaining half is the 19-min/image runs** you said were wasted effort. I did its tooling half here and left the measurement. Worth relabelling `studio`.

802 passed, `make check` clean. Guard red-proofed: removing it fails exactly the new test.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_013Bd2AfEGE3uauSXqRf1V8w

author: mvillmow
body:
The automation loop accepts `--log-file` but does not use it. This change sends loop records to the exact file path and removes console handlers after the file opens. It preserves other file handlers and per-agent evidence paths.

The loop now applies text or JSON output and gives quiet mode priority over verbose mode. An unavailable file stops the command before agent dispatch and gives the path, operating-system reason, and a direction to check the parent directory and permissions.

Validation: 328 focused tests passed. Whole-repository typing, lint, formatting, and all pre-commit hooks passed. The required pre-push suite passed 10,026 tests with 15 skipped and 7 deselected; coverage was 84.53%. An earlier parallel unit run had two timing failures in unchanged NATS and writer-claim tests. Both tests passed in the serial pre-push suite. Independent review found no required changes and passed 258 tests from the exact commit. Regression evidence is in `build/` in the repair worktree.

Closes #3025

author: cyanxxy
body:
This release makes the CLI and MCP output contracts consistent for agent consumers. `extract --jsonl` now emits protocol v2 lifecycle events, warnings reach machine results, agentic output has a published typed schema, and MCP exposes capabilities and request bounds. These breaking changes require version 4.0.0.

The runtime now stops cancelled work before provider calls, joins failed worker pools before releasing output locks, and fails closed on non-Error agent rejections. MCP discovery caching, progress, and artifact annotations are corrected. Dependency security patches restore the CI audit, and installed-package MCP coverage is included in packaging and release checks.

Upstream 3.0.1 engine restructuring, retry policy, partial-result guidance, and packaging fixes are preserved. Release metadata and notes are aligned to 4.0.0.

Validation: 698 tests across 51 files; coverage gate; typecheck; lint (zero errors); zero-vulnerability dependency audit; actionlint; installed CLI/MCP tarball and GitHub Action smoke checks; 64 eval fixtures and canary matrix dry run; release version and notes checks. Live provider calls were not made; container validation runs in GitHub Actions.

author: sidneysantossp
stephanmeijer
body:
Fixes data-loss and stale-search behavior in WebDAV writes while preserving 5 GiB uploads and indexing all large-note content with bounded buffers.

- Stage uploads in private temporary files after 16 MiB, enforce the 5 GiB limit against received bytes, and stream retryable file uploads to S3. `NOTEDTHAT_UPLOAD_TMP_DIR` is validated at startup and shared with indexing; Compose supplies a disk-backed volume owned by the runtime user.
- Reject decoded self-COPY/MOVE and malformed Overwrite headers. Use native S3 copy with source ETag and destination create-only preconditions; MOVE protects source deletion and reports partial completion explicitly.
- Index an ETag-conditioned snapshot while hashing and validating UTF-8. Replay bounded Markdown chunks with exact raw byte ranges, process one embedding/upsert batch at a time, and remove obsolete chunk indexes only after all batches succeed. Empty and non-indexable replacements remove previous points.
- Reuse each capped Depth: 1 PROPFIND listing within its request, skip enumeration for Depth: 0, and reject infinity even with X-Litmus.

### Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test --workspace --locked`: 983 passed, 0 failed; 132 ignored by default.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- Real SeaweedFS 4.18: 19 existing S3 tests, 21 WebDAV tests, and the added direct native-copy precondition regression passed.
- Real Qdrant 1.15.4: 13 worker and 10 searcher/OKF tests passed, including failed-batch repair and obsolete-chunk cleanup without a `chunk_index` payload index.
- An S3 retry test replayed the identical 16 MiB + 1 body after a failed first attempt.
- Live server with a deterministic local embedder: streamed 17,825,792 bytes, verified beginning/middle/end searches, exact range dereferences, COPY/MOVE and rewrite cleanup. Embedding batches never exceeded 32.
- Direct-process 5 GiB disk staging and chunk replay: 5,368,709,120 bytes, 1,789,570 chunks, matching full-file SHA-256, maximum 3,000-byte chunks / 12,000-byte reads, 24,672 KiB peak RSS. Replay read exactly twice the input size. Separate WebDAV tests accepted exactly 5 GiB without Content-Length and rejected an observed extra byte with 413 and no destination write. Cleanup was checked on success, errors, and cancellation.

### Operational notes

Provision disk space for each concurrent staged upload plus index snapshots. A tmpfs staging directory consumes RAM. Normal completion, failure, and cancellation remove private files; forced process termination can leave files for operator cleanup.

Chunk boundaries can change on the next write/reindex; payload meanings and collection names remain unchanged. Ordinary merged OKF metadata behavior is preserved; frontmatter recognition is bounded to 16 MiB, with larger/unclosed frontmatter indexed as raw Markdown so its content remains searchable. Indexing retains the existing asynchronous best-effort model: completed batches can be visible before a later batch fails, and final cleanup waits for a successful run.

Closes #60
Closes #61
Closes #62
Closes #65
Closes #66

Five independent review lanes (goal, code quality, security, context, and QA) passed on `dc823e5f15b5ae293815962a06277a519f0e5f9e`. A separate live runtime audit rebuilt that exact commit and passed the 17 MiB search/range, COPY/MOVE, and rewrite-cleanup scenarios; server peak RSS was 89,600,000 bytes, and temporary files/processes/containers were cleaned up. PR #58 is merged; PR #59 is closed unmerged, and its unrelated changes were not imported.

GitHub CI passed on the reviewed commit: formatting, workspace tests, Clippy, and Docker build. Conditional SeaweedFS and release/publish jobs were skipped by the PR workflow; the affected SeaweedFS suites were run locally as recorded above. [CI run](https://github.com/NotedThat/NotedThat/actions/runs/34158269169).


Commit metadata update: all four commits now carry valid SSH signatures and `Signed-off-by: Stephan Meijer <me@stephanmeijer.com>`. The new head is `5c4b006f388051ab1521a28c0c9c69776080f822`; its file tree is identical to the previously tested/reviewed `dc823e5f15b5ae293815962a06277a519f0e5f9e`. The earlier review and runtime reports remain attached to that original SHA. GitHub CI has restarted for the signed-off history.

author: navinagrawal
body:
Exported from the private tree with zero drift findings: 419 files copied, 83 stale artifacts removed, no private markers or secret patterns detected.

## The declared dependency floors are now exercised

`pyproject` allows `jsonschema>=4.25.1`, so that is what a user may install, but every run resolved the newest version and the lower bound was never executed. That is the same shape as the defect that broke the last release on Python 3.10: `requires-python` allowed it while nothing ever imported the package there.

A new `dependency-floors` CI job runs on the declared Python floor, installs the floors through `make deps-floor`, then runs the suite. `deps-floor` **derives** each floor from `pyproject` rather than restating it, so the workflow cannot go stale when a floor moves, and the installer exits non-zero on a dependency it cannot pin rather than skipping it under a green job.

The floors stay wide rather than being raised — narrowing them would cost installs for no defect. Verified beyond configuration: a throwaway venv at jsonschema 4.25.1 and PyYAML 6.0.3 imported **all 74 shipped modules with 0 ImportErrors**.

## A contract that was not running

`test_python_floor_contract.py` gains the `journey` marker it was missing. Without it the file sat in `tests/journey` but was invisible to marker-based selection, so the Python floor contract would not have run in the runs meant to execute it. A contract nothing selects is not a gate.

## No more hardcoded version literals in the distribution contract

The contract asserted a literal `pytest` version, which duplicated `requirements.txt` and would have failed on every future dependency upgrade for no behavioral reason. It now asserts the pin exists and is exact. Workflow files also gain a test-impact mapping, so changing CI selects the contracts that read it instead of selecting nothing.

Maintainer pins move to their latest releases, each verified against the index rather than from memory.

## What changed

Performs one bounded substantive depth remediation for *The Other 250* Chapter 9, “Sixty-Nine Feet Down,” and synchronizes the existing book-local depth/release bookkeeping.

## Mechanical effect

The literal September 6 `scripts/check-book-length.py the-other-250` run recorded Chapter 9 at **2,485 words**, **515 below** the repository’s 3,000-word per-chapter floor.

The Chapter 9 blob on Desk remained identical to that frozen validation source before this pass. The append-only addition contributes **574 words** under the checker’s exact `\b[\w’'-]+\b` token expression, yielding a deterministic current Chapter 9 count of **3,059 words**, 59 above the floor.

Concurrent Desk work closed additional chapter floors while this PR was being prepared. After reconciling those changes, this pass makes Chapter 9 the **16th of the 21 original short-chapter defects to close**. **Five known sub-floor chapters remain: Chapters 16, 17, 19, 20, and 21.**

## Editorial scope

The added prose stays inside the chapter’s existing Drake-well-as-catalytic-proof argument. It deepens:

- how extraction becomes an industrial system through complementary investment;
- the distinction between resource availability and infrastructure dependence;
- path dependence without claiming inevitability;
- incumbent-system advantages embedded in skills, standards, finance, suppliers, and maintenance;
- resilience and redundancy as properties of mature energy systems;
- why transitions are institutionally and politically difficult once costs and benefits are attached to real places and constituencies.

It adds no new quotation, dated statistic, named source, or volatile current factual claim. Existing boundaries remain intact: Drake did not invent global petroleum, alternate drilling success was plausible, resource value depends on surrounding technology and infrastructure, and petroleum’s environmental and political liabilities remain part of the story.

## Scope

Exactly three files under `books/the-other-250/`:

- `manuscript/ch09-sixty-nine-feet-down.md`
- `research/depth-remediation-2026-09-07.md`
- `research/release-review.md`

No root catalog/discovery, Reader, rights, tooling, workflow, Shelf, or neighboring-book changes.

The branch was reconciled without force onto Desk main `5cdd04ed383a9fc2a5c9a7dd815edd0ed45953c8`, preserving concurrent Chapter 7 and Reader/Bookself work. The post-reconciliation diff remains exactly the three files above.

## Release boundary

This does **not** publish the title. *The Other 250* remains blocked until Chapters 16, 17, 19, 20, and 21 are substantively remediated and the final frozen-source `check-book-length.py` and `check-desk.py` gates are satisfied.

author: shuangwu
body:
## Summary

- group ordered policy-to-policy state transfers into byte-bounded HA retry/watchdog windows
- optionally pack small mixed-dtype tensors into a reusable `uint8` buffer, while keeping oversized tensors direct
- keep packing disabled by default behind `[train].p2p_sync_pack_tensors`
- preserve the single-tensor hook contract for custom trainers
- cover retry ordering, DTensor state, CPU/offloaded state, scalar tensors, initialization broadcast, and dynamic-scale unicast

This changes policy-to-policy initialization and elasticity sync only. It does not alter P2R or R2R weight synchronization.

## Motivation

`LLMTrainer.sync_all_states` previously invoked the HA NCCL wrapper once per state entry. Each invocation waited for communicator readiness and entered a watchdog that records a CUDA event and drains the stream, so a model/optimizer state with hundreds of entries incurred hundreds of host-side drain points.

Byte-bounded HA batches reduce the retry/watchdog count. Packing additionally reduces the number of raw NCCL operations; this is the part that produced the material improvement.

## Benchmark

Measured on one 8x H100 80 GB node with a constructed Qwen2.5-7B-equivalent BF16 inventory: 7,615,616,512 parameters, 339 tensors, and 15,231,233,024 bytes. Results are medians of five order-rotated runs through the production `LLMTrainer.sync_all_states` path. Receivers were cleared before every run and every element was checked afterward.

| Topology | Per tensor | HA windows only | Packed 256 MiB buckets | Packed improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Four concurrent FSDP4 unicast lanes (3.55 GiB/rank) | 454.9 ms | 439.2 ms | **30.2 ms** | **15.1x / 93.4% less time** |
| Eight-rank broadcast (14.19 GiB/rank) | 463.9 ms | 456.3 ms | **132.1 ms** | **3.51x / 71.5% less time** |

HA-window batching alone saved 1.6-3.4% because all 339 NCCL operations remained. Packing reduced the unicast case to 15 transfers and the broadcast case to 86 transfers. The largest scratch allocations observed were 267,924,992 bytes for FSDP4 unicast and 194,534,400 bytes for broadcast. Benchmark Slurm job: `2142761`.

## Configuration

Packing requires explicit enablement:

```toml
[train]
p2p_sync_pack_tensors = true
```

An explicitly set `COSMOS_P2P_SYNC_PACK_TENSORS` overrides the TOML value for A/B testing or emergency disablement. `COSMOS_P2P_SYNC_BUCKET_SIZE_BYTES=0` restores per-tensor behavior.

## Correctness and validation

- Unit/contract suite: **25 passed, 2 skipped, 129 subtests passed**. The two local skips require GPUs and were run separately below.
- Real-NCCL packed broadcast and unicast: job `2142743`.
- Config-driven initialization broadcast with four two-GPU Qwen2.5-3B policies: job `2142910`; 434 DTensor entries and a 263,235,632-byte packed buffer per rank.
- Real-NCCL CPU/offloaded state copyback for broadcast and unicast, including scalar state: job `2142911`.
- Full dynamic-scale `PolicyToPolicyUnicastCommand` worker integration with two four-rank Qwen2.5-3B policies on 8x H100: job `2142965`; all four destination ranks verified source-stamped values, with 434 DTensor entries and a 267,941,448-byte packed buffer per rank.
- Ruff format/check and `git diff --check` pass.

The dynamic-scale and initialization jobs left `COSMOS_P2P_SYNC_PACK_TENSORS` unset, proving that packing was selected by the TOML configuration.

author: ken-jo
body:
## What the run showed

Every trial's stderr in the harness benchmark carried the same line, over and over:

```
{"module":"signature-shim","msg":"reasoning block missing signature — skipping (...)"}
```

Not occasionally — once per reasoning block, on a model whose trials reason for ~140,000 characters apiece. Thousands of identical warnings per run.

## Why it fired

A signed thinking block is an Anthropic construct: only that wire attaches `providerMetadata.anthropic.signature`, and only that wire requires the verbatim echo. The shim exists to catch an Anthropic block that genuinely lost its signature.

But `fullStreamToStreamEvent` asked the shim about **every** reasoning block from **every** vendor. A self-hosted model signs nothing, by design, so the answer was always "missing" — and the warning stopped carrying information. The one case the shim was written to surface is now buried under thousands of expected ones.

The collection was also wasted work: `genericToModelMessages` already drops `thinkingBlocks` for every non-Claude vendor, so the blocks were assembled and thrown away.

## The change

The wire is already known at the single production call site (`slot`), so the mapper takes the vendor and gates the signature bookkeeping on it. Reasoning deltas still reach the caller for every vendor — only the Anthropic echo bookkeeping is skipped.

Also drops the upstream issue number from the runtime message. The issue trail belongs in the file header, where it already is, not in a log line.

## Verification

- New test: an unsigned reasoning block on a non-Anthropic wire produces no warning, no thinking blocks, and still emits reasoning deltas.
- **Control run**: with the vendor gate removed the new test fails (`expected "warn" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`); with it restored, 24/24 pass. The test measures the fix rather than merely passing beside it.
- `src/engine/llm/vercel/__tests__/` — 196 tests pass across 12 files (includes the lock suites).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; `check:typecheck-tests` baseline held.

author: cipher813
body:
crucible-PR158 moved `LIQUIDITY_FLOOR_USD` behind an accessor and the
infra-literal scan reported the tree clean. It was not clean. Two sites still
published the number:

- `crucible/features/registry.py`'s `liquidity_pass_raw` entry carried
  `expression="dollar_volume_20d_raw >= 5_000_000"` — and that string is
  RENDERED INTO `docs/FEATURE_CATALOG.md`, so the tuned threshold was in the
  generated public documentation, not just in source;
- the new accessor's own docstring said what the constant "was".

WHY THE SCAN MISSED BOTH, which is the finding worth keeping: every pattern in
`tests/test_no_infra_literals.py` matched a NAME — an account id's ARN context,
a bucket stem, a role/topic identifier — and this leak was a NUMBER. The scan
graded the identifier and the value walked past it. A tuned threshold is
exactly as published in an expression string as it is in an assignment, and I
found these only by grepping the value itself AFTER the guard said clean.

So the guard now carries `LIQUIDITY_FLOOR_VALUE_PATTERN`, matching the value in
any spelling source or a doc would use (`5_000_000`, `5000000`, `5,000,000`,
`5e6`, with or without a decimal tail), with its own sample in the
detector-fires self-test.

THE FEATURE VERSION MOVES, and that is correct rather than collateral.
`DEFAULT_FEATURE_VERSION` is a sha256 digest of the whole catalogue taken at
import precisely so that a registry edit changing what a column MEANS cannot
overwrite the layer an earlier verdict was computed from. The
`liquidity_pass_raw` expression changed, so the version changed:
`v6df3c0a27b70`. `tests/test_feature_registry_contract.py` failed on the stale
generated table and was satisfied by regenerating it with
`python -m crucible.features.docgen`, which is the contract behaving as
designed. Nothing pins a feature-version literal.

Verified: 2532 passed, 0 failed; ruff clean; the extended guard reports 0
findings across `.github/`, `crucible/` and `tests/`; and a raw grep for the
value in every spelling returns nothing outside the guard's own pattern.

Carrefour **no queda terminado**: falta barrer `carrefour-bio` (631 fichas) y `carrefour-selection` (32), ya contadas y anotadas en el manifiesto para que la próxima noche empiece por ahí.
