body: ## Summary Adds an independent, durable external Telegram crash monitor and session supervisor (`workflows/portable/session_crash_monitor.py` and comprehensive test suite `test_session_crash_monitor.py`). Tracking: https://github.com/Wladefant/super-board/issues/78 and Bavariance/polysimulator #4543 Superboard card: `PVTI_lADODpNYWs4BIXPZzg53FFE` (Project #1) ## Delivered Architecture & Guarantees 1. **Target Session Identity Binding:** - Binds `session_id` (`01a0496f-64f6-733e-a9a6-89f15fc2a437`) + verified OS PID (`63864`) + exact creation time (`FILETIME` / UTC ISO8601). - Handles PID reuse: if the OS reallocates the PID to a new process with a different creation time, the original process instance is recognized as terminated. 2. **Planned Stop Suppression:** - Differentiates expected stops/restarts from crashes via `PlannedStopEvaluator`. - Checks primary session marker (`local/planned-restart-marker.json`) and fallback workflow marker (`~/.veyyon/workflows/planned_restart_.json`). - Suppresses alerts on planned stop markers with statuses `{"planned", "suppress", "expected", "restarting", "complete"}`. 3. **No False Crash on Slow/Quiet Models:** - Explicitly enforces that as long as the target process remains alive, quiet models, slow tool turns, and paused goals are NEVER classified as crashes. 4. **Durable Deduplication & Unsent State:** - State ledger keyed by `(session_id, pid, creation_time)` with cross-platform advisory `FileLock` and atomic file replacement. - Exactly one alert per owner termination. - If transport is down, records `unsent_transport_down` into `unsent_events` durably without crashing or unhandled exceptions. 5. **Verified Outbound-Only Route:** - Zero duplicate inbound poller or receiver logic; strictly outbound notifications via `TelegramNotificationAdapter` (slot `telegram-polysim`). - Alerts sanitized with `SecretSanitizer` to ensure zero secret/credential leakage or raw tool output dumps. 6. **Sanctioned Supervision:** - Runs independently under daemon supervision via `launch(..., persist=True)`, yielding `lifetime=broker-shutdown` which persists across Main exit. ## Verification Evidence - Exact head SHA: `93722a65dbeb5eca780973c056a2d1434dc74a99` - 7/7 unit and integration tests passing (`test_session_crash_monitor.py`): 1. `test_quiet_slow_model_alive_not_a_crash` 2. `test_unexpected_crash_triggers_alert_and_records_state` 3. `test_planned_stop_suppression` 4. `test_deduplication_single_alert_per_owner_termination` 5. `test_pid_reuse_detection` 6. `test_transport_failure_records_unsent_status_safely` 7. `test_real_disposable_subprocess_normal_and_planned_exit` (real OS subprocess) - Live Telegram API receipt verified: `message_id: 1319` on slot `telegram-polysim` via `python workflows/portable/session_crash_monitor.py --test-telegram`. - Active supervisor running: PID 66620 monitoring Main PID 63864 (`launch` name `session-crash-monitor`, `lifetime=broker-shutdown`). > [!NOTE] > ### Add external session crash monitor and `TelegramWorkflowFacade` > - Adds `SessionCrashMonitor` in [session_crash_monitor.py](https://github.com/Wladefant/super-board/pull/81/files#diff-65c4a18bc3331c3b2dac66d8676e5213a9e15306e32bf40982e1a0fa045a8b42) that supervises a bound session process, sends Telegram alerts on unexpected exits, and suppresses alerts for valid planned-stop markers. > - Adds `TelegramWorkflowFacade` in [telegram_workflow.py](https://github.com/Wladefant/super-board/pull/81/files#diff-b1c89950ee64cc3cc1ba00c4652f48b7d2c9ea1ad26718050ff8427902ed080c) with authenticated views for listing agents, sessions, tasks, and decisions, plus decision submission. All responses are sanitized and paginated with a max of 20 items. > - Registers both workflows and their tests in [manifest.json](https://github.com/Wladefant/super-board/pull/81/files#diff-f4a25ca083b927399954f78f66a49b9bc2cfb7287160a338ebe02d74b57f6e83). > - Risk: `TelegramWorkflowFacade` rejects cross-session requests with `PermissionError` and native snapshot identity mismatches; `SessionCrashMonitor` classifies PID creation-time changes as unexpected terminations of the originally bound process. > > > > Macroscope summarized 7aaea97. > >

author: op-bot-common
body:
Two model passes over the proposals in a decision phase. The first names the themes running through them; the second reads those themes back and reports where the proposals already agree, which ones sit outside that agreement and whether that matters, and what to merge or nudge toward it. Admin-only, behind `proposal-themes-feature`.

It follows the proposals CSV export's shape — the request returns an id, an Inngest workflow does the work, a per-run realtime channel wakes the status query, and the same `decisions: ADMIN` boundary (with the org fallback deliberately suppressed) guards both ends.

The analysis is stored in `@op/cache`, keyed `themeAnalysis:<instance>:<scope>:<id>` — every request is its own analysis, and a phase-scoped run cannot collide with a process-scoped one of the same instance. **No migration.**

Cache-only needs one guard to be safe, and it is the interesting part of this PR. `set()` reports nothing: it returns early when no cache is configured and swallows its own timeouts. So the request reads the seed back before dispatching the job. Without that, a deployment with no `REDIS_URL` accepts the request, spends both model passes, and hands the caller an id for a record that was never stored — which the client reads as *still pending*, so the button spins until it reports a timeout for an analysis that succeeded. That is the failure this feature shipped with once. It now fails at the button press, with a message that names the cause.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant UI as ThemeAnalysisButton
    participant API as decision.analyzeThemes
    participant C as cache
    participant WF as analyzeProposalThemes
    participant M as @op/ai

    UI->>API: processInstanceId
    API->>C: seed (pending) + read back
    API-->>UI: analysisId
    API->>WF: proposal/theme-analysis-requested
    WF->>C: processing
    WF-->>UI: broadcast
    WF->>M: pass 1 — themes
    WF->>M: pass 2 — common ground, outliers, suggestions
    WF->>C: completed + result
    WF-->>UI: broadcast
    UI->>API: getThemeAnalysisStatus
```

**Two surfaces, two corpora.** The control sits in the proposals list's admin group and on the results screen's All-proposals tab. Those show different sets — the list shows the instance's current phase, results shows every proposal it has ever held, including ones dropped in an earlier phase — so the request carries a `scope` (`phase` or `process`) and the surface that launches a run says which set it was showing. Without it, a results-screen analysis would report a synthesis of proposals the reader is not looking at, and the coverage line would not give it away.

**The trust boundary is the load-bearing part.** Proposal text is written by the public and goes into a prompt whose reply an admin reads as a summary of their own process, so both sides of the model are untrusted. Corpus entries are fenced and the fence characters in their own text are escaped, so a proposal cannot end its own document. The model never sees a proposal id — it is given a numbered list and answers in **corpus indexes**, which the service maps back, so an invented reference is out of range where an invented UUID would be indistinguishable from a real one. Replies are parsed by Zod before anything reads a field, and nothing the model writes is rendered as markup.

**Two architectural notes worth a reviewer's attention.** Deterministic failures are step *results*, not exceptions: an error thrown inside an Inngest step arrives at the function body as a `StepError` rebuilt from `name`/`message`/`stack`, so a custom class — and the error code the app translates from — cannot survive the boundary. Returning also stops a retry that would re-read the corpus and re-pay for a model call to reach the same conclusion. And the workflow writes whole records rather than patching: the event carries the request's `createdAt`, so every write is complete on its own and no cache read sits between a finished two-model analysis and the record that reports it.

The model is named in code — `THEME_ANALYSIS_MODEL_ID = 'zai-org/GLM-5.3'` — and passed to `@op/ai`, not read from the environment. Services here run on different models, so a deploy-wide default would apply one service's choice to every other one; `modelId` is required on `AIModelConfig` and each caller says what it wants. Only the endpoint (`AI_BASE_URL`) and its key stay environmental, so **this has to name a model that endpoint serves.**

Deferred, not forgotten: this is now the second background job an admin waits on, and it duplicates the export's cache-record read/authorize preamble, its status-patch helpers, and its button state machine. Extracting those is a real follow-up, but it changes shipped code and belongs in its own PR.

### CRAP

Threshold 30. `fallow audit` reports **0 introduced complexity, dead-code, duplication or styling findings** on this diff; the four complexity findings in the touched files are all inherited (`ProposalsList`, `ProposalsFilterBar`). Coverage below is read from the tests in this PR, not from a coverage reporter — the workspace has none, so treat the column as an estimate.

| Function | CC | Coverage | CRAP |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolveThemeAnalysisPhase` | 4 | covered (10 cases) | 4 |
| `resolveCompletedThemeAnalysis` | 4 | covered (7 cases) | 4 |
| `runThemesPass` | 3 | covered (5 cases) | 3 |
| `resolveCorpusIndexes` | 4 | covered (5 cases) | 4 |
| `askForJson` | 4 | covered (5 cases) | 4 |
| `isFollowingRun` | 3 | covered (4 cases) | 3 |
| `collectProposalCorpus` | 3 | covered (7 cases) | 3 |
| `resolveAIModelConfig` | 5 | covered (9 cases) | 5 |
| `requestThemeAnalysis` | 3 | covered (8 cases) | 3 |
| `getThemeAnalysisStatus` | 5 | covered (11 cases) | 5 |
| `useThemeAnalysisRun` | 5 | none (no DOM env) | 30 |
| `analyzeProposalThemes` | 3 | none (no test harness in `services/workflows`) | 12 |

The two uncovered entries are the ones the workspace cannot reach: `apps/app` runs Vitest under `environment: 'node'` with no DOM, and `services/workflows` has no test script at all. Everything decidable was pulled out of both into `themeAnalysisState.ts` and `runPasses.ts`, which is why they are 5 and 3 rather than the 17 the hook started at.

**Local gates:** `typecheck`, `format:check`, `fallow audit`, and the `@op/common` (704), `apps/app` (265) and `@op/ai` (18) suites all pass. The `@op/api` integration suite is red on this machine and **also red on a clean `dev`** — every failure is `Failed to create test user` from the shared local Supabase auth container, which is serving another agent's dev app on :3100 at the same time. The four theme/export gating tests pass in isolation. Worth re-running in CI.

author: chrischall
body:
`view` reached **1 of 39 tools**. `src/gql.ts` asks Vibo for media in six documents, so five reads were selecting image URLs and returning them whole with no way to say no — a model cannot look at them and pays for them either way. All five now take `view`, compact by default:

| Tool | What compact drops |
|---|---|
| `vibo_get_section_songs` | `thumbnails { s180x180 original }` per song |
| `vibo_list_song_ideas_songs` | `thumbnails { … }` per song |
| `vibo_list_event_users` | `imageUrl` per person, on **both** exits |
| `vibo_list_notifications` | `imageUrl` per notification |
| `vibo_get_me` | `imageUrl` |

## Wiring the rung, not deleting the selection

#107 weighed a cheaper option first: stop selecting the media in the GraphQL document at all, since `thumbnails`/`imageUrl` are requested by us, not forced by the API. It is cheaper, and it is worse — it takes the field away from `view: "full"` too, so a caller who genuinely wants an avatar has no route to one. The rung gives the default caller the saving *and* keeps the escape hatch.

## Still subtractive, deliberately

Compact remains `stripMediaUrls`, per `src/view.ts`'s docblock: this repo holds no captured Vibo payload, so any field projection would be invented, and an invented list is how a record comes back with holes in it looking like a verified answer. Nothing here claims a shape was checked that was not.

## The guard, which is the actual fix

The defect was not a missing feature; it was an unnoticed **gap**, because nothing tied the wire surface to the tool wiring. `tests/view.test.ts` now counts the media selections in `gql.ts` (three `${THUMBS}` sites, three `imageUrl`) and asserts the roster of view-taking tools against them. A seventh selection fails the count and points at the roster.

Two things it pins that are easy to get wrong:

- **`vibo_list_event_users` has two exits**, and the merged one runs when `usersType` is omitted — the default call. Honouring the rung on only the filtered branch is exactly the bug that already shipped here once, in `vibo_search_songs`, where `view` sat on the branch that never fired.
- **`vibo_healthcheck` runs `GET_ME` too and must NOT gain a rung.** It never returns Vibo's user object; it builds `{ok, userId, email}`. A `view` there would be a parameter that changes nothing — the kind a caller reasonably assumes does something.

## Verification

- `npm test` — typecheck clean, **177 passed** (was 167; ten added).
- `skills/vibo-mcp/SKILL.md` rewritten: it documented "exactly one of 39" and carried the five gaps as a budget-for-it warning. It now carries the table above, and the note that a test holds the correspondence.

Closes #107

author: joekaulpulse
body:
## Summary

Three independent, non-owner-gated privacy/GDPR findings from the Build board, batched into one PR since they're all "stop sending sensitive data somewhere it shouldn't go" fixes.

- **BLD-1655** (bearer-token leak to Google/Meta): `TrackingScripts.tsx`'s `NO_TRACK_PATH` excluded only `/booking` from GA4/Meta Pixel's automatic full-URL pageview capture. `/sign/[token]` (single-use clinical consent-signing token) and `/live/[token]` (reuses `Booking.manageToken`) were not excluded, so the credential's full path was reported to Google's and Meta's servers on every visit. Extended the exclusion to `/sign`, `/live`, `/follow-up`, `/review` and `/nps`, matching the existing `/booking` precedent.
- **BLD-1621** (session-replay over-capture): `BehaviorRecorder.tsx` excluded `/admin`, `/account`, `/book`, `/booking` and `/shop` from rrweb session-replay capture but never `/academy` — so `/academy/portfolio` (real client before/after treatment photos), `/academy/funding` (trainee income/employment/residency data) and `/academy/settings` (trainee contact details) were being recorded, viewable via the marketing-permission-gated replay endpoint rather than the clinical one. Added `/academy` to the exclusion regex. **Note:** this stops *new* recordings only — any replays already captured from these routes are a separate remediation-scope/review-and-purge decision the finding explicitly flagged for the owner, and is out of scope here.
- **BLD-1658** (repeated PII re-send): `formatAssessment()` re-sent every free-text health-assessment answer to Google Translate on every single clinician view, contradicting the in-form promise that answers are "seen only by your care team." Added an encrypted `HealthAssessmentTranslation` cache — a **new, additive table** (not a column on `HealthAssessment`, which is documented append-only/never-updated) keyed to a hash of the exact source values, so a repeat view reuses the cached translation instead of re-sending the special-category text. A later change to the admin-managed question set naturally misses the cache and re-translates rather than serving stale text. Wired into `lib/key-rotation.ts`'s sweep alongside `HealthAssessment`/`SignedConsent` so its cipher rotates too.

## Schema change

Additive only — one new table (`HealthAssessmentTranslation`) with no new `@unique` constraints (uses `assessmentId` as its own `@id`), consistent with the deploy gate in `scripts/db-sync.mjs` (`prisma db push` without `--accept-data-loss`).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — compiles successfully (this sandbox cannot reach the Postgres instance on port 5432 — confirmed via a raw TCP test against both the pooled and direct Neon endpoints, and unrelated to this change since HTTPS egress works fine — so `prebuild`'s `db-sync` step was skipped by unsetting the DB env vars for this local verification)
- [ ] `prisma db push` against a real database to confirm the additive migration applies cleanly (recommend before merge, or as part of the review pass, since this sandbox could not reach any Postgres instance)
- [ ] Manual check that `/sign/[token]` and `/live/[token]` pageviews no longer appear in GA4/Meta network requests

author: jose-villegas
body:
bd `esp32c6-e6c`. Every frame-budget row in this file times `sand_step()` with the
present **excluded**. Every present row does the reverse — `run_present_against_scene()`
steps the sim *outside* its own timer and times only `gfx_present()`. Both halves
of a frame are measured and their sum never was.

## Why now

Tonight's two merges took water's step 20 777 → 15 168 µs. A full present measures
~17 600 µs. **The display transfer is now the larger half of the frame**, and the
next big lever (`esp32c6-91i`, overlapping present with the next sim step) cannot
be justified — or sized — without a real frame number.

## What it measured

Falling-sand checkerboard scene:

| phase | µs/frame |
|---|---:|
| sim | 7 375 |
| mark | 1 785 |
| **present** | **9 738** |
| **total** | **18 898** |

Present is 51% of the frame. And `sim + mark = 9160` against `present = 9738` —
**the two halves are within 6% of each other**, which is the best possible case
for a pipeline: bounded by `max(a, b)`, so where `a ≈ b` the ceiling is half the
sum. That frame would go ~18.9 ms → ~9.7 ms.

## Honest about its limits

- **It is a lower bound on a real frame.** The actual pixel writes are excluded:
  `draw_dirty_rows()`, `draw_one_row()` and `paint_row()` are `static` in
  `app_sand.c` and unreachable from a suite. Closing `e6c` properly needs
  `app_sand.c` to expose a phase-timed entry the way `boot_anim.c` already does
  for `suite_boot_anim_perf.c` — that touches the app/shell contract, so it is a
  design decision rather than a mechanical addition.
- **9738 µs is not "the present cost".** This scene dirties part of the screen, so
  the dirty-band system sends a subset; a full repaint measured 17 482 µs in the
  same capture. Busier scenes move toward that ceiling.
- **It prints, it does not assert.** No budget has been argued for a frame, and
  pegging one from an unmeasured guess is what this project forbids. Peg it from
  a capture, deliberately, if it is wanted.

## Reviewer notes

`run_present_against_scene()` gains three nullable out-params and times its three
phases separately; its return value is unchanged and the three existing callers
pass `NULL` — what they measure and assert is untouched. The scene construction is
factored into `build_falling_sand_present_scene()` shared with the existing present
test, rather than copied — two copies that could drift is a bug this file has been
bitten by before.

- [x] `./launcher/test/run_tests.sh` — 871 tests, 0 failures; count unchanged, as
      the new test is `DEVICE_BUILD`-only
- [x] `RUN_TEST` registration confirmed — an unregistered benchmark has cost this
      campaign a whole capture before
- [x] Builds and captures on device; numbers above are from that capture
- [ ] `report_fingerprint.sh --check` reports `sealed_lava` changed — **pre-existing
      on `main`** from #87's dislodge change, verified by reproducing it on a clean
      checkout. Fixed separately in #90; this branch neither causes nor fixes it.

author: ghajaymore
body:
I signed in as an actual entrant for the first time, in a match-play tournament, and the player app never once named their opponent.

**Today** showed a stroke-play position and a to-par — *"Position 23, +4"* — over a round that is three match-play fixtures. **My card** said *"your score is recorded against your opponent"* without saying who that was. There was nowhere in the player shell to find out who you were playing or how the match stood.

The pairing has been in a `Match` row since the draw was generated. The console reads it on three screens.

## Why it never reached the player

*"Who am I with"* was read off the **tee sheet** — which an organizer has to draw *and then publish*. A match comes from the **draw**, and exists the moment flights are generated.

Those are different questions with different answers, and conflating them meant a match-play player saw nothing at all until a sheet appeared that their round never depended on. For the format this app leads with.

`MyRound.matches` now carries them, separately from `group`, as a list — a round robin puts several matches in one round, and choosing among them would be arbitrary.

**Before:** Position 23 · +4
**After:** Match 1 — v Andre Costa · *Not started* · Match 2 — v Zoe Sullivan · *Won 2&1* · Match 3 — v Hannah Voss · *Lost 5&4*

Cross-checked all three against the stored draw before believing the screen.

## The flip is the dangerous part

`resolveMatch` reports `lead` as **A minus B**, so every reading has to be negated for the player on the other side of it.

Wrong, that does not fail loudly — it tells **half of every field that they are winning a match they are losing**, in the app's signature format, on the screen they have open on the tee.

And the seeded demo puts its test player on **side A in all three** of their matches, so walking the app proves exactly half of it. Every case is therefore asserted from **both ends of the same match**, and asserted to disagree.

Mutation-tested: removing the negation takes three tests red.

## A concession is checked before the card

Rule 3.2b(1) — a conceded match is over and the opponent has won it. The fixture is the trap: a player **3 up** when they walk in would otherwise be reported as *winning* the match they conceded. Mutation-tested too.

## And a broken sentence on a player-facing screen

> "Every player meets every other in their group over 3 rounds. **is match play**, so your score is recorded against your opponent…"

`MyRound.label` prefers the organizer's description, and a description is prose — Demo Cup's is a whole sentence, full stop and all. There is now a separate `name` for the noun ("Round 1"), kept beside `label` rather than sanitised at the call site, because the next sentence somebody writes will reach for whichever field is nearest.

## Also

"My card" on a match round was a dead end — told the card isn't yours, offered only the whole board. Their own match is one tap away and is what they came for.

## Verification

tsc clean · vitest **4511 passed** (10 new) · lint clean · build compiled · **smoke: all 39 routes rendered**.

Note on that smoke run: the first one reported `fetch failed` because `npm run smoke` defaults to port 3000 and this worktree's server is on 3100 — it had tested nothing. Re-run with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` and it is genuinely green.

Both load-bearing rules mutation-tested — the perspective flip and the concession ordering. Walked as a real player at 375px.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: hermes-david
body:
## Description

Fixes two related bugs in author identity propagation for Hermes provider writes (upstream issue #914).

**Bug 1 — provider-instance construction missing author identity.** Both Hermes provider surfaces (`hermes_memory_provider` and the `mnemosyne_hermes` integration) construct `BeamMemory`/`Mnemosyne` instances without any author identity, so every write path inserted `author_id=NULL`. This PR adds per-write `author_id`/`author_type` kwargs to `BeamMemory.remember()` and the `Mnemosyne` wrapper (threaded through to beam), and resolves identity at write time in the provider surfaces using the same precedence as `mcp_tools._create_instance`: tool args > `MNEMOSYNE_AUTHOR_ID`/`MNEMOSYNE_AUTHOR_TYPE` env > None. The identity is threaded through **all** provider write paths: `remember`, batch (`apply_beam_batch` `default_author_id`/`default_author_type` with per-operation override), `apply_pending` (stamp captured at stage time), `sync_turn`, identity signals, the shared surface, and `on_memory_write`. Tool schemas expose the new args. `beam.author_id` itself stays unset so prefetch/recall remains session-scoped (no `(1=1)` bypass).

**Bug 2 — episodic INSERT copying `self.author_id`.** `consolidate_to_episodic`'s INSERT copied the beam's own `self.author_id` instead of the row-level author, dropping write-side stamps at consolidation. This PR adds `author_id`/`author_type` kwargs to `consolidate_to_episodic`, fetches `author_id`/`author_type` in `sleep()`'s source SELECT, and aggregates per group: a unanimous row author is preserved, while mixed/absent groups fall back to beam identity (previous behavior). `sleep_all_sessions` alien-beam fallback semantics are unchanged.

## Related Issue

- https://github.com/mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne/issues/914

(Not marked as "Closes" here — this PR targets the review fork; the upstream PR will reference the issue.)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor / performance
- [ ] Test improvement
- [ ] CI / build tooling

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Existing tests still pass (`pytest tests/` — 142 passed, 1 skipped)
- [x] New tests added for any new functionality
- [ ] Manual verification (describe what you tested)

New coverage (22 tests):

- `tests/test_beam_author_id_914.py` — `remember()` kwarg stamping (override/fallback/dedup), `consolidate_to_episodic` kwargs, `sleep()` preserving unanimous/mixed/absent author groups.
- `tests/test_hermes_provider_author_914.py` — both provider surfaces (parametrized over `hermes_memory_provider` and `mnemosyne_hermes`): env and tool-arg resolution on `remember`, batch `default_author` vs per-operation override, and shared-surface stamping.

Note: two pre-existing `tests/test_beam_e3_additive_sleep.py` timezone failures reproduce on clean main (naive-vs-UTC comparison on a CDT host) and are unrelated to this change. `ruff` CI gate (E9, F63, F7, F82) should be run by CI.

## Checklist

author: forrestisrunning
body:
## Problem The Volume content sequence diagram in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` does not render on GitHub: ```text Parse error on line 12: ... for BYOC teams;
SDK stores it and f -----------------------^ ``` Mermaid sequence diagrams treat `;` as a statement separator (equivalent to a newline). After `BYOC teams;`, the parser starts a new statement at `
` and fails. The same diagram also uses HTML `<` / `>` for domain placeholders; those are invalid tokens in current Mermaid. This is a docs-only bug. CONTRIBUTING.md says documentation fixes can skip the issue-first step. ## Fix Use [Mermaid entity codes](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/sequenceDiagram.html#entity-codes-to-escape-characters) in that sequence diagram, which is the documented way to keep the original text: | character | in source | |---|---| | `;` | `#59;` | | `<` | `#lt;` | | `>` | `#gt;` | The rendered note and `api.` placeholders stay the same. Surrounding prose is unchanged.
Diagram after the change (should render below) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant U as SDK participant API as API participant PG as PostgreSQL participant VC as volume-content API (belt) U->>API: POST /volumes (create) or GET /volumes/{id} API->>PG: persist / load volume row API->>API: mint JWT (aud = https://api.#lt;domain#gt;)
resolve domain API-->>U: { volumeID, name, token, domain? } Note over U: domain is returned only for BYOC teams#59;
SDK stores it and falls back to api.#lt;E2B_DOMAIN#gt; otherwise U->>VC: /volumecontent/{id}/... at api.#lt;domain#gt;
Authorization: Bearer token VC->>VC: verify token (audience must match its own origin) VC-->>U: file content ```

author: thestuartchan
body:
#70 dropped single-holding chains but named them in a muted line:

> *Ethereum, Arbitrum — a single holding each, not shown.*

The reasoning was that a holdings overview which quietly omits a holding cannot be trusted as a list. In practice the line was more noise than the two rows it replaced, which was the thing being fixed. Removed — a thin chain now leaves no trace on the card.

**Final shape:**

```
Wallet · today
No changes today.

  🪶 Robinhood Chain
  PONS 0.713
  STONKBROKER 0.01477
  NUDES 0.01588
  AU 0.001419
  ETH 2484.80

  Market prices at time of post
```

The concern the line was protecting still holds, but the card was the wrong place for it: a **trade** on a dropped chain is still announced in the events above, so activity always surfaces even when a standing balance does not, and the console shows everything. What is lost is only the standing balance of a chain holding one thing — which is the definition of what this filter was asked to hide.

## Verification

- `npm test` — exit 0, 107 assertions still. The tests were inverted rather than deleted: they now assert the dropped chains are *not* named and nothing they hold appears, so the behaviour stays pinned in the opposite direction.

author: cklxx
body:
main's CI is red at `60a6f0af` (and `08dcb142`) on `harness.py --selftest`. Cause is PR #55's on-main refusal firing inside harness.py's own fixtures. **Three fixtures, not the one the traceback names.**

## What CI could and could not see

| fixture | asserts | after #55 |
|---|---|---|
| allowed data file (~22084) | hook **passes** | FAILs — this is the red CI reports |
| pre-merge-commit (~21884) | merge is **refused** | **still green, for the wrong reason** |
| manifest regeneration (~21908) | commit **succeeds** | FAILs, but only once reached |

The middle row is the finding, and it generalises past this incident. That world exists to prove the `data/` allow-list stops a non-fast-forward merge carrying an unlisted path — a real defect that landed in main through a merge on 2026-08-31. Its assertion is `rc != 0`, which my refusal **satisfies**. So it keeps passing while the allow-list has stopped being the cause of anything it observes, and nothing in the artifact shows the difference.

**A positive assertion breaks loudly when a new gate fires early; a negative assertion absorbs it.** After adding any refusal, the fixtures to audit are not the ones that failed — they are the ones asserting a refusal, which cannot fail. Two of the three assertions in the world CI names have that shape.

Found by scanning for the class rather than following the traceback (62's call).

## One fixture stays on main, deliberately

`harness.py:21954` inits on main to exercise `git commit-tree --with-tree=main` and installs **no hook**. Its own comment records a CI break from getting that branch name wrong — green on every dev box, red in CI, because the default branch name is a property of the environment. So the rule is *"no fixture that installs the **real** hook on main"*, not "no fixture on main". A rule phrased the second way sends the next reader to change that fixture.

Also not subjects: two fixtures that write their own two-line stub (`#!/bin/sh` printing `GIT_INDEX_FILE`; a file holding only `SELFTEST_FILES`). They reach no gate.

## `git init -b fixture`, not a checkout

`-b` names the initial branch, and the first hook run in these worlds happens before any commit exists, where HEAD is unborn. The merge world also checked `main` back out by name, so that line moves too — four line changes total, plus comments.

## No check for the class, and that is deliberate

I wrote one and dropped it after three attempts, each wrong in a different direction:

| attempt | outcome |
|---|---|
| function-level escape test | broken world read as **clean** — `_demo` is ~900 lines, so one `-b fixture` anywhere excused every world in it |
| per-init, function-level hook attribution | flagged the legitimate `--with-tree=main` fixture |
| per-init, per-repo-variable attribution | 26 hits across 20 functions that install no hook, while `_demo` — the only true subject — **disappeared** |

A scan that misses the instance that matters is worse than no scan, because it certifies. The class is uncovered and §273's `open:` line states the narrower machine-checkable form: for every fixture asserting `rc != 0` against a real hook, require the assertion to name the refusal string it expects — then a gate firing early fails the fixture instead of satisfying it.

## Verification

`harness.py --selftest` → **105 of 109 checks each verified to FAIL on a broken world**, rc=0, 4 SKIPPED and named (`card_held_without_claim`, `coresident_cache_refusal`, `lane_respected`, `snapshot_logs_say_so_at_the_tail` — need a GPU box). `shapes_table_covers_doc` PASS at 238 incidents, max §273.

Running `--selftest` directly is the **only** available evidence here: `readlink -f "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks/pre-commit"` resolves to the integration tree's copy, so for a hook change *"main is green"* and *"your commits work"* are independent in **both** directions — the file you run and the file you edited are different. 62 had the one direction (a fix on main does nothing for a branch until it merges); this is the mirror.

4c's question about the `scripts/integration_tree.py did not import (ModuleNotFoundError)` line in that world: **expected, not a defect.** `repo_root()` there is the temp dir, which has no `scripts/`, so the import genuinely cannot succeed — and the hook's own comment says an unimportable predicate must be loud rather than silent.

§273 lands as a separate doc commit so this one stays reviewable as the CI fix.

author: cityage
body:
Three commits off `main`, after the audit reported in the thread.

**(a) /contact as a note.** Kicker CONTACT, "Write to us.", the city line, the deck. One sentence at 22px Newsreader, line-height 1.75, with inline blanks on hairlines (name, organisation, email) and a subject select styled as a blank with seven subjects: sponsoring, speaking, The Northern Century, The Next West, the Studio, press, something else. One message textarea ("Say as much or as little as you like."), one brass button "Send the note", "Or write directly: info@cityage.com" beneath. Sent: "Sent. Miro will read it." Failure keeps the form and says "That didn't send. Try again, or write to info@cityage.com." Honeypot kept; name is one field; city gone; placeholders italic and light; focus in brass. Wraps on a phone.

**(b) Delivery.** `/api/contact` is the single route. A row is written to `contact_submissions` first, every time: `source` = page slug, `enquiry` = subject, `email_sent` = false. Resend is removed. The notification goes to info@cityage.com with nodemailer through smtp.gmail.com:465 using **`SMTP_USER`** and **`SMTP_PASS`** (from SMTP_USER, reply-to the reader, subject "Note from name, organisation — subject", plain text with a link to the table). Success sets `email_sent`; failure or missing variables sets it false, stores the error in `email_error`, logs it, and the reader still sees the success state. Recording the outcome needs **`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`**: the table's policy lets the public key insert but not update, and policies cannot be added from this session. No migration.

**(c) One door.** `NoteForm` is the one component, taking `source` and a pre-selected `subject`. The Next West page's invitation form (Google Sheet + Resend + formsubmit.co) is replaced by the note set to The Next West. The Northern Century page, which had no form, gains an invitation band with the note set to The Northern Century; its rooms point at it. The AI policy page's contributor form (formsubmit.co) becomes the note. No parallel submit path remains.

Test rows from the preview are listed in the thread and will be deleted on your word.

body:
Nightly E2E has been red since Aug 4 (44 failed of 236 on the last nightly). This traces every failure to its root cause and turns the suite green again, then closes the gap that let it rot: the blocking job never ran on pushes to an already-ready PR.

## App fixes (real regressions from the Aug 4 chrome redesign)

- The bottom sheet captured pointerdowns on `<summary>` elements to start a drag, so native disclosures inside it (editor More fields, calendar term cards) never toggled on mobile at all.
- The one-tap day route (#839) lost its mount when the redesign dropped DayRouteChip from the bottom band. It now lives as a Route my day tool in the Map tools toolbox, hidden when nothing is routable today. The dead component is deleted.
- A selected jeepney stop outranked panel content in SidePanel and nothing cleared it, so browsing from the chips or App menu painted lists under the stuck stop panel. Browse entry points now clear the stop selection.

## E2E fixes (spec and helper drift)

- waitForAppBoot focused the search box, and the redesigned chrome hides the filter chips while search is focused, which timed out every browse test. It no longer focuses.
- Helpers now expand the mobile bottom sheet before reaching editor fields, and collapse either chrome's details surface before pin drags.
- Selector and label drift: Class Buildings chip, review queue as a side panel, leaderboard under the community disclosure, calendar term cards as disclosures, bottom-sheet panel containers, landing modal auto-marking itself seen, Escape intentionally clearing an active result.

## CI

- The blocking E2E workflow adds the `synchronize` trigger for non-draft PRs. Per-PR concurrency cancels the stale in-flight run, and per-run DB schemas keep overlaps isolated. Drafts stay cheap. docs/testing.md updated.

Local scoreboard on this branch: lint clean, unit 886 pass, components 323 pass, integration 80 pass, and every previously failing Playwright spec passes in isolation on both projects. This PR's own run is the full-suite proof.

author: phenobarbital
body:
## Summary

Implements FEAT-001 — Optional uvloop, Python 3.14 build, Windows wheels.

- `uvloop` moved from a hard dependency to the optional `python-datamodel[uvloop]` extra, with an explicit opt-in `datamodel.libs.uvloop.install_uvloop()` helper (no import-time activation).
- `setup.py` now selects MSVC-compatible compiler/link flags (`/O2`, no extra link args) on `win32`, keeping `-O3`/`-lstdc++` elsewhere.
- New `scripts/stage_rust_ext.py` replaces the previous Linux-only inline extractor, staging `_rs_parsers*.so`/`.pyd` cross-platform for both `make stage-rust` and the release workflow.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger and a `{ubuntu-latest, windows-latest} × {3.10–3.14}` matrix, a `CIBW_TEST_COMMAND` asserting `HAS_RUST`, OS-qualified artifact names, and a deploy-time wheel-inventory check.
- `README.md`/`INSTALL.md`/`CHANGELOG.md` updated; version bumped to `0.11.0`.

## Tasks

6/6 tasks verified:
  ✅ TASK-1 — Add the optional uvloop helper and packaging constraints
  ✅ TASK-2 — Test uvloop fallback, activation, and wheel packaging
  ✅ TASK-3 — Make Cython extension flags MSVC-compatible
  ✅ TASK-4 — Add cross-platform Rust extension staging
  ✅ TASK-5 — Add Windows and Python 3.14 release matrix coverage
  ✅ TASK-6 — Document the install path and publish version metadata

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -v`: 252/252 passed locally (Cython + Rust extensions built in-worktree).
- `ruff check` clean on all new/modified files (one pre-existing, unrelated `EXE001` on `setup.py`'s shebang).
- Adversarial code review completed; 3 Important findings fixed (Windows PATH step shell, musllinux wheel filtering + strict inventory count, `make stage-rust` maturin-binary pinning), 1 suggestion fixed (softened a CHANGELOG claim), 1 suggestion + 1 nitpick noted below for the reviewer.

### Known limitation (documented, not a defect)

AC7/AC8 (a live green `workflow_dispatch` run across all 10 legs, and the deploy inventory check) cannot be exercised outside GitHub Actions. Static YAML structure, `rg` checks, and no-macOS/ARM checks all pass. **Recommend triggering a `workflow_dispatch` dry run on this branch before merging** to validate the Windows + Python 3.14 build legs end-to-end.

### Outstanding review notes (not blocking)
- 🟡 `scripts/stage_rust_ext.py` uses `--interpreter python` (previously explicit `python3`) — very likely fine under cibuildwheel's per-target venvs, but unverified on an unfamiliar image variant.
- 💡 `datamodel/libs/uvloop.py`'s `uvloop: object | None` annotation is immediately shadowed by the `try/except` import; could be simplified to match `rs_parsers.HAS_RUST`'s simpler style.

---
_Closed by /sdd-done_

## Summary by Sourcery

Prepare the package for optional uvloop usage and cross-platform Python 3.14 and Windows wheel releases.

New Features:
- Add opt-in uvloop support through the `python-datamodel[uvloop]` extra and `install_uvloop()` helper.
- Add Python 3.14 and Windows wheel coverage to the release pipeline.
- Provide cross-platform Rust extension staging for Linux and Windows builds.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent unsupported GCC-style compiler and linker flags from being used for Windows builds.
- Ensure release artifacts include the Rust parser extension and fail validation when the expected wheel inventory is incomplete or contains unexpected wheels.

Enhancements:
- Raise the supported Python baseline to 3.10 and align Cython requirements with the new build targets.

CI:
- Expand release builds to a manually dispatchable Ubuntu and Windows matrix covering Python 3.10 through 3.14, with Rust-extension smoke tests for every wheel.

Deployment:
- Add release artifact naming by operating system and strict validation of published wheels and source distributions.

Documentation:
- Document supported Python and wheel platforms, optional uvloop installation and activation, and the Rust staging workflow.
- Add 0.11.0 release notes, including the uvloop dependency change.

Tests:
- Add coverage for uvloop fallback, explicit activation, platform handling, package inclusion, compiler flags, and cross-platform Rust extension staging.

Chores:
- Bump the package version to 0.11.0 and update packaging metadata for the new package and optional dependency.

body:
## What & why

`gb-kata-vm channel` connects a port inside a sandbox to an address on the machine that runs it. It reported success as soon as its socket file appeared, never checking the address. It now dials the address first, through the transport that carries the traffic, and refuses the launch when nothing answers. Only the supervision and egress legs ask for that check. A Mac Kata launch now stops with a message. The diff also carries a provisional copy of #6029's supervision-channel fix, which this branch's `host-port` live check needs to run at all.

On a Mac `bin/lib/sbx/vm-exec.bash` routes the verb through `limactl shell`. The verb then runs inside the Lima virtual machine, while the monitor and the proxy run on the Mac. `config/kata/lima.yaml` sets `mounts: []` and declares no `portForwards`, so both Mac addresses resolve to nothing there. The sandbox then ran unsupervised, with no proxy on its outgoing traffic.

`--require-upstream` is per leg because only some callers await their target. An `--allow-host-port` leg does not take it: nothing awaits the operator's own database, and a refusal there would fail the launch into `sbx_teardown`. The dial is a `reach` subcommand of `bin/lib/kata/vsock_transport.py`, the file the forwarder runs. `kata_vsock_upstream_reachable` gives it the argument `kata_vsock_listen_bg` gets, so probe and forwarder dial as one identity:

```
$ drive-kata-vsock.bash reachable /unreadable/ch-vm.sock unix:/nowhere.sock
# `id` stubbed to 1000, `sudo` stubbed to record its argv:
-n python3 .../vsock_transport.py reach --upstream unix:/nowhere.sock
```

The ported commit is separate. `sbx_kata_open_supervision_channels` refused whenever `SBX_MONITOR_PORT` was unset, so `bin/checks/sbx/host-port.bash` — which grants a host port against bare probe sandboxes and starts no monitor — died in phase 3 of 8. It now returns without opening a channel when the caller started no monitor at all, and still refuses a monitor that started and published no port.

## Decisions made

- The requirement is a flag each caller sets, not a rule `cmd_channel` applies to every leg: the second shape refused an operator's host port that was merely slow to start, and `bin/lib/sbx/real-stack.bash` turns that refusal into a full teardown.
- The probe is a subcommand of the transport, not a dial written into `gb-kata-vm`: `parse_upstream` and `connect_upstream` already own the family split and the 1-65535 port check, and a second copy answered `tcp:localhost` as an address nothing serves rather than as a malformed argument.
- The supervision fix is #6029's change copied verbatim rather than a smaller one written here, so the merge that brings #6029 in is a no-op instead of a conflict on a supervision boundary.

## Review focus

Read `kata_vsock_upstream_reachable` in `bin/lib/kata/vsock.bash`: its first argument must stay the one `kata_vsock_listen_bg` passes, or the probe and the forwarder dial as different users, and no one screen shows both call sites. In the ported commit the part to check is that the new early return sits above the existing refusal, so a started-but-silent monitor still fails the launch.

Bumps `prismor/runtime/__init__.py` (the single version source — `release.yml` derives the immunity-agent shim from it) and writes the changelog for everything merged since v1.46.0.

## What ships
- **`prismor mode`** — three governance postures (`dev-safe`, `trusted-workspace`, `regulated-airgap`) that compile into `.prismor/policy.yaml` + `.prismor/agents.yaml`. No new enforcement path. (#353, via #369)
- **`prismor setup` offers a posture** when enforce is selected, instead of going straight to the 77-rule picker. (#370)
- **Tag inference narrowed** — `untrusted_content` no longer fires on every in-workspace `file_read` / unmapped `tool_result`, which had made the trifecta rule mean "no command may follow a read".
- **Egress false positive fixed** — `ssh-keygen -C dev@example.com` is no longer a destination.

#356 shipped and was reverted in #369 in favour of #353's design, so it is deliberately absent from the changelog.

## Testing
- `bash scripts/run_security_tests.sh` — all checks passed
- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q -p no:randomly` — 21 failed, 2495 passed. The FAILED set is **byte-identical** to the same run on `v1.46.0` (diffed), i.e. all 21 are pre-existing and machine-dependent (enrollment/keychain), none introduced here.
- Wizard driven through a pty end to end: enforce → GOVERNANCE MODE step (coverage/friction bars, `e` explain pager) → picking a named mode skips the rule picker and renumbers correctly → install logs `Compiling governance mode 'trusted-workspace'` → the written policy carries `mode_id: trusted-workspace`, 27/80 rules, deny-by-default egress.

After merge: tag `v1.47.0` to trigger the GitHub Release + PyPI publish.

author: lesternare
body:
## Summary

Add an experimental acquisition-context contract in `@disclosureos/instruments/experimental/v2`. Raw products now have a standalone declared history connecting physical instrument IDs, exact manifest revisions, deployments, channel calibration bindings, capture times, and clock metadata. Missing legacy history remains explicit and is never resolved by choosing the newest or first inventory entry.

Pinned context must match the instrument, configuration, and channel. Acquisitions must fit their declared deployment and calibration windows; calibration performed after acquisition cannot backfill acquisition-time calibration. Half-open interval rules distinguish an interval ending at expiry from a point sample at expiry. Adding a later manifest or calibration preserves existing bindings.

Preserve unknown configuration, sampling, clock, site, and calibration details as incomplete archival context. Review metadata remains separate from calibration declarations. Add a standalone versioned JSON Schema, synthetic example, portable conformance corpus, CI coverage, and documentation. Reuse a new plain records `compareUtcInstants` helper for exact fractional/offset ordering without passing Zod schemas across packages.

Follows #16. Existing v1 and experimental schema artifacts remain unchanged.

## Validation

- All package builds and type checks passed; 176 package tests passed.
- 71 new acquisition checks passed, including independent Ajv/runtime structural agreement, artifact drift, round trips, exact temporal boundaries, non-resolution of legacy labels, and 1,500 explicit channel/calibration bindings.
- All 191 existing experimental checks and the 22-fixture legacy runtime/JSON Schema/CLI matrix passed.
- Records and instruments publication/declaration gates passed under the existing ESM policy.
- A clean consumer installed packed records/instruments, compiled the public types, exercised exact UTC ordering and calibration-after-acquisition rejection, and loaded both new schema aliases and the legacy entrypoint.
- Historical schema artifacts are unchanged; whitespace checks passed.

## Boundaries

This validates declared nominal history, not scientific calibration adequacy, artifact bytes, synchronization accuracy, or timing-uncertainty propagation. Profile and external checks remain explicitly not checked. The parser cannot enforce immutable storage across separate submissions. Binding this inventory to Observation products by verified identities/digests, dataset/session composition, native adapters, research-profile integration, and independent reproduction remain subsequent work. No package publication, partner import, or application deployment is included.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [playwright](https://playwright.dev) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright)) | [`1.62.1` → `1.63.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/playwright/1.62.1/1.63.0) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/playwright/1.63.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/playwright/1.62.1/1.63.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>microsoft/playwright (playwright)</summary>

### [`v1.63.0`](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases/tag/v1.63.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/microsoft/playwright/compare/v1.62.1...v1.63.0)

#### 🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named `lock`.
Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and [projects](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-projects), while
everything else keeps running in parallel:

```js
test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});
```

A test can hold multiple locks, and [test.describe()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-describe) accepts a `lock` for the whole group.
Learn more about [test locks](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-parallel#test-locks).

#### 🪟 Locate across frames

[page.frameLocator()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-frame-locator) and [frame.frameLocator()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-frame#frame-frame-locator) called without a selector search in any frame of the
subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

```js
// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();
```

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it
matches elements in several frames.

#### 👁️ Visible-only locators

New [locator.visible()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-visible) returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended
replacement for the `:visible` CSS pseudo-class:

```js
await page.locator('button').visible().click();
```

#### 🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments,
and [test.step()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-step) accepts `subtitle` and `params` options for your own steps:

```js
await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });
```

Reporters receive them via [testStep.subtitle](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-teststep#test-step-subtitle) and [testStep.params](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-teststep#test-step-params). For Playwright API
steps, the subtitle is the locator or the navigation url — for example, `Click` with subtitle `getByRole('button')`.
Both are rendered next to the step title in the trace viewer and the HTML report.

#### 🖼️ Aria and screen snapshots in traces

The `snapshots` option of [tracing.start()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-tracing#tracing-start) and the [testOptions.trace](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-trace) fixture option now accept an
object selecting what to capture on every action:

```js
// playwright.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  use: {
    trace: {
      mode: 'on',
      snapshots: { dom: true, aria: true, screen: true }
    },
  },
});
```

With aria and screen snapshots recorded, the new **Display Aria** mode in the trace viewer shows the action screenshot
side by side with the aria snapshot, and hovering an aria node highlights it on the screenshot.

#### New APIs

##### Browser and Context

- [`httpCredentials`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-http-credentials) now also accepts an array of credentials. The first entry matching the request origin is used, and entries without an origin match any request.
- New option [`opfs`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-storage-state-option-opfs) includes the [origin private file system](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/File_System_API/Origin_private_file_system) in the storage state, so it can be persisted and restored into later contexts.
- New events [page.on('dialogclosed')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-event-dialog-closed) and [browserContext.on('dialogclosed')](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-event-dialog-closed) are emitted when a JavaScript dialog is accepted, dismissed or closed by the user.

##### Locators

- New [locator.ariaSnapshotJSON()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot-json) and [page.ariaSnapshotJSON()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-aria-snapshot-json) return the aria snapshot as a JSON value instead of YAML markup, with `mode`, `depth` and `boxes` options.
- [apiRequestContext.get()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-get) and other request methods accept a type argument that types the response `json()`:

```js
const response = await request.get<User>('/api/users/42');
const user = await response.json(); // typed as User
```

##### Test runner

- New standalone [testOptions.reducedMotion](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-reduced-motion), [testOptions.forcedColors](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-forced-colors) and [testOptions.contrast](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testoptions#test-options-contrast) options.
- New `--add-reporter` command line option appends a reporter on top of the ones configured in `playwright.config`, instead of replacing them like `--reporter` does.
- New `omitTags` option for the `list`, `line`, `dot`, `github` and `junit` reporters suppresses the tags that are automatically appended to test titles.

##### Command line

- `npx playwright install --no-remove` keeps the browsers of other Playwright installations instead of removing them.
- `npx playwright codegen --http-credentials` records against pages behind HTTP authentication.

##### Miscellaneous

- New built-in [`perfetto`](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#perfetto-reporter) reporter writes a Trace Event Format file for the [Perfetto UI](https://ui.perfetto.dev) or `chrome://tracing`, rendering the test run as a timeline with a lane per worker.
- The HTML report renders a duration waterfall next to test steps.

#### Announcements

- ⚠️ The experimental `@playwright/experimental-ct-react`, `@playwright/experimental-ct-react17` and `@playwright/experimental-ct-vue` packages will no longer be updated. Follow the [migration guide](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-components#migration-from-the-experimental-packages) to move to the stories model introduced in 1.62. Story ids passed to [fixtures.mount()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-fixtures#fixtures-mount) can now be typed through the generated `Stories` registry.
- ⚠️ Ubuntu 20.04 is not supported anymore.
- 🐧 On Linux arm64, Playwright now downloads the [Chrome for Testing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-for-testing) build of Chromium, the same build used on all other platforms.

#### Browser Versions

- Chromium 153.0.8010.12
- Mozilla Firefox 155.0
- WebKit 26.6

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

- Google Chrome 153
- Microsoft Edge 153

</details>

**Human co-sign required: yes** — touches `crates/wkp-git` (CODEOWNERS-gated).

## Summary
- New `crates/wkp-git/src/allowed_signers.rs`: `parse`/`append` for the store's `allowed_signers` file, in the exact minimal format git's own `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` consumes (`<principal> <key-type> <base64-key>`) — no wkp-specific superset, git can read this file directly.
- Role (`human`/`agent`) is not a separate column — it's read off the principal's `human:`/`agent:` prefix, the same convention design 5.4's `provenance.actor` field already uses.
- `wkp init` (via `apply_init_settings`) now creates the file if missing and sets `gpg.format=ssh` / `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` (local config, absolute path).
- `commit_all` is untouched — it stays the unsigned, test-only helper its own doc comment already describes; real signed-commit plumbing is M2-2 (#38).

- [x] `allowed_signers` file format documented (header comment in the file itself + module doc comment)
- [x] `wkp_git::allowed_signers::parse(&str) -> Vec<SignerEntry>`, tolerant of malformed lines

- [x] Confirmed `ensure_min_git_version()` (ADR-0001) is unaffected — no change to that gate, all its existing tests still pass

## Out of scope (per issue #37)
OS keystore/Keychain ACL integration for agent private keys (deferred alongside M4's keystore work). Generating keys. Signing commits (M2-2, #38).

author: pengxu9-rgb
body:
## What

`#2113` stopped ingestion **discarding** real merchant variant ids. This is the other half: the curated feed never put them into the record for ingestion to keep.

`shopify_product_to_record` gated variant emission on `product.get(FOLDED_INTO_KEY)` — a listing the shade-fold had just *built* out of separate per-shade rows. That excluded every storefront publishing its shades **natively**, as one product with many variants, which is the normal Shopify shape rather than the exception.

## Measured (flowerbeauty.com, from prod egress, 2026-09-07)

`/products.json` serves 49 products, **29 multi-variant**, carrying **185 real numeric Shopify variant ids**. `fold_shade_listings` folds **zero** of them (`bases=0, shades=0`), so the gate refused all 185.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ids surviving `records_for_brand` into the record | **0** | **185** |
| planned `catalog_skus` | 49 | **234** (49 canonical + 185 variant) |
| variant SKUs with a real numeric id | 0 | **185** |
| …paired with a `catalog_offers` row | 0 | **185 / 185** |
| Tier-A try-on variants present | **0 / 4** | **4 / 4**, each with an offer |

The prod baseline confirms the outcome today: 49/49 `catalog_skus` with `source_variant_id = product_key`, 0 real ids, and — because the identity was never crawled *into* `seed_data` either — **0 rows the #2113 backfill can recover**. All four Tier-A ids (`17281773207622`, `32120934727750`, `39777342488646`, `39406294532166`) were absent from the plan, from `catalog_skus` and from `seed_data`, while all four sit in the storefront's own feed.

## The pair is the point

A SKU written without a `catalog_offers` row is **inert** — the serving price gate and recall both read `catalog_offers`. That is why this goes through ingestion's variant lane rather than the promoter, which writes SKUs and no offers (5,271 promoter-built `::v::` SKUs on the external track carry 0 offers; 1,583 of 1,583 ingestion-built `::v:` SKUs carry one).

## Still opt-in

Emitting variants adds one SKU + offer per variant, which moves recall fan-out, offer aggregation and INCI attachment for every row a caller ingests. So `records_for_brand` takes a new `emit_real_variants` (CLI `--emit-real-variants`), default off — **no existing caller changes behaviour**.

## The two lanes admit on different rules, deliberately

- A **folded** row's variants were assembled by us and may carry a synthesised `<handle>:<i>` id — display data the shade selector needs, and one of the fourteen fabricating writers `#2113` registered. Ingestion's own provenance check decides whether such a row may also be sold, so the fold lane is left exactly as it was.
- A **native** row has no such excuse: its ids come straight off the merchant's feed, so anything `services/variant_identity` cannot place as `MERCHANT_ISSUED` is dropped here rather than carried forward as a decoy that looks purchasable — the failure the gateway's `isRestatedProductId` guard exists to catch.
- A **single** native variant is admitted on that same rule, not refused for being alone: flowerbeauty's Petal Pout Lip Color is a one-variant product whose id is real.

## Tests

Four new tests; verified they **fail against this branch's parent** and pass with the fix. author: mvxtechnologies
body:
Fixes #232 (both owner decisions on the issue), plus the scale-bar relocation
from PR #224's follow-up as a separate, trivially revertable last commit.

## The chip is now the point-action hub

Tap the map → the existing readout chip shows the tapped coordinates plus
distance/bearing from your position (muted, absent without a fix) and two
actions: **Navigate** opens the coordinates dialog **prefilled with the tapped
point** (Go / Set destination); **Waypoint** opens the editor **for the tapped
point**. Long-press remains the destination pin. No new gesture, no new popup.

"Go to coordinates" is renamed **Navigate to coordinates** everywhere — dialog
title, entry label, the "+" sheet row (kept as the secondary, empty-box
entry). Zero leftover strings in `src`, `app`, `.maestro`.

## Waypoint form takes a name — create-with-name, not create-then-rename

Both new-waypoint entries open the editor on an *uncreated* waypoint and
create on Done, so backing out leaves no pin. A **Name** field, prefilled with
the auto-number, sits at the top. The `^Waypoint (\d+)$` scan moved into
`src/core/library/waypoints.ts` so the store's stamp and the editor's prefill
cannot drift; a *named* waypoint takes no number, so the sequence is untouched.
Live recording waypoints get a label through `recorderStore.updateWaypoint`.
The dialog title is a static "Waypoint" — echoing the name would put two
`Waypoint \d+` matches on screen, which is exactly what `waypoint.yaml` reads.

## Two iOS platform traps, found by bisecting against a rebuilt baseline

1. **A Paper `Icon` or `Pressable` inside the chip's MapLibre marker stopped
   the whole marker from drawing on iOS** — no chip at all. Bisected against
   `c8716f3` under identical conditions to confirm it was the change, not
   pre-existing. Buttons are plain `View`s with raw responder props.
2. **On iOS, a tap anywhere on the marker is reported to `onMapPress` as the
   marker's own anchor** (instrumented `map.project` vs `nativeEvent.point`:
   a tap 56 pt away came back at the anchor), so a map-level hit-test can
   never tell the two buttons apart. Final design: responder props take the
   tap on iOS; the same rectangles are published and hit-tested in
   `onMapPress` for Android, where marker children are rasterized; and an
   `onClaimTouch` at touch-start makes MapScreen ignore the map press for
   600 ms — without it iOS fired both and dismissed the chip under the action.

## Scale bar → bottom-left (owner decision, separate commit `dd96d72`)

Mounted as the first child of the bottom chrome column rather than absolutely
positioned, so it stacks **above** the recording bar / legends without knowing
about them, and sits just above the tab bar when they are absent. Proven with
a mid-recording screenshot. The top-left column lost its now-empty gap.

## Tests — 2197 total, zero lint warnings

`waypoints.test.ts` (numbering: ignores renamed labels and near-misses,
order-independent) · `libraryStore.waypoints.test.ts` (explicit name +
coordinate, trimming, fallback, sequence untouched) · `recorderStore.test.ts`
(live label) · `MapPointChip.test.tsx` (11: both actions, each responder fires
only its own callback, touch claim before press, map-level geometry routing)
· `WaypointEditorDialog.test.tsx` (5: prefill, no title echo, Done submits,
Return dismisses without closing) · `GoToCoordinatesDialog.test.tsx` (opened
from the chip: title, prefill, Go/Set destination live without typing).

## Maestro on iOS (iPhone 17, final build)

`waypoint.yaml` **PASS** (`copyTextFrom 'Waypoint \d+'` now reads the Name
field; `n2 === n1 + 1` holds). `smoke.yaml` **PASS** — note its `Map point
readout` block is *skipped* on iOS because the map view masks marker
accessibility from XCUITest, so #236's reported re-tap failure could be
neither reproduced nor refuted; flow untouched.

## Device-only / open

- **Android is unverified** for the chip's press handling: the responder path
  and the geometry fallback are complementary by design, but only iOS was
  exercised. Worth a tap on the Samsung after the OTA.
- An intermittent iOS-26 simulator flake: twice the editor opened from the
  chip with keyboard + scrim but no dialog visible to XCUITest; a third run
  rendered it. Logged, with pixels of the working case.

author: hc12r
body:
ADR-033 §3 lists `jvm` as *"deferred until adapter exists"*. Both
required reference adapters (`pyharness`, `nodeharness`) now exist and
prove the protocol is language-neutral, so what is left is a decision
about the adapter, not about the protocol.

**Status is `proposed`** — this is a design for review, not an
implementation. No code changes.

## The measurement that shaped it

The JVM differs from Python and Node in the one way that matters here:
it is compiled. Both existing adapters `//go:embed` harness *source* and
hand it to an interpreter the host already has. Java 11's JEP 330
(`java Harness.java`) would preserve that pattern exactly — embed
source, launch it, no build step anywhere.

It works, and measurement rules it out (OpenJDK 24, 3 runs each):

| Launch mode | Per-invocation |
|---|---|
| `java Harness.java` (JEP 330) | **1.07 – 1.16 s** |
| `java -cp . Harness` (precompiled) | 0.07 – 0.08 s |
| `java -jar harness.jar` | 0.08 – 0.09 s |
| `node harness.mjs` (existing) | 0.05 – 0.07 s |
| `python3 harness.py` (existing) | 0.05 – 0.07 s |
| `javac` (one-time) | 1.63 s |

ADR-035 gives task nodes a fresh child per attempt with **no warm pool**,
so source-launch would add ~1 second to *every* attempt — 20x the two
adapters it sits beside, in exchange for a pattern rather than a
property.

## Decision

Embed `.java` source (so `go build` alone still yields a complete
binary), compile it **once** per harness-version/JDK-version cache key on
first use, and launch the compiled class thereafter — 0.07 s, within
30 ms of both existing adapters.

ADR-026 carries over unchanged: no JDK is ever downloaded, and a missing
`javac`, a JRE-only host, or a JDK below the Java 17 floor is refused
**by name at validation**, never discovered mid-run.

## The cost, stated plainly

This requires a **JDK at run time, not merely a JRE**. That is a genuine
narrowing neither existing adapter imposes, and JRE-only container images
are common. The alternative that avoids it — embedding a prebuilt harness
JAR — is recorded in full with the trade it makes: it would move a JDK
into Brokoli's *own* build, so `go build` from a clean checkout would no
longer produce a working JVM adapter. I judged buildable-from-source
worth more than JRE-only support today, and the decision is reversible if
that changes. Reviewers who weigh those differently should say so — this
is the load-bearing choice in the ADR.

## Two things pinned rather than left to care

- **Hand-rolled JSON.** The JDK ships no JSON parser and the harness must
  not acquire one (a harness dependency lands in every JVM task's
  classpath and will eventually conflict with the task's own). So the
  harness hand-rolls a minimal reader over a closed frame vocabulary, and
  its number handling must satisfy **the same fixtures that caught #479**
  — where `json.Unmarshal` silently decoded `9007199254740993` as
  `...992`. Java's `long` is natively 64-bit and better positioned than
  either existing adapter, but "better positioned" is not "verified".
- **Explicit entrypoints.** `fully.qualified.Class#staticMethod`,
  resolved through a `URLClassLoader`, never inferred by scanning for a
  single public method — that would make *adding a second method* a
  silent behavior change.

## What static typing buys

Java's signature *is* the ADR-032 contract, so port types and
`parameter_bindings` are derived from the method signature by an
annotation processor at compile time rather than from decorators or
inference. A signature and its declared contract are produced from one
source in one step and cannot drift — something neither existing SDK can
offer.

## Follow-ups

Six phases, each provable alone, staged the way ADR-033's own phases
were. Phase 4 (engine wiring) is the real test of ADR-033's claim that
the engine holds no language-specific invocation code: Python and Node
are both interpreted and dynamically typed, so if `prepareTaskHarness`
needs more than a new case, the claim was weaker than believed. Phase 6
(the `brokoli-jvm` SDK, a new repository) does not begin until phase 4
proves the runtime contract, matching the ordering both existing SDKs
followed.

author: tinycute00
body:
## Problem

When a user selects a session from the session selector (via /resume or app.session.resume), the selector was closed (done()) before the session was actually resumed (handleResumeSession). This caused the selector to disappear silently without any visible feedback, making users think nothing happened.

## Root Cause

In `showSessionSelector()`, the `onSelect` callback called `done()` before `handleResumeSession()`:

```typescript
async (sessionPath) => {
    done();  // Selector closes immediately
    await this.handleResumeSession(sessionPath);  // Resume happens after
},
```

Since `handleResumeSession` is async and shows status messages via `showStatus()`, calling `done()` first meant the selector closed before the user could see any feedback.

## Fix

Reorder the operations: resume the session first (which shows appropriate status messages), then close the selector and return focus to the editor:

```typescript
async (sessionPath) => {
    await this.handleResumeSession(sessionPath);
    done();
},
```

This ensures:
1. The session resume happens first
2. Status messages ("Resumed session", "Resume cancelled", or errors) are visible to the user
3. Then the selector closes and focus returns to the editor

## Testing

- [ ] Select a session from the session selector
- [ ] Verify status message is shown before selector closes
- [ ] Verify selector closes after resume completes
- [ ] Test with a session that fails to resume (should show error)
